<!-- lecture 1 -->

A'udhu Billahi min al-Shaytan al-Rajim. Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. Wa sallallahu 'ala rasulihi wa alihi al-tayyibin al-tahirin wa sallama 'alayhim ajma'in. (I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah's blessings be upon His Messenger and his pure and purified family, and may peace be upon them all.) Believing brothers and sisters, the lessons of the book *Anwaar al-Latifah* are comprised of the lofty contents of the sciences of realities (*'uloom-e-haqa'iq*), which have been interpreted based on the sciences of the *anbiya'* and *awliya'*. I had recorded these lessons with the permission (*ijazat*) of Maulaya 'awliy al-ne'mati al-mansub al-karim wal-faqeem, Hadrat 'Abdullah Sahib, 'atala Allahu baqa'ahu wa ja'alna fida', for the benefit of my father and other members of my family. By the command of my Aaqa and Maula, this recording has now been deposited in the treasury of the *Da'wat Sharief*. I most humbly request (*istida'*) that you please do not email these lessons, nor attempt to exchange them in any way on the internet, nor store them on your computer. Because despite all secure exchanges, there is a possibility that once something is on the web, then after that, all these things become accessible to everyone. And these lessons can fall into the hands of the undeserving (*ghair-mustahiqqeen*). Now, if anyone, despite this request, commits this act, then on the Day of Judgment (*baroz-e-qiyamat*), before Allah and His Messenger, the one who does this will be solely responsible, and I will be free of responsibility for it. If you are copying, listening to, transmitting, giving to someone else, modifying, or committing any such act (*fe'l*) with these lessons without permission which is a sin (*gunah*) in the sight of Allah and His Messenger, then you and only you are responsible for it, and I will be free of responsibility for this act on the Day of Judgment. The *Awliya'* of Allah have warned of a most severe punishment (*'azab*) for those who do not safeguard these lofty sciences (*'uloom-e-'aliya*), specifically giving news of the punishment of cold iron, which is the most severe in its terribleness. A'adhana Allah (May Allah protect us). May Allah prolong the shadow of Sayyidna al-Da'i and the Manasib-e-Kiram over us and make their lights (*anwaar*) flow upon us. Ameen. Bi-haqqi Sayyidina Maulana Muhammadin wa 'ala aali Sayyidina Maulana Muhammadin wa barik wa sallim. (By the right of our master, Maulana Muhammad, and upon the family of our master, Maulana Muhammad, and grant blessings and peace.)

<!-- lecture 2 -->

Bismillah. Al-Fatihah. Al-Fatihah. Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim (In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful). Alhamdulillah rabb al-'alamin (All praise is for Allah, the Lord of the worlds). Al-Rahman al-Rahim (The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful). Malik yawm al-din (Master of the Day of Judgment). Iyyaka na'budu wa iyyaka nasta'in (You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help). Ihdina al-sirat al-mustaqim (Guide us to the straight path). Sirat alladhina an'amta 'alayhim (The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor), ghayr al-maghdubi 'alayhim wa la al-dallin (not of those who have earned [Your] anger, nor of those who are astray).

<!-- lecture 3 -->

Bismillah. Several copies need to be made. One should study beforehand. Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. Al-Suradiq al-Awwal. Suradiq, as they say, is a curtain. One must see its original meaning, which is not even in my mind. Al-Suradiq, al-Suradiq al-Awwal. A discourse... This book, Sar Dard, is called Suradiq. In Suradiq, there are five chapters. In every chapter, there are five sections. Suradiq means palace, and it also means curtains. So, if they write al-Suradiq al-Awwal... Suradiq itself is what it is. It is plural. Its singular is... its wahid (singular) is... al-Suradiq al-Awwal. The first Suradiq from Kitab al-Anwar. From Kitab al-Anwar, the first Suradiq. From Kitab al-Anwar... It has `khamsatu abwab` (five chapters). In it, there are five chapters. It has been stated that `Bab al-Awwal`, `Suradiq al-Awwal`. From Bab al-Awwal, Suradiq al-Awwal. `yujma'u khamsata fusul` (it gathers five sections). So in it, there are five sections. Five, five sections. So how many did it become in total? How many sections? 125 sections are in it. `Al-faslu al-awwalu minha` (The first section from it). From the first section of it. `Naqulu wa lamma kana ma huwa al-maqsudu wa al-kalamu 'ala al-mawaddati al-sharifati al-mu'addati ila al-wajibat al-sharifah haqiqatan mahdatan` (We say: and when that which is intended and the discourse is about the noble affections that lead to the noble obligations, it is a pure reality). `la ta'weela fiha` (in which there is no interpretation). `wa la ramza minha` (and no symbol from it). `la ta'weela`—why is it read this way? Without `ta'weel`. This is called `nafi al-jins` (negation of the genus) in the terminology of grammar and syntax. "No" whatsoever. Meaning, there is no interpretation in it. La... If you say `la ta'weelun fihi`, what does it mean? There is no interpretation in it. No... The word "any" is not there. If you say `ta'weelun`, then what is it? The word "any" will not come. There is no interpretation in it. Right. If you say `la ta'weela`, then it means there is no interpretation at all in it. This is called `nafi al-jins` (negation of the genus). `Nafi`. `la ta'weela fihi` (there is no interpretation in it). `wa la ramza minha` (and no symbol from it). And no `ramz` (symbol/allusion) is there. And no `ishara` (indication). What is being said? We say that when the purpose, the intention, is that which has been intended, it is such a discourse, on the noble beginnings, as a pure reality. In it, we do not want to express `zahir` (exoteric) and `ta'weel` (esoteric interpretation), but rather we want to express a pure reality. This is our objective. `la ta'weel`, in which there is no interpretation, no `ramz`, no `ishara`. `Thumma al-kalamu 'ala kaffati al-mawjudat` (Then the discourse is upon all existing things). Then the discourse on all existing things. That is, we want to address all existing things that have appeared before our existence. We will have a discourse on them. `idh bi-ma'rifati dhalika wa al-ittila'i 'alayhi wa ta'ati awliya' Allahi wa muhabbbatihim wa al-taqarrubi ila Allahi bihim wa bi-luzumi hududihim al-mansubina min qibali al-qa'im al-'ilmi wa al-'amali bima warada min al-shara'i' allati la yutada ila tawhidi Allahi ta'ala wa takabbar` (For by the gnosis of that, and the acquaintance with it, and the obedience to the Friends of God, and the love for them, and drawing near to God through them, and by adhering to their appointed Hudud from the direction of the Qa'im, with the knowledge and action that has come from the religious laws through which one is guided to the Oneness of God, the Exalted and Great). For... because with the `ma'rifah` (gnosis) of that... of that thing. The `ma'rifah` of what thing? Of all those existing things that came into being before us. Then the discourse is on all existing things that came into being before us. Because through its `ma'rifah`, what will happen? `idh bi-ma'rifati dhalika` because through its `ma'rifah`, and by gaining knowledge of it and through obedience to the `Awliya' Allah` (Friends of God)... and through their love... their love, and drawing near to Allah and through attaching to their `hudud` who have been appointed (`mansubin`). `Mansubin` means appointed. Those who have been appointed, from their side, and through the action (`'amal`) which is placed from the `shari'ahs` (religious laws)... So there is love, and there is action. And that which has been appointed from the `shari'ah`, from the `shari'ah`... guidance... guidance is given towards the `tawhid` (oneness) of Allah Ta'ala. Through this path, one can reach the `tawhid` of Allah. What are the two? `Ibadah` (worship) and `tawhid`. `Muwalat` (allegiance/love), `muhabbah` (love), and `'amal` (action). `Wilayah` and `'amal`. Through these two, one can attain access to the `tawhid` of Allah. `wa bi-dhalika ta'lu darajatu al-ma'ad` (And by that, the ranks of the afterlife are elevated). And through this, the ranks of the `ma'ad` (afterlife) are elevated. From this, the ranks are elevated. `wa yakunu al-khalasu min hadha al-'alami al-kawni wa al-fasad` (And salvation occurs from this world of being and corruption). And salvation occurs from this world of being and corruption. Who is its writer? Who is its author? Sayyidi Dawud bin 'Ajabshah. In the year 1000... 99. 1099. Your handwriting is very good, it's very... And these writers... Mulla Aminuddin Sahab. This book is from 1099. Navab Jama Masjid. 1099. And who is this? This is... `bi-khaṭṭi al-ḥaqīr `Abdillāh Nāṣir al-Dīn`. And it was written in the year... 1000... Sayyidna Ibrahim... Sayyidna Muhammad bin Isma'il. In fact, Sayyidna... as we have written a gloss (`nash`)... you... on this... Sayyidna Hasan Khan Sahab. At that time... This is the time of Sayyidna Hasan Khan. And we have glossed it after Sayyidna Muhammad bin Isma'il... Sayyidna Muhammad bin Isma'il bin Ibrahim... they were living in that era. And at that time, a gloss was written on it by Sayyidna Hasan Khan Sahab. Where is Sayyidna Hasan Khan's grave? Near Sayyidna 'Ali Sahab. On that side... And salvation occurs from the world of being and corruption. `wa yumkinu al-qawdu ila al-mabda'i alladhi minhu al-ibtida'atu al-sharifah` (And it is possible to return to the origin from which the noble beginnings came). And it is possible to return... `qawd`, to return towards the `mabda'` (origin), from where they had come, there one returns. This can happen in the same way. How can the return to the original homeland (`watan-e-asli`) be possible? What is our original homeland? The world of spirits (`'alam al-ruh`). From where we came. That is the original homeland. `wa al-kawnu ma'ahum fi dar al-quds` (And being with them in the Abode of Sanctity). And to be with them in `dar al-quds` (the Abode of Sanctity). `ballaghana Allahu ilayhim` (May Allah make us reach them). `wa a'anana 'ala al-irtiqai wa al-wusuli ilayhim bi-haqqi Muhammadin wa alihi al-tahirin, salawatullahi 'alayhim ajma'in` (And may He aid us in the ascent and arrival to them, by the right of Muhammad and his pure progeny, the blessings of Allah be upon them all). Here it has come. It has become crooked. It has become like this. This... this is it. This one. `Salawatullahi 'alayhim ajma'in`. `wa hadha huwa al-'ilmu alladhi yaduruna 'alayhi wa yajuruna ladayhi`. Above there is some difference. `yaduruna`. `yaduruna ladayhi`. And that... and this is that knowledge... it is that knowledge... For example, all creations (`khala'iq`) are circling around it. And are making rounds around it. They are making rounds around it. The knowledge of what? It is such a knowledge, for the attainment of which every person wants to move forward. The knowledge of the origin (`asl`), the knowledge of the `mabda'` (origin). For this, every person... what was our `mabda'`, from where did we come? All the creations are circling around it. They are making rounds, but they cannot reach the origin. They want to know where their `mabda'` is. They are making rounds, but they do not find it. `wa la sabila li-ahadin minhum ilayhi` (And there is no path for any of them to it). And there is no path for anyone among them to that knowledge. They cannot attain that knowledge. `illa al-qalil` (except for a few). A few people. `mimman i'tasama bi-al-a'immati min al-i Muhammad, salamu Allahi 'alayhim ajma'in. Wa iltazama hududahum al-mayamin` (From those who held fast to the Imams from the progeny of Muhammad, peace of Allah be upon them all. And they committed to their blessed Hudud). And they committed to them. They were attached to the true `hudud`. Only they can attain that side. The rest are all revolving around it. `al-faslu al-thani min al-babi al-awwali min al-suradiqi al-awwal` (The second section of the first chapter of the first Suradiq). The second section... the second section of the first chapter from the first `suradiq`. `wa kana la dalila 'ala dhikri dhalika illa bi-dhikri Allahi ta'ala wa takabbar alladhi bi-dhikrihi fi kulli shay'in yustaftahu` (And there was no guide to the mention of that except by the mention of God, the Exalted and Great, by whose mention everything is opened). `wa bi-asma'ihi al-husna yutawassalu ilayhi fi kulli matlubin wa yustanjahu` (And by His most beautiful names, a means is sought to Him for every desired thing and success is sought). And there is no path to its mention except by the mention of Allah Ta'ala. And `takabbar` Allah Ta'ala, `takabbar`. So first of all, it is necessary for us to mention Allah. Without it, there can be no mention. `alladhi bi-dhikrihi` (He by whose mention)... that is, with His mention... with whose mention? With the mention of Allah. `fi kulli shay'in` (in everything)... `yustaftahu` (it is opened). It is opened. That is, it is opened. `yustaftahu` means to open, to seek the opening. The chapter of `istif'al`. What is its root? `Fataha`. And `istiftah`, which is also called `iftitah`. And in Arabic, `istiftah` means to seek, to express a desire. To seek the opening. The request to begin is made. This is the meaning of `istiftah`, `alif-sin-ta`. To seek to be opened. The request to be opened is made. A request is made. `wa bi-asma'ihi al-husna` (and by His most beautiful names). And by His `asma' al-husna` (most beautiful names)... What is `ism`? Is it masculine or feminine? Masculine. What is `husna`? Is it masculine or feminine? Plural. Plural. What is it? Feminine. It is feminine. Its masculine is `ahsan`. `Asma' Allah al-husna`. `Husna` is plural... What is its plural? `Asma' al-husna`. What kind of plural is it? `asma' Allah al-husna`. What is `husna`? Is it feminine or masculine? You tell me. It's a noun. `Husna`, the word, is it masculine or feminine? We call a wife `husna`, Husna Bibi. So what does that mean? It's a woman's name, isn't it, Husna? So, whose feminine is it? What's its masculine? `Ahsan`. `Ahsan`. We name men Ahsan, and women Husna. So, the feminine of `ahsan` is `husna`. So why did the word "feminine" come here? Because `asma'` is a plural of non-rational beings (`ghayr dhawi al-'uqul`). Therefore, its... the adjective that is brought for it, this is an attribute, this is the qualified noun. `Asma'` is the qualified noun, `husna` is the attribute. So its attribute will come as if that noun is a feminine singular. Although it is a plural, the Arabs, in their way, consider it a feminine singular. This is an Arabic rule. `wa bi-asma'ihi` (and by his names)... And by his `asma' al-husna`. `yutawassalu ilayhi` (a means is sought to Him). `Tawassul` is not the doer here, so it's read in the passive voice. A means is taken to Him. What is the root of `yutawassalu`? `Wasala`. `waw-sin-lam`. `yutawassalu ilayhi fi kulli matlubin` (a means is sought to Him for every desired thing). What is the root of `matlub`? `Talab`. From `talab` comes `talib`. What does `talib` mean? One who seeks. What does `matlub` mean? That which is sought. One is the doer, and one is the object. `fi kulli matlubin wa yustanjahu` (in every desired thing, and success is sought). What does that mean? What is this from, `yustanjahu`? `Najaha`. `nun-jim-ha`. And from it, `istinjah`. To seek success. So, success is sought. By what means? Through His means. In our every request, through His means, success is granted. Or rather, the desire for success is made. `wa kana musabbahan muta'aliyan 'an an yaqa'a 'alayhi isharatu mushirin` (And He was glorified, exalted, above an indicator's indication falling upon Him). If you say `musabbih`, Allah Ta'ala cannot be a `musabbih`. Who is the `musabbih`? We are. The one who does `tasbih` (glorification), he is a `musabbih`. And Allah Ta'ala is `musabbah`, the one whose `tasbih` is done. `wa kana musabbahan` (And He was glorified)... And He is `musabbah`, whose `tasbih` is done. `muta'aliyan` (exalted), one who is high. What is the root of `ta'ala`? `Uluww`. `'ayn-lam-waw`. `Muta'aliyan`, what is it? It's on the pattern of `mutafa'ilan`. One who is high. Such that an indication from any indicator could fall upon Him, to indicate towards Him. Meaning, He is so high that no indication can fall upon Him. This is the real statement, this is the foundation of beliefs. This is the basis of beliefs. That no indication can fall upon Him, from which... to indicate. `an an yaqa'a 'alayhi isharatu mushirin` (that an indicator's indication should fall upon Him). That an indicator's indication should fall upon Him. `wa yatajasaru nahwahu khatiru khatirin bi-tawahhumin aw tafkirin`. `Yatajasaru`, what is `jasara`? Its root is `jisrun`, meaning a bridge. `Ta'weel` and the bridge of realities. `Tajasara` means one cannot cross over. One cannot cross over that... that. One cannot cross over. One cannot pass. `tajasara nahwahu` (towards Him). What does `khatir` mean? The heart. The heart cannot dare to cross over towards Him... with `tawahhum` (imagination) or `tafkir` (contemplation). By imagining or thinking, no objective is achieved. We just have to understand that we were created, so there is someone who created us. What He is like, what He is, we don't know anything. A man from the time of Imam Ali, Ibn al-Kawwa', asked a question. He said today I will ask Ali such a question that Ali will not be able to answer it. He came and asked, "O Ali, tell me, have you seen your God? `Hal ra'ayta Allah?` (Have you seen Allah?)" "Have you seen God?" He said, "You fool, can I worship God without seeing Him?" "How can I worship God without seeing Him?" He asked, "How did you see Him then?" "How did you see?" He said, "I did not see Him with the eyes, I saw Him with the `basirah` (insight)." A very big statement from our Mawla. I saw in such a way, I saw in such a way, I saw in such a way. `wa kana al-i'rabu 'anhu bi-Allahi ta'ala wa bi-al-mubdi'i bi-al-huwiyyati al-muta'aliyah ghayra waqi'in 'alayhi hadhani al-ismani wa al-sifatu` (And the expression about Him with "Allah, the Exalted," and with "the Originator," with the exalted Ipseity, these two names and attributes do not fall upon Him). And to express about Him... to express... with "Allah Ta'ala"... from thought, with Allah... To call Him Allah... `wa kana al-i'rabu 'anhu bi-Allahi ta'ala`. To call Him "Allah Ta'ala". What is it? `wa bi-al-mubdi'i` (and with the Originator)... or to call Him `mubdi'`. `Mubdi'` means Originator. `bi-al-huwiyyati al-muta'aliyah` (with the exalted Ipseity)... and to say He is `huwa`, `huwa` means He, who is exalted. The indication... with `huwa`, the indication is made. `Muta'aliyan` means He is exalted. `ghayra waqi'in 'alayhi hadhani al-ismani wa al-sifatu` (not falling upon him these two names and attributes). They do not fall... upon Him... these two... name and attribute. Both name and attribute. Neither name nor attribute falls on Him. Why? `idh al-asma'u wa al-sifatu la taqa'u illa 'ala misliha` (For names and attributes do not fall except upon their like). Because names and attributes do not fall except on their like. What do we do? We say "Allah" to recognize Him, we want to know Him, so we give Him a name. From our own tongue. And the tongue... you are its creator. You are the creator of the tongue. The thing you are the creator of, with that you are interpreting Allah. `kama qala amiru al-mu'minin` (as the Commander of the Faithful said). `al-asma'u wa al-sifatu dalalatun 'ala al-musamma` (Names and attributes are indicators of the named). Names and attributes point to their like. Its attribute is such... its attribute is such that he is Merciful. So we saw mercy in someone, so we applied Merciful to him. `wa fi shay'in min dhak`... and in its form... they fall. `'ala al-'ilmi wa al-tadbir` (upon knowledge and arrangement). And these names and attributes are `muhdathatun` (created/originated). `Muhdith` means the one who creates, `muhdath` means the created things. They have been created. They are not their own creators. But names and attributes are created by humans. A human is one who says "names and attributes" are `muhdathah`. They are created by humans. You named the child. Who is the one who gives the name? You are the one who gives the name. So they are our given names. `Muhdathah`. `wa al-muhdathu la yaqa'u 'ala al-muhdithi misluhu` (And the created thing does not fall upon its creator in a like manner). Here, specifically, they have put a `zabar` (vowel mark)... `muhdith`. And `muhdath`, which is... it does not fall upon its `muhdith` (creator) like itself. `kama qala Sayyiduna Mu'ayyad al-Din` (as our master Mu'ayyad al-Din said). Sayyidna Mu'ayyad al-Din, who is he? He is in the time of Mawlana Mustansir Billah. `Babul Abwab`. `wa lamma kanati al-hurufu al-mu'jamu muhdathatan` (And when the alphabet letters are created things). That when they are `huruf al-mu'jam`... `muhdathatun`. They are created. Sir, a question arises. It's a very good argument you've used that we are the creators of words. But there is a limitation in us too. The concept of a creator is that... because we do produce words, we are creators, but many things happen by His command, and then the words come out, otherwise the words don't come out. His command is a different matter, but are you the creator of these things or not? The words you are speaking... I am speaking, I am its creator, of these words I am speaking. Your argument... your argument is that we have the choice... We... with our creation... we... our creator, who is our creation, with that we want to place it on our creator. This is the whole thing. Then the choice is not with us. The choice is with you, but you do not have the choice to recognize Him. He is in such a `ghayb` (unseen) that you cannot lift its curtains. Only, to prove our existence, we say that there must be an originator for us. Who created... `lam takun tadullu 'ala al-mabda'i al-sani'i laha dhalalatan muhaqqiqatan musaddiqatan 'ala misliha` (They did not indicate the originating principle that made them, a true and verifying indication upon its like). `wa idh kanat al-qaulun kadhalika kanat hadhihi al-asma'u wa al-sifatu manfiyyatan 'an Allahi ta'ala wa takabbara wa kanat waqi'atan 'ala ibda'ihi alladhi huwa al-'aqlu al-awwal` (And when the saying was thus, these names and attributes were negated from God, the Exalted and Great, and they were falling upon His origination, which is the First Intellect). `al-mabda' al-awwal`. What does that mean? The first `ibda'` (origination) has happened. That is the `mubda' awwal`. Its relationship with our... whatever names, attributes are there, they are not from Allah Ta'ala. `wa kanat waqi'atan 'ala ibda'ihi`. Upon His `ibda'`. Yes. What is its `ibda'`? The `'aql al-awwal` (First Intellect). And the `mawjud al-awwal` (first existent). And the `sadir al-awwal` (first emanation). Whatever names, attributes are there, they are negated from Allah Ta'ala. `wa kanat waqi'atan 'ala ibda'ihi`. From whom? From... `wa ma zahara min fi'lihi fi ikhtira'ihi, la min jihati ismin wa la sifatin yakhtari'ani 'alayhi` (And what appeared from His action in His creation, not from the aspect of a name or an attribute that would be specific to Him). That which appeared from His action, from His creation. Not from the aspect of a name, nor from an attribute that would apply to Him... that would apply to His `mubda' ta'ala`. `li-ann dhalika maslubun 'anhu` (because that is stripped from Him). Because that is `maslub` (stripped) from Him. `Maslub` means it has been taken away, it is separated from Him. `waqi'un 'ala ibda'ihi` (falling upon His origination). Falling upon His `ibda'`. Which He created, all names and attributes fall upon that, which you are applying. That is a whole other matter. These names and attributes do not even fall upon His `ibda'`. How will they fall upon Allah, the `mubdi' ta'ala`? `wa al-'ijzu shamilun li-jami'i 'alam al-'aql wa 'alam al-hiss` (And inadequacy is comprehensive for the entire world of intellect and the world of sense). And `ijz` (inadequacy) is comprehensive. For whom? For all. The world of intellect and the world of `hiss` (sense). And the world of `hiss`. So `ijz`... inadequacy is comprehensive for all. The `mubda' awwal` too, the `'aql awwal` too, and we too. We are all equal in this. `yatasawa fi dhalika al-qadiru wa al-maqdur wa al-mahsusu wa al-ma'qul` (In that, the powerful and the overpowered, the sensed and the intelligible are equal). They are equal. What is the root of `yatasawa`? `Sawa`. `Sawa` means equal. `Yatasawa`... they are equal to each other. `Tasawa`, the chapter of `tasawi`, what does it imply? The meaning of "each other" comes. They are equal to each other in that matter. Who? The powerful and the powerless. And the sensed and the unsensed. `min al-'alamayni jami'an` (from both worlds together). The world of intellect and the world of body. `wa qawluna Allahu i'rabun bi-hadha al-ismi li-ilhani al-'aqli al-awwal` (And our saying "Allah" is an expression with this name because of the bewilderment of the First Intellect). And our saying "Allah", expressing with this name, `alhan`. It is bewildered about it. Imam is equal to it, `ashiqun` is equal to it, all are equal to it. So whoever is bewildered about Him, for him, "Allah" is used. It is the center of the circle, around which the circle revolves. The circle is bewildered. It is the central point. `wa dar al-da'ira`. The circle is revolving. Why is it revolving? It is bewildered about the center. It is a circle. Then another circle comes, it is bewildered about its center. Every circle revolves around its center, why is it revolving? It is bewildered. So the energy to revolve is its bewilderment, actually. `wa qawluna huwiyyatu al-muta'aliyah lamma nafa 'anhu abna'a jinsihi`. And our saying `huwiyyah al-muta'aliyah`... `huwa`... which is exalted... when he negated... from him... `abna' jinsihi al-ilahiyyah`. `lamma nafa 'anhu abna' jinsihi`. When he negated the sons of his genus, the divine... from himself. First, what did the first intellect do? He said I am not the creator of myself. `la ilaha`. First, `la ilaha`. First, negation. I do not have the power to create. My genus does not have the power to create. `al-ilahiyyah` (the divinity). `wa athbataha lahu ta'ala` (And he affirmed it for Him, the Exalted). And he affirmed it for Allah Ta'ala. `wa takabbar kama akhbara 'anhu al-kitabu al-karim` (And He is Great, as the Noble Book informed about him). `bi-qawlihi shahida Allahu annahu la ilaha illa Hu` (With His saying: "Allah testifies that there is no god but He"). Allah testified. Who is this Allah? The `'aql al-awwal`. The first intellect testified, `annahu la ilaha illa Hu` (that there is no god but He), the `mubdi' ta'ala`. So that means the perfect `juz'iyyat`... in that, this was not there, that it could create itself. All... the first intellect and everyone first said that I am not the creator of myself. Not my genus, which can create itself. `illa Hu`. `Huwa`. The indication. `wa laysa yaqa'u 'alayhi shay'un min dhalika illa kabiran min qawlihi huwa, wa sa-nuzihu haqqiqata dhalika in sha' Allahu ta'ala` (And nothing of that falls upon Him except perhaps His saying "He," and we will clarify the reality of that matter, God willing). It is a very special meaning, who has a very special meaning... `fa a'raba 'anhu bi-ma kana min sifati ibda'ihi wa fi'lihi` (So it expressed about Him through what was from the attributes of His origination and His action). So, he expressed about him with what was... from the attributes of his `ibda'` and his action. That is, the `ibda'` that was created, from what was manifest in it, he said He created us like this, created us like this. We cannot praise the creator, we do not know him. But from our existence, he made us in this way, gave us life, gave us knowledge, gave us power. We can say that, what we have, we know. `tamjid`. Praise. God is highest. The highest thing to say is not there. What did we say? The last thing we have is "Allah". Above that is "Huwa". He. We say that. We don't have anything else with which to interpret Him. So what did we say? Allah or Huwa. `fa-waqa'a li-nuqi'a 'ala al-huwiyyati al-muta'aliyah li-'ijzina wa diqi jawharina` (So it happened that we might make it fall upon the exalted Ipseity due to our inadequacy and the narrowness of our essence). `li-'ijzina`. Why? Because of our inadequacy. `wa diqi jawharina`. And the narrowness of our essence. The narrowness of our essence. `jawhar`. The essence of speech (`nutq`). We don't have the essence to understand Him, so we have named Him with the last thing that comes to our mind. There is nothing beyond this. So that means they were given `ilm al-kulli` (total knowledge). Not of the essence. `Ilm al-hayat` (knowledge of life), as Sayyidna Mu'ayyad says. What knowledge were they given? What powers are there in life? Nothing more than that. It's not that they were given the knowledge to know Allah. They weren't given the knowledge to know Allah. You can't even understand it. Sayyidna Mu'ayyad explains what `hayat` (life) is, what `'ilm` (knowledge) is, what `quwwah` (power) is, what `ikhtiyar` (choice) is, he has explained all of it. What is life? And after giving it, can He take it back? That if a human gives something, he doesn't take it back from someone else, then Allah Ta'ala also, after giving existence, does not take back existence. Once in our... we have... among the Aryans... in... he debates, the Arya Samaji and the Muslims had a debate. So he asked the Muslims, "Your Allah can do everything?" He said, "Yes." "Can He do `zulm` (injustice)?" When He can do everything, He can also do `zulm`. Can Allah Ta'ala do it or not? You are limiting Allah's power by saying He cannot do `zulm`. So the Muslims replied, "Can you eat everything?" "I have the power to eat, yes, I have." "I have everything in the book." "Can you eat everything?" He said, "This filth is in front of you, eat it." The ability... So, in the same way, Allah Ta'ala can do everything, but He does not do `zulm`. We have it, his... the debate between the Arya Samaji and the Muslim. `wa hisrina wa qusurina` (And our confinement and our deficiency). Our `hiss` is confined, we are deficient. `kama qala Sayyiduna Mu'ayyad fi ba'di kalamihi` (as our master Mu'ayyad said in some of his speech). Your name? Hibatullah bin Musa al-Shirazi. You are the spiritual son of Mawlana Sayyidna Mu'ayyad al-Din. As Sayyidna Mu'ayyad said. And `mabda'` and `ma'ad` are his. From the book `Mabda' wa Ma'ad`. As Sayyidna Mu'ayyad said in some of his speech. `Allahumma ya man waqa'a i'tirafuna bi-sidqi ma qalahu fi hakimi dhikrihi, idh yaqulu, wa qawluhu al-haqqu, wa ma qadaru Allaha haqqa qadrihi` (O Allah, O You for whom our confession occurred with the truth of what He said in His wise remembrance, when He says—and His word is the truth—"And they have not appraised Allah with His true appraisal"). O Allah, O That Being, it has occurred, our confession, with the truth of what he said... his saying in his wise remembrance (`hakimi dhikrihi`). What? When he says, and his saying is the truth. That they have not appraised the worth of Allah with His true worth. We have not been able to appraise the worth of Allah Ta'ala truly. We cannot appraise it because we do not know Him. We say that Allah Ta'ala has created such a good thing based on our existence. `inna nas'aluka al-musamahata` (Indeed, we ask You for forbearance). He is saying a very big thing. In this prayer of yours, what is he saying? `inna nas'aluka al-musamahata` (Indeed, we ask You for forbearance). We ask for forbearance. `Musamahata` means forgiveness. From what is `musamahata`? From `samaha`. `Samaha` means to forgive. `Musamaha`, mutual forbearance. That is, we ask for pardon. From you. `inna nas'aluka al-musamahata liman huwa min rubqi al-'ubudiyyati fi madiqi al-hisari wa al-tadkhiri` (We ask you for forbearance for one who is in the snare of servitude, in the narrow straits of confinement and constraint). From that person, who is in the bondage of servitude, in the slavery. We are slaves. In the snare of servitude (`ubudiyyah`). We are bound slaves. In the snare of `ubudiyyah`. `fi madiqi al-hisari` (in the narrow straits of confinement). And we are confined. We are surrounded by confinement. Our... there are special limits. We do not go beyond that. We are what? In the snares of servitude and in the narrow straits of confinement. `idha aradna wala dhikrika bi-ghayri ma anta ahluhu` (When we intend to undertake Your remembrance with other than what You are worthy of). We intend to take up your remembrance with that which you are not worthy of. You are worthy of that which we cannot understand. We... as much as we can say, as much as we have the power, we say that much. Now after that, if we cannot say it, then we ask for forbearance from you. We ask for your pardon. So this `istighfar` is for the physical world, or for all? For all worlds. All are equal. `Mubda' awwal`, everyone is equal in this. So that means this `istighfar` is not for a sin. Because if the first intellect also said that, and confessed it, then there is a paradox in that, that... in that too, there is a scope for `istighfar` that, "You created, but I ask for forgiveness, I..." So that is also a sin, in a sense. The `istighfar` also. The sin is paired with... what has been said? `Dhanbun mashfu'un bi-al-istighfar`. Now the difference will come. So the first intellect's saying this, first of all, that "You are `mubdi' ta'ala`," with an indication... `shahida Allahu annahu la ilaha illa Hu`, that too is paired with... that there is nothing beyond that. So that also includes a sin. This is for everyone. `li-anna tana'a wala dhikrika bi-ghayri ma anta ahluhu bi-hukmi al-idtirari` (Because undertaking Your remembrance with other than what You are worthy of is by the rule of compulsion). Because `tanawal`, to take up... your remembrance with that which you are not worthy of... `bi-hukmi al-idtirar` (by the rule of compulsion). We are compelled. Due to compulsion, we have no other word to say. So we say that. `fa-innama huwa dhanbun mashfu'un bi-al-istighfar` (For it is only a sin paired with seeking forgiveness). This is a special... This is a `Du'at`'s term that they have established. `Dhanbun mashfu'un bi-al-istighfar`. It is such a sin, which is paired... `mashfu'` means paired. `Shafa'a`, `mashfu'`. `Mashfu'un bi-al-istighfar`. It is paired with `istighfar`. Why is `shafa'` called `shafa'`? Two `rak'at`. These two... `witr`... the prayer that is paired, `shafa'`. Why is `witr` called `witr`? A single `rak'at` prayer. Why is `julus` called `julus`? Because two `rak'at` are prayed sitting down. Upon whom is `shafa'` based? Imam Husayn. Many Imams have... `witr` is based on... what is its `ta'weel`? The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and Lady Fatima. The object of `shafa'` is the Prophet and Lady Fatima. The object of `witr` is Lady Ali, peace be upon him. Imam Husayn used to say in Karbala that my... `shafa'`s object is the Prophet, `witr` is my... my father was the object of `witr`. And `witr`... Lady Ali... The word is `witr`. And the Prophet... And `julus`'s object is Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn. `wa tilka 'ayatun wahidah` (And that is one sign). Both are one sign. How many `rak'at` are there in `julus`? Two `rak'at`. In one `rak'at`. There are two `rak'at` in `julus`. One `rak'at`. `fa-innama huwa dhanbun mashfu'un bi-al-istighfar` (For it is only a sin paired with seeking forgiveness). So it is a sin that is paired with `istighfar`. We commit a sin, and we also do `istighfar`. Because we are compelled. Compulsion is permissible. The utmost humility is shown. Utmost humility. In this... Mawlana Ali has... it has been mentioned that a woman was brought before Umar. And she was about to have a child. He asked, "Who is your husband?" She said, "I have no husband." "I have no husband." Then he said, "How did this child happen?" She said, "The child happened like this..." She explained that "I was going, passing through the desert, and I was extremely thirsty. I had been thirsty for three days. And I met a shepherd. He said, 'I am ready to give you water, but on the condition that you give yourself to me.'" She was compelled. She said, "I gave myself for water." I am so thirsty, I am near death. He fulfilled his lust with her. And after that, she had a child. She was brought before Umar Sahab. He said, "Stone her. Stone her." A child without marriage. A child without a husband. Mawla-e-Kainat arrived and said, "What's the matter?" He said, "This has happened." He said, "She is `mustarr` (compelled), she is helpless. Leave her, because this sin happened in `idtirar` (compulsion)." In many places, he has explained this. Three or four people have explained this incident. `Idtirar` means helplessness. No, but this... a little bit of a thought... in a pure world, the world of spirits, where everything is illuminated, everything... except for His essence. In that too, there is a possibility of sin... it's a bit of a paradox. It is paired with `istighfar`. That we cannot do anything beyond this. It's a compulsion. Neither can the first intellect do anything, nor can the tenth intellect do anything. And it is the world of... as far as his matter is concerned, of God Almighty, the creator, the originator, there everyone is equal. This has been explained, that everyone is equal. We cannot recognize him. Yes. `Rutbat al-ilahiyyah`. `Rutbat al-ilahiyyah`. After that? Imamate of spirituality... `Rutbat al-ilahiyyah`. After that? `Hujjiyyah`. `Hijabiyyah`. Then? `Khayaliyyah`. Then? `Fathiyyah`. Then? `Jiddiyyah`. Then `Anza'iyyah`. After `anza'iyyah`, what is there? `Qa'imiyyah`. Then `Jussiyyah`. Then `Ahadiyyah`. Then `Samadiyyah`, then `Ahadiyyah`, then `Ilahiyyah`, then `Huwiyyah`. The last rank is `huwiyyah`. There are ten ranks that have been mentioned.

<!-- lecture 4 -->

Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim.
The fourth *fasl* (chapter).
The fourth *fasl* (chapter) of the first *bab* (gate) of the first *suradiq* (canopy).
And from what has been related in that...
...of the first *bab* (gate)...
Fourth *fasl* (chapter)... what does *Suradiq* mean?
*Sardil*... *sardil*... they call a *shamiyana* (marquee). A large *shamiyana* is a *khaima* (tent). That is called *sardaq*. The book of five *shamiyanas*. Comprising five *shamiyanas*. Each *shamiyana*... how many *babs* (gates) are there in it? Five *babs* (gates). How many gates are there? Five. And within every gate, what is there? Five *fasls* (chapters). There are five rooms. How are rooms made in a *shamiyana*? By putting up a curtain. What do they call *Suradiq*? A *shamiyana*. A *shamiyana*, a *khaima*. A very large encampment is called *Suradiq*. *Suradiq*. Where will you find this book *Suradiq*? This book, which... *sardit*. *Sin*. *Sin*. *Sardaqa*, which is its verb form... *Sardaqa*. ...*Sardaqa*. *Sin*, *ra*. It means to put up a curtain, to put up a *shamiyana*, to put up a *khaima* (tent). *Suradiq* is the *shamiyana*. The *khaima*. The *khaima*. Five *khaimas* are set up. And in the five *khaimas*, each *khaima* has five *babs* (gates). Understood? Five doors. And under each door, there are five rooms. Five *fasls*. Five *fasls*, five curtains are up. We are in the first *Suradiq*, the first *shamiyana*. ...fourth... Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. `Wa mimma warada fi dhalika qawl al-hudud 'alayhim al-salawatu, inna al-tawhida huwa ma'rifat al-hudud wa al-tanzihu nafyi al-ilahiyyat 'anhum wa al-tajrida salb al-asma'i wa al-sifati 'an Allah Ta'ala. Wa hadha qawlun mujmalun...` (And among what is related in that is the saying of the *hudud*, peace be upon them, that verily *Tawhid* is the gnosis of the *hudud*, and *tanzih* is the negation of divinity from them, and *tajrid* is the divestment of the names and attributes from Allah, the Exalted. And this is a summarized statement...). The basis of all things... what is *Tawhid*? We say that considering Allah as one. Whereas here, what is it? Three things. That is not *Tawhid*. That is *shirk*. To consider Allah as one is *shirk*. What is *Tawhid*? `Ma'rifat al-hudud` (The gnosis of the *hudud*). `Ma'rifat al-hudud`. The gnosis of the *hudud* (ranks/limits). And to understand that every *had* (rank) is unique (`yekta`) in its own place. Allah is not unique. Rather, every *had* is unique in its own place. That's it. This is the greatest thing, the *Tawhid* of the *hudud*. And to have the gnosis (`ma'rifat`) of that *had*, that at what position and at what station that *had* is, at what level it is, that is *Tawhid*. As for Allah, you can neither call Him one, nor two, nor three, nor can you call Him a part of one. You cannot say anything. No definition can be applied there. What is *Tawhid*? The *hudud* that Allah created and gave them authority (`ikhtiyar`), that "use your powers." Each *had*... in its own similitude... its power... it was given authority (`ikhtiyar`). And the difference that occurred, from that, the hierarchy (`tartib`) of the *hudud* was established. To know that hierarchy is *Tawhid*. But Maula, there must be levels of *Tawhid* too, because not everyone can fully comprehend it. For example, the Noble Prophet said, "I have not been recognized except... no one has recognized me except me and Allah." That *had*... as one's station (`martaba`) increases, so does their *Tawhid*. There are many stations of *Tawhid*. So it means, in one's life, how many beings' *Tawhid* will a person perform? The knowledge of *Tawhid* is the highest knowledge of all. `Ajall al-'ilm`. `Ajall al-'ilm`. The highest knowledge is that of *Tawhid*. To recognize the station (`martaba`) of each one. Now, within your body, how many parts are there? 360 parts. Each part of that organ... which part is greater than which part? What is the quality of each one? To have gnosis of that is the gnosis of the body. All the beings (`zawat`) that Allah Ta'ala has created, when did the beings achieve their `kamal-e insani` (human perfection)? That is the real *ma'rifat* (gnosis), the *Tawhid*. So that... it means... this is... this is the limit of gnosis (`ma'rifat`). The limit. That they... the `kamal-e insani`... When was `kamal-e insani` achieved? And for salvation (`najat`), which of the `hudud`'s gnosis is necessary? As much gnosis as you can achieve in your lifetime, your station (`martaba`) will be established accordingly. And according to that, the hierarchy in the `haykal` (spiritual form) will be established. Through knowledge (`'ilm`) and action (`'amal`), the hierarchy in the `haykal` is established. Salvation (`najat`) is what? `Khatima bil-khair` (A good end). That is salvation. `Wa huwa ma'rifat al-hudud`. The gnosis of the *hudud*. Will they do gnosis or will gnosis be made to happen to them? Will we do gnosis or will gnosis be made to happen to us? The effort (`juhd`) you make... you do gnosis. And the grace (`fazl`) of those above will also be upon you, so gnosis will also be made to happen. What do they call `hudud`? A limit. Every *had* has a limit. It cannot go beyond that. What is the final point, the `nuqta-e irtifa'` (point of ascent) of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him? `Hijabiyyat`. What is the limit of Janab-e Fatimah? `Hujjiyyat`. What is the final point of Janab-e Abd al-Muttalib? `Jaddiyyat`. To attain the gnosis of that. In `jaddiyyat`, there are ten stations (`maratib`). At which station is who found? The seventh stage is lower, the higher is different. This is a very great science. *Tawhid*. How many beings (`zawat`) has Allah Ta'ala created? Innumerable. Innumerable beings. And for the innumerable, there is innumerable gnosis. That is what... the intellect is bewildered by how much can be achieved. As much as can be achieved. So, *Tawhid* has three branches. One is *Tawhid* itself. What is that? `Ma'rifat al-hudud`. Gnosis of the *hudud*. `Wa al-tanzih`. And *tanzih* is... `nafyi al-ilahiyyat 'anhum` (the negation of divinity from them). What is *tanzih*? To declare as transcendent, to declare as pure. That divinity is not in them. There is no divinity in the *hudud*. The attribute of creating is not in them. From *ilahiyyat* (divinity), what is meant here? `Ibda' al-zawat` (originating the beings). That they can create a being. Yes, that creating a being... There are two meanings of *ilah*. Now it will be explained. `Wa la ya'lamu alihan`. `Alihan` means `ijad al-zawat` (the creation of beings). And `waliha` means to be bewildered about something. What is the bewilderment? Every person is bewildered, to the extent that... all are bewildered, even the `Aql al-Awwal` is bewildered about `Mubdi' al-Awwal` (the Originator of the First). So it is being said: `wa al-tanzih nafyi al-ilahiyyat`. That no one has the power to perform `ibda'-e zawat` (origination of a being). Not even the `Aql al-Awwal` has the power. All are created (`paida kiye hue`). `Wa al-tajrid salb al-asma'i wa al-sifati 'an Allah Ta'ala`. What is *tajrid*? To strip the bark of a tree is called *tajrid*. `Salb al-asma'`. To divest the names and attributes from Allah Ta'ala. That no name can be true for Allah. Even "Allah" cannot be true for Him. Therefore, out of compulsion, we call Him "Hu" (He). And upon saying "Hu," we say, "O Allah, we are helpless. What things of Yours... to prove our existence, how should we call You?" `Zanbun mashfu'un bil-istighfar` (A sin coupled with a plea for forgiveness). It is attached with sin, the `istighfar`. What is sin? We do it, and forgiveness is also granted with it. Because man is helpless. Is this not like how sin has been placed in one's very nature? Yes. It's a sin, but one has to do it. If one doesn't do it, then there is a denial of Allah's existence. He will have to call upon something to go towards Allah's existence. He will have to give Him some name. To call upon Him. When he gives a name, it becomes a sin (`zanb`). But its accompaniment is that Allah Ta'ala understands our helplessness, that this servant is helpless. He does not have any words with which he can call me. By whichever name he calls, I will accept it. The `istighfar` is accepted. `Zanbun mashfu'un bil-istighfar`. `Salb al-asma'`. All the names and attributes that are there, their negation from Allah Ta'ala. `Wa hadha qawlun mujmalun`. It needs explanation. And this is a summarized statement. This is... an encompassing statement. It needs to have its details explained. It is in need of details. `Li-anna al-ma'rifata bil-hududi ma'rifatan`. `Ma'rifatun zahiratun yu'rafu biha shakhs al-had wa maqamuhu wa hadhihi al-ma'rifah yatasawi fiha al-wali wa ghayruhu min al-azdad wa al-tughat. Wa ma'rifatun batina...` (Because the gnosis of the *hudud* is of two kinds of gnosis. An outer gnosis, by which the person of the *had* and his station are known. And in this gnosis, the friend and others from among the adversaries and tyrants are equal. And an inner gnosis...). Because the gnosis... Because the gnosis of the *hudud*... has two kinds of gnosis. It is of two kinds. One is outer gnosis... Outer gnosis... by which is recognized... the personality of the *had* and his station. And this gnosis... they are equal in it... the friend (`wali`) and besides him, the adversaries (`azdad`). His lover, his enemy, everyone is seeing that person. And they are seeing... how tall he is, how many feet. Is his face round? Does he have a beard? What are his hands like, what are his feet like? Everyone is seeing. The friend is also seeing, the enemy is also seeing, the lover is also seeing. In this outer gnosis, all are equal. `Wa ma'rifatun batina yakhtassu biha ahl al-ma'arif min ahl al-haqq. Wa huwa ibtida' wujud al-had`. The inner gnosis is a very high thing. `Yakhtassu biha`. Outer gnosis is also very difficult. But in it, they all become equal. The inner gnosis... what is inner gnosis? Specific to them are the people of gnosis (`ahl al-ma'arif`) from the people of truth (`ahl al-haqq`). `Wa huwa ibtida' wujud al-had`. That the existence... the beginning of the existence of the *had*. When did the existence of the *had* begin? The `hudud` which have been created... where were they created? They were created where the `fatahun` were. After that, they were called. Then the first call was made. In the first call... the second call was made, the third call was made, the fourth call was made. In every room, they were called. In which room did they confess? It is a very long story. The beginning of the existence of the *had*. The gnosis of this... who can have it? Imam al-Zaman, peace be upon him. When did its beginning happen? The beginning of the existence of the *had*. The *had*'s existence began. `Wa ghayatuhu`. And its end. Where did the `had`... why did the `had` become a `had`? How did its beginning happen? That is inner gnosis. The bodies in which they came... it means... what is the secret? The `hudud` that were created here, where were they created? From whom were they created? From the `fatahun`. Whose sins were few. After that, they were called. The first time, they were called. The first call was made. In the first call, they did not confess. The second time, they were called. The third time, they were called. The fourth time, they were called. In every room, they were called. In which room did they confess? It is a very long story. The beginning of the existence of the *had*. Gnosis of this... who can have it? Imam al-Zaman, peace be upon him. When did its beginning happen? `Ibtida' wujud al-had`. The beginning of the existence of the *had*. `Wa ghayatuhu`. And its end. At what point was its essence (`khamira`) established? At which level of `mu'min` was he, that he passed away? Was he in the ninth level, eighth level, seventh level? Or from `mu'min` did he become a `mukathir`? From `mukathir` did he become a `ma'dhun`? At what level was he? `Wa ila ayna ma'aduhu wa nihayatuhu`. And where will be his return and his end? It is a gnosis that is extremely difficult. It cannot be reached except by the `murtazin` (disciplined ones) and the `muhiqqin` (verifiers). And there is no *Tawhid* at all for one whose gnosis is deficient. And here I am... clarifying something from that so that it may be a help for our brethren in the gnosis of the *Tawhid* of Allah Ta'ala. And I am clarifying here... I do... I clarify... that thing... some things, so that it may become a helper for our brethren in the gnosis of the *Tawhid* of Allah Ta'ala. `Fa-aqulu bi-'awn Allah subhanahu wa lahazati waliyyihi fi ardihi, salamullahi 'alayhi, inna aqrab al-hudud ilayna huwa al-mukathiru wa ma thabata min al-qawl fi al-dani min al-hudud thabata fil-'ali`. So I say, with the help of Allah Subhanahu and the glances of His `Wali` on his earth, peace of Allah be upon him, that verily the closest of the `hudud` to us is the `Mukathir`, and what is established of the saying regarding the lower of the `hudud` is established for the higher. What are the levels? First is `Mustajib`. `Mustajib` means one who accepts. The one who takes the noble pledge (`'ahd sharif`). The one who says that "I accept the noble pledge." Whether he does it with his heart, with his actions, or not. If he says it with his tongue, then he is... this is the definition of one who takes the noble pledge, that he says it with his tongue. That I am the Imam of the time... After that is the level of `Mu'min`. That person who takes the noble pledge, with what power, with what intensity (`hiddat`) he is taking the noble pledge, according to that, the levels of `Mu'min` are established. At the same time... the levels of `Mu'min` are established. In which level... some are such that they come for marriage to take the noble pledge. Some are such that they... like Sayyidna Ja'far. They also took the noble pledge. The Imam also takes the noble pledge. So, the intensity (`hiddat`) of the one taking the noble pledge... what do they call it? `Hiddat`. The `hiddat` of the gaze... how much sharpness is there in that person who is taking the noble pledge. According to that, the level is established. There are ten levels of the noble pledge. After that is `Mu'min`. What is the definition of `Mu'min`? `Al-qawl bil-lisan wa al-tasdiq bil-jinan wa al-'amal bil-arkan` (To profess with the tongue, to affirm with the heart, and to act with the limbs). To say with the tongue, to affirm with the heart, and to act with the limbs. `Mu'min`. Ten levels of that are established. These do not come under the `hudud`. `Mustajib` and `Mu'min` do not come under the `hudud`. But the `Mukathir` after that, he enters the `hudud`. The first rank. The first rank. In the `hudud`, the first is the `Mukathir`. The Prophet has mentioned him. He is the one he is explaining. Verily the closest of the `hudud` to us... the closest of the `hudud` to us is the `Mukathir`. What is the meaning of `mukathir`? From `kasr`. The one who breaks with his proofs (`hujjat`). First, whom will he break? He will break his own self. `Kasr-e nafs`. `Kasr-e nafs`. To perform `kasr-e nafs`. First of all, `kasr-e nafs`. To break one's own self. What does that mean? That one thinks whether my every statement is in accordance with the command of Allah and the Prophet. Is my every action... and my every intention... am I thinking, is my thought in accordance with the command of Allah and the Prophet? What I am saying, is it in accordance with the command of Allah and the Prophet? This action that I am doing, is it in accordance with the command of Allah and the Prophet? To make one's self bound by that. That is called `Mukathir`. When he breaks his own self, then he can break all. That when he establishes his self on this matter, then he can break everyone. He couldn't break his own self, he has given freedom to his self, that this is right and that is right. How will he break others? For the `Mukathir`, it is necessary to acquire knowledge (`'ulum`). Without knowledge, a `Mukathir` cannot be formed. He must know the command of Allah and the Prophet. He will know, then he will say that my one statement that I said... is not in accordance with the command of Allah and the Prophet. This that I did, is not in accordance with the command of Allah. This that I thought, is not in accordance with the command of Allah. When he thinks himself, then he can break the one in front of him with his proofs. `Wa ma thabata min al-qawl fi al-dani min al-hudud thabata fil-'ali`. And that which is established by the saying regarding the lower of the `hudud`, is established for the higher. And what is established by the saying for the lower of the `hudud`... then it is established... in the same way, for the higher of the `hudud`. The levels that are there, `Mukathir`, `Ma'dhun`, and `Da'i Mutlaq`, `Da'i Mahsur`, how many ever levels there are, the same saying is established for them all. If he is a `Ma'dhun`, then he will be a `Mukathir` in his place and a `Ma'dhun` as well. `Wa dhalika annahu wa in kana yajma'uhu wa ghayruhu min al-ashkhas al-insaniyya al-hudud wa al-aqtar wa kawnuhuma jami'an min lahmin wa damin wa 'izamin wa 'asabin wa 'uruqin wa ghayri dhalika fa-laysa bi-sawa'in`. Although he is gathered... although this is the matter, that he is gathered... and... he and others from among the human persons are gathered by the limits and the regions. His companions and other human persons... he and besides him, from among the human persons... the limits and the regions. And their both being entirely of flesh and blood and bones and nerves and veins and other than that, but they are not the same. Although he gathers it... although this is the matter, that he and others from among the human persons are gathered by the limits and the regions. He and his companions and other human persons... a human being... he and besides him from among the human persons... the limits and the regions. And their both being entirely of flesh and blood and bones and nerves and veins and other than that, but they are not the same. Although he is gathered... he and his companions, and besides him from among the human persons, are gathered by the limits and the regions. The limits (`hudud`) and the regions (`aqtar`) surround him as well, and they surround other human persons as well. The limits and the regions. By `hudud` is meant the `mu'min`. And their both being entirely of flesh... And both of them... the other human persons and the `Mukathir` himself... they both are made of flesh and blood. They are made of flesh. They are of blood, they are of bones, they are of nerves, they are of veins, and besides that, but still they are not the same. Although both are the same. Other human beings are also of flesh and bone. He is also of flesh and bone. But there is a difference between them and him. `Li-anna hadha al-had alladhi huwa al-mukathir qad talattafa mizajuhu wa safa jawharuhu wa hadha su'udan maratiban jumma`. Inwardly they are different, or outwardly? Outwardly they seem to be of flesh and blood and all, but his flesh is different, his blood is different, everything of his is different. Outwardly as well. Because that `had` which is the `Mukathir`... his temperament has become refined, and his essence has become pure, and he has ascended through numerous stations. This... which others did not attain. And the ignorant did not perceive it. `Wa taqarraba biha fa-taqarraba biha min al-mabda' al-awwal hatta sara fi a'la maratib al-insaniyya`. So he, that is, has drawn so close through that matter, from the first principle, because of that... he has become close to the first principle. His home is closer than... It means, where his creation took place... he is closer to going there now. Even to the extent that he has reached the highest stations of humanity. `Allati hiya awwalu rutab al-malakutiyya`. That which is the first of the spiritual ranks. The `Mukathir` is the first level of the spiritual ranks. `Wa huwa mahbat li-wahyi Allah`. So that `Mukathir` is the place of descent for the revelation of Allah. `Wa baytun min buyutihi`. And a house from His houses. And a house from the houses of Allah. Why is he like this? Because whatever he thought, in it he kept the command of Allah and the Prophet before him. Whatever he said, in it he kept the command of Allah and the Prophet before him. And whatever action he did, in that he kept them before him. Because of this, he became `baytun min buyut Allah`. It becomes the place of its descent... Of the revelation. The place for revelation to come. `Mahbat al-wahy`. The place for revelation to descend. And `baytun min buyutihi`. And a house from His houses. `Buyut` is... it is generally used... `buyut`... he becomes a house from the houses of Allah. `Kama ramada bihi Ta'ala fi kitabihi al-karim wa qala: fi buyutin adhin Allahu an turfa' wa yudhkara fiha ismuhu yusabbihu lahu fiha bil-ghuduwwi wa al-asal`. As Allah Ta'ala has alluded to it in His noble book, and He said: "In houses which Allah has permitted to be exalted, and His name is mentioned therein. In them, He is glorified in the mornings and the evenings." To which Allah Ta'ala has alluded in His noble book, and He said... Allah Ta'ala said... "A few houses... a few houses... that have been permitted by Allah... that they be exalted... and His name be remembered in them... and glorified in them, His name... in them... in the morning and in the evening." `Thumma haqqaqa fil-ayah anna al-buyuta hum al-hudud`. Then he verified that in this verse, the "houses" are the `hudud`. `Fa-qala Ta'ala: rijalun la tulhihim tijaratun wa la bay'un 'an dhikri Allah wa iqam al-salati wa ita' al-zakati`. And Allah Ta'ala said, he said... in his noble book, that "men... such men... whom commerce does not divert... and buying and selling does not divert them from the remembrance of Allah, and from establishing prayer, and from giving the `zakat`." `Yuridu iqamat al-da'wah`. What he intends from that is to establish the `da'wah`. What do you understand by `tijarah` (commerce)? `Surah al-Jumu'ah`. `Ya ayyuha alladhina amanu idha nudiya li-s-salati min yawm al-jumu'ati fas'aw ila dhikri Allah wa dharu al-bay'a` (O you who have believed, when the call is proclaimed for the prayer on the day of Jumu'ah, then proceed to the remembrance of Allah and leave trade). `Dhalikum khayrun lakum in kuntum ta'lamun. Fa-idha qudiyat al-salatu fantashiru fil-ardi wabtaghu min fadli Allah wadhkuru Allah kathiran la'allakum tuflihun`. They fall into amusement, commerce. `Wa la bay'un 'an dhikri Allah`. Buying and selling does not... does not stop them. Does not stop them from the remembrance of Allah. `Iqam al-salati wa ita' al-zakati`. To establish prayer, to give `zakat`. `Yuridu iqamat al-da'wah`. He intends by that statement... from prayer, what is meant? To establish the `da'wah`. What is the meaning of `wilayat`? To repent in the world of motes. And what is `taharat`? To purify oneself from the filth of Iblis with the knowledge of the Tenth. After that, what is the meaning of `salat`? The Tenth has... or in whose sphere you have reached, whose `da'wah` has begun, the commands he has given, to act upon those commands. And that's why they say `qad qamat al-salah`. `Qamat`. `Qiyam` means to stand. After that, what is `zakat`? The knowledge that has been given to you, when that knowledge reaches a certain limit, then from it, a small portion is made obligatory to be given. From that... and what is that `zakat`? There are many kinds. There is `zakat al-fitra`. Which is obligatory on every person. What is `zakat al-fitra`? Every person... what does that mean? Some sciences are such that they are given to every person by nature. It is obligatory to explain them. Some things are such that when money accumulates, a portion of it is given. That is called `zakat al-mal`. From the knowledge that is given, what is the... the general commands, explain them. He will explain. And what is `sawm` (fasting)? Not to tell the knowledge. Not to tell the knowledge to the undeserving. To conceal. To conceal that. Yes. `Khums`. And `khums` is the fifth part. Fifth part. If you get some booty unexpectedly, which you were not expecting, then its fifth part should be given. Hazrat Imam Husayn, peace be upon him, his house... he used to collect his salary, and from it he would take out the `khums`, thinking that "I was not expecting this money to come to me." He used to deposit the `khums` of his salary every month. Does the fifth part also apply to knowledge? Yes. If some knowledge is given to you unexpectedly, from your saints of Allah, then its fifth part must be given. For example, now `Tawam` has become very high. `La yajidu 'anhu sanan`. Imam Husayn, peace be upon him, had knowledge and virtues descend upon him. Its fifth part, what did he do? He propagated it. He clarified the matter. The fifth part. The other four parts you don't have. That is your right. After that, `jihad`. `Hajj`. `Hajj` is... `al-qasdu ila bayt Allah`. To intend towards the House of Allah. Who is the House of Allah? Imam al-Zaman, peace be upon him, is Allah, he is the place of Allah. What is the `bayt`? `Bab al-batin` (the inner gate). To prepare your form and appearance to go towards the `bab al-batin`. To prepare your form and appearance... with a true heart... `Bab al-batin`... that is called `hajj`. What is `jihad`? When the command comes from Imam al-Zaman, peace be upon him, then to take one's self... not to take, but to sacrifice it in the way of Allah. That is `jihad`. And the `jihad` that... when it comes, and if it doesn't come, then what is the command? The `jihad` of the seventy-two. What `jihad` should they do? Their self... a lioness, a hero, a lion of war, what deed have you done? You have killed a great beast... you have killed the commanding self. `Yuridu iqamat al-da'wati allati hiya mansur al-salati al-zahira`. And he intends by that verse... Allah Ta'ala... to establish the `da'wah`. That is such that it is the object of the outer prayer. `Wa la qiwama laha illa biha`. And the `da'wah` is not strengthened except by prayer. `Wa ghayruhu min hadhihi al-ashkhas al-insaniyya wa in kana 'ala al-halati allati huwa 'alayha fa-inna mizajahu ghayr mutalattif wa jawharahu ghayr safin wa shakhsuhu sa'irun fil-inhidar wa al-bu'di min al-mabda' al-awwal sa'irun fi akhiri rutab al-insaniyya muqahqaran ila ma dunahu min al-surat al-'alfiyya`. And besides him from these human persons, even if he is in the state in which he is... but... `ghayruhu`... other human persons, even if they are in that state upon which he is... The `mukathir`... and even if the `mukathir` is in the same state in which he is... other human persons, even if they are in that state... upon which the `mukathir` is... but his temperament... no... other human persons, even if they are in that state... `ghayr`... its pronoun is towards `ghayr`. The pronoun is towards `ghayr`. `Ghayr` is used as a singular here. Other human persons... `ghayr`. `Ghayr`... `ghayr mukathir`. `Ghayr` means `ghayr mukathir`. `Mu'min`. Other persons. Those who are his opponents. Their temperament is not refined. And their essence is not pure. And his person is proceeding towards decline. They are gathered on one platform. The `mukathir` is going to ascend, this one is going to fall. They are on the same platform. And his person... and his personality is going towards decline. And moving away from the first principle. One is going towards the first principle, this one is moving away from the first principle. They are on the same platform. One is going to the cinema, one is going to the mosque. They are gathered together. If `iqamat al-salah` (establishing prayer) does not happen. If `iqamat al-salah` does not happen, then it is like this. Moving away from the first principle. They are in one world, on one platform. After coming, now one will go that way, one will go this way. He is proceeding to the last of the human ranks. And is being pushed back to what is below it from the thousand-fold forms. He is going, being pushed back to what is below him from the `surat al-alfiyya`. A thousand-fold form. That is such that it is more astray than cattle in terms of path. Then to the crooked path, ending in that to the `barzakh al-khawf`. He is proceeding, proceeding to the `barzakh al-khawf`. To the `barzakh al-khawf`. May Allah keep us... and all our brethren far from that matter, for the sake of the master of the prophets, peace and blessings be upon him and his pure progeny, blessings of Allah be upon them all. So, the human being... one human being is on one platform. He is also of flesh, he is also of blood, he has everything. But what is his condition? One is going up, one is going down. His condition is also because he is not establishing prayer there. Outwardly he is not even praying. His temperament has become like that. His actions have made him like that. He will go up, he will go down. Here, establishing prayer is with the inward, so he is becoming a `mukathir`. There, he is not even establishing the outward prayer, so he is falling down. `Wa fil-ashkhas al-haywaniyya 'ibratun li-man i'tabara`. In the animal forms, there is a lesson for one who takes a lesson. `Wa basiratun li-man tabassara wa tadabbara`. And insight for one who reflects and contemplates. The animal forms, meaning animal figures. `Shakhs` here does not mean human. Figure. Animal figures... are a place of lesson for one who... takes a lesson. And insight for one who understands and contemplates. `Wa dhalika anna al-baha'im al-muhallalah min al-baqari wa al-ghanami wa al-ibili wa ghayri dhalika mutamathilatun fil-khalqi hiya wa al-siba' al-muharramah li-kawnihim jami'an min lahmin wa damin wa 'izamin wa 'asabin wa 'uruqin wa basharin wa jildin wa wabarin ghayra anna al-baha'im qad sarat ghidha'an lil-insan`. And that is because the lawful animals, from the cattle... what do they call `baqar`? Cow. ...from the sheep, from the camel, and besides that, which are similar in creation, they and the forbidden predatory animals... because of their all being of flesh and blood and bones and nerves and veins and skin and hide and fur. However, the animals... have become food for the human. Except for this matter, that the animals... the lawful animals... they have become food for the human. That human who is the caliph of Allah on His earth. `Musta'nisatan ilayhi`. Taking intimacy with him. Who? The animals. The animals take intimacy with him. `Sa'iratan ila al-su'ud wa al-taraqqi fi al-sirat al-sawiyy`. Proceeding towards ascent and progress on the straight path. That which is the human person. That which is his path? The human person. `Sirat al-mustaqim` is the human person. The straight path. `Alladhi huwa al-shakhs al-bashari`. Which is the human person. `Qaribatan min al-mabda' al-awwal`. He is close to the first principle. The first principle is our starting point. He is close to the human person. The human eats, so what will happen? It, by becoming part of the human, will progress. So, it means the `mukathir` is like the ascending and pure lawful animals, and the one who is falling is like the forbidden predatory animals. `Wa al-siba'u nafiratun 'an al-insan mu'adiyatun lahu sa'iratan fil-inhidar`. And the predatory animals are averse to the human, hostile to him, proceeding in decline. `Sa'iratan ila al-bu'd al-ab'ad min al-mabda' al-awwal`. Proceeding to the furthest distance from the first principle. It is moving further away from the first principle. This one is getting closer. Although both are of the same kind of created beings. `Fa-laysu bi-sawa'in fi hadhihi al-dawahir wa al-khalq al-mushtarak`. So they are not the same in these outward appearances and the shared creation. `Wa kadhalika al-ta'i'una wa al-'usatu wa al-ba'idu ab'adu min dhalika`. In the same way, the obedient and the disobedient servants, and the distance is greater than that. The two kinds of animals, one is falling, that is how the human, one is on the platform, one is `muti` (obedient), one is `'asi` (disobedient). They have a lot of distance between them. That one is going up, this one is going down. One is on the platform. The last... the last... the last part of the chapter... The last... the last part of the gate is... `al-fasl al-khamis min al-bab al-awwal min al-suradiq al-awwal. Wa idha kana dhalika kadhalika`. And when that matter was so. And when that matter was so, just as that matter was, `fa-inna nafs al-had alladhi huwa al-mukathir qad talattafat wa safat wa 'alat bi-irtifa' al-sifati al-mawdu'atiha wa 'uluwwihi thumma ittasala biha min al-'ulum al-ilahiyya wa al-asrar al-malakutiyya ma ahkamaha sifa'an kulliyan wa altahaha taltifan malakutiyyan wa sabaghaha sibghatan ilahiyyan wa ashraqaha wa jawharaha wa ashfaha`. And when the matter happened in this way, just as the matter was, then the `nafs` (soul) of the `had` (rank)... that which is the `mukathir`... had become refined and pure and elevated through the elevation of its established attributes and its highness. Then it connected with it from the divine sciences and the spiritual secrets what perfected it as a universal attribute and refined it with a spiritual refinement, and dyed it with a divine dye, and made it shine and made its essence and made it transparent. Now he is talking about the `nafs` of the `mukathir`. The `nafs hissi` or `nafs nami`? The `nafs hissi` of the `mukathir`. What was its condition? Verily the `nafs` of the `had`, which is the `mukathir`, has become refined and pure and elevated with the elevation of its established attributes and its highness. Then connected with it were the divine sciences... he became a human with a holy spirit. The `nafs hissi` became... the `nafs hissi` also became refined. A common person's `nafs hissi` and his `nafs hissi` are separate. Because he has acquired such things until he became a `mukathir`. He passed the ten stations of the `mustajib`, he passed the ten stations of the `mu'min`, then in his own, from the levels of the `mukathir`, in which level is he? From that, his `nafs` also has a subtlety in it. So is this not a criterion, that if the `nafs` has become refined, it is not necessary that the person in front is a `mukathir`? It happens sometimes that the person's stations are hidden and only Allah knows them. So his `nafs`'s subtlety, according to that, his station is established. It is known from outward... outwardly it appears that it could be that he is a `mukathir`, but his `nafs` is also refined. But the demand of justice is that if the `nafs` has become pure, then it is necessary for him to become a `mukathir`. He will have passed the ten stations of the `mu'min`. If he has reached the station of `mukathir`, then his `nafs`'s subtlety, because of that... it is not necessary for it to be apparent. The designation is not necessary. I mean, the station is with Allah. `Thumma ittasala biha min al-'ulum al-ilahiyya wa al-asrar al-malakutiyya ma ahkamaha sifa'an kulliyyan wa altahaha taltifan malakutiyyan wa sabaghaha sibghatan ilahiyyan wa ashraqaha wa jawharaha wa ashfaha`. `Fa-idha qabalahu al-mustafidu bil-sidqi wa sihhati al-niyyati wa safa'i al-tabi'ati wa takallama ma'ahu wa afadahu min al-kalami al-malakuti wa al-'ilmi al-ilahi alladhi lam yakun qad khatara qabla dhalika bi-balihi wa la zanna bi-masami'ihi qattu wa masami'i amthalihi hara fihi lubbuhu wa walaha fa-sara lahu ilahan malikan li-riqqihi 'arifan bi-dalalatihi wa 'azimi sabaqatihi`. So when he met him... an `arif`... when some `mustafid` meets him, a `mustafid`, this `mukathir`... it means the connection of a teacher and student begins. With sincerity and with sound intention and with purity of heart he speaks with him. And the `mukathir` benefits him from the spiritual speech and from the divine knowledge, which had not crossed his heart before that, nor had his ears ever suspected it, nor the ears of his likes. His intellect was bewildered in it, and he was astounded, and he became for him a god, a master of his neck, knowing of his guidance and his great precedence. The spiritual speech is the divine... it is that from the `mukathir`'s speech, when the `mustafid` gets benefit, then his intellect becomes bewildered. And he becomes astounded that how has he achieved this station, these kinds of sublime matters. It means the student becomes perplexed about his teacher. And he becomes for him a god, a master. He becomes for him a god, a master. Of his neck. He becomes the master of his neck. In what sense is he a god? That he is the center of the circle. The center. Around the center, the circle revolves. So that revolving is a result of bewilderment. In that sense, he becomes a god for him. In this sense, he is a god. Not in the sense that he is the creator of beings. In this sense only. He becomes the master of his... for the release of his neck. And `arifan bi-dalalihi`. That `mu'min`... recognizes his guidance, his greatness, and his great precedence. `Fa-idha tahakkaqa iftiqarahu ila man fawqahu min al-hudud`. And when he verifies... the `mu'min` verifies... that `mukathir`'s need for the one above him from among the `hudud`. When the `mu'min` sees that I am bewildered by this `mukathir`, but he himself... the `mukathir`, is bewildered about the one above him. He is bewildered. `Ila man fawqahu min al-hudud wa hajatahu ilayhi`. And his need for him. And his poverty for him, and his bewilderment about him. It means the `mukathir` is bewildered about his `mufid`. `Wa iftiqar alladhi fawqahu`. Then the need of the person who is above him... it means the `mufid`'s `mufid` who is above him... above and above... towards the one who is above him, proceeding in that way in a similar manner in the physical ranks. Until he reaches the Imam, peace be upon him. `Wa minhu ila man fawqahu min al-'uqul al-mujarradat mutanahiyan dhalika`. And from him, towards the one who is above him from the abstract intellects, ending in that. Then from him, towards the one who is above him from the ranks, the abstract intellects. What are the abstract intellects? Those that are not in the physical world. The angels who are in the higher realms. Ending in that matter at the First Intellect. Which was bewildered by all the originated beings and the created things. That how did it achieve precedence? Although we were all born at the same time. `Thumma tahakkaqa wulhuhu fi mubdi'ihi`. Then he verifies the bewilderment of the First Intellect about its Originator. The `mu'min` is verifying it. This is... the bewilderment is such that it seems like a jewel which was given to the beings in the beginning. Like a... a prime... that is... Yes, to verify... bewilderment in every single thing. How did he achieve perfection? How did this one achieve perfection? How did that one achieve perfection? The gnosis of knowledge is... the first step for acquiring knowledge is to adopt humility, that I do not have knowledge. To be ignorant, only then can one acquire knowledge. So the station of bewilderment is necessary for the `da'i`. His circle is around his center. He revolves. So that revolving is bewilderment. The cause of bewilderment. `Thumma tahakkaqa wulhuhu fi mubdi'ihi`. He verifies his bewilderment about its originator. `Wa mubdi'i ajna'ihi`. And the originator of his kinds. `Wa hayratihi fihi`. And his bewilderment about him. `Nafa 'an haddihi alladhi huwa fi ufuqihi`. And then he negates from his `had`, which is in his horizon... and that is the `mukathir`... and from all the other `hudud` which are above his `had`, physically and spiritually, until he reaches the very end. He says that no one is a god who gives me being. About whom everyone is bewildered. That `aql-e awwal` was bewildered about `mubdi'-e ta'ala`. That same condition, the `mu'min` is bringing upon the `mukathir`. That this `mukathir`, from him I am getting so much... but he himself is bewildered about his `mufid`. And what is my `mukathir`? My `mukathir`'s greatness, I have recognized. Despite recognizing the great status of the `mukathir`. And the majesty of his station. And the bewilderment of each one of them in him who is in his horizon. And their bewilderment, each one of them, about him who is above him. And his need, his poverty towards him and his need. `Wa athbataha lillah Ta'ala wa takabbara`. And he affirms it for Allah Ta'ala the most exalted. `Alladhi la ilaha illa hu`. He who... there is no god but He. It means the `mu'min` negates divinity from the `mukathir` and from all above him, and now the `ilah` who is truly Allah, he affirms divinity for Him. Upon whom he was bewildered. The `mukathir`'s greatness, keeping that in mind, he affirms that this is not my god. Above him is someone, above him is someone, up to the top. They are all bewildered about him. And the real one is who? He is `mubdi'-e ta'ala`. So, these different circles... the `mukathir` has his circle, above him is his `mufid`'s circle, and above them is another circle. So all these circles are linked with each other. The final circle is that of `aql-e awwal`. Yes, the circles... a circle, one after another, are linked. That linking is a bit... The circles... A... this subject has made me understand that a `mu'min`, regarding the `mukathir`, first confesses that the `mukathir` has become a god for me. Then he denies that he is not a god. In what sense is he a god? That his bewilderment about him... he is bewildered. He became a god, and then he confesses that he is not my god.
