And the circle of `aql-e awwal`... when the `da'wahs` take place, in the spiritual world, when the `da'wahs` were given, and along with the `da'wah`, those people who... `tawabu bi-tawbatihi` (they repented with his repentance)... they ascended. They went with him. `Lam yuni da'awti`. They went with him. And those who were left behind, he gave them the command, "You give the `da'wah`." A new circle was formed. One circle was of the `shakhs-e ibtida'i` (the initial person). Along with him, what happened? This... the real one is where? With the `aql-e awwal`. From the `aql-e awwal`. What did the `aql-e awwal` do? Precedence, by himself. After that, what happened? Seeing him, they went ahead. They are at the station of `tawabu bi-tawbatihi`. After that, what happened? The `da'wah` happened. That is "ha". The `ashir` did not... the seven `uqul` did the `da'wah`. Three conditions are there in the `mushrikin` (polytheists). In all circles, everything is there. The whole story of the life of the universe is in it. `Alif, lam, ha`. These three conditions will always be present. The center of every circle will be what? First of all, the `sabiq` (the forerunner). His... he will call those who joined, joined. Those who didn't join... they will be given the `da'wah`. If they don't accept the `da'wah`, they... their matter... the ones who accept the `da'wah`, they will go. His final individual who is left... what will happen to him? He will be given the command, "Our work is finished, now you do the work." To the one below him. The final individual who is left, he will be given the command. He will become the center of his circle. Around him, what will happen? `Tawabu bi-tawbatihi`. `Lam yuni da'awti`. Then what will happen? Then his final individual will be given the command. So the circles are established in it. The circle of the Imam, the circle of the `Bab`, the circle of the `Hujjat`, in the same way, the circles are established. The same pattern is there everywhere. The first pattern was established there. Because it is the bewilderment of one circle that... the center that he is, the ones around him who are revolving, but one circle which is below another circle, he also has to revolve. That final individual... "You have been spoiled by seeing us. Now you correct them." It is like this. All are in `La ilaha illallah`. In `La ilaha illallah`, what are... what is `din` (religion)? `Alif, lam, ha`. `Alif` is correct. `Alif, lam, ha` has formed the word `ilah`. What does `alif` show? `Alif` shows that precedence is without an inspirer. Without an inspirer, there is precedence. What is the condition of the second one, `lam`? It shows that by seeing, they are moving forward. The `da'wah` has not started yet. `Tawabu bi-tawbatihi`. To repent with his repentance. As he attained `munba'ith bi-sabab`, he also attained it. Whose status is `alif`? `Aql-e awwal`. Whose status is `lam`? `Munba'ith min al-awwal`. After that, the `da'wah` began. That is "ha". The `ashir` did not, the seven `uqul` did the `da'wah`. Three conditions are there in the `mushrikin`. In all circles, there is everything. The entire story of the life of the universe is in it. `Alif, lam, ha`. These three conditions will always be present. The center of every circle will be what? First of all, the `sabiq`. His... he will call those who joined, joined. Those who didn't join... they will be given the `da'wah`. If they don't accept the `da'wah`, they went. The ones who accept the `da'wah`, they will go. His final individual who is left, he will be given the command, "Our work is finished, now you do the work." A new center is formed. In this way, the `da'wah` of the spiritual world was formed. Then the circle of `ashir`. Then the circle of `adam-e dha'i`. Then the circle of the `qa'ims`. The `da'is`... the `qa'ims`, the `hujjats`, the Imams, the `n`... the `ain`... the circle of `ain`, the circle of `mim`. All the circles were established. One after another. `Wa athbataha lillah Ta'ala wa takabbara`. And when he affirmed this matter for Allah Ta'ala and proclaimed His greatness... `Alladhi la ilaha illa hu min hadhihi al-aliha al-makhluqa wa al-mukhtara'a wa al-mubtada'a al-shamil li-kulli wahidin minhum ism al-murabbi alladhi fawqahu wa al-hajatu al-da'iyatu lahu ilayhi`. And he proclaimed His greatness, such that there is no god but He... There is no god from these created, invented, and originated deities, which includes for each one of them the name of the nourisher who is above him, and the need that calls him towards him. He will affirm it for Allah Ta'ala and for Allah Ta'ala's greatness, such that there is no worthy object of worship. From these gods... from these `alihas`... that are created, and that are invented, and that are originated. Which includes for each one of them the name of the `murabbi` (nourisher)... the one who is above him... and the need that calls him towards him. `Illa man tawwahamat hayratu 'alihi wa danihi 'ala 'uluwwi halatihi`. Except for one whose bewilderment of his high and his low has deluded him regarding the loftiness of his state. Except that there has occurred bewilderment of his high and his low regarding the loftiness of his state. And the majesty of his... and the lowliness... on the loftiness of his state, in that... and his bewilderment is on his `mufid`, and his lowliness on the loftiness of his state, and his bewilderment is on his `mufid`. `Fa-la ilaha siwahu`. So there is no god besides Him. Besides that divine being. `Laysa juzuriyyatun minhum`. It is not that it is a compulsion for them. Because he must say this, because of his helplessness. `La yajidu 'anha muhasan`. He does not find any escape from it. `Thumma nazzaha Ta'ala wa takabbara 'an al-hudud al-jismaniyya al-mahduda`. Then he declared him transcendent... he declared his transcendence... Allah Ta'ala, and proclaimed His greatness, from the limited physical ranks. `Wa 'an al-hudud al-ruhaniyya al-ghayr mahduda`. He said that God, the nourisher, is beyond the limited physical ranks and beyond the unlimited spiritual ranks. `Thumma salabahu Ta'ala ma athbatahu lahum min al-asma'i wa al-sifati`. Then he stripped from him, that is, from `mubdi'-e ta'ala`, what he had affirmed for them from the names and attributes. He said these names and attributes are for the physical ranks, for the spiritual ranks, but for `mubdi'-e ta'ala`, he is God. And `al-nu'ut wa al-idafat`. And the descriptions and the relations. `Wa 'ada ila haddihi`. And he returns to his rank. It means he returns to his rank. After all the affirmation and negation, he returns to his rank. `Wa wulhihi fihi`. And in it, he is bewildered. It means a `mu'min` is bewildered about a `mukathir`. There are `hudud` above the `mukathir`. Above him are also some `hudud`. Until he reaches `aql-e awwal`. He says even `aql-e awwal` is bewildered about someone. Then he returns. I will do my work. Everyone should do their own work, I will do my work. `Wa ta'atuhu`. And his obedience. He is bewildered in it, and he obeys. The `mu'min` obeys his `mukathir`. And he is committed to him. He becomes at that time... one... He who does true *Tawhid*, true *tanzih*, true *tajrid*. With `ma'rifat` and `din` and `ilm` and `yaqin`. And Allah Ta'ala says to him: `Ya ayyuha al-nafsu al-mutma'inna irji'i ila rabbiki radiyatan mardiyya`. "Return"... the word `irji'i` is there. He goes up to the top and then returns. To return is this. Return. O tranquil soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing. "Return to your Lord" means to your `mufid`. `Radiyatan mardiyya`. `Radiya`, you also be happy, and your `mufid` should also be happy with you. `Itmi'nanuha bi-ma 'arafat`. Its tranquility is in what it has known. And its pleasure is in the command of its Lord. `Alladhi ilayhi yurja'u`. That Lord to whom he is returned. `Mardiyyatan 'indahu`. Well-pleasing in His sight. And in the sight of all the `hudud`. `Alladhina ila ma'rifatihim intaha wa balagha`. Those to whose gnosis he has reached the end and arrived. `Wa alhamdulillah alladhi hadana li-hadha wa ma kunna li-nahtadiya lawla an hadana Allah. Laqad ja'at rusulu rabbina bil-haqq`. And praise be to Allah, who guided us to this. And we would not have been guided had Allah not guided us. Indeed, the messengers of our Lord have come with the truth. That... the messengers... of our Lord... have come to us with the truth. They have brought the truth to us. He is brought with the truth. He is brought. He has brought the truth. That `ayat` is there, right? Up there... `irji'i ila rabbiki`. She goes up and then comes down. O tranquil soul, who for the knowledge of your `mufid` have reached the end. Now return to your Lord. `Radiyatan mardiyya`. You also be pleased and he should also be pleased. This question was arising in the mind that this... `mubdi'-e ta'ala` who created... is there any mention of it in the Holy Qur'an? The world of souls... like any... `tafsir` or any verse where it is explained, or in our `du'a` where it is mentioned? `Inna khalaqnakum min nafsin wahidatin`. Different... different phrases have come. At different places, different commands have come. And in the Holy Qur'an, which... the explanations that have been given, their summary is `Surah al-Hamd`. And its details, as `Sayyidna` has explained, that `Surah al-Hamd` is `Alhamdulillah Rabb al-'Alamin`. Then what should be the qualities of Allah? He is `Rabb al-'Alamin`. All the details he has based on this verse in the book `Kitab al-'Alim wa al-Ghulam`. If you read it, you will understand. So it means it is mentioned in the `du'a` as well, and in the Holy Qur'an as well. Its summary is `Surah al-Fatiha`. And in `Surah al-Fatiha`, our `du'at`... have explained the matter. You have understood this much. For example, the `da'i` is saying that Allah has made three... what kinds? What has He made? Repentant ones. `Nadimin`. Then those who doubt. Then what? Those who seek forgiveness. Three kinds were made. Where is it mentioned? So he said, `Ihdina al-sirat al-mustaqim. Sirat alladhina an'amta 'alayhim`. Whose mention is there in `an'amta 'alayhim`? The `nadimin`. The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor. The `nadimin` were given the favor that they should return. After that, he said, `ghayr al-maghdubi 'alayhim`. Who are they? The insistent ones. The `maghdub` (those who have incurred wrath). Who are the `maghdub 'alayhim`? The insistent ones. Who insist. Upon whom wrath has descended. Third... `wa la al-dallin`. What is it? Bewilderment. The astray. Who are astray. The `sirat` that has to be crossed. In three ways. The `nadimin` have been mentioned. Then the `musirrin` have been mentioned. Then the `mutahayyirin` have been mentioned. The `mubdi'-e ta'ala` has... the beings that he created, the details of that... that is in the world of the physical body. Of course... it has come in his pure speech, which has been revealed to the people of the world. The mention of the people of the world is there. Of course. The `mubdi'`'s... who can understand the reality of `mubdi'`? That is... he has said that... `subhan alladhi`... what is it? Allah is pure from... you cannot understand His reality. You cannot understand Him. At many places in the Holy Qur'an, it is mentioned. From that, this is what is proven, that we cannot understand the reality of Allah Ta'ala. `Amma yasifun`. From what they describe. `Subhan alladhi`... `Subhan Allah 'amma yasifun`. Whatever attributes you describe for Him, He is pure from that. He is beyond all of them. `Tanzih`. `Subhan Allah 'amma yasifun`. Who were `ajiz` (incapable) in `ma'rifat`. They were `ajiz`. Complete `ma'rifat`. And their `mufid` who is `aql-e awwal`, he was `ajiz` in `ma'rifat`. He did not have his `ma'rifat` and neither did `aql-e awwal` have `ma'rifat` of `mubdi'`. About him, he was bewildered. Because of that, he became a god for them. And what did they say about `mubdi'-e ta'ala`? What word? "Hu". "Hu". And that too, what? Compulsorily. `Zanbun mashfu'un bil-istighfar`. Out of compulsion, they say it. Because we have no other word to say. To prove our existence, it is necessary to believe in the existence of the existent. Therefore, we use the word "Hu". Because we have no other word to say.

<!-- lecture 5 -->

*A'udhu billahi min al-shaytan al-rajim* (I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan). *Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim* (In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful). *Wa bihi nasta'in. Wa salla Allahu 'ala rasulihi Sayyidna Muhammadin wa alihi ajma'in.* (And in Him we seek help. And may Allah's blessings be upon His messenger, our master Muhammad, and all his progeny). *Al-bab al-thani min al-suradiq al-awwal yajma'u khamsata fusulin. Al-fasl al-awwal minha.* (The second chapter, from the first pavilion, encompasses five sections. The first section of them is this). *Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim.* The second chapter, from the first `suradiq`, which surrounds five sections, of which the first section is this. This `suradiq` is a very large tent. *Aqulu musta'inan billahi ta'ala wa bi-walihi fi ardhihi salamullahi 'alayhi 'ala itmami ma uhawilu mimma qad ta'ammaltuhu shukran min itmami ma qad ta'ammaltuhu shukran lahu wa li-awliya'ihi salawatullahi 'alayhim ajma'in wa iyyahu as'alul 'ismata min al-khata'i fi dhalika wa-l-zalal wa-in kuntu la ata'arra minhu illa bi-lahzati moulai... moulai.* *Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim.* I say, seeking `istighanah`, help, from Allah `zul-jalal`, from Allah Ta'ala, and from His `wali` who is on His earth—may Allah's peace be upon him—upon that matter, upon `itmam`... upon the completion of that which I present to him. That which I have obtained as a form of `shukr` (gratitude). He did it as a form of gratitude. As a form of gratitude. And for his `awliya` (saints), may the blessings of Allah be upon all of them. `Ajma'in`. And `wa iyyahu as'alul 'ismah`, and towards Him, towards the being of Allah `zul-jalal`, I ask for `'ismah` (protection) from `khata`... from errors, from `khata`, from slipping, in that matter. And from slipping in that matter. `Wa in kuntu la ata'arri minhu illa...` and I know this matter, that I will not... that thing will not overcome me, from it, except by the `lahzat` (glances) of my `moulai`. I cannot remain... I cannot be saved from it. Yes, I cannot be saved from it, except by the `lahzat` of my `moulai`. `Inna Allaha ta'ala alladhi la tatajasaru nahwahu-l-khawatir wa la tasmu ilayhi-l-awham wa-l-zama'ir, abda'a 'alam al-ibda'i al-mukanna 'anhu bi-'alam al-amri wa 'alam al-khalqi wa 'alam al-qudsi wa 'alam al-safa'i wa 'alam al-latafati wa bi-l-'alam al-ruhani daf'atan wahidatan min ghayri shay'in taqaddamahum fa-yakuna lahum hayulan ula wa la ma'a shay'in sahabahum fa-yakuna mumathilan lahum wa mushakilan wa la 'ala shay'in aqallahum fa-yakuna lahum makanan awwalan wa-khtara'ahum... makanan awwalan.` Indeed, Allah `zul-jalal`, Allah Ta'ala, is such a Being... Sayyidna Mohyuddin has given a very long explanation. This is its summary. Taking a summary from Mohyuddin, he has clarified it and brought it here. It is one section each. Allah `zul-jalal`, Allah Ta'ala is such a Being that our... heart... the heart towards Him... cannot dare towards Him. `Wa la tasmu ilayhi-l-awham` (and thoughts (`awham`) do not rise towards Him) and our thoughts cannot rise towards Him. And our inner selves (`zama'ir`) cannot rise towards Him. Our `awham` and `zama'ir` cannot become lofty towards Him. That Being created... He brought into being `'alam al-ibda'` (the world of origination). There is `khalq` and `ibda'`. `Khalq` is when you change the arrangement in created things. Changing the form. Pre-existing things were not where... `ibda'` is creating from there. And `khalq` is... a thing has been created, and from it, another thing is brought forth. A thing is broken, and a composite form is made from it. `Abda'a 'alam al-ibda'` (He originated the world of origination). He created `'alam al-ibda'`. `Al-mukanna 'anhu bi-'alam al-amr` (which is alluded to as the world of command). That `'alam al-ibda'` which was given the name, was alluded to as `'alam al-amr` (the world of command), and `'alam al-'aql` (the world of intellect), and `'alam al-quds` (the world of sanctity). `'Alam al-safa` (the world of purity)... and `'alam al-ruhani` (the spiritual world). `'Alam al-latafah` (the world of subtlety), `'alam al-ruhani`. All of them, with... there are seven names given. He created them in a single instance (`daf'atan wahidatan`), without any thing that had come before them, that it should become `hayula` (prime matter) for the thing to come. That first leaven should be made for it, its `hayula` should be made. `Wa la ma'a shay'in...` (and not with anything...). There was no thing from which he made it by shaping it. In a single instance. That it should become `hayula ula` for them. `Wa la ma'a shay'in sahabahum` (and not with anything that accompanied them). And not with any thing, made along with any thing, that its company... that it should adopt its company, so that it becomes similar (`mumathil`) to it. Or of the same form (`mushakil`). `Wa la 'ala shay'in` (and not upon anything). And not upon any thing did he make it, that it carried it. That it should become a place (`makan`) for it. A first place (`makan awwal`). It's not that he made it on something that was there before. `wa-khtara'ahum 'alaman wujudun min 'adamin ghayri mawjudin tafaddulan minhu wa judan wa tatawwulan minhu...` And Allah `zul-jalal` originated (`ikhtara`) them, in a world of existence, from a nothingness (`'adam`) that was not existent. As a favor (`tafaddul`) from Him, and as generosity (`judan`), and as a bestowal (`tatawwulan`) from Him. What is nothingness (`'adam`)? Is it some world? Nothingness. The absence of being. Once a gentleman in Sindh was teaching and asked, when all this was happening, where were we? `...minhu wa judan wa tatawwulan...` Why did the Originator (`mubdi'`) create? On this, Sayyidna Mohyuddin has written chapter after chapter. He negates everything, that there was no purpose, no need, nothing like that. Negating one thing after another, he then arrives at the point that this was the only purpose of Allah, `tafaddulan minhu` (as a favor from Him). As a `tafaddul` (favor). `Wa judan` (and as generosity), as a gift. `Wa tatawwulan` (and as a bestowal), meaning as a boon from Him. `Iz min shimati-l-karim al-qadir al-tafaddul` (since it is from the nature of the Generous (`karim`), the Powerful (`qadir`) to bestow favor). Because it is in the nature of the `karim` (generous), the `qadir` (powerful), to bestow favor (`fadl`). To do `tafaddul`. `Wa min sajiyyati-l-'aziz al-'azim al-jud` (and from the nature (`sajiyyah`) of the Mighty (`aziz`), the Great (`azim`) is generosity). And in the nature of the `aziz` (mighty), the `'azim` (great), it is one of his traits to bestow (`bakhshish`). To bestow. And to bestow and be gracious. `La muhtajan ilayhim wa la 'abithan bihim` (not needing them, nor playing with them). He was not in need of them. The Giver was not in need of them. `Wa la 'abithan bihim` (and not playing with them). And not playing with them. He did not create them unnecessarily, for sport. `Iz huwa muta'alin mutakabbirun 'an dhalika` (as He is exalted and transcendent above that). Because the creator is lofty from that matter. And is exalted and sublime from that matter. `Awjadahum ashbahan... shabahun... ashbahan suriyatan mahdatan nuraniyatan...` (He brought them into existence as forms (`ashbah`), purely imaginal (`suriyyah`), pure (`mahdatan`), luminous (`nuraniyah`)). He created them as `ashbah` (forms), as such `ashbah` that were imaginal (`suriyyah`), pure, and luminous (`nuraniyah`). `Dhawati qamatin alfiyah ka-l-qamat al-insaniyah al-bashariyah` (possessing thousand-fold statures like the human, corporeal statures). They possessed statures, like the thousand-fold statures, like the human stature, which are corporeal (`bashariyah`). He has explained that here, the human corporeal statures were like that. In reality, what is it? That the human corporeal statures are like that one. Like which one? The one that was created by Allah. The Originator, when He created, He created in such a state that the human corporeal statures were on its pattern, when they came into the world. Here it is only to make us understand that He has said, the one He created... was like the human corporeal statures. The Originator created the `dhawati qamatin alfiyah` (possessors of thousand-fold statures). In reality, it is the other way around. Meaning, what is it? The human corporeal statures that have been created are of the same state in which the Originator created them. `...mubayinatan li-anfusihim al-hayulaniyah...` (distinct from their material (`hayulaniyah`) souls...). Separating, distinguishing, their material (`hayulaniyah`) souls. Those souls did not exist. The souls are things of later. From them were created... `mubayinatan...` (distinguishing...), being separate from their material souls. So, what He created was `ashbah suriyyah nuraniyah` (luminous imaginal forms). When the souls were formed, they were later, from the degradation of these things. And the bodies of flesh and blood... those are dark densities (`katha'if al-zulmaniyah`). And those were luminous subtleties (`lata'if al-nuraniyah`). When the souls were formed, they were... what are they? A fallen form of it. And when the body was formed, it is an even more fallen form. `Fa-awjada tilka-l-ashbah al-nuraniyah mutasawiyatan fi-l-kamal al-awwali alladhi huwa-l-wujud wa-l-hayat wa-l-quwwah wa-l-qudrah...` (So He brought those luminous forms into existence, equal in the first perfection, which is existence, life, strength, and ability...). What is there here? Knowledge and ability (`'ilm` and `qudrah`). So he created those luminous forms in one state, in the first perfection (`kamal al-awwal`). In the state of the first perfection, He created them equal. The first perfection is this state. What Allah Ta'ala created, that is called the first perfection (`kamal al-awwal`). Equal, they were equal in the first perfection. What is that? It is `wujud` (existence). `Wujud`. And `hayat` (life), and `quwwah` (strength), and `qudrah` (ability). `La takhalufa fiha wa la tafadula wa la tabayuna baynaha wa la tamayula fi-ma daqqa wa jalla wa kathura wa qalla, 'adlan minhu 'azza wa jall.` (...in which there is no disagreement, no preference, no distinction between them, and no inclination in what was subtle or great, much or little—as an act of justice from Him, the Mighty and Majestic). There is no possibility of any deficiency or excess. There is no inclination of one towards another. The Originator created all the created beings, there is not even a slight difference among them. He created the first just as he created the last. In what was subtle and great, and much and little. As an act of justice from Him, `azza wa jall`. `'Adlan minhu 'azza wa jall`. As an act of justice from Him. `Iz al-'adilu yatasawa 'adluhu wa-l-fadil ya'ummu fadluhu.` (Since the justice of the Just is equal, and the grace of the Gracious is universal). `Kama akhbara-l-kitab al-karim min qawli-l-'ali al-'azim: wa law kana min 'indi ghayrillahi la-wajadu fihi ikhtilafan kathira.` (As the Noble Book has informed from the saying of the High, the Great: "And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found therein much contradiction"). It falls in `ikhtilaf`. `fihi ikhtilafan kathira`. And if it were... `Ikhtilaf` comes from what? `Khalaf`. Which `bab` (form) is it? `Bab al-ifti'al`. `Isti'al`. `Bab al-ifti'al`. `Ikhtilaf`. `Bab al-ifti'al`. `Wa law kana min 'indi ghayrillahi`, if that thing were, if that matter were from other than Allah, then they would find in it much difference (`ikhtilaf`). Allah created it, so He did this kindness to His creation, that He gave no one more and no one less. If He gave, He gave equally. The state of being created equally, yesterday there was a question about it. Has any verse about it come in the Holy Quran? This is it. `wa law kana min 'indi ghayrillahi la-wajadu fihi ikhtilafan kathira.` `Wa hadha huwa haqiqatu qawli Sayyidna Hamiruddin a'la Allahu qudsahu fi-l-mashra' al-sabi' min al-suwar al-rabi' min rahat al-'aql haythu qala...` (And this is the reality of the saying of Sayyidna Hamiruddin, may Allah sanctify his soul, in the seventh path from the fourth form of `Rahat al-'Aql`, where he said...). And this saying is the true saying of Sayyidna Hamiruddin, may Allah sanctify his soul, in the seventh `mashra'` (path), which is from the fourth `suwar` (form) of `Rahat al-'Aql`, where he said... as you have said: `wa dar al-ibda'i wa-l-inbi'athi la 'a'iqa fiha li-khuluwihima min al-mawad allati ta'uqu wa tajarruduha minha wa kawnaha suwaran mahdatan la tata'allaqu bi-maddatin wa la biha maddah li-tahjuzaha 'an al-fi'l...` And as he has said, the abode of origination (`dar al-ibda'`) and the abode of emanation (`dar al-inbi'ath`), there is no obstacle in it. There is no obstacle. Because they are free of matter. They are free from those matters which obstruct. Such things are not there that would obstruct them. `wa tajarruduha minha` (and its being abstracted from them), because of it. Meaning, its being abstracted. The pronoun `ha`... from both of them. Towards the `'alam`. Towards the `dar`. To the `dar`. `Dar` is feminine. `wa tajarruduha minha` (and its being abstracted from them). And it was taken out from the matter. To be free... that `dar`... from those matters which obstruct. And act as a hindrance in the path. Okay. And its being (`kawnaha`) `suwaran mahdatan` (pure forms). And that house's being, in the form of pure, special forms. `La tata'allaqu bi-maddatin` (that are not attached to any matter). They are not related to any matter, any `maddah`. `Wa la biha maddah` (nor is there any matter in them). And no `maddah` was created from it. `wa la biha maddah`. And no `maddah` was created from it. `Li-tahjuzaha 'an al-fi'l` (that would prevent them from action). So that it may prevent it from action (`fi'l`). In material there is an obstruction. Wherever material has come, hindrances have come, obstacles have come. Here, there is no material at all, that it should be stopped from action. There is power (`quwwah`) and ability (`qudrah`) there. And `quwwah` and `qudrah` can show their effect. No obstruction has been put in place for performing the second action (`'amal-i-thani`). For obtaining the second excellence (`kamal-i-thani`). `Wa idha kana la 'a'iqa fiha fa-wujud mawjudatiha la bi-zamanin bal daf'atan wahidatan...` (And since there is no obstacle in them, the existence of its existents is not in time, but in a single instance...). And since it happened, this matter, that there is no obstacle there, then the existence of its existents is not by time, but in a single instance. In one moment of time, their existents came into being. `Mithla wujudi ishraqi basit al-hawa' 'an daw' al-shamsi, la bi-zamanin...` (like the existence of the illumination of the expanse of the air from the light of the sun, not in time...). Just like the existence... of the spreading of light in the expanse of the air from the light of the sun. The whole air becomes illuminated. Like that, he says. `Wa id'atu-l-nar al-bayt al-muzlima daf'atan wahidatan...` (and the lighting of the dark house by a fire in a single instance...). And the fire illuminating the dark house in a single instance. When the fire is lit, the whole room becomes illuminated. `...la bi-zamanin ila qawlihi` (not in time, until his saying). No time encompasses it, until your saying... `'ala anna al-shay'a fi tilka-l-dar lam yataqaddam wujuduhu 'ala shay'in min al-'uqul al-qa'imati bi-l-fi'li wa-l-'uqul al-qa'imati bi-l-quwwah.` (That a thing in that abode, its existence did not precede anything from the intellects existing in actuality and the intellects existing in potentiality.) For understanding, some time passes. When the fire is lit, some time passes. The example... What is light? It's not like the light here. That as soon as it is lit, the whole room is filled with light. It means, of the first perfection (`kamal al-awwal`). Until your saying, upon this matter, `ala`... that `inna al-shay'a...` until your saying, `ala...` upon this matter, that any being in that house, `lam yataqaddam wujuduhu` (its existence did not precede). Its existence did not precede any thing from the intellects. Which were existing in actuality (`bi-l-fi'l`). There, the intellects which were... their existence did not precede the potential intellects. Meaning, the intellects that existed there in potentiality (`bi-l-quwwah`). Nor the intellects that existed in potentiality. Meaning, the intellects existing in actuality and the intellects existing in potentiality. The one means the powers that were given to the intellects. And after that, they established them. Their existence was not before that, something existed. `Bal wujud al-kulli ma'an.` (Rather, the existence of all was together). But the existence of all was together, at one time. Meaning, both the potential intellect (`qa'im al-quwwah`) and the actual intellect (`qa'im al-fi'l`) existed at the same time. This means that there was no period of time separating the first perfection (`kamal al-awwal`) and the second perfection (`kamal al-thani`). Now he is explaining, he is explaining it... Sayyidna Mohyuddin is explaining, `yuridu bi-dhalika a'la Allahu qudsahu fi hali wujudihim al-awwali wa kamalihim al-awwali alladhina hum fihi mutasawun...` (By that, may Allah sanctify his soul, he means in the state of their first existence and their first perfection, in which they are equal...). In the state of their first existence, and their first perfection, in which they are all equal. `Kama sabaqa min qawlihi...` (as has preceded from his saying...). Like his saying has preceded. And they, along with that, `fi bad'i wujudihim al-jami'i fi-l-fi'li wa-l-'amali ghayru ma'sumin min al-khata'` (in the beginning of their collective existence, in action and deed, are not infallible/protected from error). And along with that, in their initial existence, all of them, in action (`fi'l`) and deed (`'amal`), are not infallible (`ghayru ma'sumin`). They are not infallible (`ma'sum`) from error (`khata`). So, this is not the perfect state. The perfect state is the second perfection (`kamal al-thani`). This is the first perfection (`kamal al-awwal`). Although they are all equal, there is nothing... but they are `ghayr ma'sum` (not infallible). Error can occur from them. What is the error? That they do not attain the second perfection. That is the error. That there is a delay in invitation. And upon being invited, they do not come. Then errors occur from them, they mislead others, they put others on the wrong path, all this can happen. They were taught the first excellence (`kamal al-awwal`), in the first excellence (`kamal al-awwal`) they are `ghayr ma'sum` (not infallible). Go straight, then the power that has been given to you... this is solely for the sake of the test. Otherwise... so, is there not a return? It is not the perfect state. No. In the second perfection (`kamal al-thani`), if you go, by using your powers, etc. Using the correct method, then you will attain the second perfection. `...wa hum ma'a dhalika...` And they are not infallible from the second perfection either. And along with that, in their initial existence, all of them, in action and deed, are `ghayru ma'sumin` (not infallible). They are not infallible. From error (`khata`) and from slipping (`zalal`). `Asmana Allahu min an nazilla aw nuzilla, aw nazilla aw nuzilla, aw nazilla aw nuzilla bi-haqqi Muhammadin wa alihi-l-tahirin salawatullahi 'alayhim ajma'in.` May Allah protect us from this matter, that from `an nazilla` (that we should slip). We may slip. Or `nuzilla`... is from `zalla`, `yuzillu`. Or we may be made to slip. `Nuzilla`. `Nuzilla` or `nuzilla`. No, `nuzilla`. From slipping (`nazilla`) or we be made to slip (`nuzilla`). And we may slip or we may make others slip. `Nuzilla`. What is `zalla`? He slipped. `Azalla`, he made [someone] slip. Just like `qata'a`, he cut. `Aqta'a`, he had [someone] cut. `Sajada`, he prostrated. `Asjada`, he made [someone] prostrate. So here, `nazilla` and `nuzilla`. This matter, that we... may slip. Or may be made to slip. We may slip. Or we may make others slip. We may be made to slip. We may slip. We may make [others] slip. We may slip, or we may make [others] slip. May Allah protect us from this matter, that we may slip. Or may make others slip. Or we may go astray, or we may lead others astray. `Zalla, azalla`. `Zalla` means he went astray. `Adalla` means he led [someone] astray. The grammar of the `bab` (verb form)... the structure of `sarf` and `nahw` will always remain. `Fa'ala`, he did. `Af'ala`, he had [it] done. `Fa'ala`, `af'ala`. `Fa'ala` means he did, `af'ala` means he had [it] done. That we may slip or... may Allah protect us from these things... `Al-fasl al-thani min al-bab al-thani min al-suradiq al-awwal.` (The second section from the second chapter of the first pavilion). `Thumma inna wahidan min tilka-l-ashbah al-suwariyah nazara bi-dhatihi ila dhatihi wa ila abna'i jinsihi fa-'alima anna lahum mubdi'an bi-khilafihim fa-nafa 'anhu wa 'an abna'i jinsihi al-ilahiyata wa athbataha li-mubdi'ihim ta'ala wa shahida lahu bi-l-wahdaniyah...` Then, indeed, one from those imaginal (`suwariyah`) forms (`ashbah`), `nazara bi-dhatihi ila dhatihi` (looked with his essence at his essence). What was the process of seeing? What was its process in the first intellect? Then indeed, one of those luminous, imaginal forms, `nazara bi-dhatihi` (he looked with his essence). This is the main thing. `Ila dhatihi` (at his essence). He looked at his own essence. He, with his own essence, looked at his own essence. What did he see first? At his own essence. After that, he looked at his own kind. He saw all things. `Fa-'alima` (so he knew). So he knew, for him... that for him and for them... yes, this is it. For him and for them, there is an Originator (`mubdi'`). `Bi-khilafihim` (unlike them). Who is not like them, is different from them. `Bi-khilafihim` (unlike them). Different from them. An Originator. `Fa-nafa 'anhu` (so he negated from himself). Then he negated, that he is not... so he negated from himself. From his own self. And from the children of his own kind, he negated divinity (`ilahiyah`). I can't claim that I am, I can't claim that I am. `Wa athbataha li-mubdi'ihim` (and he affirmed it for their Originator). And he affirmed it for their Originator. So, this is `tawhid`, `tajrid`, and `tanzih`, all three. That same person is `Sahib al-Tawhid`. `wa i'tarafa lahu bi-l-rububiyah wa sabbaha lahu wa khasha'a wa tazallala wa khada'a...` (and he acknowledged for Him Lordship, and glorified Him and was humble, and submitted himself, and was subservient...). And he acknowledged `rububiyah` (Lordship) for Him. `Zalla`, the `dhal` here... a word with four letters comes. `Dhal`, `zay`, `zwa`, `zoe`. From `zay`. From `zway`. From `dhal`. `Zalla` means he became humble. `Azalla` means he humbled [someone]. `Dhal`. After that, what is there? `Zway`. `Zway` is `asaya` (disobedience). And `zoe`... `zalla`. `Toe, zoe`. That means to give shade. Four letters: `dhal`, `zay`, `zwa`, `zoe`. Each has a different meaning. `Wa tazallala` (and he made himself humble). He made himself humble, and `khada'a`, he submitted. And he sought means (`tawassul`). And he sought `tawassul`. `Bi-'azmatihi ilayhi` (through His greatness towards Him). `Wa dara'a` (and he supplicated). He sought `tawassul` with His greatness, towards Him, and he supplicated. This is a special point. He sought the means of His greatness. The greatness of the Originator, from His greatness, towards Him. The Originator's greatness, he took it as a means to reach the Originator. That is, His greatness, we cannot reach it. Through the means of that greatness, we... give testimony to Your Lordship, to Your divinity. He is confessing his own lowliness. Yes. The language is... the language is not there. Before and after is there, in this matter. When does time come? From the sun. The sun. Time. And there, it is before and after. `Qabliyat` and `ba'diyat`. He sought means (`tawassul`). He did `tawassul`. `Wa tawassala bi-'azmatihi ilayhi` (and he sought means through His greatness towards Him). His greatness, from His greatness, towards Him, he sought `tawassul`. `Wa dara'a` (and he supplicated). And he made supplication (`tazarru'`). `Fa-tadaraka min mubdi'ihi al-mawad al-ilahiyah...` (So divine supports reached him from his Originator...). So, from him... there descended upon him, from his Originator, divine supports (`mawad al-ilahiyah`). `Wa-l-ta'yidat al-wahdaniyah` (and the confirmations of oneness). And confirmations of oneness (`ta'idat al-wahdaniyah`) descended upon him. `Wa-ttasala bihi 'ilm al-jari wa-l-nur al-sari alladhi huwa kalimatullahi ta'ala.` (And the flowing knowledge and the spreading light connected with him, which is the Word of Allah, the Exalted). And connected with him from that, from that first intellect... from that first `shibh`... was the flowing knowledge (`'ilm al-jari`) and the spreading light (`nur al-sari`). Which is the `kalimah` (word) of Allah Ta'ala. That which is `kalimah` is `La ilaha illa Allah`. This is the essence. Is knowledge... flowing knowledge from him? The flowing knowledge and the spreading light. What did he say? It is the `kalimah` of Allah Ta'ala. It is the `kalimah` `La ilaha illa Allah`. Between the Originator (`mubdi'`) and the originated (`mubda'`). The `kalimatullah ta'ala`. And through that `kalimah`, there is flowing knowledge and spreading light. `Wa lidhalika qila inna-l-kalimata fawqa-l-'aqli wa dun al-mubdi'.` (And for that reason it is said that the `kalimah` is above the intellect and below the Originator). And for this reason it is said that the `kalimah` is above the intellect and below the Originator. The `kalimah` `la ilaha illa Allah` is what? It is above him. It is below the `mubdi'` and `mubda'`. `Duna-l-mubdi'i ta'ala` (below the Originator, the Exalted). `Fawqa-l-'aqli` (above the intellect). And but, where did that flowing light come from? From the `mubdi'`. Below the `mubdi'` and above the `'aql`. In the Quran, the `kalimah` `la ilaha illa Allah` has come 39 times, and you have made a `du'a` from it... In the Quran. So, it certainly has great meanings, that why only 39? It continues. `Wa yusamma aydan bi-l-amr.` (And it is also named `al-amr` (the command)). The same is also given the name `amr` (command). All the commands are placed within that `kalimah`. So the `kalimah` is a continuous link. `Mubdi'`... The `mubdi`'s will. `wa la ilaha illa Allah` is manifested in it. Now see, here too, why did the world end at seven? The first intellect happened, the `mubdi'` made seven. And the tenth is `ashirah`. Why did it end? `La ilaha illa Allah`. The `mubdi`'s will was that it should end at seven. `Wa yusamma...` this `kalimah` that has been issued, was for a period of time, or is it a link that has been established forever? As long as the creation remains, the `kalimah` will remain. The flowing light will remain. And it is also given the name `amr` (command). And this `kalimah` will be found only in the second perfection (`kamal al-thani`), not in the state of the first perfection (`kamal al-awwal`). It will be found in the second perfection. The will to take the first perfection... The first one did what? He used `wasilah` (means). From His greatness. We who are... must use the means of His greatness. We who are in this state now, are certainly in the state of the first perfection. When we become abstracted... it will be over. Then another state... We are in the fallen state of the first perfection. So, the `la ilaha illa Allah` that we are reciting, we have not even grasped the reality of the `kalimah`. So when we return, will we go to the state of the first perfection or the second perfection? Because then we will have to choose again, or... We are going towards the second perfection. The first perfection has been achieved. It has been. It cannot be taken back. But there is a choice from there, right? And for the second perfection, he... the first perfection's state can change, he is `ghayr ma'sum` (not infallible), he has stated. In the state of the first perfection, he is `ghayr ma'sumin` (not infallible). Allah does not take it away. I have fallen... the powers... you can achieve that state of excellence, of praise, of joy. Until that thing of the second perfection is achieved, you... the state of the first perfection... will remain as it is, no one can snatch it away from you. This is a thing given by Allah Ta'ala. Existence, knowledge, power, freedom. These three things are with you, given by Allah Ta'ala, no one can snatch them away. To use them better, you have to go towards the second perfection. To activate it. To go towards the second perfection. And when the second perfection is achieved, then you have... So, we are currently not able to complete even the first perfection. No, we are lacking in the first perfection. We are journeying towards the second perfection. No, we are lacking in the first perfection. We are in the fallen state of the first perfection. So, the decline that has come, has come in our first perfection. The decline has come upon the `'aql` (intellect), upon the `qudrah` (ability), and upon the `hayat` (life). Meaning, the first perfection... the decline that came in it, its meaning is... that the powers Allah gave, you were given them. You are not using them. The decline has come in their use. We are not using them correctly. The one who attained the `da'wah` also took the `da'wah` to the `munafiqin`. And he was given the `qamat-i-alfiyah`, this is the same one, from the first... when he was in the state of `kamal-al-awwal`... Then he made the choice of `kamal-i-thani`, then he was given the authority to choose. Yes. `...iz bihi ta'azzulun abadi wa-l-baqa'u-l-kulli al-sarmadi wa-l-'ula wa-l-'azmah wa-l-thana wa-l-ni'mah wa-l-jalalah wa-l-'ismah.` (Through it is eternal isolation, and universal, perpetual existence, and loftiness, and greatness, and praise, and blessing, and majesty, and protection). And through that `kalimah`, he obtained... that first intellect encompassed every thing with knowledge. There is everything in it. `bismi-llahi alladhi taqumu bihi al-samawatu wa-l-ard...` And with it... `Wa bihi ahata bi-kulli shay'in 'ilman` (and through it, he encompassed all things in knowledge). What is in the `kalimah` that was not given with the first perfection? Because complete knowledge was given, wasn't it? It was given. He did not recognize it. To use it... the power... the way to use the powers... was given to him. Through the light of the `kalimah`, it came to his understanding what I have taken. It is the remaining part. No, the remaining part comes later. He had to negate himself first. And until one negates oneself... now the first one said that I am not my creator. This matter... and we are not all our creators, but our creator is someone else. As soon as he said this, he obtained the `kalimah`, and in the light of the `kalimah`, all things were obtained by him. Our return is towards the first perfection or the second perfection? It is not towards the first perfection, because we then have to choose again or... `Wa 'alima ma kana wa ma sayakun.` (And he knew what was and what will be). He knew what had happened and what would happen in the future. `La ilaha illa Allah` contains everything. What has happened, and what will happen in the future. `Wa wajada fi dhatihi min al-sururi wa-l-jazali wa-l-huburi wa-l-'ismati wa-l-thana'i wa-l-'azmati wa-l-kibriya'i...` (And he found in his essence such joy, delight, happiness, protection, praise, greatness, and pride...). He is explaining the composition of the `kalimah` `La ilaha illa Allah`. It has `nafi` (negation) and `ithbat` (affirmation). What is the first type? Negation and affirmation. Negative and positive. Two things. After that, what does he explain? Three... three letters. `Alif, lam, ha`. After that, what is there? The jewels of the letters. Five. After that, four `kalimat` (words). `La, ilaha, illa, Allah`. How many is that? Nine. After that, what is there? The count of one ends. Seven. After that, seven `muqatta'at`. He explains the `muqatta'at`. Where does the pen stop? Seven places. In the luminous world, what happened? It ended at seven luminous forms. Why did it end? This matter, that `La ilaha illa Allah`, the will of the `mubdi'` was that it should end at seven. He has placed everything in it. That it should end only at seven. After that, then... it was in his knowledge, in his mind, that this would happen. After that, what happened? Twelve. Twelve are the `ruh-i-sa'idah`. Everywhere, this composition will work. In every Imam, in every `barzakh`, this composition will work. Two, three... Everywhere, whether it is a believer or... among existents. Everywhere. The composition is two, three, four, seven, and twelve. Seven and twelve are 19. Nineteen are where? In `Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim`, there are 19. In `Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim`, where are the two? `Bismillah`. `Bismillah`, `al-Rahman`. The additive construction (`tarkib-i-idafi`) and the descriptive construction (`tarkib-i-tawsifi`). `Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim`. `Tarkib-i-idafi`, `tarkib-i-tawsifi`. In this, what is there? The `tarkib-i-idafi` is more excellent. The `tarkib-i-tawsifi` is lesser than it. Here, the flaw has come upside down. `La ilaha illa Allah`, what is the flaw? It is upside down. First is affirmation, then negation. Regarding which it is said that "Let my affirmation be established by your negation, I should be negated such that only You remain." `Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim`. The `tarkib-i-idafi` is a very high construction. And the `tarkib-i-tawsifi`, as Sayyidna Muhammad Taher, may Allah sanctify his soul, explains, that `Bismillah` is what? The week of the seven Imams. Seven Imams' week. `Bismillah`. Seven letters. And with each Imam, there are what? Twelve of his... `naqib` (deputies). They are twelve. That is `al-Rahman al-Rahim`. `Bismillah`, the Imam and... `Sath, Imam, Ma'dhun`. On the week of the seven Imams. The seven weeks that are of the Imams, it is based on that. And the twelve that are mentioned are, in reality, with every Imam, and when the seventh Imam appears, the twelve who appear are of a very high rank, higher than the twelve who appeared before. He is a `mursal` (messenger). So he found in his essence, from joy, from delight, from happiness, from protection, from praise, from greatness, from pride... after death, there will be salvation. He knew this. From the light of that `kalimah`. The first intellect knew. `Wa wajada fi dhatihi...` (And he found in his essence...). And he found in his essence, from joy, from delight, from happiness, from protection, from praise, from greatness, and from pride... `...ma la yaqdiru an yastura sifatahu bananun...` (...that which no fingertip/pen could write its description...). It is not possible that the description of it... should be written... fingertips. A `banan` is the doer. `wa la yutarjimu 'anhu lisanun` (nor could any tongue translate it). Nor could the tongue translate its account. `Thumma izdada li-dhalika li-mubdi'ihi ta'ala tazallulan wa khudu'an wa hayratan fi 'azmatihi...` (Then, because of that, he increased in humility and submission to his Originator, the Exalted, and in bewilderment at His greatness...). Then he increased, because of that... When he obtained the `kalimah`, then he increased even more in humility and submission. Increased in that matter... for his Originator, Ta'ala, `tazallul` (humility), doing `khudu'` (submission), bewilderment in His greatness, and doing `khushu'` (reverence). `Wa lidhalika nataqa-l-kitab al-karim bi-qawlihi ta'ala: in-nama yakhsha Allaha min 'ibadihi al-'ulama'.` (And for that reason the Noble Book spoke with His saying, the Exalted: "Indeed, only those who have knowledge among His servants fear Allah.") And for this reason, the Noble Book has said, in its saying, Ta'ala, `in-nama`... `ma` here is `ma-i-nafiyah` (negational `ma`). No. The translation that is done of `in-nama` is "indeed." `Ma`... three types of `ma`. `Ma` meaning "what," `ma` meaning "superfluous," and `ma` meaning "negation." Indeed, they do not fear Allah... indeed, it is the `ulama` (the learned) who fear Allah from among His servants. Here `in-nama` is "indeed." `Ma` is superfluous. `Ma` is superfluous here. Indeed, they fear Allah Ta'ala, from among His servants, only the `ulama`. `Wa lidhalika kullu 'alimin...` (and for that reason, every knower...). The `ma` has the force of `illa` (except) here. The force of `ma` is `illa`. Every `alim` (knower) of the secret of creation and the causes of nature is the one among people who fears Allah `zul-jalal` the most. And his `awliya`. Allah's blessings be upon them. As Amir al-Din al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, used to say, that the color of your face changes, then he would say, "Do you not know in whose court you are standing?" `Thumma inna Allaha ta'ala ittakhadhahu lahu hijaban wa ja'alahu lahu baban la yutawassalu ilayhi illa bihi wa la yunaja illa min janabihi wa la yuwahhadu illa min asbabihi fa-sara ismuhu al-a'zamu wa maqamuhu al-ashrafu al-akramu.` (Then indeed Allah, the Exalted, took him as a veil for Himself and made him a gate for Himself, through which alone one may seek means to Him, and from whose presence alone one may have intimate discourse, and through whose means alone He is declared One. Thus he became His Greatest Name and His most noble and honorable station). As knowledge increases, the fear in the presence of Allah will also increase. And fear is not in fear. It is in the acknowledgment of His greatness. Then indeed, Allah Ta'ala took him... for Himself, as a `hijab` (veil), and made him a gate (`bab`) for Himself, through which one cannot seek means (`tawassul`) to Him except through him, and one cannot have intimate discourse (`munajah`) except from his presence, and He is not declared One (`yuwahhad`) except through his means. `fa-sara ismuhu al-a'zamu wa maqamuhu al-ashraf al-akramu.` (Thus he became His Greatest Name and His most noble and honorable station). Then Allah `zul-jalal` took him, Allah Ta'ala made him a `hijab` (veil) for Himself. Until they acknowledge him, they cannot attain the second perfection. He made him a `hijab` for Himself, and made him a `bab` (gate) for Him. He made that first intellect a `bab` for Himself. The `mubdi'` Ta'ala made that first intellect a `bab` for Himself, as an access gate. `La yutawassalu ilayhi illa bihi` (one cannot seek means to Him except through him). Means cannot be sought towards Him except through that first intellect. Until you acknowledge the `wali`... the first intellect, you cannot attain the second perfection. `Wa la yunaja illa min janabihi` (and one does not have intimate discourse except from his presence). And he does not perform `munajah` except from his presence. The first intellect... the `mumbai-i-thani` was deceived by a corrupt notion. That he too acknowledged it. He acknowledged the first intellect. But what happened? The notion of equality came. That my vision and the vision of the first `mumbai'` are equal. And because of this, he could not attain the second perfection. He acknowledged the superiority of the first intellect. Both of their existences... but with the first `mumbai'`, he claimed equality. In the first perfection, all are equal. In the second perfection, no one can be equal. It cannot be. He is unique. Everyone's ranks... before and after. `La yunaja...` (he does not have `munajah`...). `Munajah` cannot be performed except from his presence. `Wa la yuwahhadu illa min asbabihi` (and He is not declared One except through his means). And `tawhid` cannot be done except through his means. So he became, that first intellect... `ismuhu al-a'zam` (His Greatest Name). He became the Greatest Name of Allah Ta'ala. `Wa maqamuhu al-ashraf al-akram` (and his station, the most noble and honorable). And his station became the most noble and honorable. There is this matter that he is the first originated being. And the circle of the first `mubdi'` is there. No one has reached there yet. No, no one can reach there. That is the circle of oneness. He is the possessor of the `hijab`. A `hijab`. Unless one has his means... The circle of the first `mubdi'` is the circle of oneness. It has been asked of Sayyidna Sadiq that oneness is there, but what is the circle? He said it is a special honorific. And that `quds` is also called a circle. That the first intellect has encompassed it. The first intellect, when he saw his essence... The first state was that of `kamal al-awwal`. After that, the state that came, he took the means of the greatness of God Ta'ala. All these things happened one after another. Before and after is there too. But it is within the circle of oneness. No other being entered it. This is the `wahdat`... the uniqueness of every circle. It should be within its own time, right? Time... not in time. Before and after. And the `kalimah` `La ilaha illa Allah` is the essence. The one he appointed... that after seven, it is broken. The pen is broken. It's not a circle of time... a point is also its own circle. `Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim.`

<!-- lecture 6 -->

It is connected. It is connected with all three `jauhar`s (essences/substances). Because Iqbal says, as they say, the limit of `aql` (intellect) is `hayrat` (wonder/astonishment). So, do we have a specific `jauhar`, or is it the limit of all three `jauhar`s? The limit of the three `jauhar`s is... it is. The limit of the three `jauhar`s, the limit of `aql`... `Aql` was given three powers (`quwwat`). `Hayat` (life)... `uquul` (intellects) were created by Allah Ta'ala. He gave them `zindagi` (life)... He bestowed three powers: the power of `zindagi`, and... It was given to `aql`... to the `uquul`... to the `dhawat` (essences) He created... He created the `dhawat` and gave them three powers: of `hayat` (life), of `ilm` (knowledge), and of `ikhtiyar` (volition/choice). So, the limit of all three `jawahir` (essences) is `aql`. `Aql`. The three... `aql` is that which becomes astonished about its God. That Allah Ta'ala created it, but it cannot attain His `ma'rifat` (gnosis). Yes, begin with the `hadith`. Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. `Summa innahu... summa innahu... lima... lima...` Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. `Summa innahu abiha lima abiha hadha al-aql al-sharif lahu ithnan min tilka al-ashbah al-suwariyyah, wa huma al-mu'arrab 'anhuma bil-munba'ithayn al-awwalayn. Sabaqa ahaduhuma al-akhar. Fa-nazara bi-dhatihi ila dhatihi wa ila abna'i jinsihi kama nazara al-awwal. Fa-'alima anna lahu wa lahum mubdi'an.` `Abiha`... What will be its translation? `Abiha`... `ya-abahu`. `ay 'alima bihi` (meaning, he knew it). `ay 'alima bihi`. `Abiha ya-abahu, ay 'alima bihi` (He knew it). `Alima bihi.` So, this is it. `Ay 'alima` (meaning, he knew). The meaning of `abiha` is `alima`. Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. Yes. Bismillah. Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. The third chapter, from the second section, from `Suradaq al-Awwal`. Then, indeed, when he knew... when that `aql-e sharif` (noble intellect) knew... `lahu ithnan` (for him are two)... `lahu`... `sharif`... `lahu`. When he knew... `innahu abiha... abiha ithnan`. Yes. Its `fa'il` (subject) is `ithnan`. Yes, `ithnan`. Then, indeed, when that `aql-e sharif` knew it... wanted to know it... that `aql-e sharif`, `aql-e mubda'-e awwal`, tried to recognize God. `Summa innahu lamma abiha hadha al-aql al-sharif...` For the `mabda'-e ta'ala`, the pronoun is towards it. Yes. The two intellects tried to recognize the `aql-e awwal`. Yes. Then he wanted to know. `Abiha ithnan`. Its `fa'il` is `ithnan`. `Abiha ithnan`. The two knew... the two wanted to know. The `aql-e sharif`... Then, indeed, when... `summa innahu abiha`, leave that. I think it is only... Then, when `abiha hadha al-aql al-sharif` (this noble intellect knew)... When this `aql-e sharif` wanted to know him, meaning the `mabda'-e ta'ala` (the Exalted Originator), he tried to recognize him. So, `abiha ithnan min tilka al-ashbah al-suwariyyah` (two of those formal phantoms knew)... so... they moved forward to know from those `ashbah-e suwariyyah` (formal phantoms)... `wa huma al-mu'arrab 'anhuma bil-munba'ithayn al-awwalayn` (and they are the two referred to as the first two `munba'ithayn` [emanations/emitted ones]). And who are those two? Those `ashbah-e nuraniyyah` (luminous phantoms)... They were given a name, were defined, by `munba'ithayn al-awwalayn`. So `munba'ith` is because `alif` is the `asl harf` (original letter). From `munba'ith`, what emerges? `Laam` and `Fa`. So they are called `munba'ithayn`. `Alif` is written as `alif`, and it is read as `alif`, `laam`, `fa`. It is read... This is called `munba'ith`. `Munba'ith`. So here, from that `aql-e sharif`... what is opposite `alif`, two—`laam` and `fa`—emerged. `Munba'ithayn al-awwalayn`. Such `munba'ithayn` that are called `awwalayn` (the first two)... those who emerged... who first emerged. By seeing... they moved forward. By seeing it, they moved forward. It could also be that these `munba'ithayn` were close to the `aql-e awwal` and they saw it, whereas the others could not see it. Some... something like that... It was the realm of `ikhtiyar` (volition). There was no... `la 'a'iqa fi dhalika al-tiraz al-'aali` (there is no obstacle in that high plane). In that realm, there was no barrier of time and space. Everyone could see the other's gaze. So in that realm, when the `aql-e sharif` first gazed upon the `mabda'-e ta'ala`, then two `ashbah-e suwariyyah` saw its... his noble gaze. The noble gaze of that `aql-e awwal`. So its `hay'at` (form/state) had already been established... the `aql-e awwal`'s... Yes, the form of `aql-e awwal` had been established. `Wa huma al-mu'arrab 'anhuma bil-munba'ithayn al-awwalayn.` And those two `ashbah-e suwariyyah` were defined... those two were defined by `munba'ithayn al-awwalayn`. `Sabaqa ahaduhuma al-akhar.` (One of them preceded the other). One of them advanced ahead of the other. Although they emerged at the same time. `Fa-nazara bi-dhatihi ila dhatihi wa ila abna'i jinsihi kama nazara al-awwal.` (So he looked with his essence at his essence and at the sons of his kind, just as the first one had looked). He looked with his own `dhat` (essence)... Looked from his own `dhat` towards his own `dhat` and towards his `abna'-e jins` (members of his kind), just as the `awwal` (first one) had gazed. Meaning, he did it in the same way that `aql-e awwal` had gazed. `Fa-'alima anna lahu wa lahum mubdi'an bi-khilafihim. Fa-nafa 'an dhatihi wa 'anhum al-ilahiyyah, wa athbataha lahu ta'ala.` (So he knew that for him and for them there is an originator, unlike them. So he negated divinity from his own essence and from them, and affirmed it for Him, the Exalted). So when he knew that for him and for all the `abna'-e jins` there is a creator, unlike them... So... `alimaani`... No, `alima`. `Alimaani`? No, `alima`. `Alimaani`? No, `alima`, singular. `Alima`. One person knew. One... only one knew. Yes, only one knew. The `munba'ith-e awwal` did not know. So that `munba'ith`... of the two `munba'ith`, the one who is `munba'ith-e awwal` knew that for them... for himself and for all of them... there is a `mabda` (originator) who is a creator, unlike them. The same words are used that were used for `aql-e awwal`. `Fa-nafa 'an dhatihi wa 'anhum...` From his own `dhat`, he negated... And from them, from all of them, he negated `ilahiyyat` (divinity). And he affirmed it for Allah `Azza wa Jalla`, for the `mabda'-e ta'ala`. This `ilahiyyat`... the `dhat`... meaning, `ilahiyyat` means what here? The power to create. The power to create. The existence of the `dhat`. Was the `sabaqiyat` (precedence) in... `hiddat` (sharpness/intensity) or in... `jahat` (direction)? Difference of gaze. `Farq-e nazar` (difference of gaze). Okay. `Farq-e nazar`. The greatest... crime that was established on `aql-e thani` (the second intellect), on `aql-e thalith` (the third intellect), who is the `ashir` (the tenth), was the delusion of equality (`wahm-e masawat`). That he said, "We both are one." So from this, this deduction is made, it becomes clear from this, that both did not emanate at the same time. One came forth earlier, and one came forth later. No, no... Where... In your text, it is not mentioned anywhere that they emanated at the same time. `Al-munba'ithayn al-awwalayn`. Both emerged at the same time. `Sabaqa ahaduhuma al-akhar`. No, `sabaqiyat` is in its own place... but both emerged together. That's what I am saying. Both emerged together. They emanated together... The gaze was different. Because if both emerged together and both of you... this... the concept of `masawat` (equality) came because he recognized the `aql-e awwal`, and this one also recognized the `aql-e awwal`. This one negated, and that one also negated. Both are together. But he did not acknowledge his own... the `aql-e thani`'s... who is called `munba'ith-e awwal`'s... `sabaqiyat`. So if they emerged together, there cannot be a `sabiq` (predecessor). They emerged together. Previously, it has been explained that the gaze of one was the `nazar-e ashraf` (the more noble gaze), and the gaze of one was the `nazar-e adna` (the lower gaze). Before their emanation, two gazes of the `aql-e awwal` had been established. It has been explained previously. Two gazes were established: `nazar-e ashraf` and `nazar-e adna`. `Nazar-e ashraf`... its... the `aql-e awwal` performed `tawhid`, `tanzih`, and `tajrid` (affirmation of unity, transcendence, and abstraction). Because of that, a luminosity was attained by it. A joy... a luminous joy. What was the second thing? When the `aql-e awwal` saw that in the entire cosmos, no person had advanced ahead of it... it is the first to see, to gaze, to affirm the `tawhid` and `tanzih` of God. It is the `aql-e awwal`. So it attained a joy of `awwaliyyat` (firstness). That was the `nazar-e adna`. It has been explained. One is `nazar-e awwal`, one is `nazar-e ashraf`, one is `nazar-e adna`. The gaze of the `munba'ith-e awwal` was towards the `nazar-e ashraf`. The gaze of the `munba'ith-e thani` was towards the `nazar-e adna`. But he understood that since we both advanced together, therefore our gazes are equal (`musawi`). This he understood. That is called `tawahhum` (delusion)... `tawahhum-e masawat`. This has been explained in, I think, either here or in another book. Here, it is explained in this way. So, that `munba'ith-e awwal` knew that for himself and for all those `abna'-e jins`, there is a creator, unlike them. So he negated from his own `dhat` and from all of them... from all the `abna'-e jins`, he negated `ilahiyyat` (divinity) and affirmed `ilahiyyat` for him, for Allah `Azza wa Jalla`. For the `mabda'-e ta'ala`. `Wa sabbaha al-aql al-awwal wa qaddasahu wa tanzih wa tajrid, idh kana sabiqan 'alayhi il-tawhid al-mubdi'i wa tanzih wa tajrid.` (And he glorified the First Intellect and sanctified it with abstraction and transcendence, since it had preceded him to the tawhid of the Originator, and to transcendence and abstraction). Because `aql-e awwal` had preceded him... in its `tawhid`... in the `tawhid` of the `mabda`, in `tanzih`, in `tajrid`. `Wa i'tarafa bi-sabqihi wa tawlihi wa sharafihi 'ala abna'i jinsihi wa fadlihi.` (And he acknowledged its precedence, its bounty, its nobility over the sons of its kind, and its virtue). And he acknowledged its `sabaqiyat`... and its bounty and its nobility over the `abna'-e jins` and its virtue... the virtue of `aql-e awwal`. `Fa-wasalat-hu mawadduhu wa barakatuhu.` (So its aids and blessings reached him). So at that time, he received from its side... from `aql-e awwal`'s side, `mawad` (substances/aids) and `barakat` (blessings), and `ta'yidat` (supports) and `lahazat` (glances)... `wa-ittasala bihi 'inda dhalika nurun ilahi.` (And he was connected with it at that time, a divine light). And he was connected with it... that `aql-e thani`... `munba'ith-e awwal`... with him, meaning, with `aql-e awwal`, the `nur-e ilahi` (divine light) was connected. From `la ilaha illallah`... What is it? `Nur-e sari` (pervading light)... `wa al-nur al-jari wa al-jud al-sari` (and the flowing light and the pervading generosity). From `la ilaha illallah`, `nur-e sari` is received, and `ilm-e jari` (flowing knowledge). So, this is also like a link of the `kalimah` (sacred formula), because `aql-e awwal` gets it from the `mabda'-e ta'ala`... This one got it from `ta'ala`. This one... was connected with it. He was connected with `aql-e awwal`. Yes. Bismillah. From the `kalimah` of `la ilaha illallah`, two things flow: `nur-e ilahi` (divine light) and `ilm-e jari` (flowing knowledge). `wa-ittasala bihi 'inda dhalika nurun ilahi wa al-'ilm al-ghayr al-mutanahi.` (And he was connected with it at that time, a divine light and infinite knowledge). And knowledge such that it has no end. The other one is there. `wa balagha biha al-kamal al-thani wa sara 'aqlan azaliyyan tamman kamilan ma'suman fadilan, la farqa baynahu wa bayna al-awwal illa bi-rutbat al-sabq.` (And through it he reached the second perfection, and became an eternal, perfect, complete, infallible, and excellent intellect, with no difference between him and the first except in the rank of precedence). And he became connected at that time... with him... the `nur-e ilahi` and infinite knowledge. So he reached... the `kamal-e thani` (second perfection) was attained. And he became, and he was... that, because of that, an intellect that was `azali` (eternal), `tamm` (perfect), `kamil` (complete), `ma'sum` (infallible), `fadil` (excellent). There is no difference between him and between the `awwal`... and between `aql-e awwal`, except for the rank of `sabaqiyat`. They are all brothers on thrones facing each other. He has attained `kamal-e thani`. In `kamal-e thani`, between `aql-e awwal` and `aql-e thani`, there is only one thing... `rutbat al-sabaqiyat` (the rank of precedence). `Illa bi-rutbat al-sabq`. So this `sabaqiyat` will also remain afterwards? Yes, it will always remain. Yes. The entire... void... `kamal-e thani`... There is no... there is no difference... The difference is only of `sabaqiyat`. Everything has been leveled, everything has been destroyed. All are seated on thrones. What is the difference? Of `sabaqiyat`. The one who came late, came with a delay... there is no... The matter is of coming early or late. Just as we have the concept that this is the realm of `ikhtiyar` (volition), and we can surpass our `mufid` (teacher/benefactor)... And... in this manner... but it's not like that there. Once the ranks are assigned, that's the rank. Here, as long as one is not in the `alam-e nurani` (luminous realm), then in `munba'ith` and other `karrat` (cycles), he has the `ikhtiyar` of `tadbir` (management/planning). If he planned... he can surpass his `mufid`. But not there. The seventh intellect cannot surpass the sixth intellect in any condition. Not in `kamal-e thani`. And no `da'irah` (circle/rank) can surpass another `da'irah`. In `kamal-e thani`. The pen has been lifted. The seventh is the seventh, the sixth is the sixth. The seventh... meaning, the sixth will advance, and the seventh will be behind it. The seventh cannot go to the fifth position, leaving the sixth behind. They are equal, one after the other. A lock has been put on it. `La farqa baynahu wa bayna al-awwal.` (There is no difference between him and the first). So here, there is `ikhtiyar`... to ascend over the `mufid`. This is in our state of `kamal-e awwal`. In `kamal-e thani`, there is no `ikhtiyar`. `Kamal-e awwal` is the state where the `mabda'-e ta'ala` created everyone equal. `La farqa baynahu wa bayna al-awwal illa bi-rutbat al-sabaqiyat, wa kawnahu inbi'athan wa al-awwal ibda'an, wa al-ibda'u la ka-al-inbi'ath.` (There is no difference between him and the first except in the rank of precedence, and his being an `inbi'ath` [emanation] while the first is an `ibda'` [origination], and `ibda'` is not like `inbi'ath`). And his being `inbi'ath`... `Aql-e awwal` is called `ibda'`, this is `inbi'ath`. And `inbi'ath` is one who advances by seeing it. This is the only difference. This difference remains. To advance on one's own is one state, and to advance by seeing someone else is another state. So, after `munba'ith-e thani` attains `kamal-e thani`... although they had fallen, they were `ashir`... but when he attains `kamal-e thani`, will he come third, or tenth... Tenth. Tenth. His contemplation is over. His thinking is finished. `Kama qala Sayyidna Hamiduddin...` But the one who is `ashir`... that is, the one who is `ashir` does not attain `kamal-e thani`. `Ashir` does not attain `kamal-e thani`. Because... that... `nurani kamal-e thani` is only attained by one in whom there is not even a speck of a stain. He must be completely white... completely luminous. If there is even a little... from which... he cannot attain `kamal-e thani`. This is the state. `Kama qala Sayyidna Hamiduddin a'la Allahu qudsahu fi Rahat al-Aql.` (As Sayyidna Hamiduddin, may Allah elevate his sanctity, said in Rahat al-Aql). Just as Sayyidna Hamiduddin said... may Allah Ta'ala sanctify your... elevate your soul... in `Rahat al-Aql`, in the book `Rahat al-Aql`. `Wa law kanat kayfiyyat al-ibda'i ka-kayfiyyat al-inbi'athi, la-kana al-ibda'u inbi'athan wa al-inbi'athu ibda'an.` (And if the modality of origination were like the modality of emanation, then origination would be emanation, and emanation would be origination). Although... the modality of `ibda'`... If it were... If it were. If the modality of `ibda'` were like the modality of `inbi'ath`, then `ibda'` would be `inbi'ath` and `inbi'ath` would be `ibda'`. There would be no difference between the two. This is an impossible matter. This thing is not so. The person who advanced on his own, his modality cannot be matched by anyone. And the person who advanced by seeing him, he will be after him. So, `aql-e awwal` is ahead in every way? In every way. There is no question. It is the `mazhar-e wahdat` (locus of unity). It is the `da'irah` of `ibtida` (beginning). `Li-anna al-aql al-awwal hajama bi-dhatihi 'ala tawhid mubdi'ihi wa tanzihhi wa tasbihihi wa taqdisihi, mubtadi'an dhalika min dhatihi li-dhatihi bi-dhatihi.` (Because the first intellect rushed with its essence upon the tawhid of its originator, its transcendence, its glorification, and its sanctification, beginning that from its essence, for its essence, with its essence). `min dhatihi bi-dhatihi li-dhatihi bi-dhatihi`. Because `aql-e awwal`... it rushed in its own essence... upon the `tawhid` of `mabda'-e ta'ala`, for `tanzih`, for `tasbih`, and for `taqdis`, beginning that... initiating that from its essence, for its essence, with its essence. From its essence. From its essence, for its essence, with its essence. From its essence. For its essence. With its own self. With its own self. It rushed to the `dhat` with the `dhat` for the `dhat`. `min ghayri awwalin taqaddama 'alayhi, wa la sabiqin sabaqahu ila dhalika al-fi'l.` (Without any first one preceding it, nor any predecessor preceding it to that act). Without any `awwal` that had advanced before it... in this state... and no predecessor who had preceded it to that act... `alladhi bihi sama 'ala abna'i jinsihi wa 'ala 'alihim.` (by which he was elevated above the sons of his kind and above them). That act... by which he was elevated above his `abna'-e jins`, and was elevated above all of them. `wa-istahaqqa jami' al-asma' al-sharifah allati lam takun li-ghayrihi.` (And he deserved all the noble names that were not for anyone other than him). And because of that, he became deserving of all the noble names that will not be for anyone other than him... `illa hu` (except for him). `wa hiya al-ibda'`. (And it is `al-ibda'` [the origination]). And what is that name? It is `ibda'`, `mubda'`. He is also called `ibda'`. He himself is called `ibda'`. Meaning, `aql-e awwal` will be called `ibda'`. `wa huwa al-mubda' al-awwal.` (And he is the first originated one). And he is the `mubda' al-awwal`. And he is the first created. `al-wujud wa al-mawjud al-awwal`. (The existence and the first existent). He is existence, and he is the first existent. If he were not there, no one would have seen and advanced, and there would be no `da'wah`, and then the matter of using `ikhtiyar` in this realm would not arise. So, except for the `mabda`, everything can be said. Because of his existence, he gazed, he performed the `tawhid` of God, and seeing him, people advanced, and after that, the `da'wah` began. The word `ibda'` whenever it comes, it will be only for `aql-e awwal`. `Ibda'` is only for `aql-e awwal`. `Ibda'` and `mubda' al-awwal`. `Mubda' al-awwal` means the first created. Existence and the first existent. `wa al-haqiqah wa al-haqq al-awwal.` (And the reality and the first truth). He is the reality, and he is the first truth. `wa al-wahdah wa al-wahid al-awwal.` (And the unity and the first one). He is unity, and he is the first one. `wa al-tamam wa al-tamm al-awwal.` (And the perfection and the first perfect one). He is perfection, and he is the first perfect one. `wa al-kamal wa al-kamil al-awwal.` (And the completeness and the first complete one). He is completeness, and he is the first complete one. `wa al-azal wa al-azali al-awwal.` (And the eternity and the first eternal one). He is eternity, and he is the first to... the first to be eternal. `wa al-aql wa al-'aqil al-awwal.` (And the intellect and the first intellective one). He is the intellect, and he is the first intellective one. `wa al-ilm wa al-'alim al-awwal.` (And the knowledge and the first knower). He is knowledge, and he is the first knower. `wa al-qudrah wa al-qadir al-awwal.` (And the power and the first powerful one). He is power, and he is the first powerful one. `wa al-hayat wa al-hayy al-awwal.` (And the life and the first living one). He is life, and he is the first living one. `wa al-sabq wa al-sabiq al-awwal.` (And the precedence and the first predecessor). He is precedence, and he is the first predecessor. `wa al-'ismah wa al-mu'tasim al-awwal.` (And the infallibility and the first infallible one). And he is your `ismah` (infallibility), chastity, and he is the first chaste and pious one. `wa mudahhir al-duhur wa al-dahr al-awwal.` (And the one who rolls out the ages, and the first age). He is... who rolls out the ages, and `al-dahr al-awwal`. He is the one who makes the eras, and he is the first era. `Al-fasl al-rabi' min al-bab al-thani min al-suradaq al-awwal.` (The fourth chapter from the second section of the first pavilion). `Duhur`. `Dahr`. `Duhur` means... `zamanah` (time/age). `Zamanah`. Zamanah means... All the `duhur` (ages) that were created after that, were created because of him. The management. The one who... `qabl` and `ba'd` (before and after) are also because of him. The issue of `azali` (eternal) also comes up. When you say `azali`, then it's like... This is something we cannot understand with our translations, because of the time factor. `Al-azal wa al-azali al-awwal.` That is `adam` (non-existence). Okay. It is `adam`, meaning non-existent. It comes into `wujud` (existence). `Al-fasl al-rabi' min al-bab al-thani min al-suradaq al-awwal.` (The fourth chapter from the second section of the first pavilion). The fourth chapter, from the second section, from the first... from the first pavilion. `Wa innama waqa'at 'alayhi hadhihi al-asma' al-sharifah li-ma'anin qama biha wahdahu, wa-khtassa biha duna ghayrihi siwa ism al-mubda'. Fa-qad jama'ahu dhalika huwa wa abna'u jinsihi.` (And indeed, these noble names fell upon him for meanings that he established alone, and he was specified with them apart from others, except for the name `al-mubda'`. For that name gathered him and the sons of his kind). And indeed, these noble names fell upon that `aql-e awwal` for meanings... for a special meaning, by virtue of which... He established it alone. He... established all the meanings in his own `dhat` (essence)... With his essence, he performed the `qiyam` (establishment). He performed the `qiyam`. And he was specified with it, apart from others. And he became specified... instead of other people, he himself became specified with all these meanings. Except for `ism al-mubda'` (the name of the originated one). Except for a single name, which is the word `mubda'`. The word `mubda'` encompasses all created beings. The one who has been created. All the `mubda'at` (created things) are included under it. Except for that, all the other names are specifically applicable to `aql-e awwal`. So the one we address in our prayers is him. Here, first it is given, `wa hiya al-ibda' wa al-mubda' al-awwal`. So the word `mubda' al-awwal`... `mubda'` is applicable to every one of them. `Fa-qad jama'ahu dhalika huwa wa abna'u jinsihi.` (For that name gathered him and the sons of his kind). So that name, `mubda'`, gathered him and his `abna'-e jins`. The entire cosmos was gathered. In this, `kamal-e awwal` and `kamal-e thani` are not specified, everyone came in. `Wa dhalika annahu waqa'a 'alayhi ism al-mubda' bi-hal wujudihi al-awwal huwa wa abna'u jinsihi 'an mubdi'ihim ta'ala, fa-'ammahum jami'an hadha al-ism.` (And that is because the name `al-mubda'` fell upon him in the state of his first existence, he and the sons of his kind, from their Originator, the Exalted. So this name included all of them). And indeed, the name `ism al-mubda'` fell upon that `aql-e awwal` in the state that his existence is the first. His and his `abna'-e jins`'s. From their `mabda'-e ta'ala`. His existence is the first. First... when he first came into existence. All of them came into existence together. He was the first one to come into existence. Because of his existence and the existence of all of them, the word `mubda'` applies to him, and it applies to all the `mubda'at` (originated beings). It applies to all of them. `fa-'ammahum jami'an hadha al-ism.` (So this name included all of them). So this name became applicable to all of them. `wa amma ism al-ibda' fa-khtassa bihi`. (But as for the name `ibda'`, he was specified with it). But as for the name `ibda'`, he was specified with it. It was not given to anyone else. `lamma hajama 'alayhi wa-btada'ahu min tawhid mubdi'ihi wa fi'lihi alladhi fa'alahu wa qama bihi duna abna'i jinsihi.` (when he rushed to it and initiated it from the `tawhid` of his originator and his act which he performed and established, apart from the sons of his kind). When he... he rushed towards it... meaning, towards the `dhat` of Allah `Azza wa Jalla`... the Lord... and he initiated from the `tawhid` of his `mabda`... and from that act which he performed... and he established it apart from all others. Because of that action, the name `ism al-ibda'` came to him. Just as some people are so pious (`muttaqi`) that they are called... he has piety (`taqwa`), but he is not a `muttaqi`. He has `kamil taqwa` (perfect piety). `Taqwa-e mujassam` (embodied piety). `Adil` (just)... `adl-e mujassam` (embodied justice). When someone becomes very just, he is called `adl-e mujassam`. In the same way, the name `ism al-ibda'` is upon him... `mubda'` applies to everyone, but `ibda'` is specifically for `aql-e awwal`.
