The one who creates attributes. `Ism al-ibda'`, meaning... `khalq-e ruhani` (spiritual creation)... that which... from where did it happen? It happened from him. From `aql-e awwal`. For this reason, it is called `ibda'`. `Wa ism al-mawjud bi-hal wujudihi huwa wa abna'u jinsihi min al-'adam.` (And the name of the existent in the state of his existence, he and the sons of his kind, from non-existence). The name... the name of existence... in the state of his existence, he and his `abna'-e jins`, from `adam` (non-existence). Existence is applicable to all of them. `Wa ism al-mawjud al-awwal li-kawnihi awwal mawjudin fi kamal al-thani.` (And the name of the first existent, because he is the first existent in the second perfection). And the first existent is specific to him, because he was the first to enter `kamal-e thani`. `Mawjud al-awwal` is said to him. Existence is for everyone, but `mawjud al-awwal` is only for him. `Wa ism al-haqiqah li-anna man intaha ila ma'rifatihi fa-qad balagha haqiqat al-ashya' al-mawjudah.` (And the name of the reality, because whoever reaches his gnosis has reached the reality of the existing things). And the name of `haqiqah`... is because... whoever reached his `ma'rifat`... has reached the reality of all existing things. That is, he has become `ilm-e kulli` (total knowledge). `Ilm-e kulli`. `Wa ism al-'alim al-awwal li-annahu awwal man ittasala bihi al-'ilm al-jari min Allah ta'ala.` (And the name of the first knower, because he is the first to be connected with the flowing knowledge from Allah, the Exalted). And the first knower he was called, because he was the first to be connected with the `ilm-e jari` (flowing knowledge) from Allah Ta'ala. `Ilm-e jari` and `nur-e sari` (pervading light). `Wa ism al-qudrah li-anna bi-muwalatihi wa tasbihihi wa taqdisihi iqtadara talihi 'ala bulugh ma balaghahu min al-kamal al-thani.` (And the name of power, because by his loyalty, his glorification, and his sanctification, his follower was empowered to reach what he had reached of the second perfection). And the name `qudrah` (power) was also applicable to him because... because of his `muwalat` (loyalty), his `tasbih` (glorification), his `taqdis` (sanctification), his follower... The follower is the `fa'il` (subject). Because his follower... his follower... was empowered... through his `muwalat`, his `tasbih`, his `taqdis`... to reach that which he had reached of `kamal-e thani`. So that means that all the total intellect, total power, total knowledge, he has encompassed it all. He has encompassed it. It is from his treasures that everyone receives. So he could also be expanding. The secrets of `mabda'-e ta'ala`, the bounties... he is attaining them. He is attaining them. You cannot say... the one who put his hand in the treasure chest of Jahangir, the reward he gives is a very easy task. In Surah Yasin, what is said? He is running in the `irfan` (gnosis) of the `kalimah`. He is running in the `irfan` of the `kalimah`. As much as he wants... in its splendor, in its greatness, there can be an increase. We cannot estimate it. So that means he is also in evolution. Yes, he must be. There should be. In his splendor, in his perfection, there is only an increase. So at any one instance, he cannot be a complete intellect, right? Because if he is expanding, then obviously his intellect is also increasing, his power is also increasing. He does not have... falling is not an option for him, only rising is ahead. Only rising. For him, there is rising. Now you will say, how much will he rise? So that is `ilm al-ghayb` (knowledge of the unseen). You cannot estimate how much he will rise. Because the bounties of Allah are so many, bounties come one after another, and after that you say, "I have received so many bounties, they are finished," but no, they are not finished, then more bounties can come. There is no... limit to the bounties. He cannot be said to have received everything. If he has received everything, then it's the same thing, that you have limited... his... God's power. His bounties have been limited. It is mentioned... he attained it at that time. In that state, he attained it. Now... `Wa ism al-qadir al-awwal li-annahu awwal muqtadirin 'ala fi'lihi.` (And the name of the first powerful one, because he is the first one empowered over his act). And the name of `qadir al-awwal` was applied to him because he was the first to have power over his act which he performed. And because of that, he became powerful over whatever he willed. He became powerful over whatever he willed. `Wa ism al-hayat.` (And the name of life). And the name `hayat` was applied to him. `Li-kawnihim hayatan li-man dunahum min al-'awalim.` (Because they are a life for those below them of the worlds). Because he is life for those who are below him among the worlds. The realm of life is his doing. There is `ilm`, `hayat`, `qudrah`, all of it... The entire realm of `ilm`, `hayat`, `qudrah`... The entire `alam-e hayy`, `qadir`, `ruhani`... from which he bestowed life. The `aql-e awwal`. The things that were given in `kamal-e awwal`, `ilm`, `hayat`, `qudrah`, all those words are also being applied to him. `Wa ism al-hayy al-awwal li-kawnihim awwal man ittasala bihi ruh al-hayat al-haqiqiyyah, fa-ahyahu bil-hayat al-abadiyyah al-sarmadiyyah.` (And the name of the first living one, because they are the first to be connected with the spirit of true life, so He gave him life with the eternal and everlasting life). `Hayy`. `Hayy`. `Allahu la ilaha illa Huwa al-Hayy al-Qayyum`. `Hayyun`. `Hayyun Qayyum`. `Allahu la ilaha illa Huwa al-Hayy al-Qayyum`. `Huwa` is the `mabda'`. `Al-Hayy al-Qayyum`. `Hayy` is `mabda'`... `mabda'... `aql-e awwal`. `Qayyum` is `munba'ith-e awwal`. `Al-Hayy al-Qayyum`. And with `munba'ith-e awwal` are all the `kamal-e thani` that will be attained in the future. All of them will be with him... with `qayyum`. And with `hayy` is the station of `wahdat` (unity). The rank of `wahdat`. So all these attributes that `aql-e awwal` has are only because `kamal-e thani` was attained by him. He was the first to attain `kamal-e thani`. Okay, that's fine, but the thing is, the others who are coming, they are only coming because of... in the category of `kamal-e thani`... They are coming because of him. So it should apply to them too, right? The life that they actually received was because of `aql-e awwal`. If `aql-e awwal` had not acted in that realm, then what would have happened cannot be said. The example for this is that in the era of Muhammad, many `Imam`s would have passed who, in their own right, reached whatever ranks they reached. But because they are included in his `ummah` by seeing the Prophet, the Prophet's station is unique. `Wa ism al-hayy al-awwal li-kawnihim awwal man ittasala bihi ruh al-hayat al-haqiqiyyah.` (And the name of the first living one, because they are the first to be connected with the spirit of true life). And the name `hayy al-awwal` was applied to him because he was the first to be connected with the `ruh al-hayat al-haqiqiyyah` (spirit of true life). `fa-ahyahu bil-hayat al-abadiyyah al-sarmadiyyah.` (so He gave him life with the eternal and everlasting life). And that... He is the `Hayy`. The `ruh` (spirit) is `Hayy`. The `ruh` gave it life... that `ruh` gave life to him, to the `aql-e awwal`, with an eternal and everlasting life. He was given the `hayat-e abadi-e sarmadi`. `Wa ism al-sabq li-annahu nihayatan la yablughuha al-sabiqun wa la yantahi ilayha al-mu'ajjifun.` (And the name of precedence, because he is a limit that the predecessors do not reach and the hasty ones do not end at). And the name of `sabaqiyat` is also applicable to him, because he is a limit that no predecessor has reached, and no... hasty one has reached it. The ones who run fast. They... who run fast... they also cannot attain it. `Wa ism al-sabiq al-awwal li-sabqihi abna'a jinsihi ila ma sabaqa ilayhi min tawhid mubdi'ihi wa tanzihihi.` (And the name of the first predecessor, for his preceding the sons of his kind to that which he preceded to of the tawhid of his originator and its transcendence). And `sabiq al-awwal` is also for him because of his `sabaqiyat` over his `abna'-e jins` to that thing to which he preceded... from the `tawhid` of his `mabda` and its `tanzih`. `Wa ism al-'ismah.` (And the name of infallibility). And the name of `ismah` (infallibility/chastity) is also applicable to him because... `li-anna man iltazama bihi wa ata'ahu wa 'arafahu ya'tasimu min al-khata'i wa al-zalal.` (because whoever adheres to it and obeys it and knows it is protected from error and slipping). Because whoever adheres to it and obeys it and knows it... knows `aql-e awwal`... he becomes pure from error and slipping. `Wa ism al-mu'tasim al-awwal.` (And the name of the first infallible one). `Ismah` is there, and `mu'tasim al-awwal` is also there. He is the first pious one. Because... he was the first to be protected from error and slipping. With what was he protected? `bi-hablillah al-jari wa nurihi al-sari.` (with the flowing rope of God and His pervading light). With Allah's rope and His `nur-e sari`. With what was he protected? With the `kalimah`. He was protected with the `kalimah`. With the `nur` of `kalimah-e la ilaha`. Everything is in it. `bi-hablillah al-jari wa nurihi al-sari.` `Wa ism mudahhir al-duhur ay mufa''il al-fa'ilin.` (And the name of the one who rolls out the ages, meaning, the enabler of the doers). And his name `mudahhir al-duhur` was given, meaning... the one who also makes the doers do. The doers who do the `tawhid`, the one who brings them towards `tawhid`... he became the cause. The one who arranges. Yes. `wa muwahhid al-muwahhidin`. (And the unifier of the unifiers). And the one who also teaches `tawhid` to those who perform `tawhid`. `wa mu'azzil al-mu'azzilin`. (And the eternalizer of the eternalizers). And the one who also teaches eternity to those who are eternal. `li-anna al-duhur hum al-hudud al-'alawiyyah.` (because the ages are the higher hudud). Because the eras... they are, in reality, the `hudud al-'alawiyyah`. `wa huwa al-mumiddu lahum bil-nur al-ilahi.` (and he is the one who aids them with the divine light). And `aql-e awwal` is the one who helps them with `nur-e ilahiyyah`. `wa huwa al-muwahhid wa al-mu'azzil, wa hum al-muwahhidun wa al-mu'azzilun bima yuwasilun min barakatihi.` (and he is the unifier and the eternalizer, and they are the unifiers and eternalizers by what they receive of his blessings). And he is the `muwahhid` and the `mu'azzil`. And all of them... they are the ones who perform `tawhid` and attain eternity... by virtue of what... what he gives them... of blessings. What they receive... what they receive from his blessings. `wa yashmuluhum min sawari al-lahazati.` (and which includes them from the flowing of the glances). And that which includes them... it includes them... from his flowing glances. From the flowing of bounties. `fa-waqa'a 'alayhim ism al-duhur.` (so the name of the ages fell upon them). So the name `duhur` became applicable to all of them. These `hudud` are called `duhur`. And he is `mudahhir al-duhur`. The one who makes them. If he were not there, then no one would perform `tawhid` and `tanzih`. `Kama waqa'a 'ala al-hudud al-jismaniyyah ism al-a'wam wa al-sinin.` (Just as the name of years and eras fell upon the physical hudud). Just as on the `hudud jismaniyyah`, the names of years and different eras are given. `Wa ism al-dahr al-awwal li-annahu alladhi dahara dhatuhu.` (And the name of the first age, because he is the one who made his essence an age). And `dahr al-awwal` is also... applicable to `aql-e awwal` because he is the first one who... `dahara dhatuhu`, meaning, made his own essence an age. `ay azzalaha.` (meaning, he made it eternal). Meaning, he gave it eternity. `wa awjadaha 'ala al-wujud al-haqiqi, wa abqaha wa ayyadaha bi-fi'lihi alladhi fa'alahu.` (And he brought it into true existence, and made it endure, and supported it with his act which he performed). And he created his own essence with true existence, and he made it endure... and he supported it with his act which he performed. All these things that he is receiving are due to his own essence, or due to that light of the `kalimah` from which... The action he performed... he used his power... so the one who brought him forth is `mabda'-e ta'ala`. He used his own `ikhtiyar`. So that by seeing him, all were made. If he had not been made, then no one would have been able to be made. By seeing him, all were made. The one who praises is all praising the `aql-e awwal`. There is no mention of `Hu` there. There, it is all `mashghul bi-l-istifadah` (occupied with benefiting).

<!-- lecture 7 -->

That no one could become... by seeing which, all are made... The fifth chapter from the second section... Uh, the fifth chapter, from the second section, in *Sirat al-Awwal*, the third... *fa-ammal inbi'ath al-awwal, fa-kawnuhi kayfiyyatin ghayr kayfiyat al-ibda', fa-innahu lamma nazara ila al-'aql al-awwal, wa ma sara 'alayhi min al-'azmah wa al-'ula, wa al-jalal wa al-thana* (As for the first emanation, its state was a quality other than the quality of origination. For indeed when he looked towards the first intellect, and what came upon it of greatness and loftiness, and majesty and praise)... And when the first emanation (*inbi'ath al-awwal*) was, and its... and its quality was other than the quality of origination (*ibda'*)... *wa khafiya fi dhatihi anna dhalika bi-ma sabaqa ilayhi min al-fi'l, wa ikhtassa bihi min tawhid al-mubdi'i ta'ala wa tanzihuhu wa tasbihuhu wa taqdisuhu* (And it was hidden in his self that that was because of the action that preceded towards it, and he was specified with the *tawhid* [affirmation of unity] of the Originator, may He be exalted, and His *tanzih* [declaration of incomparability], and His *tasbih* [glorification], and His *taqdis* [sanctification])... *wa inba'atha dhalika fi dhatihi* (And that was emanated in his self)... And when the first emanation was, and its quality was other than the quality of origination, his... his quality was... other than the quality of origination (*ibda'*)... and when the quality of the first emanation was different... then he... So he contemplated that when he looked towards the first intellect, and what happened upon it of greatness and... *wa ma sara ilayhi* (and what came to it)... he reached... what reached him of greatness, of greatness and loftiness, and of majesty and praise, and praise... *waqa'a dhalika fi dhatihi* (that occurred in his self)... He contemplated that the thing that is established, that preceded towards it from the action (*fi'l*)... It was the first intellect... After that, this thought came to his mind, that this majesty and praise and greatness and loftiness that the first intellect has received, it has received it from that action of its own that it performed... *wa ikhtassa bihi* (and he was specified with it)... and... and he was specified... with that *tawhid* (affirmation of unity)... of the *Mubdi' ta'ala* (Originator, may He be exalted), and His *tanzih* (declaration of incomparability), and His *tasbih* (glorification), and His *taqdis* (sanctification). This thought came to his mind, that the *Mubdi' ta'ala*... the greatness he received was from that action, and from His *tawhid*, and from His *tanzih*, and His *tasbih*, and His *taqdis*, he attained this greatness and loftiness and majesty and praise... *wa inba'atha dhalika fi dhatihi* (and that was emanated in his self)... *wanba'atha... wanba'atha... wanba'atha*... the *nun* drops... *wanba'atha dhalika fi dhatihi* (and that emanated in his self). So that same thing emanated in his self... That thought came to his mind. *fa-qama bihi ka-qiyam al-awwal* (so he stood with it like the standing of the first)... so he stood... he did... like the standing of the first... like the standing of the first, he too acted. *mukhtafiyan lahu wa musta'imman bihi* (following him and taking him as an *Imam*)... the one who follows him, and the one who makes him an *Imam*... He made him an *Imam*... *ista'amma*... from *Imam*, what is it? *Ista'amma*... meaning he wanted to make him an *Imam*... He wanted to make him an *Imam*. He... the *munba'ith al-awwal*... *musta'imman*... *ista'amma*... *amma* means to lead as an *Imam*. *ista'amma* means to want to make someone an *Imam*. And *musta'imman*... *istif'al*... from the grammatical form *istif'al*. The meaning of *istifham*? What is the meaning of *fahima*? He understood. He understood... *Istifham* means to want to understand, to seek understanding. The meaning of *alif-sin* in Arabic is to seek, to desire... *wa qila 'alayhi al-munba'ith al-awwal, li-ma inba'atha 'indahu ma ibtada'ahu al-awwal* (And he was called 'the first emanation,' because there emanated within him that which the first had originated)... When he... when he emanated in his presence... in his presence... what the first had originated... What the first had originated (*ibtada'*)... what is *ibtada'*? To originate. What the first had done, the first intellect had done... that is, the *'aql al-awwal*, whatever thing it had first done, that same thing was emanated in him too. The only thing is that he did it after seeing... *wa hajama 'alayhi min dhatihi, la min ghayrin sabaqahu ilayhi* (And it assailed him from his own self, not from another that preceded him to it)... And he rushed towards it from his own self. It's not that the first intellect told him, or explained it to him, that's not the case. It came from his own self. The first intellect, it is from its own self... *dhatihi bi-dhatihi*... The *munba'ith al-awwal*, he rushed from his own self. Rushed meaning... he saw it, and after seeing it, this thought came to his mind. The word *min dhatihi* is there for the first intellect... the word *fi dhatihi* will not come... *min dhatihi... la min ghayrin sabaqahu ilayhi* (not from another who preceded him to it)... not from any other who was prior to him. It's not that someone told him or explained it to him... *wa la ista'amma* (and he did not take as an *Imam*)... *bi-siwahu* (anyone other than him)... And he did not make anyone an *Imam* other than him... *idh la yuqalu bu'itha shay'un illa ba'da wujudihi awwalan wa durusihi thumma wujudihi thaniyan... wa min dhalika ishtaqqa ba'th al-mawta 'inda jumhur al-khilqa fi qiyam yawm al-qiyamat al-kubra ba'd al-mawt* (For it is not said that a thing is 'sent forth' [*bu'itha*] except after its existence first and its effacement, then its existence a second time... and from this is derived *ba'th al-mawta* [the resurrection of the dead] according to the majority of creation, in the rising of the great Day of Judgment, after death)... When it is not said... It is said that... a thing was sent forth only after its existence first, and its effacement, then its second existence. A thing existed... what does that mean? There was an existence first... it was effaced by it... and its effacement... meaning, towards its being effaced. The listener asks for the meaning of *nazar*. Vision. His *tawhid*, *tanzih*, His... towards that. *Mubdi' ta'ala*... *wujudihi awwalan wa durusihi* (its existence first and its effacement). Its existence was first, and its effacement... So first, he... the *Mubda' ta'ala* (Originator, may He be exalted), he affirmed that, then after that he affirmed the superiority of the *'aql al-awwal* and making him an *Imam*. So there were two *tawhids* for him? No, he affirmed his precedence (*sabqiyyat*). That he preceded him... that he advanced ahead of me. In looking, this is the affirmation. The *tawhid*, which he did... he understood that he received this thing, greatness and loftiness, so he also performed the *tawhid*, *tanzih*, *tasbih* of Allah. After seeing his precedence. The listener asks for the meaning of "seeing". He knew. He saw the greatness he received... the radiance (*nuraniyyat*) he attained. He looked towards that... and its existence was... and its existence was a second... Its existence was first, then there is *durus*, then there is effacement... *ba'th* means... a person's existence is... then when he is put in the grave, from there his things are sent forth (*ba'th*)... they rise. First, existence, then *durus*, then existence. Then the second existence is called *ba'th*. First, existence (*wujud*)... creation. Then after that, *durus*... effacement. Then after that, *ba'th* from it. To be created and perish... *durus*... *thumma wujuduhu thaniyan* (then its existence a second time). Then its existence is a second time... The listener asks how *durus* applies to the *munba'ith al-awwal*. It means effaced... in what way? That the *'aql al-awwal*, for the perfections it possessed, its first perfection was attained. During that time when the *'aql al-awwal* performed *tawhid* and *tanzih*, the *munba'ith al-thani*'s was *durus*. It's *durus*. Meaning, it was like non-existent... Then his existence was a second time. And from that, *ba'th al-mawta* (resurrection of the dead) was derived... at the time of the rising of the great Day of Judgment after death. And from this, *ba'th* was derived... *wa inna al-ba'tha min al-qubur haqq* (and indeed the resurrection from the graves is true). *Ba'th*... So, whose resurrection from the graves will be? Those who... died. They existed first, they were in existence, then they entered *durus*... from *durus*, there will be *ba'th* again. This is called *ba'th*. And from that, *ba'th al-mawta* was derived... the rising of the dead at the time of the appearance... of the great Day of Judgment after death... So it was deserved that he be called the first emanation, because he was the first in that... in emanating, he was the first. *wa qila 'alayhi al-tali, li-ma kana taliyan li-l-'aql al-awwal, fi-ma qama bihi min al-fi'l* (And he was called 'the follower' [*al-tali*], because he was a follower of the first intellect, in that which he undertook of action)... And he was called the follower (*tali*), because he was the one who came after... after the first intellect, in that thing... in that thing in which he undertook the action... with it... that action which the first intellect did, he was the one who came after it. *wa kadhalika qawluhum al-'aql al-thani, li-makan al-thani li-l-awwal, fi-ma fi'lihi min al-tawhid wa al-tanzih wa al-tajrid* (And likewise their saying, 'the second intellect', because he was the second to the first, in that which he did of *tawhid*, *tanzih*, and *tajrid*). And similarly, in their statement... in their statement, the second intellect... The *munba'ith al-awwal* is also called the second intellect. The pronoun in *qawluhum* (their statement)? To whom... In reference to whom... Likewise the statement of... Who is it? What is said about him... The statement of people... The second intellect... the second intellect, because he was the second... after the first, in that thing in which he did *tawhid*, *tanzih*, and *tajrid*. *wa qila 'alayhi al-lawh, li-makanuhu matrahan li-shu'a' al-qalam, alladhi huwa al-'aql al-awwal* (And he was called 'the tablet' [*al-lawh*], because his place was a receptacle for the rays of 'the pen' [*al-qalam*], which is the first intellect). And the *munba'ith al-awwal* was called the tablet (*lawh*), because his place became a receptacle for the rays of the pen, and that pen is the first intellect. The pen is the first intellect, and it became a tablet (*lawh*). Just as it is written on a tablet with a pen... with the lights of the first intellect, it was written on its tablet. The tablet is the *munba'ith al-awwal*. The *munba'ith al-awwal*. *wa qila 'alayhi al-nafs al-kulliyya, li-ma kana anfas 'alamahu wa ashraf mawjudat al-awwal, wa sara kullan lahum wa ilayhi intihahum* (And he was called 'the universal soul' [*al-nafs al-kulliyya*], because he was the most precious in his world and the noblest of the existents after the first, and he became a 'whole' [*kull*] for them, and to him is their end). And... he is called... the *munba'ith al-awwal* is called the universal soul (*nafs al-kulliyya*), because he was the most precious... the most precious... in that world, and the noblest of existents after the first. So he became... he... the *munba'ith al-thani*... the *munba'ith al-awwal*... became the *munba'ith al-awwal*, a whole (*kull*) for them. A whole for them... he became... for all of them. And to him is their end. And towards the *munba'ith al-awwal* is the end of all of them. Is it to the whole? The end of all the intellects is towards the *munba'ith al-awwal*. Not towards the first intellect? Yes. The first intellect is in the circle of unity. The *jannat* (paradise) for all is what? *Jannat al-ma'wa 'inda sidrat al-muntaha* (The Garden of Abode, near the Lote-tree of the Farthest Boundary). *Jannat al-ma'wa*, its station is the *munba'ith al-awwal*. *Sidrat al-muntaha* is the self of the first intellect. Where is *Jannat al-ma'wa*? It is near *sidrat al-muntaha*. The *munba'ith al-awwal* is the closest to the first intellect. And where does everyone have to reach? To the *jannat al-ma'wa* of the *munba'ith al-awwal*. So that is the final station, for our end? No one can attain *sidrat al-muntaha* except the *'aql al-awwal*. Because he affirmed from his own self, while these others did it by seeing. So his rank is higher. The *munba'ith al-awwal* also did it from his own self? With precedence (*sabqiyyat*)... The *munba'ith al-thani* also did it from his own self... he did it from his own self. The *munba'ith al-thani* also did it from his own self. The *munba'ith al-awwal* also did it from his own self... he performed the *tawhid*, *tanzih*, and *tajrid* of Allah, and he acknowledged the precedence of the *'aql al-awwal*. But he did not acknowledge the precedence. He said that my vision and his vision are equal. There is no difference in that. This was his claim... this was his view, which stopped his rank. It's not that he was demoted. He could not attain the rank, the second perfection (*kamal al-thani*). For *kamal al-thani*, there should not be any blemish. Not even the slightest lowness in vision should be there for *kamal al-thani*. Because his mind had the darkness of equality (*masawat*), he could not attain *kamal al-thani*. And during that time, seven intellects advanced through the *da'wah*. The listener asks a question about the sequence... *Wujud*, *durus*, and *ba'th*... The *'aql al-awwal*'s existence happened, at that time the *durus* belonged to whose? The *munba'ith al-awwal*. Meaning, they were watching him... And that world is such that there is no time or space that we can understand. It's just a matter of before and after. *thumma inna al-inbi'ath al-thani... al-bab al-thalith min sirat al-awwal, yajma'u khams fusul, al-fasl al-awwal minha* (Then indeed the second emanation... the third section from *Sirat al-Awwal*, it gathers five chapters, the first chapter among them)... the third section from *Sirat al-Awwal*, it gathers... it gathers five chapters. And the first chapter from it is... *thumma inna al-inbi'ath al-thani... inba'atha fi dhatihi, ma inba'atha fi dhat al-awwal* (Then indeed the second emanation... was emanated in his self, what was emanated in the self of the first)... the first emanation (*inbi'ath al-awwal*)... Now look at the difference between the two. Then indeed the second emanation... emanated... in his self... what emanated in the self... of the first emanation. In the first emanation... there is no difference in this regard. What was in him, was also in him. *wa nazara ka-ma nazara* (and he looked just as he had looked)... He looked just as the first emanation had looked... His vision was the same as the first emanation's. *wa nafa 'anhu al-ilahiyya la ibda'an min jinsihi* (and he negated divinity from himself, not as an origination from his own kind)... And he negated... from his own self... The word *'anhu* means from his own self... divinity. *La ilaha* (There is no god)... He also said *La ilaha illa Allah* (There is no god but Allah). There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah... And he negated divinity from his own self... and from his kind... *ka-ma nafa* (just as he negated)... just as the first emanation had negated it... The first emanation negated it, just as the second emanation negated it. *wa athbataha li-mubdi'ihi ta'ala wa takabbara ka-ma athbata* (and he affirmed it for his Originator, may He be exalted, and magnified Him, just as he had affirmed). And he established it... and he established that for his *Mubdi' ta'ala* (Originator, may He be exalted) and for his magnification... Divinity... *izzat-o-zawal* (honor and decline)... is only for Him. *ka-ma athbata* (just as he had affirmed)... just as the first emanation had established it. *wa sabbaha al-'aql al-awwal wa qaddasahu wa...* (and he glorified the first intellect and sanctified it and...)... He performed the *tasbih* of the first intellect and its *taqdis*. *ka-ma sabbaha wa qaddasa* (just as he had glorified and sanctified)... just as he had performed *tasbih*, and he had performed *taqdis*. The word... is missing. *qaddasahu*... the word is not there. The word for *qaddasahu* is not there. *sabbaha al-'aql al-awwal wa qaddasa*... After *qaddasa*, then... *wa takhatta'ahu* (and he transgressed against him)... That is, he made a mistake concerning him... He made a mistake towards the *'alam*. He did not glorify... he did not perform the *tasbih* of the first emanation and he did not perform its *taqdis*. *wa lam ya'tarif bi-fadlihi 'alayhi wa sabqihi lahu* (and he did not acknowledge his virtue over him and his precedence to him)... And he did not acknowledge... he did not acknowledge his virtue... the virtue of the first emanation over him, and his precedence to him... his precedence over him... *bal takhatta'ahu wa zanna annahu wa iyyahu fi halin mutamathila wa musawat wa mushakila* (Rather, he transgressed against him and thought that he and him were in a similar, equal, and alike state). Rather, he made a mistake and was ignorant and he thought that... that he and him... he himself and the first emanation, are in a similar, equal, and alike state... they are equal. *fa-kana dhalika minhu zallatan wa khati'ah* (So that was a slip and a sin from him). So it became... it became... from him... a slip... a slip and a sin. In Arabic, there are two, three letters that come... four letters. *Zalla*, if it comes with *zal*, what does it mean? He was abased. If it comes with *zay*? He slipped. He slipped. And if it comes with *dwad*? A shadow was cast... the meaning of *dwad*, *dalla*, is he went astray... and if it comes with *zwa*? A shadow was cast... *zalla... zalla, dalla, zalla*. This... a sort of law is being formed here, that you... your predecessors, you must acknowledge them and their... their precedence. The precedence of vision... his vision was higher, his vision was lower. But now when... we who are coming behind, who... before us... countless beings have already passed. So for us too, it is... necessary to acknowledge all of them? The one who sees the reality (*haqiqat*)... that what is the reality... what should we do? What are its principles? The one who sees the principles and acts, his vision is noble (*ashraf*). And the one who sees the branches (*furu'*), his vision is lower (*adna*). And the one with the noble vision, who sees the origin, he becomes lofty. And the one who sees the branches, he becomes lower. No, my question was that... in your chain of precedence, all those who are there... in the chain... all of them, whether you know them or not, whether you do not know them... so all of those people must be acknowledged, their precedence and their loftiness must be accepted by you. That is the reality. To know the reality... that this vision is noble, it is higher than this. The vision is noble... But how do we know who preceded us? For you to know, here you have the impediments of space and time, obstacles. That world is such, the world of lights, there were no obstacles. The obstacle was not there, that it would take time to know. The obstacle... it was clear. But he said that since both of us came into being together, therefore, we are both equal. But the obstacle was not there. The difference in vision was there. He understood that there was a difference in vision, yet he said that we are equal. He understood the difference in vision, and after understanding, he still said that since we came into being at the same time... we performed the *tawhid*, *tanzih* of Allah, we acknowledged the *'aql al-awwal*, in this we both advanced together, therefore we are equal. Although that difference of vision that was there, it is a very high difference, he did not accept that. And I mean the second emanation (*inbi'ath al-thani*). I am not referring to him as a denier, the second emanation... As the *munba'ith al-awwal* had a nobler vision, the confirmations (*ta'yidat*) and bounties (*mawaddat*) from the *'aql al-awwal* became directed towards him. He did not acknowledge this... so the bounties, confirmations, and blessings were not directed towards him. And he did not attain the second perfection (*kamal al-thani*). Apparently, for example, if we also... take our own examples, that Maulana, you will give a lecture (*majlis*). In your lecture, your voice was very good, if someone came and said that, so how much can your attention be on that? And if someone... drew your attention to your scholarly points... to your scholarship... then naturally your attention will be more towards that. The one who sees the real thing... that thing... For example, we eat food. The food that is for the sake of heavenly reward (*thawab*), and... "well, the community is... we should eat with the community." One says, "For the sake of *thawab*... that Allah may give *thawab*." There is a very big difference between the two. The difference is in intentions. The difference in intentions and... "It's a custom, we have to host them..." That's it. It's not that we should seek *thawab*. So the difference in intention that occurs... *fa-inqata'at mawaddat al-inbi'ath al-awwal 'anhu wa lahazatuhu wa ta'yidatuhu wa barakatuhu* (So the bounties of the first emanation were cut off from him, and its glances, and its confirmations, and its blessings). So they were cut off... the bounties... from the first emanation... from it. From it, meaning... from the *munba'ith al-awwal*... From the second emanation... and its glances and its confirmations... The pronoun in *'anhu* refers to the *munba'ith al-awwal* or the *'aql al-awwal*? *fanqata'at mawaddat al-inbi'ath al-awwal 'anhu* (the bounties of the first emanation were cut off from him). They were cut off from the second emanation. The pronoun in *'anhu* refers to the first emanation or the second emanation? They were cut off from the second emanation. The confirmations from the first emanation were cut off from the *munba'ith al-thani*. The confirmations... the one with the nobler vision, the confirmations, all of them... because he understood the reality. That the *'aql al-awwal*'s... precedence, why did it happen? *Munba'ith al-awwal* knew the correct way... for this reason it happened, so I should also... The second emanation did not see that. The second emanation saw that... he has superiority over all these people, he only saw that. He saw that... I need to do the main thing, which is *tawhid*, *tanzih*, *tajrid*. This is the main thing. And from this, I can attain radiance. Looking at the superiority over those below will not give me... rather, this action is such that by doing this action, I will attain the second perfection. He had this thought. The second emanation did not see this. He also performed the same action, he also performed the same action. The difference is in the vision. The reality of his vision was not there. For the second emanation. So as soon as the reality... he... both emanated, so the *munba'ith al-awwal*, because he understood the correct thing, confirmations started coming to him from the *'aql al-awwal*. And the *munba'ith al-thani*... the confirmations to him did not... So the *munba'ith al-awwal* stopped his confirmations. Because he had not attained the second perfection. *fanqata'at*... so they were cut off, the confirmations of the first emanation from him, that is, from the second emanation... The confirmations would have reached him, if... Yes, if the first emanation... if he hadn't made the claim of equality, then the confirmations from the *'aql al-awwal* would have reached the second emanation? They would have. Yes, they would have. The *'aql al-awwal* designated confirmations for the one who understood the reality. He did not understand the reality. This is a difference based on the same action. For example, two people are eating. The difference in intentions is there... The second emanation understood that the *'aql al-awwal* attained greatness for this reason, that he attained superiority over the entire world. And he understood, the *munba'ith al-awwal* said, that I... the *'aql al-awwal* attained it for this reason, that he performed *tawhid*, *tanzih*, and *tajrid*. I too, by performing *tawhid*, *tanzih*, and *tajrid*, can attain this state, the second perfection. This is the difference. When a person does any work, the core purpose, why he must do it, that should be the focus of his vision. He shouldn't look at the particulars, this is the reality. Both... both advanced together, did both attain the second perfection or not? No, no. The second perfection was attained only by the *munba'ith al-awwal*. The criterion for attaining the second perfection is that you... and on the *'aql al-awwal*... The *tahmid* and *taqdis* of the *'aql al-awwal*... and attain that purpose for which you perform the *tawhid*, *tanzih*, and *tajrid* of Allah. But this... the problem was between the visions of both... between the first and the second emanation. But the confirmation... it should have come from the first intellect, because he... The one with the nobler vision... he saw the core reality. The *munba'ith al-awwal* saw the core reality, that's why the confirmations from the *'aql al-awwal* reached him. And the second emanation... for the second perfection, there should not be any blemish at all. Whatever action is done, it must be for the sake of Allah. That thing was not there in the vision of the second emanation. He saw what? He saw that the *'aql al-awwal* has advanced beyond all... all the worlds. He only saw that. This is the difference. As I have explained... a person comes, comes to prayer in the morning. After coming, he sees that... why does he come? The core purpose is... the command of Allah, he should obey it, and... through prayer, he should rise. When he comes here, he sees that he is the first one to arrive. So he feels happy about his precedence... two visions are created, two joys... they are called two joys (*masarratayn*). One joy is from the worship of God, the second joy is from superiority over all the attendees. Two joys... The listener continues... "The first joy is what he... his intention was... that is the core joy." Yes. "But if another person comes with him, who is walking with him, his first joy will still remain." He comes for this reason, that "I should be among the first to arrive," not for the sake of prayer. This is the real issue. It could be that his heart has this flaw... He does not come for the sake of prayer. This can happen. In that realm, it was the same difference of vision. The vision of the *munba'ith al-awwal* was on the higher joy (*masarrat al-'ala*), which is the core reality. The vision of the *munba'ith al-thani* was on the lower joy (*masarrat al-adna*). And despite his vision being on the lower one, he still claimed equality. He did not properly consider the difference between the higher and lower vision. *fa-inqata'at mawaddat al-inbi'ath al-awwal 'anhu wa lahazatuhu wa ta'yidatuhu wa barakatuhu* (So the bounties of the first emanation were cut off from him, and its glances, and its confirmations, and its blessings)... and so he was darkened and made ignorant of his rank... his image... and he became proud... of his rank, and he fell from his rank. And he became distant... the *munba'ith al-awwal*'s rank... from the rank of the *munba'ith al-thani*. *idh huwa hadd al-qarib ilayhi* (for he is the limit of the one close to him)... He is the limit... of the *munba'ith al-thani*... his high limit, who is the one close to him... *al-shahid 'alayhi* (the witness over him)... the witness... the one witnessing him... *al-muthab bihi* (the one rewarded by him)... the one who gives reward... *al-mu'aqab bi-sababih* (the one punished because of him)... the one who gives punishment because of him... So he knows that darkness has come upon him, upon the *munba'ith al-thani*, and that he has... sinned... He felt this after the obstacles... after the *da'wah*. In the beginning, he didn't even know that I'm not getting the second perfection, this isn't happening... He acknowledged after the seven intellects advanced past him and countless individuals advanced past him, then he understood that all these people have attained this radiance, why haven't I attained it? So, if a person doesn't know and commits a sin, then the darkness upon him... He had a delusion... He did not attain the second perfection. For attaining the second perfection, there must be complete purity. There should not be any blemish. The vision must be... it must be that "what is the core reality?" he should know that. For whom does a person work? He should know that. *al-fasl al-thani min al-bab al-thalith min sirat al-awwal... thumma inna al-'aql al-awwal ittahada bi-l-inbi'ath al-awwal, wa ittakhadhahu lahu hijaban wa ila ta'atihi wa ta'at mubdi'ihi baban* (The second chapter from the third section of *Sirat al-Awwal*... Then indeed the first intellect united with the first emanation, and took him as a veil for himself, and to his obedience and the obedience of his Originator, a gate). And he took him as a veil for himself, and towards his obedience and the obedience of his Originator, a gate. He made him a gate... So a veil was made for the first intellect. And towards his obedience and the obedience of his Originator, a gate. A gate. Here, it is not a literal gate... just as here... there are chapters of *fiqh*... and chapters of logic. They are called sections. One, people advance through *da'wah*. And one, people advance by seeing. By seeing. They are called gates. Like the *munba'ith al-awwal*. The *Imam* is opposite the *'aql al-awwal*, and the *bab* is opposite the *munba'ith*. Because in the world of intellects, he advanced by seeing him. After that, the apparent and hidden gates, they advance through *da'wah*. Just as it happened there, it happens here too. One advances on his own, the *Imam*, peace be upon him. What happened? He is at the station of the *'aql al-awwal*. What does that mean? He advanced on his own. Through whose... the *'ayn 'azima*'s... *da'wah*... towards *tawhid*. Who is the *Imam* of the *Imam*? The *'ayn 'azima*. Through the gnosis of the *'ayn 'azima*, he advanced on his own. The *bab*, the *bab al-inbi'ath*, who is he? *Inbi'ath* means... The *munba'ith al-awwal*. He is opposite the *bab al-inbi'ath*. He advanced by seeing the *Imam*. The third, the hidden gates... what are they? They advance through *da'wah*. Through *da'wah*. From it... *wa aqama al-da'wa fi dhalika al-'alam, fa-da'ahum minhu wa khatabahum bihi* (And he established the *da'wah* in that world, so he called them from him and addressed them through him). And he established the *da'wah* in that world... in that world. So he called them... all of them, towards him, and he addressed... he addressed through him. The *'aql al-awwal* established the *da'wah* in that world. So... the word *fa* is very specific. The *'aql al-awwal* established the *da'wah* in that world. So the *'aql al-awwal* called all of them through him... through the *munba'ith al-awwal*. Through the *munba'ith al-awwal*. The *da'wah* belongs to the *'aql al-awwal*, in that world. And he addressed them through him. And the *'aql al-awwal* addressed all of them through the *munba'ith al-awwal*. *fa-ajabuhu sab'at ashbahin suriyya* (So seven luminous phantoms responded to him). So they advanced... they accepted him... towards the *'aql al-awwal*... seven... seven luminous phantoms accepted him... *mutafawitun fi al-ijaba, wahidun ba'da wahid* (differing in their response, one after another)... and this is where the matter of before and after is... differing in their acceptance... one after another. *wa wahhada kull wahidin minhum mubdi'ahu wa nazzahahu wa i'tarafa bi-rububiyyat al-'aql al-awwal, wa sabqihi wa ta'ilihi wa rutbatihi, wa subbaha wa qaddasa haddahu, alladhi huwa waqifun bihi* (And each one of them affirmed the unity of his Originator and declared His incomparability, and acknowledged the lordship of the first intellect, and his precedence and his being a follower and his rank, and he glorified and sanctified his own limit, at which he was standing). So each one of them affirmed the unity of his own Originator, and declared His incomparability, and acknowledged the lordship of the *'aql al-awwal* and his precedence and his being a follower, and his rank... the rank of the *munba'ith al-awwal*. There is a *da'wah* of three here... one is of the *Mubda' ta'ala*, the *'aql al-awwal*, and the *tali*... And he praised him, and glorified and sanctified... his limit... which is his own station. He glorified and sanctified his own limit, at which he was standing. Why were there seven? Because Allah has placed seven *muqatta'at* (disconnected letters) in *La ilaha illa Allah*. Why did it end at seven? It could have been eight, nine, ten... Allah has made it so... What did the *Mubda' ta'ala* do? What is the *kalima* (word)? The *kalima* is... it is the *kalima* that is above the *'aql al-awwal*... Allah has placed everything in it... what was and what will be... Why did it have to be seven? Because there are seven *muqatta'at*. What is the meaning of *muqatta'at*? Where the tongue stops... the pen stops. A circle was drawn, then the circle ended. Another circle, a third circle, a fourth circle, a seventh circle... seven circles were made. Because Allah had decreed this in what? In *La ilaha illa Allah*, He had decreed it all. Meaning, where the *muqatta'at* are, that is the... end of a circle. *La ilaha illa Allah* comes first, and the circle is formed later. The circle... yes, Allah, in His knowledge... the knowledge He had, in it He decreed that seven circles will be formed. This was destiny. He placed the destiny in *La ilaha illa Allah*. Why were there seven circles? For this reason. Meaning, the *'aql al-awwal* also... his... everything was, like, destiny was made. Before that. The *'aql al-awwal*... Allah, the *Mubda' ta'ala*, had decreed the destiny, that seven circles will be formed, so He put *La ilaha illa Allah*... the *kalima*... *kalimatu... bayn al-mubdi' wa al-mubda' kalima* (the word is between the Originator and the originated). Between the Originator and the originated is the *kalima*. So, does that mean the choice given to beings was not absolute, in a way? In destiny... he had absolute choice in that. But regarding the seven, he did not have a choice. To advance on his own, he had absolute choice in that. But where it has to end... and after that, the turn of *'Ashir* (the Tenth) comes, that he should become the tenth... that was all his own choice. Choice also, of a person, is under the choice of the one who gives the choice. He can exercise his choice in any way. But after so many souls, this one should come, that is a matter of Allah's choice. *alladhi huwa bi-'ashara sabiqat wa 'ashara taliyat* (who is with ten preceding and ten following)... and their praise became known. What is it? Each one of them acknowledged the limit of the one above him. The first of the seven, his acknowledgment... whose acknowledgment did he make? The second one acknowledged. The third one acknowledged the acknowledgment of the second one. The fourth one acknowledged the third... until the seventh intellect, what did it acknowledge? It acknowledged the first six, then it acknowledged the *munba'ith al-awwal*, it acknowledged the *'aql al-awwal*, it acknowledged the *Mubda' ta'ala*. And their praise became known, and their ranks rose... *wa ittasala bihim nur ilahi wa 'ilmun mutanahi, al-jari min al-'aql al-awwal ila al-'aql al-thani* (and a divine light and an endless knowledge connected to them, flowing from the first intellect to the second intellect). And a divine light connected to them, and an endless knowledge... What does he mean by divine light and endless knowledge? At the beginning, he stated... *nur la ilaha illa Allah* (the light of "there is no god but Allah"). He stated it in the beginning. What is the divine light? It is the flowing knowledge. The divine light is, and the flowing knowledge is... what is flowing from the first intellect to the second intellect... *mustamirrun ilayhim* (continuing towards them)... flowing towards them, towards those seven intellects. *wa bihi al-bulugh ila kamal al-thani* (and through it is the attainment of the second perfection)... By receiving it, the path towards the second perfection opens. The *munba'ith al-thani* did not attain the second perfection, why? Because the divine light and the endless knowledge did not reach him from the *'aql al-awwal*. Why did it not reach him? He did not know the reality. He acknowledged the reality of the *Mubda' ta'ala*, he acknowledged the *'aql al-awwal*, but the difference in the precedence of vision, he did not know that. This is the main point. For this reason, it did not reach him. And during that time, the *da'wah* took place. After the *da'wah*, seven advanced. *wa al-mahall al-'ali min al-dani* (and the high station from the low)... and the high station from the low... to the perfection... the high station from the low. *wa hadha huwa akhir qawl Sayyidna Hamiduddin 'alayhi al-salam, fi al-mashra' al-khamis min al-sirr al-rabi', min rahat al-'aql, faqala: a-la inna al-wujud 'an al-'aql al-awwal wa al-munba'ith al-awwal wa 'uqul sab'a* (And this is the end of the statement of Sayyidna Hamiduddin, peace be upon him, in the fifth spring of the fourth secret, from *Rahat al-'Aql*, so he said: Lo! Indeed, existence is from the first intellect and the first emanation and the seven intellects). He says, "Lo! Indeed, existence... existence is from the first intellect, and from the first emanation, and from the seven intellects"... The *munba'ith al-awwal* is the very first... after that, eight came into being. Nine came into being... and the tenth came into being. Later, the ones who came, they say... that there are eight bearers of the Throne (*hamalat al-'arsh*)... The eight bearers of the Throne. They don't even count the first intellect. What do they say? That... of *La ilaha illa Allah*, there are seven *muqatta'at* and *La ilaha illa Allah* itself. How many does that make? Eight. That's why they say. The later ones who came... *wa inna nur kull wahidin minhum...* (and indeed the light of each one of them...) *wujud kull wahidin minhum 'an al-akhir, siwa al-munba'ith al-awwal... 'an al-akhir* (the existence of each one of them is from the last, except for the first emanation... from the last). The existence of each one of them is from the last. What happened? In that world, when the first soul was created, then the first soul was commanded, "You perform the *da'wah*." The first soul... among the existing souls, the last one that was, it was commanded... the *da'wah*. From it, the *da'wah* started. The last of the existing souls. That circle was completed, he was commanded to perform the *da'wah*, so he performed the *da'wah*. From here, the circles started to be created. This... the seven intellects... seven intellects, each one has its own circle. So like... the second... the last individual of the second circle, is he greater than the third intellect, or... He performs the *da'wah* to him. So... they were cut off, and their connection was cut off. He was commanded to perform the *da'wah*. So if he is greater, then why didn't he become an intellect? When he... the 28th limit was reached... that circle of 28 was completed... so the 28th... after being 28, because *La ilaha*, the *Mubda' ta'ala* had decreed... that it has to be 28. After 28, or 40 places it is said... after 100... when they were completed, they were commanded, "You perform the *da'wah*." A new circle should be formed. A new circle should be formed. Then from it, the last individual of the circle forms a new circle. In this way. There is a center in the middle of the circle, which is the intellect... the seventh intellect, or the sixth intellect, or the fifth intellect, which is... the center of that circle. Its last... here it started... the compass was placed here... the compass, after going around like this, the compass came back here. When the compass... both... both met, he was commanded to perform the *da'wah*. What is said is, the center of the circle is the chief... And in it, in every circle, there are twelve chiefs (*ru'asa'*). Because the letters of *La ilaha illa Allah* are how many? Twelve. In every circle, there are twelve chiefs. The chiefs of the circle. *kull wahidin minhum sa'idan ila al-'aql al-awwal* (each one of them ascending towards the first intellect)... ascending towards the *munba'ith al-awwal*. *wa inna nur kull wahidin minhum sariyan fi-ma wujida 'an al-awwal min al-hayula wa al-sura* (and indeed the light of each one of them flows in that which was found from the first, of prime matter and form). And indeed, the light of each one of them is shining... shining... it is flowing in that thing... in that thing that was found from the first, and that is the prime matter (*hayula*) and the form (*sura*)... *Hayula* and *sura*. From *hayula*, that is, from the self, and from the form... from the form of the self, it has come into being. *yuridu bi-dhalika ithbat al-da'wat lahum wa ijabatahum lahu wahidan ba'da wahid* (he intends by that the establishment of the *da'wah* for them and their response to him, one after another)... He intends to establish... that he is establishing the *da'wah* for them and their accepting it, for him... for the *'aql al-awwal*... one after another. *ka-ma sabaqa min al-qawl, ila an balaghu kamal al-thani, alladhi bihi al-najat wa al-'isma wa al-fawz wa al-ni'ma* (as has been stated before, until they reached the second perfection, through which is salvation, infallibility, success, and bounty). Until they reached... your statement goes up to where? Until they reached the second perfection, such that through it is salvation, and there is infallibility (*'isma*), there is success, and there is bounty. After that, there is no decline. There is only ascent. And joy and bounty and its increase... That's all.

<!-- lecture 8 -->

...in *kulli shan*, *thumma huwa al-bāʻith al-awwal*, and *al-ghāyah al-ukhrā*. *Wa al-samaʻ al-muṭlaq*. Then, from them... yes, this one. From the beginning, read from the beginning. *Thumma innahu rashsha*. He then sprinkled...*rashsha ʻaqlan awwalan*. The First Intellect was sprinkled. *Nūr-e shāhshānī*. The luminous, kingly light. *Ilāhi*. Divine. *Ṭāhirah jiddan jiddan*. Extremely, extremely pure. Making *wujūdāt-e ibdāʻī* (the originated existents) just, *ʻādilan*, *baynahumā* (between them two) and *bayna sā'ir al-ʻuqūl* (between the other intellects). In the same way... *dālika bi-anna Natiq*. Then it came to *Natiq*... Allahu Akbar. From *Natiq*, *nūr-e shāhshānī* flowed towards *Asas*. *Ilāhi*. After reading this, after explaining this... *sāt* (*seven*). The seven. And after that, you should explain... seven have passed. After saying seven... then after explaining them...then the explanation...then it came to *Natiq*. From the *Natiq*, *nūr-e shāhshānī* came to the *Asas*, *ilāhi*. Whatever happened, happened. Now what can be done? In the same way, the *ḥudūd* (ranks)... yes, *ʻādilan*...*baynahumā*, and *bayna sā'ir al-ʻuqūl*. So... so after this... so *sā'ir*... *sā'ir al-ʻuqūl* also... so from the *Natiq*, *nūr-e shāhshānī* came to the *Asas*... with seven... So, from the previous discussion... from the previous discussion, this is what is understood. With the previous one... the previous one that was done... After that, seven... and the reference to seven was given. After that, this... that after that, *nūr-e shāhshānī*... that which happens between them, and between all the intellects. From your statement, this is what is understood. That... *wa ḥadd waḥdah*. *wa ilāhiyyat al-waḥdat*. So they became agitated, and upon seeing that place, they were confounded. They became confounded. After that... about him... and... they are all the same. They became confounded, perplexed, and amazed. And they prostrated. Prostrated. And... made their own selves the means and prostrated to His greatness. Prostrated. From the beginning of the *daʻwah* until the end... from Sayyidna Mu'ayyad al-Din... and... *al-mas'ūl fī kitāb-e mazkūr* (the one asked in the mentioned book). Where is the *kitāb-e mazkūr* (mentioned book)? From the beginning to the end, the reality is mentioned, and it is in his, the *Da'i's*, mention... The book *kitāb-e mazkūr*. Which *kitāb-e mazkūr* (mentioned book)? It is referring to *Rāḥat al-ʻAql*. So, he says that I... *ayna sa-aʻīduhā*. Where will I find the answer to this question? Where can this be found? *Mimman lā yaʻrifu*, from one who does not know. How can he give the answer? How can I... give the answer? Yes, *daʻī*, *dāʻin* (a caller). *Fī ḥijāb*. *dāʻiyan* (as a caller). That, I will go to him... so that he... the *daʻī* of the *awwal* (first) and the *ākhir* (last), and *dāʻī* of the *zāhir* (manifest) and *bāṭin* (esoteric). That is, *dāʻī* *fī ḥijāb*, the *daʻī* who is in a veil... *fī ḥijāb*. That *daʻī* who is in a veil... they became familiarized... became *maḥjūb* (veiled) and became *mānūs* (familiarized) with him.

It did not happen, nor was it skipped. The knowledge of the *Awwal* (First) and the *Thani* (Second) is obtained through *'aql* (intellect). The knowledge of the *Imam* is obtained through the knowledge of *ghaybah* (occultation), and it will be obtained with his command, his call, his summons. From that, he will be considered as one upon whom... is a great *ni'mah* (blessing). And it is a *ni'mah* whose name is *al-ghaybah*. And through that, the matter of the *ghaybah* occurred, so it was bestowed upon him that all the rights related to *ghaybah* were given. He is doing the *zikr* (mention). So at that time, all this... *zikr* of *ghaybah*... *wa 'l-faraj 'an Awliya'ika wa 'l-muminina min Ibadika* (and relief for Your friends and the believers from among Your servants). *'alayhis salam*... as He informed them in the Book from the *Imam al-Muminin* (Leader of the Faithful), the Qur'an al-Karim, and His, the Exalted's, statement: *shahida Allahu annahu la ilaha illa Huwa wa 'l-mala'ikatu wa ulu 'l-'ilm* (Allah witnesses that there is no deity except Him, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge). As the Qur'an al-Karim, the Exalted, has given news about it. Allah, the Exalted... *shahida Allahu* (Allah witnessed). Allah has given *gawahi* (witness) that there is no *ma'bud* (one who is worshipped) except Him. So He also gives the *hukm* (judgment). *wa 'l-mala'ikah* (and the angels). The angels have given witness, and the *sahiban-e-'ilm* (people of knowledge), the learned, have given witness. These three people give witness: Allah, the angels, and the people of knowledge. *wa huwa shahid... shahid 'ala ma ya'tihi 'ani 'l-Imam 'alayhis salam... bismillah* (and he is a witness... a witness to what comes to him from the Imam, upon him be peace... in the name of Allah). So he is a *gawah* (witness). So Allah Himself gives witness, and His witness is of a kind that... He gives... the claimant also. And because of that, the name of Allah occurred upon him. *innama huwa ka-ismika 'ala ismika, ism Allah* (It is but like Your name upon Your name, the name of Allah). And the name of Allah occurred upon him. Because of the meanings of *ghaybah*... *'inda...*. In the *ghaybah*, it is called *nur-e-shashani*. And the name that occurred is the name of Allah. At Allah's place, the one who is the *mu'min* (believer) in the *ghaybah*, regarding his rights near the *Ahl al-Bayt*, that is... from the *nur-e-shashani*... when he attains that state, he becomes *nur-e-shashani*. So he is the *Ahl al-Bayt*. After that, what does the *babu 'l-anwar* (chapter of lights) say? The chapter of *anwar* which is going on... after that, the seventeenth chapter. This is the matter of the *'aql* (intellect). This *riwayah* (narration), that when he believes in *la ilaha illa...* with that *'aql*. And he is a believer in it, yes... *ilahiyyatihi 'anhu... 'an nafsika wa 'an jinsika* (His divinity from him... from your self and from your kind). And he is the one who has certainty in His divinity from his own self, from his kind, from his race. Because of his intellect, because of His statement: *la ilaha illa Huwa shahidan bihi* (there is no deity except Him, being a witness to it). From his statement *la ilaha illa...* no... *la ilaha illa Huwa* (there is no deity except Him), with this statement, he proves that there is no deity except Him. He is the witness. In this... that...

...and *takabbur* [arrogance]. *Ishārah* [indication]. Yes, the *ishārah* is there. That is, it is towards the *mubdi'* [originator]. To indicate towards the *mubdi'*. The *mubdi'* is in that direction, this *ishārah* is towards that. Towards the *mubdi'*. He says, towards the *mubdi'*. *Ta'zīman wa tanzīhan* (for the sake of glorification and declaring transcendence). *Ta'zīm* and *tanzīh*. *Ta'zīman* is for the sake of *ta'zīm* [glorification], and *tanzīh* [declaring transcendence]. *Idh lā yakūnu 'alayhi ishārah* (since there can be no indication towards Him). Without the *Nabi* [Prophet] and without the *Wasi* [Successor]. He is *al-Mumaththal al-Awwal* [the First Representative]. Then what happens upon Him? No, it does not happen. Upon whom... upon whom does it happen? Towards the *mubda'* [originated being]. The *ishārah* towards the *mubdi'* is not possible. It is that the *ishārah* towards the *mubdi'*... no *ishārah*... no *ishārah* without the *Nabi* and *Wasi* is possible. Is that right? Yes, it is possible. And if he doesn't say this, then it is a mention against *Allāh ta'ālā* [God, the Exalted]. *Wal-malā'ikatu*. *Wal-malā'ikatu*... *Wa huwa al-mumaththal al-awwal was-sābiq al-awwal* (And he is the first representative and the first precedent). *Al-mujīb li-da'watihi 'inda qiyāmi da'watihi* (The one who responds to his call at the time of the establishment of his call). And the *malā'ikah*... and the *malā'ikah* are *muba'ath awwal* [first sent forth] and *sābiq* [precedent]. There is no calculation in it. How many groups of *malā'ikah* are there? *Mala... al-malā'ikah* [the angels]... In the end... one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight. *Malā'ikah*. One... *al-mumaththal al-awwal was-sābiq* (the first representative and the precedent). That's what he's saying. *Wa huwa al-mumaththal al-awwal was-sābiq* (And he is the first representative and the precedent). That he is *al-mumaththal al-awwal* and *sābiq*. *Al-mujīb li-da'watihi 'inda qiyāmi da'watihi* (The one who responds to his call at the time of the establishment of his call). Who accepts... so that in the call, he... *mujīb li-da'watihi* (responds to his call). ...is *mumaththal awwal* from where? No... *mumaththal awwal* is not there. No, *mumaththal awwal* is not there. Where is *mumaththal awwal*? Yes, *mumaththal awwal* is above the *sābiq*. No... you're saying... *mujīb li-da'watihi 'inda qiyāmi da'watihi* (responds to his call at the time of the establishment of his call). *Mumaththal awwal*'s call will be established then... A bit of a mistake has occurred. Look... that... who are those *malā'ikah*? *Mumaththal al-awwal*. And *sābiq*. That *sābiq* who, at the time of the call, is the first to respond. The *mumaththal awwal* is the one who establishes the call. *Mumaththal awwal* does the establishing of the call. *Mumaththal awwal* does it. Without the call, he has already come. He is *'Ulū al-'Ilm* [the people of knowledge]. And *sāhibān-e-'ilm* [possessors of knowledge]. *'Ulū* meaning owners of knowledge. They have been made owners. *Hum ahl al-da'wat al-ṣaḥīḥah* (They are the people of the correct call). *Alladhī ya'tī 'alayhim al-kalām ba'da al-ishārah*. Then *fīmā ba'da al-ishārah... in shā' Allāh* (who... the speech about them will come after the indication... in that which comes after the indication, God willing). From this, it is established... *ay ya'tī... ya'tī 'alayhim al-kalām ba'da...* (meaning, it will come... the speech about them will come after...) The speech will come after this, *in shā' Allāh*. While reading, keep in mind. *Shahida Allāhu annahu lā ilāha illā Huwa wal-malā'ikatu wa ulū al-'ilm qā'iman bil-qisṭ* (Allah witnesses that there is no deity except Him, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge, maintaining [creation] in justice). *Shahida Allāhu* (Allah has witnessed)... has given witness... that He is... *annahu lā ilāha illā Huwa* (that there is no god but Him). *Wal-malā'ikatu* (And the angels). Who are they? The *Sābiq*. *Wa ulū al-'ilm* (And those of knowledge). *Ahl al-ṣaḥīḥ* (The people of correctness). With him... *al-mufassir* [the commentator]... from this *āyah* [verse], after the *Nabi*, they mentioned the entire *silsilah* [chain] until *Mumaththal al-Awwal*. The *tarkīb* [structure] of the commentary... the *silsilah* from the *Nabi*... *thumma al-Imām... 'Ālim... wa 'Ālimuhu* (then the Imam... a knower... and His knower). From this it is known... *'Ālimuhu*. His *'Ālim*. That is the tenth... the twelfth... a different issue. The *sābiq*. The *sābiq* is... that is separate. The *ḥujjat* [proof]. That is something else... its explanation will come.

...it could be *kamāl thānī*. We are reading *mabdaʾ maʿād*. And it was named this world the world of pure existence in the world of existence, for its existence from non-existence, which is not existence. And *bulūgh* means to reach *kamāl awwal* and *thānī*. *kamāl thānī*. That which is its *bulūgh* in reality. The first existence is the *kamāl thānī* of something. Then this is... a name was given. *Wujūd*. *Wujūd* means... the path of existence... to come into being. To come into being from *ʿadam*, which is non-existent. *ʿadam*... what kind of time was *ʿadam*? No... no... there was no time. Nothing was there. From there, everything became existent. And *bulūgh* is to reach. Reaching from the state of *kamāl thānī*. It is not *kamāl awwal*. The *bulūgh* mentioned here is *kamāl thānī*. It could be *kamāl awwal*, meaning to come from *ʿadam* to the state of *kamāl awwal*, that could also be the case. [unclear] *kamāl thānī*... [unclear] *kamāl awwal*... On *kamāl thānī*. [unclear] *kamāl thānī*. The copy (*nuskha*) is made. It could be *kamāl awwal*, it could be *kamāl doyum* (*second perfection*). The word *bulūgh* implies perfection (*kamāl*). The word *bulūgh* is used. The copy says, *al-ladhī huwa bulūghuhum al-ḥaqīqī* (which is their true attainment). What is this existence? Such an existence is the *kamāl thānī* in reality (*ḥaqīqat*), it is existence. What is the first existence? It is only life (*zindagī*). And what is this true existence (*wujūd ḥaqīqī*)? It is *kamāl thānī*. *wa fī hādhā al-ʿālam* (and in this world)... See, this world is also called *ʿālam al-amr*. *wa huwa al-amr wa al-ʿilm al-muttaṣil billāhi taʿālā ittṣālan ʿaqliyyan* (and it is the Command and the Knowledge connected to God, may He be exalted, an intellectual connection)... from which a flow of command comes. From this *ʿālam* (world), a flow... that is, the *amr* (command)... from which there is a flow of command. It is the knowledge that is connected to Allah Ta'ala. *ittṣālan ʿaqliyyan* (an intellectual connection). How did the *amr* become connected? By the *kāf* of the word. And from it, a flow towards what is below it, which are the intellects (*ʿuqūl*). *wa huwa al-rūḥ* (and it is the Spirit). It is the spirit. And it is also called the spirit. *wa li-dhālika summīya hādhā al-ʿālam ʿālam al-arwāḥ* (and for that reason, this world was named the world of spirits). And for this reason, a name was given. Because of it, this world... it was called *ʿālam al-arwāḥ* (the world of spirits). Yes. It is also called *rūḥ* (spirit). *ʿālam al-rūḥ* (the world of the spirit). And *ʿālam al-arwāḥ* (the world of spirits) is derived from it. *iḍāfatan ilā hādhā al-rūḥ* (in relation to this spirit). Meaning, in relation to this spirit, which... *al-muttaṣil billāh...* [unclear] *ḥayāt abadiyyah* (eternal life)... *ḥayāt* (life)... *al-muttaṣil* (the one connected) to it, the one that grants eternal life. It attains eternal life. They get eternal life. *wa ʿālam al-ibdāʿ wa ʿālam al-ʿaql al-kull wa ʿālam al-quds* (and the world of origination, and the world of the Universal Intellect, and the world of sanctity). It is also called *ʿālam al-ibdāʿ* (the world of origination), *ʿālam al-ʿaql al-kull* (the world of the Universal Intellect), and *ʿālam al-quds* (the world of sanctity). Meaning, the *rūḥ* itself is this world. *li-nisbatihi ilā amrillāh* (due to its relation to the command of God).

...from the *ṣadr-i-awwal* (the first emanation). Then, from the *ṣadr-i-awwal*, *al-ladhī huwa sārī fī al-ashyā’i kullihā* (the one who is pervasive in all things), when it is found… when a denier is found towards it, then, the attribution is to the *sābiq* (the Precedent) and the *tālī* (the Subsequent). It is from the *ṣadr-i-awwal*. They call it *ʻālam-i-latāfat* (the world of subtlety). There is no physical density in it. Now, *ʻālam-i-ṣifāt* (the world of attributes), because of its *ṣifā* (purity/clarity). They are pure essences. Because of their purity, they are [free] from impurities and densities. *ʻālam-i-wujūd* (the world of existence) was brought forth. Then… There are eight *ʻālam* (worlds). *ʻālam-i-rūḥānī* (the spiritual world), *ʻālam-i-abdān* (the world of bodies), *ʻālam-i-ʻaql* (the world of intellect), *ʻālam-i-nafs* (the world of the soul), *ʻālam-i-latāfat* (the world of subtlety), then he described *ʻālam-i-ṣifāt* (the world of attributes). Eight have been completed. *Thumma innahu ansha’a minhu sabʻa ṣuwarin wa-ṣuwaran kathīran* (Then indeed, He created from it seven forms and many forms). Then, from the first *ḥukm* (command/decree), seven forms emerged from the one *ḥukm*. From the *ḥukm*, seven forms emerged. From those seven forms, what happened? Many forms, *ṣuwaran kathīran* (many forms). *Ijābat* (response). Now, from this it is understood that the first seven forms were established. After that, the gate of *ijāzat* (permission) was closed. After the emergence of these forms, it was commanded that in the emergence of each one, there would be innumerable forms. The last form of the first is superior to the second circle. The last form of the first circle was more excellent than the second circle. First, He brought the *latāfat* (subtlety) before us. And when the second circle was called, *daʻwat* (the call) was given to the last individual of the first circle. Then, within each of these seven, many *ṣuwar* (forms) appeared. Many forms. *Ijābat* (response). *Bi-ijābatihim* (through their response). The one that was accepted, became accepted. *Wa-taṣawwara lahum fī ṣūratih… fa-ʻalā bi-fiʻlihi mā faʻalahu qabl* (And He appeared to them in His form… so by His action, He elevated what He had done before). *Wa-huwa lahum kal-imām wa-hum lahu kal-ma’mūm* (And he is to them like the Imam, and they are to him like the followers). He is like an Imam for them, and they all pray behind him. *Wa-kal-ḥadd lahum, wa-hum lahu kal-maḥdūdīn* (And like the boundary for them, and they are to him like the bounded). And he is like a boundary, and they are bounded for him. *Wa-kar-ra’īs lahum, wa-hum lahu kal-mar’ūsīn* (And like the chief for them, and they are to him like the subjects). And he is a chief for them, and they are all his subjects. *Wa-li-dhālika qālū… ghālibun bi-wujūdihī* (And for that reason they said… victorious by his existence).

qawl say, Kanzul Anwar Ma'ad [unclear] is in it. There is no `awwalayn` (first ones), no `sab'a` (seven), `la ghayr`, `la ghayr` (nothing else), `wa 'ala al-awwalayn wal-thani` (and upon the first ones and the second), meaning `ta'leef` (composition). And for this reason, they say `darud`... `darud`... for this reason, `wa 'ala`... sanctify with `darud`, `du'a`... to these individuals, to these `insan` (humans), the command is... na their `masabat`, na their `masabat` (accountability)... if it is wrong, then [unclear]... but the `darud sharif` of the seven, the `sardar` (chief) has been mentioned. `wa 'ala al-awwalin` (and upon the first ones), upon the `awwal` (first), before them, those whose `ta'leef` (composition) has been done. `Ta'leef` means this... this `mubahatha` (discussion) is... `ta'leef` `mubahatha` is called... `wa huwa al-qawl al-awwal wa 'ala alladhina ghayrahum 'ala al-hukm fi ha'ula'i al-sab'a` (and this is the first `qawl` and upon those other than them, according to the `hukm` concerning these seven). The `qawl` was left, the command was left upon those people who do not know these seven in the `hukm` (command). Who do not know these seven in the `hukm`. There were incorrect `aqwal` (sayings) regarding them. They are not... `li-qawlihi ta'ala fi dhimni` (for His, the Exalted's, statement regarding)... this `Surah Al-Baqarah`'s one `ayah`... `la farqa bayna...` (`la farqa bayna ahadin minhum` - we make no distinction between any of them)... `kama bayna al-awwal wal-thani` (just as between the first and the second). For them, for each one, for `wahid`... `momin` (believer)... `fi dhimnihim` (within their responsibility)... `wa yahdu...` the one... in the same form, it is not, and there is no difference... `kama bayna al-awwal wal-thani` (just as between the first and the second). What does this mean? Meaning, just as he... in the `mubahatha` (discussion)... just as he accepted the `da'wat` (mission) in one form, the `da'wat` is built upon his form, and from his form, from his `fe'l` (action), a very large gathering came under his control. There was no need to do `da'wat` (preach). From that `da'wat`, everything was... After that, the last `fard` (individual) was given the command that you should now do `da'wat`. Just as he did `da'wat`, a very large gathering accepted his `da'wat`. 89 companions who were his... from there, this `da'irah` (circle) was closed, the `da'irah` was closed. This is the same form that we have before us. And from there then... there is only the difference of `qabl` (before) and `ba'd` (after), that's all. This is one thing. That... understood... `qabl` and `ba'd` is understood. `'ala man kun fi dhimnihim` (upon those who are within their responsibility). `'ala man kun fi dhimnihim... min ba'd al-hajr... min... al-awwalin...` (`min ba'd al-hajr` - from after the restriction)... `min... al-awwalin` (from the first ones). ...`wa al-haqq fi jumlat ma dhukira` (and the truth in all that has been mentioned) is `mazmumun` (contained within), `mansubun` (attributed to). And that `wahid` (one), for that `wahid`... look at the `riwayat` (narration), from the seven `usul` (principles), for each one, from the seven `usul`, for each one, `'ala man kun fi dhimnihim` (upon those who are within their responsibility). Upon those people who are within his... responsibility. `'ala al-hajr` (upon the restriction), which is for the `hajr` (restriction), from the `sawabiyat` (correct things), upon his `mu'minin` (believers), from the `sawabiyat`...

*bi-ismika*. They are connected to him. *ilayhi*, towards him. They are drawn towards him. *wa huwa waahidun* (and He is one). And he is one, he is one. And that... that... the one who is the chief, that form, that form... seven hundred... seven hundred... Every single form that is, that is one form. And as many as are in their circle, they and those in their circle are in a *falak* (sphere), one, in just one *falak*. That circle, *al-munfasalah* (the separate) *al-muttasilah* (the connected), just as the circle becomes connected... what happened? This became the chief, one form. After that, a circle was drawn. What happens? The beginning and the end meet. As many as there are, all are connected to this one. This is the center. They are under the authority of the circle. After that, the last person, the last person in the circle, the one in the circle, is given the command, "You create another circle." He calls, he gives an invitation. After giving the invitation, he becomes the center. And under him, another circle is established. *wa hadha al-'alam bi-ajma'ihi 'alamun kabirun 'azimun* (And this entire world is a great, magnificent world). And this world, all of it, is a very great world. *la yuhsihi al-'adad* (number cannot encompass it). *la yuhsihi al-'adad*. What does it mean? Number cannot surround it. Number cannot surround them. *kama dhakara Sayyiduna al-Mu'ayyad al-Shirazi radiyallahu 'anhu fi hadha al-'aql* (as our master, Sayyiduna al-Mu'ayyad al-Shirazi, may Allah be pleased with him, mentioned regarding this Intellect), just as... *Sayyiduna al-Mu'ayyad al-Shirazi radiyallahu 'anhu fi rahati al-'aql* (Sayyiduna al-Mu'ayyad al-Shirazi, may Allah be pleased with him, in *Rahat al-'Aql*)... *wa hadhihi al-saba'a 'uqul bi-hiddatiha wa sur'atiha bi-qabuli... al-qurubiyyah* (And these seven intellects, with their sharpness and their speed in accepting... the *qurubiyyah* [those brought near]). And these seven intellects, due to their sharpness, with what quickness and speed they accepted... *al-hiddah*. *Hiddah* means vision. There are two visions at one time, but one vision has *hiddah* in it, that it reaches the essential reality. One is an external thing... So, the vision makes a difference. So what is he saying here? These seven intellects, *min hiddatiha* (due to their sharpness), due to their sharp vision, *rabatu al-sama' bi-al-saba' al-qurubiyyah* (they linked the heaven with the seven *qurubiyyah*). The seven *qurubiyyah*, the *mala'ikah qurubiyyah* (angels brought near) are what they are called. *wa alladhina fi zimamihim summu bi-al-mala'ikah al-ruhaniyyin* (And those under their charge were named the spiritual angels). What does it mean? Those who are under their charge, whom God the Exalted accepted... What is their name? *Mala'ikah ruhaniyyin* (spiritual angels). The *qurubiyyin* are called *ru'asa'* (chiefs). And under them, those who are, are *mala'ikah* (angels)... what are called *ruhaniyyin* (spiritual ones). *Mala'ikah ruhaniyyin*. *wa amma al-sabi' alladhi ja'a 'an kulli 'alamin wa tawallada minha...* (And as for the seventh, which came from every world and was generated from it...).

*Sab'ah Kurūbiyyīn*, *wa yuqālu lahum al-Malā'ikat al-Muqarrabūn* (and they are called the Angels Brought Near). *Malā'ikah Muqarrabūn* are mentioned in the Qur'an. *Malā'ikah Kurūbiyyīn*... and those who ascend from the entire *'ālam al-tabī'ah* (physical world), after the tenth *hadd*, they... are finished, so they become... what are they called? *Malā'ikah Kurūbiyyīn*.
