When the second teacher (al-mu'allim al-thānī) moved his pen from the second tablet ('an surād al-thānī) and caused his entire essence to grow within it, it was obtained and arrived. Then he began to manifest upon him the higher world (al-'alam al-a'lā) and became the place of the red ruby (mahal al-yaqūt al-ahmar) from among the mineral gems (min al-jawāhir al-ma'daniyyah), and the place of pure gold (mahal al-dhahab al-ibriz) from among the malleable bodies (min al-ajsām al-mutarriqah), and the place of the date palm (mahal al-nakhlah) from among the plants (min al-nabāt), and of man (al-insān) from among the animals (min al-hayawān). Rather, he is more noble (ashraf), more subtle (altaf), and more exalted (a'lā). Then, *thumma innahu* (then, indeed), when he was from among these twenty-two persons (*al-ashkhās al-thāniyah wa al-ishrīn*), one person (*shakhsan wāhid*), the purest of them (*asfāhum*), the most subtle of them (*altafahum*), the most excellent of them (*afdalahum*), and the most noble of them (*ashrafahum*). *illa minhā mahal al-yaqūt al-ahmar min al-jawāhir al-ma'daniyyah al-musaffāt, wa mahal al-dhahab al-ibriz min al-ajsām al-mutarriqah, wa mahal al-nakhlah min al-nabāt wa al-insān min al-hayawān bal huwa ashraf wa altaf wa a'lā*. Then *thumma innahu*, it is said that when he was among these twenty-two persons, one person who is purer than all, more subtle than all, more excellent, more noble. *illa minhā* (except from it). And he is such that his place is that of a red ruby (*mahal yaqūt al-ahmar*), from the mineral gems that are pounded. Just as gold is, in malleable bodies, the way rubies are considered precious, and their place is the most excellent. He is better than that. This is his place. That place which, where this is found. The place of pure gold (*dhahab al-ibriz*) from the malleable bodies. *Ibriz* means pure. Pure gold. 100%. From the things that are pounded. *min al-nabāt*, from plants, which are pounded, among them the date palm. *wa al-insān min al-hayawān* (and man from among the animals). Just as man is the best among animals. In the same way, the red ruby is among the mineral gems, and the date palm is among the plants, from the pounded ones. And man is from the animals. But he is more noble, more subtle and higher than them. So all these—all these analogies that are given, are for his nobility (*sharafiyyat*). *bal huwa ashraf wa altaf wa a'lā*. He is much more noble. The *Musannif* is saying that he is much more noble and subtle than them. *wa 'alā jumlat al-qawl* (and in summary of the statement). *wa 'alā jumlat al-qawl fa-huwa zubdat al-'ālamayn al-jirmānī wa al-jismānī wa safwatuhumā* (And in summary of the statement, he is the essence of the two worlds, the celestial and the physical, and the choicest of them both). The summary of the statement is this: that he is of both worlds, the celestial world and the physical world. The celestial world is what is above. It has all the worlds. And the physical world is also... the essence of both of them. There, the purest thing... is the form of the *nātiq*. That upon which the *wahy* (revelation) descends. And the physical... and both of them... their essence... and the essence of both of them. *thumma innahu nazara bi-dhātihī ilā dhātihī wa ilā abnā' jinsihī wa mā fawqahū*. Then, he looked—*innahu* (indeed he), surely he—as it is, as it is, he looked at his own self, with his self to his self. Meaning, of his own self. *bi-dhātihī*, with his own self. *ilā dhātihī*, to his self. Meaning of his own self. What does *bi-dhātihī* mean? Without any speaker, teller... without their aid... without them, he looked at his own self. First, who was there to teach? His own self. His own self. *wa ilā abnā' jinsihī* (and to the sons of his kind). *wa mā fawqahū min samā' marfu'ah wa arz mawdu'ah wa nujūm sayyārah wa anhār jarrārah wa falak dawwār wa layl wa nahār*. So he looked, what is above him, from the raised sky, the laid-out earth, the moving stars, the flowing rivers, the revolving firmament, and night and day. So he looked. *wa li-abnā' jinsihī wa li-hādhā al-'awālim al-mukhtalifat al-anwā' wa al-ashkhās mūjidan huwa ghayru mumāthilin lahā wa lā mushābihan... fa-'alima anna lahū...* So he knew... that for him and for the sons of his kind, and for all these worlds... you see, heaven, earth, stars, rivers... for these worlds... *mukhtalifat al-anwā'* (of different kinds), different kinds of things, and persons, there is a creator. Who is not similar to them, nor does he resemble them. There is a creator. He is not similar to them. Nor does he resemble them. *fa-nafā 'anhū wa 'an abnā' jinsihī sā'ir tilka al-mawjūdāt al-ilāhiyyah wa athbatahā li-mubdi'ihim wa mūjidihim ta'ālā* (So he negated from himself and from the sons of his kind all those divine existents, and he affirmed them for their Originator and their Creator, may He be exalted). So he negated from himself and from the sons of his kind... so he negated from himself and from the sons of his kind all those existing things, the divinity, and he affirmed it for their Originator and their Creator, *ta'ālā*, who is high. *wa shahida lahū bi-al-wahdāniyyah wa sabbahahū wa qaddasahū fa-ittasala bihi al-ma'ādin al-ilāhiyyah wa al-anwār al-sha'sha'āniyyah wa al-tā'idāt al-malakūtiyyah wa al-mutahhid bi-dā'irat al-'aql al-'āshir wa nazara ilayhi wa ayyadahu bi-al-dirham wa balagha al-kamāl al-thānī wa ja'alahū min ashwāq shu'ā'ihī fa-ashraqat dhātuhū bi-ishrāq kullī wa intakhaba lahū min al-mawā'iz al-hasanah wa ittala'a min al-mughayyabāt wa al-hādirāt 'alā jamī' al-funūn wa 'alima mā kāna wa mā sayakūn*. And he was blessed, and blessed with kindness and with good counsels. And he was informed of the unseen things and the present things, of all the arts. He became aware of all of them. And he knew what had been and what will be. *mā kāna wa mā sayakūn*. The physical state. What was that? In this—in this physical, it is also *mā kāna wa mā sayakūn*. Yes. *'ālam al-jismānī*. In that, the *mā kāna wa mā sayakūn* comes, right? That is what is being said here. The matter is of the *'ālam al-jismānī*. In the *'ālam al-jismānī*, the *mā kāna wa mā sayakūn* comes, right? Well, that is stated first, that the matter of the *'ālam al-jismānī* is being discussed. The *'ālam al-jismānī* has been mentioned, right? *wa qāma fī 'ālam al-jismī muqābil al-'aql al-awwal fī 'ālam al-'aql wa maqām al-'aql al-'āshir fī maqāmihī munfaridan bi-rutbat al-wahdah wa maqām al-'azamah mawsūman bi-al-ibdā' fī hādhā al-'ālam wa da'ā tilka al-ashkhās al-sab'ah wa al-'ishrīn ilā tawhīd Allāh*. He stood in the world of bodies. He stood in the world of bodies. Just as... the first intellect. In the world of intellect... The tenth intellect... In its station... in the world of intellect, his station is that. Just as the first intellect... his station in the world of intellect... Just as in the world of intellect, the station of the first intellect... in the world of bodies, his station is that. And the station of the tenth intellect... in its station... unique in the rank of Oneness. Unique was the rank of Oneness... the station of greatness, marked with origination in this world... that this is the one who will originate in this world. And he called those twenty-seven persons to the Oneness of Allah (*tawhīd Allāh*). *wa tanzīh wa tajrīd fa-ajābūhu musri'īna wa labbaw da'watahū mu'ti'īna wa akhadha 'alayhim al-'uhūd al-mu'akkadah wa al-mawāthīq al-mughalladhah al-mushaddadah wa 'allamahum mā ittasala bihi wa ilayhi min al-mutahid... min al-mutahhidīna bihi wa attala'ahum 'alā min al-'ulūm al-ghaybiyyah wa al-asrār al-malakūtiyyah*. And he took from them confirmed covenants and reinforced and strengthened pacts, and he taught them what he was connected with and to it, from those who were united with him. Whoever accepted his call from among them, to them... all of them. And he informed them of the sciences, the unseen sciences and the secrets of the kingdom (*asrār al-malakūtiyyah*). *ba'da an awdaha lahum al-halāl wa al-harām wa 'allamahum al-qadāyā wa al-ahkām wa qannana lahum qawānīn al-diyānah wa afādahum jamī' mā yahtājūna ilayhi min al-ifādah wa amarahum an yash'urū al-'ālam nikāh tilka al-harā'im al-lātī qad sunna lahum wa manna 'alayhim bihi min al-minnah wa awda'ahum jamī' dhālika wa awz'ahum mā qad laqqa' wa ikhtāra minhum sittata 'ashara shakhsan*. After—after he had clarified for them the lawful and the forbidden, and taught them the judgments and the rulings, and legislated laws for them, and benefited them... with all that they needed of benefit. And he commanded them to make the world aware, to have them do *nikāh* with those forbidden women for whom the *sunnah* had been established. So he made those women permissible for them, marriage with whom is forbidden. These are all the things that are the unseen sciences that were given to them. And He bestowed upon them a favor. He bestowed a favor on them with this favor. And he entrusted them with all those things. He entrusted those things to their minds, whatever he was commanded. And from them he chose sixteen persons. Sixteen persons. *afdaluhum bābun wa al-thānī lahū hujjah wa dā'iyayn ahaduhumā dā'ī balāgh wa al-thānī dā'ī mutlaq wa ithnā 'ashar ja'alahum hujaj al-layl wa tarakahum bi-hadratihi lā yufāriqūnahu hādhā ihdā 'ashara shakhsan wa hum al-bāqūna fī al-jazā'ir*. This is eleven persons. And the second is... and called... eleven and the second... sixteen persons. Sixteen out of twenty-seven. And the first is himself. With him are sixteen. In the sixteen, four are his *du'āt*. Four *du'āt* means the *Bāb*, the *hujjah*, the *dā'ī al-balāgh*, and the *dā'ī al-mutlaq*. Sixteen, so... and the twelve are in the islands (*jazā'ir*). They are the *hujaj al-layl*... in their presence. The sixteen... sixteen, so four are his two... four means *Bāb* and *hujjah*... *dā'ī al-balāgh* and *dā'ī al-mutlaq*. And the twelve are in the islands, the *hujaj al-layl*... in his presence. So there are sixteen, and he himself is seventeen. So how many are left? Eleven. Eleven. The eleven are... the eleven are those in the islands... *wa hum al-bāqūna fī al-jazā'ir ihdā 'ashar shakhsan wa sānī... wa sānī 'ashar... fī jazīratihi al-latī huwa fīhā wa rutbatuhum mahfūzah fī jamī' al-jazā'ir ilā al-ān wa ilā ākhir al-zamān*. And they are the ones remaining in the islands, eleven... eleven persons. And the second is... and the second is in his island, in which he is... And their rank is preserved in all the islands until now and until the end of time. *wa amara kulla wāhidin minhum bi-al-da'wah lahū fī jazīratihi al-latī ja'ala ilayhi wa ja'ala lahum hujajan nahāran ithnā 'ashar*. And he commanded each one of them to call to him in their island, which he had assigned to them, and he made for them twelve *hujaj al-nahār*. Those twelve are the *hujaj al-nahār*. So their subordinates... there are twelve of those gentlemen in the islands. They are also *hujaj*. These are *hujaj al-nahār*. *wa qāma bi-al-da'wah lahū salāmu Allāhi 'alayhi kamā umira wa anzajara jamī' ahl al-jazā'ir 'ammā nahāhum wa hādhā al-hujaj 'āriyūna 'an afwāl al-bātil al-muhiss wa marfu' 'anhum af'āl al-sitr wa al-takāyid zāhiran li-'ulūwwi darajātihim*. And these *hujaj* are devoid of the afflictions of pure falsehood, and the afflictions of the veil (*sitr*) and deception (*takāyid*) are lifted from them, outwardly, due to the loftiness of their ranks. Since these are gentlemen, so all his afflictions of the veil are lifted from them. So... it won't be in concealment (*kashf*) for them. No. Yes. The *sharī'ah* which is for the *da'wah*. That is what it is. For the *da'wah*, the *sharī'ah* is... That is what is for the veil (*sitr*). The *sharī'ah* is for the veil. For them, it is said that all of its... whatever its rulings are... they are not for them. Is the *kalimah* "Lā ilāha illā Allāh" only given to the Prophet, or to every *Nātiq*? All of them. The first *Nātiq* is *Ādam al-ṣafī*. *wa hum afdal jamī' al-thamāniyah wa al-ishrīn*. And they are the most excellent of all the twenty-eight. That is, the twelve. They are more excellent than the twenty-eight. Then from the twelve... then the four. From the four, the *Bāb*. Then the *Imām*. *wa Bābuhum wa sā'isuhum al-Imām 'alayhi al-salām wa hujaj al-nahār 'ārifūna bi-hadhihi*. The four are the *Imām*'s house... and the four are the *Imām*'s house... *Bāb*, *hujjah*... and the two *dā'īs*... *dā'ī al-mutlaq* and *dā'ī al-mahdūd*. These *hujaj al-layl*... all of these are more excellent than those who are except the *Imām* and the *Bāb*. *wa hujaj al-nahār 'ārifūna bi-hadhihi al-maqāmāt kullihā illā annahum dūna maqām hā'ulā'i*. These are the *hujaj al-nahār* who are established. They are aware of all these stations, except that they are below the station of these. *wa qā'imuna bi-al-dā'irah wa muta'allimūna jamī'an hā'ulā'i al-thamāniyah wa al-ishrīn hum al-ulū al-'ilm al-ladhīna dhakarahum Allāh min ahl al-shahādah wa ibdā'ihim 'azza wa jalla*. And these twenty-eight are the possessors of knowledge (*ulū al-'ilm*), those whom Allah mentioned from among the people of witnessing (*ahl al-shahādah*) and their origination, may He be mighty and glorious. And these twenty-two... these twenty-eight are the possessors of knowledge, such that those mentioned by Allah are from the people of witnessing and His origination, may He be mighty and glorious. As it is said: *ay sabaqa Allāh ta'ālā fī kitābihi al-karīm shahida Allāhu annahū lā ilāha illā huwa wa al-malā'ikatu wa ulū al-'ilm*. And the remaining of them. *wa al-bāqī 'alayhim 'alayhi salāmu Allāh wa al-mubdi' al-awwal al-ladhī wa lahad fīhi jamī' al-rūhāniyyah wa al-malā'ikah wa hum al-'uqūl al-rūhāniyyah wa ulū al-'ilm wa hā'ulā'i al-thamāniyah wa al-ishrīn shakhsan al-ladhīna hum 'alā al-jasad al-ibdā'iyyah al-mawjūdūna bi-ghayri tanāsul*. That is, as Allah, the Exalted, said in His Noble Book: *Shahida Allāhu annahū lā ilāha illā huwa wa al-malā'ikatu wa ulū al-'ilm* (Allah bears witness that there is no god but Him, as do the angels and the possessors of knowledge). Just as Allah has said... Allah has said in His Noble Book, *Shahida Allāhu*, Allah testified... that there is no god but Him... *lā ilāha illā huwa*... *wa al-malā'ikah*, and the angels... and the possessors of knowledge (*ulū al-'ilm*) testified. Allah... who is He? The First Intellect. The angels... who are they? The other intellects. And the possessors of knowledge... who are they? These twenty-eight persons. *'alā al-jasad al-ibdā'iyyah al-mawjūdūna bi-ghayri tanāsul*. Those who are upon the originating bodies, who exist without procreation. *kamā sabaqa bihi al-qawl anna al-nāfī al-muthbit ra'īsuhum al-wāhid al-ladhī aqāma al-sharī'ah wa huwa muqābil al-mubdi' al-awwal al-nāfī al-muthbit al-muwahhid*. He who denies any god besides Him. And affirms Him. The one who establishes unity (*muwahhid*). The establisher of unity (*muwahhid*) is one. One. Who is he? The one who establishes the *sharī'ah*. He is opposite the first originator (*al-mubdi' al-awwal*), the negator (*al-nāfī*), the affirmer (*al-muthbit*), the unifier (*al-muwahhid*). He who negates any god besides Him. He who negates, and he who affirms. He taught the unity of God, that there is no god. He negated. *illā hu*, except Him. He affirmed. So he negated and affirmed. He who does this, the one who establishes the *sharī'ah* does this. In the first *dawr* (cycle), the *shāri'* of the first *dawr* is who? *Ādam*. *al-ladhī ta'allama al-tawhīd min ghayri mu'allim yutaqaddamahu wa lā yasbaquhu... bal ahjamahu min dhātihi bi-dhātihi*. He who learned the unity of God without any teacher preceding him or coming before him. Rather, he understood it from his own self by his own self. He understood. His own self, from his own self, with his own self. *min dhātihi bi-dhātihi*.

The 28 individuals from the *Du'at* who are called *Da'iyah*. What was ordered regarding them? The first four of the 28. The first is *Dhu'l-Saif Da'iyah*. With him are three individuals who are in his *hadrat* (presence). Who are they? The *Bab*, the *Da'iyah matlab*, the *Da'iyah baatin*. Four individuals. Four individuals. *Da'iyah*... *Bab*, *Hujjat*, *Da'iyah matlab*, *Da'iyah baatin*. And 12 *Jaza'ir*. The number 18, 18. 12 and 5 is 17. 18. Now how many remain? Four and one is five. 10 *dhu'l-saif da'iyah*. Four, five... 17. It became 17. 12... 17. 17... 17. And after that, 11 *Jaza'ir*. 11 *Jaza'ir*. And *mujiza-e-nahari*, *mujiza-e-nahar*. They are the complete two miracles. The point that he made in his command is that these are the 28 individuals. And these 28 individuals, with every Imam, their appearance will happen. *Imam Dhu'l-Saif Da'iyah* will be at one station. With him will be 27 individuals. The *Qa'im* ('alayhi al-salatu wa al-salam) will come, with him will be 28 individuals. All the *dhu saif* who come, with them will be 28. Allah has established a pattern (*naqsh*). On this pattern, it will always, always... go on. He said that Allah Ta'ala created the world in six days. So these six days... in them what happened... On its basis... in six days. Six days. Allah's six days. So, Allah Ta'ala has one thousand years... the day of Qiyamah... One *yawm* (day) with Allah is equal to one thousand years. In 6,000 years, the time that is mentioned in it, in 6,000 years, the creation happened. And in the era of 'Utarid (Mercury), its... 'Utarid... in which era it happened... what happened... that needs to be seen, research needs to be done. Always in the choice of faith, because its reliance is on what? *La ilaha illa allah* (There is no god but Allah). In this, what is there? 28. In every circle, it is necessary to have 28. Where it says 100, that... For every single one, the number 100 that comes, what did he command for it? *La ilaha illa allah*. What is it? *Nafi* (negation) and *ithbat* (affirmation). Who is *nafi*? Who is *ithbat*? *Ithbat* is *Dhu'l-Saif Da'iyah*. *Nafi* is who? The *Bab*. *Hujjat* is not there. *Bab*. Besides that, what is there? There are three. The common letters are *jim*. *Alif lam ha*. *Alif lam ha* are common. What are they? The common ones... The *alif* is from *Dhu'l-Saif Da'iyah*. Two are... two are... that *Imam*, those who perform *qiyam* (stand in service) in his *hadrat* (presence), whether they are *Bab* or *Hujjat*. Three types of people. One is the Imam himself, who is *Dhu'l-Saif Da'iyah*. Then after that, those who live in his *hadrat*. And the third, those who live outside the *hadrat*. These three will always be there. After that, there are four. Four *kalimat* (words). What are the four *kalimat*? *Dhu'l-Saif Da'iyah*, and his *Bab*, and then those who live in his *hadrat*, and one *muza'aya*. After that, he commanded seven. What are the seven? The seven are... The seven are... what was commanded in it... in the seven... *Dhu'l-Saif Da'iyah*, its division was commanded. The *Da'iyah* and his *Bab*. Two... seven, right? Seven. With him are the *Hujjat*. The *Hujjat* and the *Da'iyah*. Five. Five. And he took *nahari* and *nahari*. Seven. Seven. In this way, seven. What are the 12? 12 *jaza'ir*. The exegesis of *la ilaha illa allah*. In everything, he has ordained... in everything, there is the manifestation (*jalwah*) of *la ilaha*. In *namaz*, in fasting, in purity, in this, in that, in everything, there is the manifestation of *la ilaha*. And here too, it is the same. *Summa innahu*. What is its principle? What is the *kalimah*? *bayna al-mubdi'i wa al-mubda'i kalimah* (Between the Originator and the originated is a Word). *Mubdi'* and *mubda'*... between them... what is the thing higher than the *mubda'-e-awwal*? *Nur* (light). The *nur* of the *kalimah la ilaha illa allah*. *Thumma innahu ittusila bi hadha al-shakhs al-fadil al-sharif al-kamil, 'ammud al-nur. Ittusila 'ammud al-nur alladhi huwa liman ittusila bihi al-fawz wa al-ni'mah. Wa al-kawn fi jumlat ahl al-rahmah*. (Then he connected with this virtuous, noble, perfect person, the pillar of light. The pillar of light connected, which belongs to whomever connects with it success and grace. And the universe is among the people of mercy). In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Then, verily, he was connected with this virtuous person who is noble and perfect. The *'ammud al-nur* was connected. Such that he, for whom it was connected, to him belongs success and grace. Such that he who... He said... That *'ammud al-nur*, where is it from? The *nur* of the *kalimah la ilaha illa allah*. It is connected from there. So, *'ammud al-nur*, what is... what is its link? What is its link? With whom is it? With everyone. Whoever takes the noble covenant (*'ahd al-sharif*), with him. The one who takes the noble covenant is the last one. Upwards? From where? From *'aql awwal* (the First Intellect). From *'aql awwal*. From *'aql awwal*. From *mubdi'-e-ta'ala* (the Exalted Originator). From the *kalimah la ilaha illa allah*. The *'aql awwal*... from the *'aql awwal*, all... up to here. So what is the difference between this and *kamal al-thani* (the second perfection)? *Kamal...* *Kamal al-thani*... will not create... The one who takes the *'ahd al-sharif* is the *ibtida'* (beginning). It is the *ibtida'*. He explained that the trunk of the tree... all the branches (*makhshiyat*) cling to it. It is called *'ammud al-nur*. Alright. All who are connected to it are connected through it. Because it... the *mubdi'-e-ta'ala*'s link is our... original. So, this from the celestial spheres (*aflak*) and the whole... is a complete, continuous chain (*musalsil kadi*). It is just one chain. *Nur...* from the constellations of the firmament (*falak al-buruj*) and from the firmament of... It is one chain. That is the chain of the *kalimah la ilaha illa allah*. Up to the *'aql awwal*. Up to the *'aql awwal* it went. Rather, above it is the *kalimah la ilaha illa allah*. There is a very good explanation of *'ammud al-nur* in this. It was connected with that virtuous, noble person, the *'ammud al-nur*. Such that whoever connects with it, he attains success (*fawz*) and grace (*ni'mat*). And he becomes among the people of mercy. And it is said... And it becomes... he becomes among the people of mercy. *Wa huwa al-'ilm al-muttasil min allah ta'ala ila al-'aql al-awwal*. (And it is the knowledge connected from God, the Exalted, to the First Intellect). And that *'ammud al-nur* is knowledge. What is it? That same *nur*. And knowledge connected from Allah Ta'ala towards the *'aql awwal*. *bayna al-mubdi'i wa al-mubda'i kalimah*. (Between the Originator and the originated is a Word). *'Ammud al-nur* is the connecting knowledge from Allah Ta'ala towards the *'aql awwal*. Towards the *'aql awwal*. That is *'ammud al-nur*. That is the perfect knowledge. *Wa minhu ittusila bi al-'aql al-thani al-tali lahu*. (And from it, the second intellect that follows it is connected). And from it, from the *'aql awwal*, the *'aql thani* (Second Intellect) is connected to it, which comes after that *'aql awwal*. *Wa minhu ila al-thalith*. (And from it to the third). And from it towards the third. *Wa halumma jarran ila al-'aql al-'ashir al-munتهي ilayhi amr al-tabi'ah*. (And so on, to the tenth intellect, to which the command of nature terminates). In this same way, it continued to flow until it reached all the principles towards it. Reaching the end... towards the *'aql 'ashir* (Tenth Intellect)... reaching towards the *'aql 'ashir*... which is the administrator of the world of nature. *Al-mawkulu ilayhi amruha*. (To which its command is entrusted). To whom it was entrusted... the command of that world of nature. *Al-qa'im fiha maqam al-'aql al-awwal*. (Standing in it in the station of the First Intellect). The one who performs *qiyam* in that world of nature, in the station of the *'aql awwal*. The one who establishes the station of the *'aql awwal*. *Al-munfarid bi al-rutbat al-wahdah*. (The one who is unique in the rank of unity). The one who becomes unique with the rank of unity. After reading an *ayat* (verse), what happens to a person? He forgets many things. But its method is that one should then come towards that book. What did the book say? Then it gets collected, it gets gathered. The scattering... every person has a doubt. But what should one make their standard? One should make the book their standard. What did the book say? That is the original. This *'ammud al-nur* is also the *'aql kamil* (perfect intellect). The *'aql kamil*... it is *nur* (light). It is not a *dhat* (being). That starts from the *'aql awwal*. *Saba'atu asbahin nuraniyyah*. (Seven luminous specters). No, so within it there is perfect knowledge. It is the light of Allah Ta'ala, it is support (*ta'id*), it is knowledge (*'ilm*). So, everything is connected to it. And just as there is a channel, within which everything is flowing, one just needs to tap it. So we too are connected to it, but due to our darkness (*zulmat*), we cannot do that. ...and it is the strong rope (*rassi*) from the side of Allah Ta'ala, which connects towards all the *hudud* (ranks). This is called... the firmest hand-hold (*'urwat al-wuthqa*)... *fa qad istamsaka bi al-'urwat al-wuthqa la infisama laha*. (He has grasped the firmest hand-hold, that never breaks). I have firmly grasped that rope for which breaking is not possible. What is it? This is the strand of *'ammud al-nur*. So does it have a station? A physical one within it? It is not a physical thing at all. It is above physical density (*kasafat*). It is *nur* (light). And the *nur* too, which is physicality... the light of the sun is physicality. This *nur* is a much higher *nur* than that. It has not come into density at all. How will it come into density when it has been connected from Allah, the *Mubdi' Ta'ala*, to the *'aql awwal*. And its connection... Our connection is with the *'aql 'ashir*. How can we recognize the *Mubdi' Ta'ala*? Through connection with that *nur*. So, it doesn't descend upon our body, it descends upon our *natiqah* (rational soul). Upon the *natiqah*. *Nafs natiqah*. The *natiqah* has a connection with our body. Since at the time of the *'ahd al-sharif* the *nafs natiqah* is present, therefore it remains related to it. ...from the side which is connected to all the *hudud*. *Wa jami' ahl al-wujud*. (And all the people of existence). And from all the people of existence. *Wa huwa al-muttasil min kulli maqamin ila kaffat hududihi wa mustajib da'watihi*. (And it is the one connected from every station to all its ranks and to the respondents of its call). And that same one is connected from every station towards all its *hudud*. And to the acceptors of his call. *Wa huwa al-jazib li suwar al-mustafidin ila suwar al-mufidin*. (And it is the attractor of the forms of the beneficiaries to the forms of the benefactors). And it is the one that attracts the forms of the beneficiaries towards the forms of the benefactors. The magnet that is beneficial, becoming a magnet, it pulls the forms of the beneficiaries. What is in it? Which magnet is it? It is the *'ammud al-nur*. By the effect of *'ammud al-nur*, the form of the beneficiary goes and becomes connected to the form of the benefactor. After death, that form's... *nafs natiqah*. *Nafs natiqah* of the beneficiary connects with... the *nafs natiqah* of the benefactor. It attracts it. It's a magnet. *'Ammud al-nur* is a magnet. It is a medium in a sense. A medium. *Wa huwa al-jazib*. It is the attractor, the one that attracts the forms of the beneficiaries towards the forms of the benefactors. *Wa huwa maghnatisuhum*. (And it is their magnet). He has commanded... *Wa huwa maghnatisuhum al-mumsik li suwarihim wa nufusihim 'amma yaqul al-zalimun 'uluwwan kabira*. (And it is their magnet, the holder of their forms and their souls, far above what the wrongdoers say in great arrogance). This has become mixed up, forward and backward. One became more, one became less. *Wa huwa maghnatisuhum*. And it is their magnet. *Al-mumsik li suwarihim*. The one who stops their forms. And their souls. *Al-hafiz li kulli shay'in minhum*. The protector of every single thing from them. What are they? Their forms and their souls. The forms that have ascended, with them their souls, through the sensory faculty (*hissiyah*), have progressed. To keep both together is also its job. The *'ammud al-nur*'s sensory... the sensory is physical. The sensory is not physical. It is the *nafs hissiyah* (sensory soul). *Nafs hissiyah*. It became related to the form, and luminosity (*nuraniyat*) was created in it. The form takes its companion with it, the *nafs hissiyah*, and it ascends. To keep both together, the form and the *nafs*, in one place, whose job is this? It is the job of the *'ammud al-nur*. *Wa huwa maghnatisuhum*. And it is a magnet for them. *Al-mumsik li suwarihim*. The one that stops their forms and souls together. So... this, as it is... with the *nafs natiqah*. Stopping means to gather them here. It keeps them gathered in one place. A protector. So this... this is not a physical structure (*haykal*), is it? It is not a *haykal*. It's just a link-like thing that is... *Al-hafiz li kulli shay'in minhum*. The protector of every single thing of theirs. The form that has gone up, now that form cannot be ruined. The *nafs hissiyah* that has become good, now it cannot be ruined. It has separated from the body, now it cannot be ruined, the *nafs hissiyah*. This is also completely fixed. The thing that is good... The part that the *natiqah* took with it, now it cannot be ruined. So this... this is also one of the methods (*tadabir*). Allah Ta'ala has ordained that the thing which has become pure, now it cannot fall down. If it goes to such a rank which is "living," where there is still an opportunity for it to become good or bad, the outcome of good is a condition. If it becomes bad, its high rank becomes bad, then whatever form of it had become pure, that is taken out from it, and the *nafs hissiyah* becomes corrupted. The *nafs hissiyah* becomes corrupted. So in that, our... The form of the rank does not get corrupted. The form does not get corrupted. It has been made. The part that became pure has become pure. What will be corrupted is that the sensory faculty will be corrupted. So now the sensory faculty has created corruption. By coming into whose company has he ruined his own form? In the future, the form that has become pure, has become pure. The rest... That means we can't even name his form. If it's corrupted, it's the sensory faculty that is corrupted. The *natiqah* cannot be corrupted. The one that was the *nafs natiqah* has ascended. It left it and ascended. *Nafs lawwamah*... The *nafs lawwamah* does not ascend. If the *nafs lawwamah* makes progress, it will become the *nafs hissiyah*. It will progress from there. The form that it takes with it is the *nafs hissiyah*. There are people of a very high rank who... their *nafs lawwamah* also ascends. But here we are talking about ordinary people. So how is this related to the *haykal*? Because... We will explain that later. We will explain it in the future. A whole chapter has come on the *haykal*. The *nafs ammarah* is... *Nafs ammarah bis-su'*. *Bis-su'*. *Bis-su'* means commanding evil. *Nafs ammarah bil-khayr*. Commanding good. So both things are separate. *Wa yuqalu 'alayha 'inayat al-ilahiyyah wa al-qudrat al-ilahiyyah*. (And it is called the divine providence and the divine power). And it is said of it, *'inayat al-ilahiyyah* and *qudrat al-ilahiyyah*. Where is the *'ammud al-nur*? And the divine power. It is the protector, it is the *'inayat al-ilahiyyah*, it is the *'ammud al-nur*, the divine power, it is all of them. *Wa huwa al-hafiz li al-'uzw wa al-qit'ah 'ala sahibiha hatta la ya'kul dhalika illa al-ma'bar alladhi huwa nafs kabsh fihi*. (And it is the protector of the limb and the piece for its owner, so that none may eat that except the passage which is the soul of a ram in it). And it is the one that protects every limb and every piece for its owner until that owner does not eat it, except the *ma'bar* (passage). Such that it is a single soul... the soul of a ram is in it. The ram that is slaughtered, its effect is also on that. Its parts are present. So what happens? The *'ammud al-nur* pulls it and brings it to that person whose portion it is destined to be. Water is flowing. The water for *wudu* (ablution) that comes is the same one. The *'ammud al-nur*, with everything... its special... its connection is... The protector... The thing that comes and touches your body is that which is destined to be your portion. The *'ammud al-nur* is its protector. How great a task does *'ammud al-nur* do. So I will eat only that piece of meat which is my own thing. And the one protecting it is that *'ammud al-nur*, ensuring that my thing comes to me, not something else. So this... this... the thing... the parts that come to us, is it the effect of the extending hand, or do those parts themselves automatically... There are two or three mechanisms. The portion that is his, it is his share. It has to reach him. Who is protecting it from going somewhere else? The *'ammud al-nur*. So, for instance, there is food placed in a dish. I am extending my hand. So is it the effect of my hand that those parts are being pulled, or are those parts already present and my hand will go there? It is your thing. Your thing is... it has to go to you. *'Ammud al-nur* protects it so that your thing reaches you. So it's not the effect of the hand, but it's already... it's a plan of Allah which is... With *Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*... by saying *Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*, the effect of *'ammud al-nur* starts, and you get that thing. Otherwise, even if it is our thing, it takes a long time to reach us. *Ma'bar*. *Ma'bar*. *Ma'bar*. *Ma'bar*. The place of passage. *Al-ma'bar alladhi sara nafs al-kabsh fihi*. (The passage in which the soul of the ram has traveled). ...he does not eat it except the place of passage. The human. *Ma'bar insan*. From which that thing passes. *Wa huwa al-hafiz li fuzalat al-awliya'*. (And it is the protector of the leftovers of the saints). And it is the one... And it is the one who protects the *fuzalat* (leftovers/grace) of the *awliya'* (saints). The *fuzalat* of the *awliya'* of Allah, which are left over from their meals and all things, the *'ammud al-nur* protects them so that they reach specific, special people. *Wa al-mumayyiz laha min ghayriha*. (And the one that distinguishes it from other than it). And it distinguishes... things get mixed in air, water, and earth. But how do they get separated? In 1000 years, the limbs of that same person appear again in the same way. Who protects them? *'Ammud al-nur*. This is called *'inayat ilahiyyah* (divine providence), divine arrangements (*tadbirat*). It is called divine decrees (*muqaddarat ilahiyyah*). All are related to it. Is this solely related to *wilayat* (devotion)? In whom does this capability lie? In *awliya'*. The *awliya'*... The noble elders. It is related to *wilayat*. *Awliya'* means those who love. Those who have the leaven of *wilayah*, they are called *wali*. The *wilayah* of Mawla Ali is necessary for this, because *'ammud al-nur* is only and only for those who take the *'ahd al-sharif* (noble covenant) and have *wilayah*. *Wa al-mumayyiz laha min ghayriha*. (And the one that distinguishes it from other than it). And the one who differentiates it for them from other than them. *Wa al-mustakhrij laha min haythu kanat*. (And the one who extracts it from wherever it may be). And the one who extracts it from wherever it may be. Wherever they may be, whether in fire, air, water, earth, or minerals, wherever they may be, it extracts them and brings them. Is this for every single thing? For our forms, for the *fuzalat*, for... for every single thing. *Wa yuqalu 'alayha al-'ilm al-jari wa al-nur al-sari wa al-ruh wa al-kalimah wa jami' suwar al-wujud al-ruhaniyyah wa al-jismaniyyah*. (And it is called the flowing knowledge, the pervading light, the spirit, the word, and all the forms of spiritual and physical existence). And it is said about it that it is flowing knowledge, it is pervading light, it is spirit, and it is the word. The word. *Kalimah*. The *kalimah la ilaha illa allah*. *Wa jami' suwar al-wujud al-ruhaniyyah wa al-jismaniyyah wa atba'uhum min al-'aql al-awwal ila al-mustajib bihi muttasilun wa ilayhi ma'dhufun*. (And all the forms of spiritual and physical existence, and their followers, from the First Intellect to the respondent, are connected by it and are joined to it). And all... and all the forms of spiritual existence and all the forms of physical existence and their followers, their followers, from the *'aql awwal* up to the *mustajib* (respondent), are connected to that *nur*, to that *'ammud*. And to it they are joined. *Wilayat* is love. As Hasan Shakir Sahab stated in a discourse, *al-mar'u yuhsharu ma'a man ahabba* (A person will be resurrected with whom he loves). A person will be resurrected with that same one with whom he loves. As soon as you love from your heart, your connection is established with him. *Al-mar'u yuhsharu ma'a man ahabba*. And they are connected with that same *'ammud al-nur*. *Wa mathaluhu ka mathali 'udin mamdudin qad asabahu al-'asal*. (And its example is like the example of an extended stick of wood that has been touched by honey). And its example is like the example of a stick of *'ud* (aloeswood), an extended stick on which honey has been applied. *Fa idha waqa'a 'alayha al-dhubab lam yakid yubarihu*. (So when flies land on it, they can hardly leave it). The 'm' of *lam* has been erased. In the book... It says *lam yakid yubarih*. What is written? *Lam*... a 'q' has been hidden. *Lam yakid yubarihu*. From here itself that book was copied. It's not there, it's not there in the beginning. *Lam yakid yubarihu*. And when flies land on it, when flies land on it, they do not leave it. They are not close to leaving it. They stick to it. *Wa kadhalika al-suwar la tubarihu hadha al-'ammud*. (And likewise the forms do not leave this pillar). In the same way, these forms do not leave this *'ammud al-nur*. All the forms are connected to it. It is a powerful magnet. The forms... with the forms, the souls are also connected. *Li anna huwa al-hamil laha*. (Because it is the carrier of them). Because that *'ammud al-nur* is the one who carries those forms. *Wa al-jazib wa al-murtaqi laha 'inda su'udiha*. (And the attractor and the one that elevates them at the time of their ascent). And the one who attracts and the one who gives progress to those... to that *'ammud al-nur*... to those forms, at the time of the ascent of those forms. *Wa min dhalika anna al-munafiq wa al-murtadd wa al-maghdub 'alayhi tuslabu suratuhu tilka al-ilahiyyah allati kanat 'indahu li ta'alluqiha bi dhalika al-'ammud al-munasib laha. Wa ta'udu nafsuhu naqisatan sha'i'atan fi jismihi*. (And from that, the hypocrite, the apostate, and the one who has incurred wrath, his form is snatched away, that divine one which was with him, because of its connection to that pillar which is appropriate for it. And his soul returns, deficient and base in his body). And from this matter, this is also a matter, that the hypocrite and the apostate, the one who changes his religion, and the one upon whom Allah has sent His wrath, his form is snatched away. That divine one... The divine one which was with him, because of his connection with that *'ammud* which is appropriate for it. And his soul returns... returns, deficient, base, pervading his body. And this, the *maghdub 'alayh* (one who has incurred wrath), is that his *hadd 'ali* (high rank)? The one who... upon whom wrath came... Is it Allah's wrath or the wrath of the *Rabb* (Lord)? The *Rabb*'s. *Tuslabu suratuhu tilka al-ilahiyyah*. It means... what was explained... his divine form which had been created, a good one... that *'ammud al-nur* snatches it away. Snatches it away. A good form was created. Because of which its connection was established with that *'ammud al-nur* which is appropriate for that divine form. And his soul returns... the soul that had become good, what happens? It is... *'Ammud al-nur* takes it. The form that has become good, *'ammud al-nur* takes it. Like in the case of Dawood, the wife of Uriah... a form, a good one, was created... that was... it was said that this form was taken out from him and given to whom? To Zainab, the daughter of Hukman. For her training. In the same way, that *'ammud al-nur* takes that form. Takes it. Who is its owner, the *'ammud al-nur*? It doesn't have an owner. To whomever it needs to be given, it will be given. For now, it is kept there, taken. *'Ammud al-nur* takes its thing. And his soul returns, deficient. Deficient, meaning base. Pervading the body. Pervading his body. *Li anna dhalika al-'ammud huwa al-mumsik li tilka al-suwar al-ilahiyyah al-jabidh laha*. (Because that pillar is the one that holds those divine forms, the one that attracts them). Because that... because that *'ammud al-nur* is the one that holds and attracts those divine forms. *Wa mata talaba wahidun min al-hudud aw al-mustajibin mubasharat ahlihi*. (And whenever one of the ranks or the respondents desires intimacy with his spouse). And when any one of the *hudud* or *mustajibin* seeks to be intimate with his spouse. Meaning, when... at the time of beneficence and benefiting... When he has intimacy. *Malat 'anhu tilka al-suwar*. (Those forms turn away from him). That *'ammud al-nur* turns away from him. Turns away. *Wa inharakat 'anhu*. (And deviates from him). From him. *Hatta la tu'ayinu min dhalika shay'an illa waqt al-firagh*. (Until you do not see anything of that except at the time of completion). Until he does not see from that matter any thing except at the time of completion. Who does not see? The *'ammud al-nur* does not see. *Wa 'adat ka halatiha*. (And it returns to its state). It returns to its state. In the state of *janabat* (ritual impurity). In a state of non-purity. In a state of non-purity. *Wa 'adat ka halatiha*. (And it returns to its state). And that form returns to its original state. *Lutfan min allah ta'ala*. (As a kindness from God, the Exalted). As a kindness from Allah Ta'ala. As a kindness from Allah Ta'ala towards His servants. And looking upon them. And by Allah Ta'ala looking upon them. *Wa rahmatan lahum*. (And as a mercy for them). And as a mercy for them. *Fa subhanahu wa ta'ala 'amma yaqul al-zalimun 'uluwwan kabira*. (So glorified and exalted is He above what the wrongdoers say in great arrogance). So Allah is pure from that matter and is exalted from that matter which the unjust people say, a great saying. The form that was disconnected, when he performs *ghusl*, then it gets reconnected. And for women too, when they perform *ghusl*... *'Ammud al-nur*... The child is not touched until... Because of this, prayer is forbidden during menstruation. She does not perform *ghusl*. She is in a state of impurity. That's one thing he explained, an example. So in the intention for *ghusl*, what is that thing we say that makes the *'ammud al-nur* reconnect with us? Just by making the intention that we are purifying ourselves... The greatest thing is the *kalimat*. *A'udhu billah min al-shaytan al-rajim, Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*. This is the greatest *kalimah*. They say, the Prophet, peace be upon him, says, *fi kulli sha'ratin janabah*. In your every hair there is *janabat* (ritual impurity). In every single hair there is *janabat*. One should wash with water so much that every hair... the hair should be washed very well. And women especially, their hair should be washed very well. They have long hair. *Fi kulli sha'ratin janabah*. The clothes that were there at the time of intimacy, they should not be worn at the time of prayer.

<!-- lecture 19 -->

...and the *mabda* and *ma'ād* of light is what we have explained. *Wa yazīduhu bayānan*, and it further clarifies it, *an al-Nāṭiq al-dawr ṣalawātullāhi 'alayhi kāna fī ibtidā'i amrihi*... *ibtidā'i amrihi*, *amrihi*, *idhā 'āyana sūrat al-malak*, *sūrat al-malak*, *al-malakī*, *alladhī yatajallī lahū*, *alladhī yatajallā lahū*, *alladhī yatajallā lahū al-musammā bi-Jibrā'īl, aah, ghashiya 'alayhi min 'aẓm nūrihi*, *'aẓm nūrihi*, *alladhī yu'āyinuhū*, *alladhī yu'āyinuhū*, *yu'āyinuhū, ḥattā khālat al-aḍdād wa ahl al-fikr wa ahl al-kufr wa al-'inād annahū junna, wa anna dhālik al-ghashyah*, *junna*, *junna*. Aah. And that supports our statement and confirms our statement and it gives it further clarification, *an al-Nāṭiq al-dawr* (that the *Nāṭiq* of the era), the *Nāṭiq* of the sixth era, blessings of Allah be upon him, was in the beginning of his affair, that when he would see, when he would see the form of the angel, the form of the angel, who would manifest before him, who was named, whose name was Jibrā'īl, a state of being overcome would descend upon him from the greatness of his light, which he used to see, that is, he used to see him... *ghashiya 'alayhi*, meaning, he would fall down unconscious. *ghashiya 'alayhi*. He would fall down from being overcome. From the greatness of that light which he used to see. *Ḥattā khālat al-aḍdād*, to the extent that the opponents and the people of thought and the people of disbelief and the people of stubbornness would say that a jinn had come upon him, that a jinn had taken possession of him, *wa anna dhālika al-ghashiyah ṣara'*. And that being overcome was epilepsy, meaning, it is epilepsy. *Fa-qāla Waraqah li-Khadījah bint Khuwaylid raḍīyallāhu 'anhumā*. So, Waraqa bin Nawfal, may Allah's mercy be upon them both... So, Waraqa bin Nawfal said to Khadījah bint Khuwaylid, for... Allah's mercy be upon you both. *Wa kāna... Wa kāna 'āliman kāhinan*. He was a scholar. And he was a soothsayer. *Muntaẓiran li-ẓuhūr al-Nāṭiq al-sādis*. Awaiting the appearance of the sixth *Nāṭiq*. Who? Waraqa bin Nawfal. He was waiting in the era of 'Īsā 'alayhis salām for the appearance of the sixth *Nāṭiq*, Muḥammad al-Muṣṭafā ṣalawātullāhi 'alayh.

So here, the purpose of saying this is that Jibrā'īl 'alayhis salām is also a part of the Column of Light. That's the intention of saying this, the whole thing. And he will explain that further. Good.

*Alladhī huwa Muḥammadun ṣalawātullāhi 'alayhi*. That is, he is, Mawlānā Muhammad ṣalawātullāhi 'alayhi is... *Idhā 'āyanti*, *idhā 'āyanti dhālik al-amr*. When you see that matter. That is, Waraqa bin Nawfal said to Janāb Khadījah that, "When you see this matter about Janāb Rasūlullāh, *fa-ajā'ahu*, *fa-ajā'ahu fa-atrukīhi 'alā fakhidhik al-yumnā*. So when he comes, then place him, on your right thigh. So when Jibrā'īl comes to you, then make him sit on your right thigh. *Wa qūlī lahū hal tarā shay'an*. And ask him, do you see anything? *Wa huwa yaqūlu na'am*. So he will say, yes. *fa-atrukīhi 'alā fakhidhik al-yumnā*, *fa-atrukīhi 'alā fakhidhik al-yusrā*. Then make him sit, place him on your left thigh. *Wa qūlī lahū hal tarā shay'an*. And say to him, "Do you see anything?" And Janāb Waraqa bin Nawfal is telling Khadījah to do this. And for Rasūlullāh, "What, do you see anything?" *Thumma ḥawwilihī 'alayhi 'alā sadrīki*. So he will say, you, "Yes." Then he will say that, "Yes." Then turn him towards your chest. *Wa sa'alīhi kamā sa'alti awwalan*. And ask him as you had asked the first time. *Thumma ikshifī ra'saki*. Then uncover your head. Uncover the hair on your head. *Wa sa'alīhi kamā sa'alti awwalan*. And ask him in the same way you had asked the first time. *Fa-in kāna majnūnan fa-yaqūlu na'am, fa-in kāna nabiyyan mursalan Nāṭiqan fa-yaqūlu mā arā shay'an*. For if he is possessed, then he will say yes, and if he is a Prophet, a sent messenger, a *Nāṭiq*, he will say, "I see nothing." *Li'annahū wallā 'an 'awratiki*. Because he, he turned away from your private parts. Because the one who is an angel will turn away from your private parts.

That is why the ruling is that a woman, without covering her hair, if she prays, her prayer is not accepted. That is, from the private parts. And this is why it is said of 'Amr ibn al-'Āṣ, may Allah curse him... When Amir al-Mu'minin ṣalawātullāhi 'alayhi... pursued him to kill him, *kashafa 'an saw'atihi*. He uncovered his private parts. And for this reason, it is said that 'Amr ibn al-'Āṣ had heard from this statement of Waraqa bin Nawfal, by way of Khadījah 'alayhas salām, that the angels do not look at private parts. This is why it is said, and about this, Abū Firāz, may Allah have mercy on him, said... *Wa lā khayra fī daf' al-radā bi-madhammatin kamā raddahū yawman bi-saw'atihi 'Amr*. And there is no good in averting destruction with disgrace, just as 'Amr averted it one day with his private parts. That is, it is better to be killed than to avert destruction with disgrace. As he repelled it one day from his private parts, 'Amr ibn al-'Āṣ averted his own death. He exposed his private parts, and Janāb 'Alī turned his face away. So, a famous incident about 'Amr ibn al-'Āṣ. In the Battle of Siffin, he did this.

And what is it? It is 'Amr, 'ayn mīm rā. One word is 'Umar, one is 'Amr. 'Umar is... 'ayn mīm rā, with a pesh on the 'ayn. 'ayn mīm rā wāw is how it is. With a pesh. So that is read as 'Amr. If it is 'Umar, then it is 'ayn mīm rā. So, after Hazrat Qibla Sahab passed away, some incidents happened. One day, you went to a gathering. So, in it, the speaker, who was the *khatib*, he began to narrate the story of the conqueror of Egypt. He had conquered Egypt. He had attacked and conquered. 'Amr bin al-'Āṣ, on behalf of Mu'āwiyah. He was narrating his incidents, how he conquered, how he took his armies and what he did. So, he used to say, Amrū bin al-'Āṣ. He would read it as Amrū bin al-'Āṣ. Instead of 'Amr, 'Amr, he would say 'Amrū. Because there is a wāw in it, isn't there? One is 'Umar, one is 'Amrū. He used to say 'Amrū bin al-'Āṣ. So, he would say 'Amrū bin al-'Āṣ. So, when the sermon ended, he came and met Hazrat. So, he said, "Mawlānā, what kind of gathering did you find?" He said, "You gave a powerful speech, but I don't know who this Amrū sahib is." "Who is this Amrū bin al-'Āṣ, I don't know." He said, "He is the conqueror of Egypt, and you don't know him?" He said, "The conqueror of Egypt, his name was 'Amr bin al-'Āṣ. You have invented a new 'Amrū bin al-'Āṣ." So, he said, "You have read the book, but you have not heard it from an *ustādh* how that word should be read." "You have not studied properly with an *ustādh*. You just saw the word and read it as 'Amrū bin al-'Āṣ." Now, you write "khud" yourself. I came myself. How do you write it? You write khay dāl. No. What do you write? Khay wāw dāl. Khay wāw dāl. The Persian word is "khud". You write khay wāw dāl. "I came myself in person." If one reads that as "khawd", "I came myself in khawd." Does he say, "I came myself in khud"? If someone has not heard it from an author or composer, and says, "I came in 'khawd' myself," then what is this person reading? So, at that time, Hazrat was the principal. So, whenever we used to have the ḥakīm Imām Bakhsh's residence, Hazrat would say, "Come on, we're going to 'Amrū bin al-'Āṣ's majlis."

The Column of Light was being discussed, that in a state of nakedness, the Column of Light does not come.

But here, you are talking about angels. That is related to Jibrā'īl, to Jibrā'īl. It is an *ittiṣāl* of light that is being described. That Janāb the Prophet has an *ittiṣāl* with the Column of Light. The *ittiṣāl* of Janāb Jibrā'īl is through him. And the Column of Light, it is cut off when private parts appear in front. The Column of Light which is connected becomes disconnected.

So here, Jibrā'īl means the Column of Light? The one who brings the Column of Light. The one who establishes the connection with the Column of Light.

*Al-Faṣl al-rābi' min al-bāb al-thānī min surādiq al-thānī, wa qad ramaza al-kitāb al-karīm bi-hādhā al-umūr, wa huwa qawluhu ta'ālā, yunazzil al-rūḥ min amrihi 'alā man yashā'u min 'ibādihi*. (The Fourth Chapter of the Second Section of the Second Pavilion. The Noble Book has alluded to these matters in His, the Exalted's, saying: He sends down the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants.) And an indication has been given in the Noble Book about this matter, from Allah's saying, that... and that is the saying of Allah the Exalted. He sends down the Spirit. By His command. Upon whomever He wishes from His servants. The Spirit refers to the Column of Light. What is in it? *Yunazzil*, what is in it? *Tanazzul al-malā'ikatu wa-l-rūḥ*. *Tanazzul al-malā'ikatu wa-l-rūḥu fīhā*. The angels descend upon your soul... the angels and the Spirit descend. The Spirit is... so the connection of the Column of Light is established. *Wa huwa ayḍan ḥaqīqat al-waḥy*. And that is also the reality of revelation. That the Column of Light itself is revelation. Knowledge flowed from it, the light became manifest. And where did it emerge from, the Column of Light? The word of *Lā ilāha*. From there it emerged. That same word is called light. It is called the flowing light, the manifest light. As it was mentioned *alladhī yajrī 'alā thalāthat aqsāmin*, that is, revelation flows in three types. *Kamā qāla Allāhu ta'ālā wa mā kāna li-basharin an yukallimahullāhu illā waḥyan aw min warā'i ḥijābin aw yursila rasūlan fa-yūḥiya bi-idhnihi mā yashā'*. As Allah the Exalted has said, "And it is not for any human being that Allah should speak to him." It is not for any human being that Allah should speak to him except by *waḥy*. That is, through revelation. *Aw min warā'i ḥijāb*. Or from behind a veil. *Aw yursila rasūlan*. Or He sends a messenger. *Fa-yūḥiya bi-idhnihi mā yashā'*. And He reveals with Allah's permission what He wills.

As Allah the Exalted says, that it is not for any human, that Allah should speak to him, except through revelation, or from behind a veil, or by sending a messenger, and He reveals what He wishes with His permission. There are three ways. Revelation, from behind a veil, or a messenger. *Al-awwal minhā rutbat al-Jadd, alladhī kallafa-hullāhu ta'ālā al-waḥy*. And the first of them is the flowing of the *Rūḥ al-Quds* without an intermediary, connected to the chosen messenger (*mab'ūth al-mukhtār*) at every time and moment. And that is upon the ranks of... And its special meaning has been explained. And... the rank of revelation is the highest. That which is done through revelation, its rank is high. And the first thing of speech is the rank of *Jadd*. The first of them is the rank of *Jadd*. Meaning, with every Imam, there are three individuals who are above, who convey the commands of the one above. The *Jadd*, the second is *Fath*, the third is *Khayal*. These three are there. The first is what? *Jadd*. They do it through revelation. Meaning, Allah and the Imam, between them the intermediaries are three. Three intermediaries. *Jadd*, *Fath*, and *Khayal*. The rank of *Jadd*. This rank of *Jadd*, as Allah the Exalted has appointed for the matter of revelation. And that is the flowing from the *Rūḥ al-Quds* without an intermediary, connected to the one who has been sent, the chosen one. He who is the chosen one, every time and moment, at the ranks. And he is at the ranks. In the three ranks, the highest rank is what? It is the rank of revelation. It is *Jadd*. They are the *Jadd* who... their job is to bring the commands from Allah the Exalted. It is the responsibility of the *Jadd* of the Exalted. They reveal it through revelation. All their commands. *Jadd* of the Exalted. And it is flowing from the *Rūḥ al-Quds*. *Rūḥ al-Quds* means what? *Rūḥ al-Quds* is from... It is flowing from *Rūḥ al-Quds*, meaning the *Nafs 'Azīmah*, it can also mean the Tenth. Without an intermediary. Meaning, there is no intermediary. *Jadd* and *Rūḥ al-Quds*, there is no intermediary between them. From the *'Ayn 'Azīmah*. From the *'Ayn 'Azīmah*. The commands that come to *Jadd* come without an intermediary. It is connected to the sent one, the chosen one. It is connected to whom? To the one who has been sent with a mission, the chosen one. Such as the Prophet and every Imam of the time, there are three above them: *Jadd*, *Fath*, *Khayal*. The Imam is, above the Imam are *Jadd*, *Fath*, *Khayal*. They are of a higher rank. They reveal the commands to him. *Jadd*, *Fath*, *Khayal*, a *Nāṭiq* who is... the seventh, who is... an Imam of a higher rank. *Jadd*, *Fath*, *Khayal*, and the Prophet, the Imam is higher than him. No. *Jadd*, *Fath*, *Khayal* are of a higher rank than the Imam.

So, these three are realities. They are abstract realities. They are... from the realm of pure intellects. *Wāḥid*, *tajrīd*. *Wahdajīd*. *Jadd*, *Fath*, and *Khayal*. So they are above the Imam in rank, from whom the Imam receives aid from the 'Ayn 'Azīmah. The Imam of Imams is who? The 'Ayn 'Azīmah. The Imam of Imams. The 'Ayn 'Azīmah, the 12 Ḥujjats, they are... how are they connected to the Imam? Through *Jadd*, *Fath*, and *Khayal*. These are three ranks that are above the Imam, through which all things are received.

So these, are they, are they mostly Shari'ah commands or... for running all the world's affairs? If it is the Shari'ah of the time, Shari'ah commands. If not that, then the commands of the ṭarīqah, it will be according to that. Whichever rank one has, if one is a *Rasūl Nāṭiq*, then it is the ranks of *Risālat*. And if he is only a Prophet, then it is the things of *Nubuwwat*. If it is Imamate, then it is the things of spiritual Imamate. Whatever mission one is entrusted with, it is according to that.

So, as the hidden Imam is here now... He has, I mean, a passage inside him. For him, there are three ranks: *Jadd*, *Fath*, and *Khayal*. With every Imam, there are three ranks. Above them are those of a higher rank. If the Imam is of the first degree, then the second, third, fourth ranks... if he is of the seventh degree, then whoever is higher than the seventh will be his *Jadd* and so on. If it is a Prophet, then above him are *Jadd*, *Fath*, *Khayal*. If it is an 'Ayn 'Azīmah, he also has a *Jadd*, *Fath*, *Khayal*. Above him are the three ranks which are *Jadd*, *Fath*, *Khayal* of the *Manzil*. With every rank, there are three ranks, which have been commanded that Allah does not speak. The conversation takes place so that His commands can be delivered. For the betterment of the world, for the progress of religion, and for this universe to progress, commands are delivered. How are the commands delivered? By God the Exalted, in three ways. Revelation, from behind a veil, or He sends a messenger. These are the three ways. They are explaining the three ways, that *Jadd*, *Fath*, and *Khayal* are there.

So, an Imam, an Imam, and a Rasūl, if they are there at the same time, Mawlānā 'Alī and Rasūlullāh. So their *Jadd*, *Fath*, *Khayal* will be different? They will be different, different. Their *Jadd*, *Fath*, *Khayal* will be separate. Janāb 'Alī's will be separate, Rasūlullāh's will be separate. And for Rasūlullāh, it is necessary that his grandfather, uncle, and father are... For the Prophet, it has been explained. For *Jadd*, it is Janāb... it has been explained, for *Jadd* it is Janāb 'Abd al-Muṭṭalib, Janāb Abū Ṭālib, Janāb 'Abdullāh. This is the physical... grandfather, uncle, and father. It could be anyone for them. Yes, it could be anyone. This is not necessary. For a *Muntakha* also, they are there. Janāb 'Alī, Janāb... for 'Alī, for whom... it has been explained separately for him. *Jadd*, *Fath*, *Khayal*. And for every Imam, there are separate ones. At the time of every Imam... *Satr* or *kashf*, as it may be, according to that. There are ten ranks of Imamate above him. So *Jadd*, *Fath*, *Khayal*, should it come in the physical lineage of the Imam? No, they are of a higher rank. So, now this is coming in the physical lineage of the Imam, Janāb 'Abd al-Muṭṭalib, Abū Ṭālib, and 'Abdullāh. So, I mean, of a higher rank. *Walad*, *wālid*, *dādā*. That should be *walad*, *wālid*. No, it's explained there, that those of a higher rank. The rank of Imamate, what is it? The Imamate has ten degrees. For the one of the first degree, who will be his *Jadd*, *Fath*, *Khayal*? The three ranks before that. If it is the seventh, then the three ranks above the seventh. If he is the one who possesses two *ḥujjats*, then the three ranks above that. If he is the *Qā'im*, then the three ranks above that. As is the case, it will be according to that.

For a *Muntakha* too, there is a *Jadd*, *Fath*, and *Khayal*. For an Imam, it is not necessary. It is necessary for everyone. For everyone. *Muntakha*, Imams. For *Awliyā'* also? For *Awliyā'*, for everyone. *Awliyā'* have... for Imams, the rank is high. Imam. The rank of... So in the verse, for 'Ayn 'Azīmah also there will be? Yes, there will be. Three ranks, which are above it. The rank which is of 'Ayn 'Azīmah, above that, there is the rank of *Jadd*, *Fath*, *Khayal*. *Wa huwa 'alā al-marātib*. And it is the highest of ranks. The rank of *Jadd* is the highest of ranks.

*Wa al-thānī rutbat al-Fath alladhī huwa min warā'i ḥijābin, wa huwa idrāk al-ashyā' bi-l-fikrat al-ṣāfiyah wa al-ibṣār al-maḍrūbah*. And the second, in rank, is *Fath*. Which is from behind a veil. And that is the perception of things, through pure thought, and from the examples that are given. How many times in the Quran, it has worked with *amthāl maḍrūbah*. The stories of Mūsā, etc., and this and that, wherever it is, it has worked with *amthāl maḍrūbah*. The matter is explained through examples. Like, by knowledge, water is meant. To build a wall. This... to build a wall, as Janāb Khidr and Mūsā... they built a wall. To make a hole in the boat. These are all *amthāl maḍrūbah*. Meaning, an example, the one who understands, understands. That what the person in front is saying. But outwardly, it is an example. As if I said to you, "Look, a palm tree is coming from the front." What does that mean? A tall person is coming. A tall person is coming. "A Dunlop tire is coming from the front." What does that mean? A fat person is coming. It's an example. The one who understands, understands what it is. If a child says, "Where is the Dunlop tire?", "Where is it?". "A fast horse is coming from the front." What does that mean? A rider is coming, riding swiftly. So, as the person in front says, if both understand, then action is taken accordingly.

So what, what are you trying to explain here? He is perceiving things. With thought. *Wa al-thānī rutbat al-Fath, wa huwa min warā'i ḥijāb*. That is, behind a veil, it happens. What? It is the perception of things with pure thought and from the given examples. He gives a ta'wil. What is the ta'wil of a thing? Behind a veil, meaning, the matter is not said plainly. It is said within the veil of words. Commands come within the veil of words. That is, it is not announced publicly.

*Wa al-thālith rutbat al-Khayal, wa huwa al-malak al-mursal, fa-yūḥiya bi-idhnihi mā yashā'u, al-mumaththal basharan sawiyyan, dhū al-quwwah, allatī tuwāṣiluhu min Dār al-Quds*. And the third is the rank of *Khayal*. And he is the angel who has been sent, so he reveals with His permission what He wills. The one who appears as a well-proportioned man, possessing power, which connects him from the Abode of Holiness. That is, as speech that is heard, or as a form seen by the eye. The voice can be heard. Both can also happen. Syedna Ali Sahib used to narrate that during Aurangzeb's court, at that time he was the governor of Gujarat. And he... Syedna Hasan Khan, he... what happened? There was a debate about religion, and he gestured to someone to take them outside and kill them. "Take them outside." So at that time, two horsemen came before them. So he says in the *diwan*, Syedna Muhammad 'Izzuddin appeared in that form. And said, both of them, *lā takhāfā wa-lā taḥzanā, innanī ma'akumā asma'u wa arā* (Do not fear and do not grieve, for I am with you both, hearing and seeing). You should not fear, nor should you grieve. I am with you. And they brought them into the market. And after bringing them, there was some chaos in the market there. They said to you, "Go." So you came out. Meaning, a person came. A person came, and his voice was heard. *Lā takhāfā wa-lā taḥzanā, innanī ma'akumā*.

So they are people of the rank of *Khayal*. *Khayal*. And in other incidents, many incidents have been narrated. One incident is narrated that it was the first of Rajab. And... the one who... Dawood bin Qutub, Qutub bin Dawood, Qutub Shahīd, whose shrine has been built... his son. So, Aurangzeb had... Aurangzeb's... he had him killed. He was killed. His corpse, it was... dogs were eating it, all these things. And after that, Syedna Ali Sahib, everyone told him that you should leave from here. Leave Ahmedabad and go to some other place. So you said, "Until I receive the command from my Master, I will not go from here." And on the night of the first of Rajab, you prayed. On the first of Rajab, the day it dawned. And during the prayer, you received the command that you should leave from here. Leave this place and go. So in this way, you heard a voice that someone is giving a command that you should leave this place now. You... your family, all of them... you had said to your followers, but you said, "Until I receive the command, I will not leave." You received the command at night. At dawn, at the time of Fajr prayer, you reached there, to the mosque of the common people. You prayed the Fajr prayer there, and at the earliest time, you prayed Fajr and left from there. To Gujarat... to the countryside of Gujarat. For six months, you were in the countryside of Gujarat. You are narrating this whole story. Until Aurangzeb... after six months, when the Eid al-Fitr... you again... again, Ahmedabad, at the place of the shrine... the Eid prayer was held. The incidents are narrated that at night you received the command. And Aurangzeb's men came looking for you. To capture you and to kill you. The people of the whole mosque, the family members said that he has gone to the mosque. When they reached the mosque, the Imam said, "He just prayed the prayer. After praying here, he left a little while ago." And they were searching behind. You reached the countryside of Gujarat. And you were in the countryside of Gujarat. So here also... So *Khayal* means what they are saying? A vision can also appear, or in the form of a voice, it can also happen. *Ammā qawlan bil-sam'i, wa ammā tashakhkhuṣan bi-ru'yat al-'ayn*.

*Wa hādhihi al-quwwah allatī tuwāṣiluhu min Dār al-Quds, wa huwa al-ḥadd al-sārī min Rūḥ al-Quds. Fa-idhā al-Quds mubda' al-awwal kamā sabaqa bihi al-qawl*. So, this is the power that connects him from the Abode of Holiness. And that is the flowing limit from the Spirit of Holiness. So, Holiness is the first principle, as has been preceded in speech. This power, which... connects from the *Dār al-Quds*. And that is the flowing limit, which is flowing from *Rūḥ al-Quds*. So, *Rūḥ al-Quds* is the first intellect. It is the chain. From the first intellect, there is a chain. From them, the luminous limit... is established, which, in the form of *Khayal*, is heard or seen.

*Wa ilā hādhā al-'umūd ishārah Sayyidnā Ibrāhīm...* 'umūd. *Wa ilā hādhā al-'umūd ishārah Sayyidnā Ibrāhīm bin al-Ḥusayn qaddasallāhu rūḥahumā, qāla... 'inda naqlatihi Sayyidnā 'Alī bin al-Ḥusayn, an al-laqab al-sārī*, *al-laqab al-sārī ta'allaqa bil-jārī*. And towards this pillar, there is an indication from our master Ibrāhīm bin al-Ḥusayn, may Allah sanctify their souls. He said, "At the time of the passing of our master 'Alī bin al-Ḥusayn... The flowing title became attached to the flowing." And towards this pillar, Syedna Ibrāhīm... Syedna Ibrāhīm bin al-Ḥusayn al-Ḥāmidī said, may Allah elevate their rank, he commanded, he said, at the time of the passing of Syedna 'Alī bin al-Ḥusayn, *al-laqab al-sārī, ta'allaqa bil-jārī*. The connection was made with the flowing. He became united with the flowing. Meaning, it is an indication towards the Column of Light. Upon his passing, the Column of Light drew you in.

*Wa lam yulā'im, wa lam yulā'im, wa lam yulā'im jānib al-ṭabī'ah 'ālī wa-l-dānī*. And he was not suited, the high and low aspects of nature. He was not suited. The world of nature. For him... what does it mean? In the world of nature... the *qāfiyah* is... that the Column of Light, your connection was established with it. The Column of Light drew your form. *Lammā ittaṣala bil-'ināyat al-sāriyah, warada 'alā ahl al-na'īm al-bāhirah al-sāmi'ah ilā ḥaḍrat al-ẓāhirah, majma' ajzā' al-ṭāhirah, allatī hiya ilayhā sā'irat al-mawjūd fī al-ḥāḍirah, al-muntaẓir li-wujūdihim wa wurūd amthālihim wa atbā'ihim wa ashbāhihim, ḥattā idhā wafā al-'adad wa balaghat muddat al-amad, ẓaharat al-qubbat al-'abbāsiyyah*.

This is what they are saying. After the passing of Janāb 'Alī bin al-Ḥusayn, Ibrāhīm bin al-Ḥusayn Ḥāmidī, who is the second *Dā'ī*... Sayyidnā Ibrāhīm bin al-Ḥusayn al-Ḥāmidī, the second *Dā'ī* is... and Sayyidnā 'Alī bin al-Ḥusayn, Sayyidnā Dhu'ayb had appointed him. After his passing... Sayyidnā Ibrāhīm bin al-Ḥusayn became the *Dā'ī*. After him...

When he became connected with the flowing grace, he appeared to the people of bliss, in the brilliant, sublime, manifest presence, the gathering place of the pure parts, towards which the entirety of existence in the present world is journeying, awaiting their existence and the arrival of their likes, followers, and counterparts. To the extent that when the number was fulfilled and the duration reached its term, the Abbasid dome appeared. It is the gathering place of the luminous spirits. The gathering place of the spirits. He reached there. *Al-muntaẓir li-wujūdihim wa wurūd amthālihim wa atbā'ihim wa ashbā'ihim*. Awaiting their existence, and the arrival of their likes, followers, and counterparts. *Ḥattā idhā wafā al-'adad, wa balaghat muddat al-amad*. Until, when the number was complete, and the term reached its limit. When the number is complete in one of the paradises, then the next paradise appears. *Bi-anwār al-shā'sha'ah*. By the radiant lights. *Wa tajallā bi-hādhihi al-'umūd*. And it was manifested by this pillar of light. *Wa ẓahara bil-ḥaqq fī awān al-ẓuhūr, fī ḥaḍīrat al-quds 'inda bāb al-ḥijāb*. And it appeared with truth at the time of manifestation. In the enclosure of holiness, near the gate of the veil. The veil of the Imam, near its gate, you reached. This is what they are explaining. You reached that paradise.

So the radiant lights, what is that? The radiant, luminous spirits. The souls that are ready. They reach the Column of Light. The paradise of the Column of Light. Yes. They all are related to the Column of Light. Where there is flowing light, flowing knowledge. And its connection is with what? With the gate of the veil. The veil of Imam al-Zaman, with its gate. The gate of the inner Imam. Yes. The sacred enclosure means the Imam's presence. Not in his presence, but near the gate of the veil he reached. The Jannat al-Ma'wa, as it is called.

*Fa-lammā istaqarra dhālika ayyuhā al-akh al-mu'min, fa'lam anna hādhā al-'umūd...* So, as this is a subtle point, so know, O believing brother, that for this pillar... a flowing example... the Column of Light is all... spiritual. Not physical. Not physical light. Not physical. That which is luminous. Spiritual luminosity. That our prayers, they... can be seen in the Column of Light actually... if it becomes dense. The prayer of someone... it can be seen, it's not a thing that can't be seen. Like the vision. That is... that Syedna Muhammad 'Izzuddin appeared. Syedna 'Alī sahib has mentioned, Syedna Muhammad 'Izzuddin appeared in the form of... Syedna 'Alī sahib has mentioned. Syedna... 'Izzuddin... is in the rank of *Khayal*. And Syedna Ja'far is in the rank of *Fath*. And Syedna Sulaymān is in the rank of *Jadd*.

So this... these souls that... our *nafs nāṭiqah* that is going, is it being processed in the Column of Light or is it just being stored? It joins. A connection is established. The connection of its light is established with it. Its *nafs nāṭiqah*... if he has had a good end, then its connection is joined with the *nafs nāṭiqah*. Its virtues... become connected to it. Whatever its portion is.

Yes.

*Ayyuhā al-akh al-mu'min, fa-lammā istaqarra dhālika*. So, for this is a subtle point, so know, O believing brother, that for this pillar... an example has been given. We should proceed from here.

So the Column of Light is all... spiritual. Not physical light. Not physical. That which is luminous. Spiritual luminosity. Luminous means, it's not physical light. Physical light is a very dense thing. The real light is that of the Column of Light. Spiritual light.

<!-- lecture 20 -->

*Bismillah*. *Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*. Then, this virtuous person, *Salāmu'llāhi 'alayh* (peace of Allah be upon him), established his mission until he brought out—until he brought out from it his son who—when he brought out from it his son who deputizes in his place and stands in his position. He is the one designated as *al-inbi'āth* (the Evolved/Emanated), just as this person is designated as *al-ibdā'* (the Origination). He is designated as *al-ibdā'* because whatever is in this world, they are counterparts to *al-ibdā'* (the Origination) and *al-inbi'āth* (the Emanation) in the lesser world. *Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*. The fifth *fasl* (chapter), from the second *bāb* (section), from the second *surādiq* (canopy). Then that virtuous person—may Allah Ta'ala's peace be upon you—this virtuous person. This virtuous person. *Salāmu'llāhi 'alayh*. Established—established his mission, until—*ṣāḥib al-juz' al-thānī*. The second part. He established his mission, until he desired to bring out from it his son. Such a son who would be his *nā'ib manāb* (deputy) and his *qā'im maqām* (successor). And he was designated as *inbi'āth* (the Evolved/Emanated). Just as this person was given the name *ibdā'* (Origination). *Ibdā'*. So we will call the *ibdā'iyyah* (the origination), in one sense, *ibdā'*, and we will call their son *inbi'āth*. *Inbi'āth*. *Munba'ith* (the emanated). Where we are seeing, it means *mubda'* (the originated). If they say, it means up to the *'aql al-awwal* (the First Intellect). No, he is also there, and this is also there. They are of the *'ālam-e nūrānī* (luminous world), and these are of the *'ālam-e ṭabī'at* (physical world). *Munba'ith al-awwal li-hādhā al-'ālam al-ṭabī'ī* (The first emanated for this physical world). For this world of nature. Yes. Before that... He is the *mubda' al-awwal* (first originated). And here, in his position, who is there? The second part of *ibdā'*. And along with him, there is *bāṭinī khushī* (inner joy). Yes? In the position of *munba'ith al-awwal* (the first emanated), their son is there. *Bāṭinī khushī*... Yes? Inner joy, from *inbi'āth*... With *munba'ith*... *munba'ith*. Just like we say *alif*, right? When you write *alif*, what do you write? You write 'one'. But what? We say *lift* in it, don't we? From it... it is issued from that. By seeing them, by seeing *mubda'-e Ta'ālā* (the Exalted Originator), by seeing *mubda' al-awwal* (the first originated), the *kamāl-e thānī* (second perfection) that was attained... What is he saying? And he is the son who was named *inbi'āth*, just as this son was named *ibdā'*... this virtuous person was given the name *ibdā'*, because both of them in this world are counterparts to *ibdā'* and *inbi'āth* in that world of the intellect. *Wa-kaunu hādha al-walad...* The world of nature. They are counterparts to *ibdā'* and *inbi'āth* in the world of the intellect. *Wa-kaunu hādha al-walad awwala munba'ithin fī hādha al-'ālam* (And the being of this son the first emanated in this world). And the being of this son, the first one to be emanated... emanated in this world. *Wa-kadhālika kullu maqāmin ba'dahumā fa-yuqālu lahā al-ibdā'* (And likewise every rank after them is called al-ibdā'). In the same way, every rank that comes after those two will be called, it will be said that it is *ibdā'*. One *Imām* will also be called *mubda'* (originated), he will be called *mubda' al-awwal* (the first originated). At the rank of the *'aql al-awwal* (First Intellect). And the *ḥujjat* is the *'aql al-awwal*, then there is the second part of *ibdā'iyyah* at the rank of *'aql al-awwal*. Then every *Imām* is at the rank of *'aql al-awwal*. In his own circle, the first one will be at the rank of *ibdā'*. Okay, and this... In the same way, the sons of the *Imām* who will be there, they will be at the rank of *inbi'āth*. *Munba'ith*.
