In every condition, they are Imams. And who performed *qiyam*? Al-Hasan and al-Husayn. Hasan and Husayn, both are Imams. Now what did he say here? What a strange Hadith of the Prophet. Hasan is the first Imam. Husayn is later. But what did the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, do? He placed the condition of *qiyam* (rising) first, and the condition of *qu'ud* (sitting) later. In sequence, he is there, but in *qiyam*, whose number is it? It is Husayn's. And Hasan is after him, in *qu'ud*. Meaning, to perform *qiyam* among the common people with the commands of the Imamate, that is called *qiyam*, as Husayn did. And Hasan remained silent. Whether they perform *qiyam* or *qu'ud*. `wa min hadhihi al-halah`... And from this state, there manifested from you the divine miracles and the brilliant, great signs. `wa anfa'ala lahu jami' ma fi 'alam al-tabi'ah hatta iftana bihi man arahu ma Yurid.` `wa anfa'ala lahu`... and they became obedient to you... all the things that are in the world of nature. `Salamun 'alayh... Salamun Allah 'alayh`. And... they said about you, some of your Shi'a, out of `ilahiyat` (deification), they said that you are God. When they saw... your miracles... that astonished them. `salamun 'ala Allah 'alayk` (Peace from Allah be upon you). `wa lamma nutiqa bihi fi qawlihi` (And when he was made to speak it in his saying). When you spoke, in your saying, `ana al-awwal wa al-akhir` (I am the First and the Last). I am the first, and I am the last. `is kana awwal suwar al-adwar al-mutaqaddimah` (as he was the first of the forms of the preceding cycles). As you are... when you are the first in the preceding cycles (`adwar`). What does that mean? Meaning, he said, all the *suwar* (forms) that have occurred in the `adwar` (cycles), in them the very first number is yours, in sequence. `wa huwa al-akhir min hadhihi al-jiha`. What state is he talking about? `dhu al-sa'y al-ibda'iyah`... the rank that was attained, which you attained after `dhu al-sa'y al-ibda'iyah`, such a rank was not attained by anyone. `ana al-awwal wa al-akhir`. He is explaining this meaning. `wa huwa al-akhir min hadhihi al-jiha`... `wa huwa al-akhir min hadhihi al-jiha`. And you are the last from this aspect. `lamma kana awwal al-adwar wa akhiraha`. When he was the first of the cycles and the last of them. 'The last of them' means... the Qa'im 'alayhi al-salam. Yes, the last of the cycle. The pronoun `ha` in `akhiraha` refers to `adwar`. `adwar` is plural, isn't it? `dawr` is what? It is singular. And `adwar` is what? Plural. The plural is used as feminine. `lamma kana awwal al-adwar`... when you are the first of the cycles and the last of them. You are the first of the cycle and also the last of it. `awwal suwar al-adwar al-mutaqaddimah` (the first of the forms of the preceding cycles). `awwal surat adwar al-mutaqaddimah`. What meaning will we take?

And the nature of the plural... last night this was being discussed, all of it... in this... `wa al-shamsi wa duhaha` (By the sun and its brightness). Is *shams* (sun) feminine or masculine? What did we learn last night? It is feminine. So, what is the meaning of `wa al-shamsi`? By the oath of the sun. `wa duhaha` (and its brightness). And by the oath of its light. Whose? The sun's. Because it is feminine, `ha` is used. If it were masculine, `hu` would be used. `wa al-shamsi wa duhaha, wa al-qamari idha talaha` (and the moon when it follows it). And the moon when it follows it. Who does it follow? The sun. So the pronoun `ha` refers to the sun. `wa al-qamari idha talaha, wa al-nahari idha jallaha` (and the day when it reveals it). And the day when it... who does the pronoun `ha` refer to? `nahar` is plural, that's why... no, it's not plural. For the night... for the night? No... For the night? Yes. `wa al-nahari`... the day... `idha jalla ha`. The pronoun `ha` refers to whom? To the night. Where is 'night' here? Night... in the later... later... The word 'night' isn't there. It refers to the sun. All of it refers to the sun. `wa al-nahari idha jallaha` (and the day when it reveals it). And the day when it makes it manifest. What does it make manifest? The sun. It makes the sun manifest. `wa al-nahari idha jallaha`. If `nahar` were feminine, what would they say? `idha jallat ha`. From `jalla`... `jalla`, `jallat`. `ha` is what here? Is it the subject or the object? It is the object. The doer. `wa al-nahari`... `nahar` is the subject. Yes. `wa al-nahari`... why is there a `kasra` on the subject? Because of the `waw`. The `waw` is for oath. `wa al-nahari`. And oath is of the day. `idha jallaha` (when it reveals it). When the day makes that sun manifest. This is the meaning. `wa al-nahari idha jallaha`. If `nahar` were feminine, what would it be? They would say `idha jallat ha`. From `jalla`, `jalla`, `jallat`. `wa al-layli idha yaghshaha` (And by the night when it covers it). And oath is of the night, when it covers the sun. It covers the sun and diminishes its light. `idha yaghsha`. `wa al-sama'i wa ma banaha` (And by the sky and what built it). And oath is of the sky. And what built it. What does it mean? And oath is of the sky. And of that Being who built it. Oath is of the sky. And that which Allah Ta'ala built it as. `sama'` is feminine. Yes. One is feminine by analogy (`qiyasi`) and one is feminine by convention (`sama'i`). In Arabic, they make something feminine or masculine as they wish. Talha is there. Talha has a `ta` at the end, it should be feminine, but Talha is used for a masculine name. Zaynab. Zaynab does not have a `ta` at the end, but it is used as feminine. This is all in grammar. So, it is feminine by convention (`mu'annath sama'i`). `qiyasi` and `sama'i`. Feminine is `mu'annath`. According to that, as they wish. Usually, if `ta` comes, it is feminine. But sometimes `ta` comes and it is still masculine, like Talha. And Zaynab has no `ta`, but it is feminine. Likewise, `sama'` (sky), `ard` (earth), `shams` (sun), all these, `shams`, although it is masculine... there is no `ta`, it is not feminine, but it is considered feminine. `qamar` (moon) is considered masculine. And similarly `sama'` and `ard`. Does `ard` have a `ta`? No. The short `ta`? No. It is considered feminine. It is called feminine by convention (`mu'annath sama'i`). There are 14 oaths in it. In which one? In `wa al-shams`, there are 14 oaths taken, then `qad aflaha man zakkaha` (He has succeeded who purifies it). `wa al-sama'i wa ma banaha` (And by the sky and what built it). And oath is of the sky, and that which built it. And as He built it. `ma` has the meaning of 'that which' and 'as'. As He built it. What did He build? The sky. `wa al-sama'i wa ma banaha`. `wa al-ardi wa ma tahaha` (And by the earth and what spread it). And the earth, as He made it flat (`musattah`). He spread it. It refers to that.

`wa qawluhu ana al-batin` (And his saying, "I am the Batin [Hidden]"). `lamma kana min 'ilm al-batin alladhi minhu kanat al-suwar al-latifah al-batinah al-ilahiyah wa al-nufus al-mutajawharah al-nuraniyah al-lati hiya wa iyyaha`. The one which is... the one which is... it is... the one which is... the one which is... it is. The one which is... he is. The one which is... she is. `allati` is used for plural. `wa qawluhu ana al-batin`... and his saying, "I am the First and the Last." And this saying, "I am the Batin and I am the Zahir." And my saying that I am the Batin, is when it was... from the `ilm al-batin` (hidden knowledge) such that from it were those subtle, hidden, divine essences and those substantial, luminous souls, such that it is you. From the aggregate of all of them, the subtle essences and the substantial, luminous souls, your *haykal* (form/structure) was formed. `ladhi huwa iyyah`. `wa qawluhu wa ana al-zahir`. Of whose souls? `'Ayn al-'azimah`. The *haykal* of `'ayn al-'azimah` is made of all these subtle essences and souls. The Batin, from this aspect... the *haykal* of `'ayn al-'azimah` is Batin. It is not visible. Its effects are manifest in the world. `wa qawluhu wa ana al-zahir` (And his saying, "And I am the Zahir [Manifest]"). `lamma zahara lil-absar bi-al-mu'jizat al-ilahiyah` (when he appeared to the sights with divine miracles). And your saying that I am the Zahir is when you appeared to the sights with divine miracles. `wa kanat al-a'mal al-zahirah al-mardiyah al-salihah awwal al-suwar al-lati anbatat...` It is `anbatat`. There's `inbatat`... `inbatat`... with a dot on top? Yes. `anbatat`. `anbatat`. `anbatat`. There's `inbatat` written on the side. `inbatat`. `inbatat lil-awliya' min al-qulub al-ta'wiliyah wa al-hikam al-ilahiyah al-lati anbatat fi jami' al-adwar al-salihati`. Yes... `anbatat`. And the manifest, pleasing, righteous deeds are the first form that... was established for the *awliya'* (friends of God) from the interpretative hearts and the divine wisdoms, which was established in all the previous cycles and connected with you. All the manifest wisdoms, interpretative wisdoms, real wisdoms, divine wisdoms that were established in the past cycles, they became connected with their Imams, and ultimately, with the Imam of Imams, Janab Abu Talib, they became connected. This is what is being said.

So, in the *haykal* of an Imam, there are only lights and the wisdoms of interpretation, all of them gather there. In the form... in the Prophet's *haykal*... what is in the Prophet's *haykal*? The Prophet... in the Prophet's *haykal*, then from there... they all gathered, and from there, the Prophet obtained them. From there, the sign of the *muhtajib* of `'ayn al-'azimah` is that it happens that there is an Imam, the Imam establishes his *bab* (gate). All the knowledge gathers with the *bab*. Similarly, Janab the Noble Prophet, through him, as has been explained, right? What has been explained? That they gather with the *bab al-abwab*. Before that, where do they gather? With the *hujjat*. Before that, with the *da'i*. That same process is established here as well. All the Imams, through which process do they go? Through your *bab*, who is Janab the Noble Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, they gather with `'ayn al-'azimah`. There are two processes for the Imams. There are separate *haykals*... one Prophet of the Universe and one... the *haykal* is separate for each, but just as the process that has been explained, in the same way, those *haykals* go and connect with `'ayn al-'azimah`. With `'ayn al-'azimah`. Those who are capable of being included in that *haykal*, they are, and the rest, they are given to the coming ones. They will then take it with them. That's how it all happens.

`wa qawluhu ana nuqtat ula Adam wa Nuh wa Ibrahim wa Musa wa 'Isa 'alayhim al-salam` (And his saying, "I am the first point of Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, peace be upon them"). What is this word? `wa qawluhu ana... nuqiltu`. `nuqiltu`. I... I transported. I transported Adam, Noah, Ibrahim, Musa, 'alayhim al-salam. Transported. I... I transported. It was transported. `wa ana naba'tu al-nabiyyin` (And I made the Prophets prophets). And I made the prophets prophets. `wa ana arsaltu al-mursalin` (And I sent the Messengers). And I sent the Messengers. `wa al-natiq bi-dhalika al-suwar huwa al-natiq 'an indih min awwal suwar al-sittat alaf sana ila qiyamihi sallallahu 'alayhi`. `sallallahu 'alayhim`. And the one who speaks these matters, he is the one who speaks from him, from the first form of the six thousand years until his rising, may Allah's prayers be upon them. The one who speaks these *suwar* (forms) is from you. From the first three thousand years' cycle... the *dawr al-kashf*... from the end of the *dawr al-kashf*... from the end of the *dawr al-kashf* until your rising, blessings be upon him. A declaration of those *suwar* is that they sent the prophets, they sent the messengers. 40, 49, 50... Three thousand years is the duration of the *barzakh*, and six thousand years... `wa hum ahl al-haqa'iq wa al-maqamat` (And they are the people of realities and stations). And they are the people of realities and of high and lofty stations. `wa qawluhu ana bi-kull shay'in 'alim` (And his saying, "I am knowledgeable of all things"). And your saying, "I am knowledgeable of all things." `lamma ittasalat bihi dhalika al-nur al-jari ittisalan kulliyan, 'alima bihi ma kana wa ma huwa ka'in` (when that flowing light connected with him, a total connection, he knew through it what was and what is to be). And when that flowing light connected with you, a total connection, you knew through it what was and what is to be. `wa sara jami' 'alam al-tabi'ah bayna yadayhi ka-al-kurah al-mulqat la takhfa 'alayhi minha khafiyah` (And the entire world of nature became before him like a cast-down ball, with no hidden thing being hidden from him). And the entire world of nature became before you like a ball that is thrown down, from which no hidden thing is hidden from you. `wa min hadhihi al-jiha qala 'alayhi al-salam` (And from this aspect, he, peace be upon him, said): `inna li manzilah lam takhtur 'ala qalb bashar` (Indeed, I have a station that has not occurred to a human heart). `wa haddan lam yablugh ma'rifatihi ahad` (and a limit whose gnosis no one has reached). And indeed, for me there is a rank... such a rank that it has not occurred to the heart of any human being. It does not know that station. `wa haddan lam yablugh ma'rifatihi ahad` (and a limit whose gnosis no one has reached). And such a limit that no one's gnosis has reached it. `wa inna al-rububiyah wa al-ilahiyah la takhturu 'ala qulub al-bashar fa-ya'rifuha illa al-qa'im minhum` (And indeed, Lordship and Divinity do not occur to the hearts of men that they might know it, except for the Qa'im among them). And indeed, Lordship (`rububiyah`) and Divinity (`ilahiyah`) certainly do not descend upon the hearts of men, that they may know it, except for the Qa'im among them.

Which rank is it... Lordship and... No... Which rank has descended upon you? A rank such that no human can understand in which rank I am, how I have gathered the *suwar*. This is what he is saying. No, this mention that has come, that upon a human, it cannot descend, so what rank is that which has descended upon you? No, I mean... Lordship (`rububiyah`) and Divinity (`ilahiyah`). In the meaning they have taken it, *rububiyah* and *ilahiyah* means the one above and the one below, the one who is the Lord. In that sense. They haven't taken it in the sense of claiming divinity. `wa anna al-khalqa bi-ajma'ihim ya'rifuna Allah bi-al-ma'rifah al-zahirah` (And that all of creation knows Allah with the outward gnosis). That the creation, all of them, know Allah with the outward gnosis. `wa ahl al-haqa'iq ya'rifunahu bi-haqiqat ma'rifatihi wa yuwahhidunahu min wajh tawhidihi` (and the people of realities know Him with the reality of His gnosis and they declare His oneness from the aspect of His oneness). And the people of realities know God with the reality of His gnosis, and they declare His oneness from the aspect of His oneness. `wa anna 'Aliyyan lam ya'rifhu ahadun bil-jumlah bi-haqiqat ma'rifatihi illa Rasulullah wa al-a'immah min wuldihi` (And that no one at all knew Ali with the reality of his gnosis except the Messenger of Allah and the Imams from his progeny). And indeed Ali, no person knew him, at all, with the reality of his gnosis, except the Messenger of Allah and the Imams from his progeny. `wa 'arrafahu ahl al-haqa'iq bi-zahir al-ma'rifah` (And he made himself known to the people of realities with the outward gnosis). And you made yourself known to the people of realities with the outward gnosis. The real gnosis was only known by the Messenger of Allah and the Imams. And as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, has stated in the hadith. And the outward gnosis, the people of realities gained. `bi-ithbat al-ayat wa al-burhan wa al-mu'jizat al-lati azharaha lahum marratan ba'da marratan` (by the establishment of signs, proofs, and miracles that he manifested for them time and again). By establishing the signs and proofs and miracles that you manifested for them, time after time. `wa lamma sami'a al-nass hadha al-qawl qala fih qawmun huwa al-ghayb, huwa al-ghayb, ta'ala wa takabbara 'amma yaqul al-jahilun 'uluwwan kabira` (And when the people heard this statement, a group said about him, "He is the Unseen." He is Exalted and Greatly Exalted above what the ignorant say). And when you were heard saying this, a group of people in your regard said, "He is the Unseen (`al-ghayb`)." "He is the Unseen." He is Exalted and Transcendent. You are lofty and grand, and you have adopted majesty from this statement that the ignorant and unjust say, a great elevation. `wa qala akharuna huwa al-mubda' al-awwal` (And others said, "He is the First Originated Being"). And others said, "He is the First Originated Being." `wa qala akharuna huwa al-inbi'ath al-awwal` (And others said, "He is the First Emanation"). `wa tasha'abat fihim al-aswat wa al-aqwal` (And voices and sayings diverged regarding him). And various opinions were formed about you. Opinions about you became varied. `wa ghabba 'anhum...` `wa ghabba 'anhum hadha al-sirr al-daqiq` (And this subtle secret was hidden from them). And it became hidden from them, this subtle secret. `alladhi lam yattasil bihi illa al-aqall min al-awliya'` (with which none connected except the fewest of the friends of God). such that none connected with it except for a very few of the believers. The true gnosis of Allah is the greatest thing. What true gnosis did you impart? That your *nuqta*, which is the spiritual *nuqta*, is the highest *nuqta* after `dhu al-sa'y al-ibda'iyah`. This is the true gnosis. Now, the Qa'im who is to come, his *nuqta* will be higher than yours. This is true gnosis. `wa ghabba 'anhum hadha al-sirr al-daqiq`. Ya Mushkil, whom the Messengers have called, Ali, Ya Mushkil, whom the Messengers have called, Ali. `alladhina an'am Allahu 'alayhim bi-fayd barakat mawalihi` (those whom Allah has blessed with the effusion of the blessings of his masters). Such that Allah blessed them and bestowed His grace upon them, with the effusion of the blessings of their masters. `salamun Allah 'alayhim` (Peace of Allah be upon them). `wa al-hamdu lillahi 'ala dhalika kullih al-hamd alladhi ja'alana minhum wa lam ya'dil bina 'anhum` (And praise be to Allah for all of that, the praise of the one who made us from them and did not turn us away from them). And for Allah is praise for this matter. And praise such that He made us from them and did not turn us away from them. He made us from them. From the effusion of blessings, from the `awliya' Allah` (friends of God). And He did not turn us away from them. All these statements that are said about Janab Ali, the Prophet himself has said them. "Ali, your gnosis was not attained except by me and Allah." Many sayings of yours... during the era of the Bani Umayyah, they tried to suppress it a great deal. They fabricated hadiths against you. In every sermon of yours, the Prophet, whatever he said for you, they made it a defective hadith. Anyone who fabricated and brought a hadith would be rewarded. This was the practice of the Bani Umayayds. It is a great story. To hide the virtues of Ali, what kinds of efforts were made. Outwardly, the miracles of the Prophet were greater than those of the Master of the Universe. Why? A strange state of affairs. One is the *hijab* (veil), one is the *adna hijab* (lower veil). Whose? Ali's hijab. And the *adna hijab* is whose? The Prophet's. Why was he revealed? Ali's hijab was revealed after `dhu al-sa'y al-ibda'iyah` was revealed. Because in the previous times, the prophets who did the service of the *mustaqarrin* (the established ones), the service that the prophets did for the *mustaqarrin*, getting into troubles and all those things they did, their accounts had to be settled. So Ali, who is the *mustaqarr*, they sent him to the world in the veil of the *mustaqarr*, so that he could settle those accounts that were owed to the *mustaqarrin* on behalf of the prophets. And who is the Qa'im over the prophets and messengers? Janab the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. All the prophets are gathered with him. With whom? With the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. Ali, as a representative of the *mustaqarr*, was sent so that all the services that the prophets had done for the *mustaqarrin*, their account could be settled. All its things, giving and taking, would be completed. So Ali came and performed *qiyam* in this manner. And Husayn, with what did he perform *qiyam*? In the time of Ali, the wars that happened, in the time of the Prophet, the wars that happened, and in the time of Ali, in which there were many transgressions, to settle their accounts, Imam Husayn, peace and blessings be upon him, performed *qiyam*. Without that, the *haykal* of Imam Husayn could not have developed, which was with the Master of the Universe. Its reasons have been explained.

This *durud* (salutation), why is there so much reward in it? The salutations we send to the Prophet and his family, so the reward that is kept for us... It has been kept so that your connection with them may be established. `salli 'ala`... what does it mean? That our spiritual connection may be established with them. With whom? With the Prophet and the family of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon them. So it is a prayer. It is a prayer. So with the prayer, one gets the reward from there as well. The acceptance is the reward. Yes. One gets a reward from them, from their unseen treasuries. It's a very big treasury. One cannot estimate it. In it are things of crores of years gathered, *suwar* are gathered. From this side, it is gathered. How many years old is this world? How many years old is it? A thousand years? A thousand years. One *mawr* has passed. That is fine, that happened. But what is its age at this moment? How long has it been since `dhu al-sa'y al-ibda'iyah` manifested? 399... 399 *qawrs* are happening. 399. The 400th *qawr* of the *dawr al-kashf* will manifest. So the 400th *qawr* will manifest... Four hundred thousand *dawr*. It is a `qawr`. Four hundred thousand `dawr`... it is a `dawr`. It is a `qawr`. Four hundred thousand `dawr`... a `dawr`. So the four hundred thousand `dawr` that have passed of this universe, four hundred thousand `dawr`. This is the first `dawr`. `dawr`. What does `dawr` mean? Four hundred thousand years. We are in the last part of this four hundred thousand years of this *dawr*. The *suwar* of these four hundred thousand years are with `ayn al-'azimah`. A long, long time.

*Al-Fasl al-thani min al-Bab al-thani min al-Suraj al-thalith*. *A'udhu billahi min al-shaytan al-rajim. Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*. *Al-Fasl al-thani min al-Bab al-thani min al-Suraj al-thalith*. The second chapter from the second part of the third *Suraj*. *Wa min hadhihi al-halat al-'azimah, wa al-manzilat al-'aliyat al-jasimah, al-sabiq dhikruha, qala Siyyidna Ja'far ibn Mansur al-Yaman, a'la Allahu qudsahu. Fa-qad dhakarna... fa-qad dhakarna... fa-qad dhukira fi al-tawarikh wa al-siyar, inna Allaha Ta'ala la yuqbalu... nubuwata nabiyyin wala istifa'a wasiyyin wala imamata waliyyin*. *La yaqbalu*. *La yaqbalu*. *La yaqbalu nubuwata nabiyyin wala istifa'a wasiyyin wala imamata waliyyin, wala 'amala ta'atin min 'amilin, wa law taqatta'a bi al-'ibadati awsalihi, wajibatin wa mustahaddah, illa... bi wilayah 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. Wa man ata bi ghayri wilayahhi, asqatat nubuwwatuhu, wa wasayatuhu, wa salih 'amaluhu. Wa lam yaqbal Allahu minhu, wala yuzakki 'amaluhu, li-annahu, salawatullahi 'alayhi, majma' al-a'immati wa al-awsiya'i min awwal al-adwar ila qiyamihi, salamullahi 'alayhi*. *Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*. And from this magnificent state and lofty, grand station, which was mentioned previously, Siyyidna Ja'far ibn Mansur al-Yaman—may Allah elevate his sanctity—says. And we have mentioned in the histories and biographies... it has been mentioned... has been mentioned. No, it is not noon. *Dhakarna* is written here. *Dhakarna*. *Dhukira*. *Dhukira*. And it has been mentioned in the histories and biographies that verily, Allah Ta'ala does not accept the prophethood of any prophet—of any prophet. Of any prophet. The prophethood of any prophet, and the selection of any successor (*wasi*)... And succession. Sincerity of intention. And nor the imamate of any *wali*. And not the act of obedience... the act of obedience of any doer, even if he has spent his nights in worship... *taqatta'a*. *taqatta'a*. *Taqatta'a bi al-'ibadah*. *Taqatta'a* means he was cut into pieces. He has destroyed himself. In obligatory... obligatory and... and made effort... he made effort, except with the *wilayah* of Mawla 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. And whoever comes without the *wilayah*... The prophethood of the prophet, and the successorship of the *wasi*, and the imamate... the imamate of the *wali* is also not accepted, this is what he is saying. Except with the *wilayah* of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. The Imam of the names. *Wa man ata bi ghayri wilayah*. And who came... with... without his *wilayah*, his prophethood became void. He who brought... *ata*. He who brought. Okay, he who came. He who came without his *wilayah*, then that prophet's prophethood... he who did not come with your *wilayah*... *'ata*. *'ata* with *ba* is a connection. *Asqatat... asqatat nubuwwatuhu*. His prophethood became void... becomes void. And his successorship. And his successorship. And his righteous, good deeds. And Allah Ta'ala does not accept from him, nor does He purify his deeds... nor does He purify his deeds. Because he, *salawatullahi 'alayh*, Mawla 'Ali, is the confluence of the Imams and the successors (*awsiya'*) from the beginning of the cycles (*adwar*) until your advent... your advent. May the peace of Allah be upon you. *Wa min hadhihi al-jiha wa al-hala, sahha qawl al-da'i... sahha qawl al-da'i Abdan, qaddasa Allahu ruhahu, inna al-jum'ah 'ala khidmat...* Where is this? This saying of Maulana Abdan, from which book is it? It is in Majmu' al-Tarbiyah. A reference from Majmu' al-Tarbiyah is also given. How many books has he written? Six to seven. How many books has he written? Maulana Abdan. Many. A hundred. In which Siyyidna Ja'far has written... the number of books you have written... how many books has he written? Eighty, above eighty. Yes. No, here, where it says, "without the *wilayah* of Mawla Ali," there is no mention that one must recognize your station, or consider you the caliph, or accept your authority. Is mere love sufficient? Without *wilayah*. With *wilayah*, there is also obedience to commands, no? If a servant only says, "I... acknowledge the master," but does not consider him a master... He expresses love but doesn't consider him the master. He doesn't obey the master's commands. And from this direction and this state... from this subject... it is correct... the saying is साफ होता है (made clear), proven. The saying of Maulana al-Da'i Abdan, *qaddasa Allahu ruhahu* (may Allah sanctify his soul), is proven. That the *jum'ah* is upon the service of the master for his slave... The *jum'ah*'s focus is... on that subject which has been stated, that the master served his... his slave. In this cycle. Because the people of the manifest *da'wat* in the past cycles, who were the children of Is-haq, peace be upon them... The *jum'ah* is established upon the service of the master for his slave. The master's service for his slave. The master served his servant. It is focused on that *jum'ah*. In this cycle. Because the people of the manifest *da'wat* in this... in the past cycles, who were those people who were the children of Is-haq, peace be upon them, they were *hujjahs* and *du'at* and servants for the masters of the esoteric *da'wat*, for the masters of the esoteric *da'wat*. Who are the children of Isma'il, peace be upon them. They are the lofty stations. The children of Is-haq, from Siyyidna Adam until your era, served the children of Isma'il. The children of Isma'il remained hidden in concealment, and the children of Is-haq endured hardships. *Fa-lamma ijtama'at 'inda Amir al-Mu'minin, salawatullahi 'alayhi, wa ijtama'at awladu Is-haq 'inda... 'inda Natiq al-dawr, salamullahi 'alayhi, wajaba fi maziyyati... 'adli Allahi Ta'ala, khidmatu Amir al-Mu'minin wa al-Payghambar, salawatullahi 'alayhi*. *'alayhima*. *'Alayhima qadha'an bi-ma sabaqa min khidmati awladi Is-haq li-awladi Isma'il, salamullahi 'alayhim*. And when they gathered with Mawla Amir al-Mu'minin, *salawatullahi 'alayhi*, and the children of Is-haq gathered with... with the *Natiq* of the era... with the *Natiq* of the era, may Allah's peace be upon you, it became obligatory in this... in the will of the justice of Allah Ta'ala... *maziyyah*. *Maziyyah* means... in the distinction, in the speciality... in this speciality of the justice of Allah Ta'ala... of the just one... the service of Amir al-Mu'minin and the Prophet, *salawatullahi 'alayhi*. *Qadha'an*. As a requital... to complete that matter which had already passed. The service of the children of... *qadha'* means? We say, "I performed the *qadha'* of the prayer." To complete it. In Urdu, *qadha'* is used to mean that the prayer was missed, now it's *qadha'*. But in Arabic, *qadha'* means to complete. And the prayer that is missed... performing the *qadha'* of the prayer is called *qadha'an ma fata* (fulfilling what was missed). *Qadha'an fa'itan*, they say. This is what it's saying. *Qadha'an fa'itan*. Fulfilling the missed prayer is called *qadha'*. In Urdu, we take *qadha'* to mean, well, it wasn't performed, so now it is *qadha'*. The meaning is... to complete... complete what was established of the service from the children of Is-haq for the children of Isma'il... towards Isma'il. May Allah's peace be upon all of them. Because the balance of justice is established. *Mizan...* *mizan al-'adli*. *Mizan al-'adli qa'imun*. Because the balance of justice is established. *Wa hadha al-ma'na li-khidmat al-mawla li-'abdihi wa qiyamuhu bayna yadayhi wa sa'yuhu ma'ahu wa muharabatuhu li-azdadihi wa qatlihi li-man ankara manzilatahu wa janaba 'an ta'atihi wa jihadihi li-ahl al-kufr al-mu'anidin lahu, kama kana khadiman lahu fi dawri Ibrahim wa Musa wa 'Isa, 'alayhim al-salam, hazwan bi-hazwin, wala yughadiru saghiratan wala kabiratan illa ahsaha*. And this meaning... of the service of the master, the master serving his slave... towards the slave, and his standing... Now here Maulana Abdan writes, "*Inna al-jum'ah 'ala khidmat al-mawla li-'abdih*." What did he say regarding the *jum'ah*? We will have to see. Where is it? It is not understood, the master for his slave... did service... what did he mean by this? The masters were who? The *Qa'im* of the children of Isma'il is who? Siyyidna 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. The *Qa'im* of the children of Isma'il. And the *Qa'im* of the children of Is-haq is who? The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. When the era of the Prophet came, it happened that in the past eras, for 6000 years, the services that the children of Is-haq rendered... for the children of Isma'il, they were to be rewarded for it in the balance of justice. So 'Ali served the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. "The prophets called upon 'Ali in times of difficulty." So you rendered all those services, you gave your life in battles, and you fought, and you defended the Prophet. This is the meaning... that... the requital was fulfilled. The requital was fulfilled. *Wa hadha al-ma'na*. And this is the meaning... of the service of the master, the master serving his progeny... his slave, and his standing before you, meaning Maulana Ali's standing near the Prophet, and striving with you, and fighting your enemies... your enemies, and killing... that person who denied your, Mawla Nabi's, station, and killing you... *wa janaba 'an ta'atihi*. And who turned away... he turned away from your obedience... Mawla Nabi's obedience, and fighting against the people of disbelief, those people of disbelief who are hostile to Mawla Nabi, just as he was a servant to him... meaning, the prophets in the eras of Ibrahim and Musa and 'Isa served. In the same manner as it had happened. *Wala yughadiru saghiratan wala kabiratan*. And it will not be repaid... a reward will be given. Neither the small nor the big... Prophet Ibrahim and Prophet Musa and Prophet 'Isa, the services they rendered in their eras for Siyyidna... for the children of Isma'il, the *mustaqarrin*, in the same way now the *mustaqarr* served the *mustawda'*. And it will not be diminished in measure, neither for the small nor for the big, except... that which he earns. He counts it. He counts it. *Wala yughadiru*. It does not leave a small thing nor a big one, except it has enumerated it. It has counted it. *Wa kana al-'Aql al-'Ashir huwa al-muhtajibu bi Muhammad 'alayhi al-salam wa al-mu'ayyidu lahu al-naziru ilayhi al-mumiddu lahu bi-wasatit al-jadd wa al-fath wa al-khayal, 'inda kamalihi wa bulughihi rutbatahu, al-hijabiyyah*. And verily, Mawla 'Aqil... *'Aql al-'Ashir*... he is veiled by the Prophet, Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and is the supporter for you, and the one who looks upon your direction, and the one who provides aid to you through the mediation of *jadd* and *fath* and *khayal*... near... The Tenth Intellect, who is he? The *musta'id da'iya*. The *musta'id da'iya* who is in the world of life, he is veiled by the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. The biggest point in this from Mumbai-sahib has come... *Al-mu'ayyidu lahu*. The one who gives support... gives support to you. The one who looks upon your direction. *Wa al-mumiddu lahu*. The one who gives aid... gives aid to you through the mediation of *jadd* and *fath* and *khayal*. *Jadd* is? *Khanas al-'Alam*. *Jaddu 'aba da'iyat al-'alam*. After the death of *khumsa*, several sections emerged. This section, the *musta'id da'iya*, is of the initial period. The *musta'id da'iya* who appeared... Yes. He is... he is dominant over all. This *musta'id da'iya* of Sarandib... of Sarandib. The master of Sarandib. And now he is before you, so he is the past *da'iya*. It can be taken as the Tenth Intellect of the beginning... all his arrangements are ongoing. *Wa al-muhtajib*. The one who is veiled... by the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, is the one who gives support to you... and looks upon you with compassion, and *mumidd*... gives you aid through the mediation of *jadd* and *fath* and *khayal* near your perfection and your reaching the rank of *hijabiyyah*. Because every *natiq* and every *wasi* and every imam... who? Mawla Ali. Yes. From the Prophet. The rest... the one who grants reward and the Prophet... when he went for the *hijrah*, he came late. He said to the Prophet's servant, "What should I do?" He said, "I... when... when he was silent, you would inform me... and... When he was silent, I would ask. I would ask. Yes. He has said this, it is a very famous saying. Someone asked, "What did you do with the Prophet's servant?" He said, "The Prophet... *idha sakattu ibtada'a*. *Ibtada'a*. When I was silent, he would begin. And when he was silent, I would ask. As the Noble Book says, when the son of Mary was presented as an example... *kama qala al-kitab al-karim, wa lamma dhuriba ibnu Maryama mathalan*. As the Noble Book says, "*Wa lamma dhuriba ibnu Maryama mathalan, idha qawmuka minhu yasiddun*." And as the Noble Book says, when... an example was given... An example was given. Maryam... the son of Maryam... meaning Siyyidna Ali was said to be Ibn Maryam. At that time, what happened? "*Idha qawmuka minhu yasiddun*." At that time, your people will disobey him and stop him. *Wa kana salawatullahi 'alayhi yaqulu, 'allamani Rasulullah alfa babin min al-'ilm, infataha li min kulli babin alfa babin*." *Alfa bab*. In this way, *salawatullahi 'alayhi* said, saying that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, taught me a thousand doors of knowledge, and from every door a thousand doors opened for me. A thousand, thousand doors. How many doors opened from this perspective? One lakh. One lakh. *Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*. This passage, because the power went out, it was missed. So its translation, this same *Fasl al-thani, Bab al-thani, Suraj al-thalith*, its translation that was missed, about one page was missed. So that is being done for you again. *Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*. *Wa kana al-'Aql al-'Ashir huwa al-muhtajibu bi Muhammad 'alayhi al-salatu wa al-salam, al-mu'ayyidu lahu wa al-naziru ilayhi wa al-mumiddu lahu bi-wasatit al-jadd wa al-fath wa al-khayal, 'inda kamalihi wa bulughihi rutbat al-hijabiyyah*. And verily, the Tenth Intellect, who is the veiled one by Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and the supporter for you, and the one who looks upon you with compassion, and the one who provides aid to you through the mediation of *jadd* and *fath* and *khayal* near his perfection and his reaching the rank of *hijabiyyah*. Because every *natiq* and *wasi* and imam, it is necessary for him to receive instruction and to progress rank by rank. *Kama qala Allahu Ta'ala, wa Allahu akhrajakum min butuni ummahatikum la ta'lamuna shay'a*. As Allah the Exalted has said, "And Allah is the Being who brings you out from the wombs of your mothers in a state where you know nothing." *Fa-kana Muhammad, salawatullahi 'alayhi, akhidhun min Ubayy ibn Ka'b fi hali ta'limihi wa ibtida'ihi, wa huwa al-mukanna 'anhu bi-Jibra'il*. And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was one who acquired knowledge from Mawla Ubayy ibn Ka'b in the state of his instruction and his beginning, and it is in a way that Mawla Ubayy ibn Ka'b is alluded to by Jibra'il. *Fa-lamma istakmala ma 'indahu, rafa'ahu ila Zayd ibn 'Amr*. And when the Prophet completed that which was with Ubayy ibn Ka'b, then Ubayy ibn Ka'b elevated you to Zayd ibn 'Amr. *Wa huwa da'i jaziratihi, wa huwa al-mukanna 'anhu bi-Mika'il*. And that Zayd ibn 'Amr was the *da'i* of his island, and he is alluded to by Mika'il. *Fa-lamma istaw'aba wa istakmala ma 'indahu, rafa'ahu ila man fawqahu, wa huwa Israfil*. When the Prophet had fully absorbed and perfected what was with you, that is, with Zayd ibn 'Amr, then Zayd ibn 'Amr elevated the Prophet to the being who was even higher than him, that is, higher than himself, and he is Israfil. *Wa kadhalika jadduhu Ibrahim*. And similarly is the case of your grandfather, Ibrahim. *Fa-innahu taraqqa fi al-maratib shay'an ba'da shay'in*. That you made progress, Siyyidna Ibrahim, in the ranks, one after another. *Kama akhbara 'anhu al-kitab al-karim bi-qawlihi*. As the Noble Book has informed about it with its saying: *Fa-lamma janna 'alayhi al-laylu ra'a kawkaban, qala hadha rabbi*. When the night fell upon you, you saw a *kawkab*, a star. So you said, "This is my Lord." *Fa-lamma afala*. When that too set, then *qala la uhibbu al-afilin*. You said that I do not like those who set. *Fa-lamma ra'a al-qamara bazighan, qala hadha rabbi*. Then when you, Siyyidna Ibrahim, saw the moon, that it was rising, you said, "This is my Lord." *Fa-lamma afala, qala la-in lam yahdini rabbi la-akunanna min al-qawm al-dallin*. You said that I do not like those who set. It was said that this is my Lord. When that moon set, you said that if my Lord does not guide me, I will become one of the misguided people. *Fa-lamma ra'a al-shamsa bazighatan*. Then Siyyidna Ibrahim, when he saw the sun, that it was rising, emerging, *qala hadha rabbi*. He said, "This is my Lord." *Hadha akbaru*. "Because it is big." *Fa-lamma afalat, qala ya qawmi inni bari'un mimma tushrikun*. Then when that too set, the sun too set, you said, "O my people, verily, I absolve myself from that which you associate as partners." Similarly, for Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali, *salawatullahi 'alayhi*, it was the same situation. *Fa-innahu ta'allama 'inda Muhammad wa 'inda Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, allati hiya hujjat Imam al-'asr, alladhi huwa Abu Talib, salamullahi 'alayhim ajma'in*. And similarly, for Mawla 'Ali, Amir al-Mu'minin, *'alayhi salawatullahi 'alayh*, this was the case, that you learned at the side of the Prophet and at the side of Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, who was the *hujjah* of the Imam of the Age. And that Imam of the Age was Mawla Abu Talib, *salamullahi 'alayhim ajma'in*. *Wa li-dhalika rumiza 'alayhi bi-ibn Maryama*. And for this reason, you were alluded to as Ibn Maryam, meaning Mawla 'Ali was called Ibn Maryam. When you were analogized to 'Isa, and Khadijah was analogized to Maryam. When you were analogized to 'Isa, and Khadijah was analogized to Maryam. *Kama qala al-kitab al-karim, wa lamma dhuriba ibnu Maryama mathalan, idha qawmuka minhu yasiddun*. As the Noble Book says, and verily, when Ibn Maryam was presented as an example, for Ibn Maryam, as an example, when your people would stop him from it and disobey him. *Wa kana salawatullahi 'alayhi yaqulu, 'allamani Rasulullah alfa babin min al-'ilm, infataha li min kulli babin alfa bab*. And as Rasulullah, *salawatullahi 'alayh*, as Mawla 'Ali has said, saying, "The Messenger of Allah, *salawatullahi 'alayh*, taught me a thousand chapters of knowledge. From every chapter, a thousand, thousand chapters opened for me."

*Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*. The Third Chapter.

And due to this hidden secret (*sirr al-khafi*) and this sublime meaning, Amir al-Mu'minin, *'alayhis salaam*, said, "*Ana wa Muhammad, Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad wa 'alihi wa sallim, min nurin wahid.*" (I and Muhammad, O Allah, bless Muhammad and his family and grant them peace, are from one light.) *Ta'ala*.

And... And this hidden secret... *wa li-hadha al-sirr al-khafi*. *wa li-hadha al-sirr...* 'li' has come, hasn't it? Because of 'li', 'sirr' will have a *kasra* [vowel 'i']. And because of this hidden secret... And because of this hidden secret, and because of this noble and great meaning... because of this great and noble meaning, Amir al-Mu'minin, *salawatullahi 'alayh*, said that I and the Prophet are from one *nur* (light), from the *nur* of God. From the *nur* of God.

"*Fa-amara Allahu dhalika al-nur an yanshaqqa nisfayn.*" (So Allah commanded that light to split into two halves). And Allah commanded... Allah commanded that *nur* that it should be separated into two parts. Into two parts.

"*Fa-qala li-l-nisf al-awwal 'Kun Muhammad.' Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad wa 'alihi wa sallim.*" (And He said to the first half, 'Be Muhammad.' O Allah, bless Muhammad and his family and grant them peace). So He said to the half... for the first, for the first half, that "Become Muhammad." "*Wa li-l-nisf al-thani, 'Kun 'Aliyyah'.*" (And to the second half, 'Be Ali.'). And for the second half, "Become Ali."

"*Isharatun ila lata'if awlad Ishaq wa awlad Isma'il, 'alayhim al-salaam.*" (An indication towards the subtleties of the children of Ishaq and the children of Isma'il, peace be upon them). It indicates... it indicates towards the subtleties of the children of Ishaq... of Ishaq and the children of Isma'il, peace be upon them. It points towards their invitations (*da'wat*). The invitation of Prophethood (*nubuwwat*) and... Apostleship (*risalat*), and the invitation of Imamate (*imamat*) and Guardianship (*wasaayat*).

So this *nur* came, meaning some... Yes. corporeal parts came, or... No, the forms (*suwar*). The forms. The forms (*suwar*), the forms. Forms and souls (*nufus*). The form and the soul, which are of two types, were divided. One, the forms which were the bearers of the ranks of *nubuwwat* and *risalat*, they went over there. And those of *imamat* and *wasaayat* went over there. Isma'il, *'alayhis salatu was-salam*.

"*Kama sabaqa min qawlihi...*" (As was mentioned previously from his statement...). As was established by the statement... the statement.

"*Wa qala aydan: Muhammadun 'Ali al-yaqut al-asfar...*" (And he also said: Muhammad is Ali, the yellow sapphire...). And he said that Muhammad is the yellow ruby. "*...wa ana al-yaqut al-ahmar min hadhihi al-jihah.*" (And I am the red ruby from this direction). And I am the red ruby from this direction. And which is the most excellent sapphire? The red ruby. The red ruby.

"*Wa kana Muhammadun, salawatullahi 'alayh, yaqul...*... *'Aliyyun minni wa ana minhu.*" (And Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, used to say... 'Ali is from me, and I am from him.') So the Prophet used to say that Ali is from me... Ali is from me... and I am from Ali. I am from him. "*La yu'addi 'anni illa 'Ali.*" (None delivers on my behalf except Ali). None will fulfill on my behalf... except Ali. Except Ali.

"*Wa lamma irtaqa Muhammadun, salawatullahi 'alayh, fi al-rutab, wa balagha ila rutbat al-hijabiyyah wa al-nutq al-haqiqi, intaqala imam al-'asr al-naqib al-muqim lahu, alladhi huwa Abu Talib, salawatullahi 'alayh.*" (And when Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, ascended through the ranks and reached the rank of *hijabiyyah* [the rank of the veil] and the *nutq al-haqiqi* [the true utterance], the Imam of the Age, the established chief for him, who is Abu Talib, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, transferred/passed away).

Sir, this saying of yours that if the Noble Prophet had not come to the world, then the world and the universe itself would not have been created. So this means that if there was no one to bear these *anwar* (lights) and these *suwar* (forms), then the world's... creation... would not have happened? Is that the meaning?

"*Lawlaka lama khalaqtu-l-aflak.*" (Were it not for you, I would not have created the celestial spheres). Yes. Meaning, if the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, had not existed, then the celestial spheres (*aflak*) would not have been created. This is what was said. So now, its meaning which has been stated here is this: that what things were gathered in the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him? Those which were the bearers of *nubuwwat* (prophethood) and *risalat* (apostleship). And those who were the bearers of *nubuwwat* and *risalat*, upon them were certain *qisasat* (retributions/accounts). There were *qisasat* of the world. The children of Isma'il did not have *qisasat*. So the *nubuwwat*- वाले (people of prophethood) are the ones who... *aflak*... when they come, the chapter of *qisasat* begins with the *aflak*. The chapter of *qisasat* begins with the *aflak*. There is friction of the *aflak*. In it, there is revolution. All things are created. And those who are veiled (*muhtajib*), who are Ali, those who are... these are... people of *imamat* and *wasaayat*, for them, it is not meant to come into the revolutions (*inqilabat*) of the world.

So, the Prophet can sin, but... Nubuwwat and risalat. It's not a question of the Prophet sinning. With them are such people upon whom *qisasat* remain. I see. I see. The people who are with them.

And when Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, ascended... ascended in the ranks and reached the rank of *hijabiyyah*... and the *nutq-e-haqiqi* (true utterance)... What is your final station, what is the station called? *Rutbat al-hijabiyyah* (the rank of the veil). This is for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. And about this, it is said, "*'An tab'athahu maqaman mahmudan alladhi wa'adtahu.*" (That You may raise him to a praiseworthy station which You have promised him).

In whose *haykal* (temple/form)? In the *'ayn-e-'azimah* (The Great Essence).

So send... send you, raise you to the Praiseworthy Station (*maqam-e-mahmud*) which You have promised. He would always pray. And that prayer will always remain. As the *'ayn* (essence) will be, so will the *mim* (manifestation) be. Of whatever rank the *'ayn* is, of that rank the *mim* will be. If the *'ayn* is... for one thousand... for seven thousand years... the establishment of the *'ayn* occurs in seven thousand years. The establishment of the *sar-mim* occurs. They are together, both are side-by-side. Then if, after seven thousand years, another such seven seven-thousands come, then as the *'ayn* rises higher, so will the *mim* rise higher.

"*...wa intaqala imam al-'asr al-naqib al-muqim lahu, alladhi huwa Abu Talib...*" (...and the Imam of the Age, the established chief for him, who is Abu Talib, transferred/passed away...). And... when the Imam of the Age, who is established for you, such that he is Abu Talib, passed away... "*...wa sara fi maqamatihi hijabun li-l-'aashir.*" (...and he became in his station a veil for the Tenth). So he reached... and he became in his station... and he became in his station a *hijab* (veil)... a *hijab* for the *'aashir* (Tenth). *'Aashir*, for the *'aql al-'aashir* (Tenth Intellect).

This is about the Prophet? No, it's about Janab Abu Talib. When he passed away, what did his station become? That you, Janab Prophet... were aided by him (*mumidd ho gaye*). It is *thalathat*... it is, isn't it? What do we call it? *Thalathat sufara'*... The three emissaries. Through the three emissaries, the support of the *'ayn* continued. "*Mumiddan lahu...*" (Aiding him...). Aider to you. Aider to you. Through the medium... "*Matrahan li-shu'a'ihi.*" (A place for his rays to fall). A place for falling... "*...sara fi maqamihi hijaban...*" (...he became in his station a veil...). A place for the rays to fall. Janab Abu Talib, peace and blessings be upon him, and he became... "*wa intaqala imam al-'asr...*" (...and the Imam of the Age transferred...). He passed away, Imam al-Asr, who is the establisher for you, such that he is Abu Talib, peace and blessings be upon him. "*Wa sara fi maqamihi hijaban.*" (And he became in his station a veil). And he became in his station as a *hijab*. *Hijab* of the *'aql-e-'aashir* (Tenth Intellect). "*Matrahan li-shu'a'ihi.*" (A place for his rays to fall). A place for his *shu'a'* (rays) to fall. "*Mumiddan lahu bi-wasatat al-jadd wa-l-fath wa-l-khayal.*" (Aiding him through the mediation of *jadd*, *fath*, and *khayal*). Aider to you through the mediation of the *jadd*, the *fath*, and the *khayal*.

So this *thalathat sufara'* is *jadd*, *fath*, and *khayal*? *Jadd*, *fath*, and *khayal*. *Thalathat sufara'*. The phrasing is such. Most likely, it's an allusion to the *'ayn*.

So "*sara fi maqamihi hijaban li-l-'aashir*," who reached? "*Wa sara fi maqamihi...*" (And he became in his station...). He became a veil for the Tenth... *'aql al-'aashir*... It's an allusion to *'ayn-e-'azimah*. "*Matrahan li-shu'a'ihi.*" (A place for his rays to fall). So *sara* means... It is an allusion to *'ayn-e-'azimah*. The phrasing is a bit... Abu Talib is *fath*. Abu Talib is in the station of *fath*. So who became the *hijab*? *Hijab li-l-'aashir*. "*Sara fi maqamihi...*" (He became in his station...). *'Ayn-e-'azimah*. And the *'ayn-e-'azimah* became a veil for the *'aql-e-'aashir*. The discussion is about the Prophet and Abu Talib. So with that, what is the difference in this phrasing? I don't understand it. That you... *'ayn-e-'azimah* are the veil of the *'aql-e-'aashir* because then it says, "*mumiddan lahu*" (aiding him), meaning aiding you, i.e., the Prophet. Aiding the *mim*. Through the mediation of *jadd*, *fath*, and *khayal*. This is the meaning of it. What the difference in phrasing is, I don't know.

"*Alladhina hum al-ruhaniyyun.*" (Those who are the spiritual ones). Such that they are spiritual. *Jadd*, *fath*, and *khayal* are spiritual. "*...al-muqabilat al-thalathat al-jismaniyyun...*" (...opposite the three corporeal ones...). Opposite them are three corporeal ones. In opposition to you, in your opposition, are three corporeal ones. "*...al-ka'inuna baynahu wa baynahum...*" (...who exist between him and between them...). Existing between you and between them. "*...wa 'ala al-haqiqah...*" (And in reality...). And in reality, they are 'Abd al-Muttalib... 'Abd al-Muttalib, 'Abdullah, and Abu Talib. *Jadd*, *fath*, and *khayal* are... are corporeal, 'Abd al-Muttalib. And *jadd*, *fath*, and *khayal* are spiritual, as he said. They are spiritual. What does spiritual mean? In the world of veiling (*'alam-e-ihtijab*). And in the world of veiling are 'Abd al-Muttalib, 'Abdullah, and Abu Talib.

"*Li-annahum qad saru 'uqulan mujarradan 'an al-hawasi... sufara'a baynahu wa bayna al-'aql al-'aashir al-mudabbir li-'alam al-tabi'ah, al-qa'im maqam al-'aql al-awwal li-dhalika al-'alam.*" (Because they had become intellects divested of the senses... emissaries between him and the Tenth Intellect, the governor of the world of nature, which stands in the place of the First Intellect for that world). So they... Because they... because they had become... had become intellects... divested of the senses, from the corporeal. Emissaries between him... emissaries, being emissaries between you... between you and the *'aql-e-'aashir*... Tenth Intellect. Who are the governors... governors of the world of nature. And the Tenth is... in the station of the First Intellect. And the Tenth is... the one who establishes... in the station of the First Intellect in that world. In that world. Meaning the Tenth is... it is in the station of the First Intellect... and *'ayn-e-'azimah* is... it has taken on the deputyship of the Tenth.

In that world, meaning the spiritual world? Yes, the spiritual world. It is the world of life.

"*Fa-'Abd al-Muttalib huwa al-jadd, wa-'Abdullah huwa al-fath, wa-Abu Talib huwa al-khayal.*" (So 'Abd al-Muttalib is the *jadd*, and 'Abdullah is the *fath*, and Abu Talib is the *khayal*). What is written here? What is written here? Abu Talib, is he *fath*? 'Abdullah is *fath*, Abu Talib is *khayal*. What is written there? In what you have? No, this is... it's the same. It's the same. This is a copy. What is written? "*Wa-'Abd al-Muttalib huwa al-jadd, wa-'Abdullah huwa al-fath... wa-Abu Talib huwa al-khayal.*" (And 'Abd al-Muttalib is the *jadd*, and 'Abdullah is the *fath*... and Abu Talib is the *khayal*). He has explained it further.

"*Wa huwa bi-lisan al-shari'ah Jibra'il...*" (And he, in the tongue of the Shari'ah, is Jibra'il...). And he, in the tongue of the Shari'ah, is Jibra'il. And he, in the tongue of the Shari'ah, is Jibra'il. "*...al-jabir li-Muhammadin fi awwalihi wa aakhirihi.*" (...the one who supports Muhammad in his beginning and his end). The one who joins for the Prophet, in his beginning and his end. In the beginning and in the end. "*Wa Mika'il 'Abdullah...*" (And Mika'il is 'Abdullah...). In the beginning and in the end, it means. In the beginning and in the end. In the beginning... beginning means you were raised in the beginning, weren't you? And in the end, you became superior to him (*manfuq*), who? The three are superior. Their connection is with the *'ayn-e-'azimah*. *'Ayn-e-'azimah*, which is *jadd*, *fath*, *khayal*. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him... when it was with *'ayn-e-'azimah*, its dispersal did not happen. This is with the Qa'im, peace and blessings be upon him, *jadd*, *fath*, *khayal*.

Sir, this Jibra'il, peace be upon him, did he have any existence in and of himself? Because in a previous lesson, it was said that Ubayy ibn Ka'b is associated with Jibra'il. Here, Hazrat Abu Talib is being associated with Jibra'il. So does this mean that in every era, there is an associated... As their ranks are, as the ranks increase, the nature of Jibra'il also changes. The helper becomes different. For example, a teacher... in childhood, a teacher teaches the Quran. Yes. A *sahifah* teacher. As they advance, there is some other teacher. As they advance further, the helper (*mumidd*) becomes someone else.

So Jibra'il in and of himself is not some entity? Jibra'il is a station (*maqam*). I see, a station. A station. Whoever comes to that station, at that station... So according to him, whoever is the helper... at what level is the one receiving help? At what rank is he? I see. The rank of *istijabat* (response). When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, had a certain rank, the rank of *istijabat*... Yes. Meaning, when you began... began the training, that was your rank. The same is for Ali. At Ali's rank, Ibn Maryam... Janab Khadijah were your teachers. So as he was at a certain rank, accordingly, Jibra'il... Ultimately, when he reached that station, then that luminous form of life (*surat-e-nurani-e-hayat*) ... So there, Jibra'il is not needed? That station is not needed. From life itself... the three stations will be there. The three representatives who come from the Tenth, they become Jibra'il, Mika'il, Israfil for him.

"*Wa Mika'il 'Abdullah, wa Israfil 'Abd al-Muttalib.*" (And Mika'il is 'Abdullah, and Israfil is 'Abd al-Muttalib).

"*Fa-kana al-nur al-muttasil bi-Muhammadin salawatullahi 'alayh min al-'aashir kulliyyan.*" (So the light connected to Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, from the Tenth [Intellect] was total/complete). And so the light... the light connected with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, from the Tenth... from the Tenth was total. "*Wa li-dhalika kana natiqan...*" (And for that reason, he was a *natiq* [speaker]...). And for that reason, he was a *natiq*. "*...wa huwa 'inda Amir al-Mu'minin shu'a'.*" (...and it [the light] with Amir al-Mu'minin is a *shu'a'* [ray]). And with Amir al-Mu'minin, peace be upon him, it is a ray. What does this mean? "*Wa li-dhalika kana samitan.*" (And for that reason, he was *samit* [silent]). And for that reason, he was *samit*. Meaning the Prophet was a *natiq*, and opposite him, he was a *samit*. Silent. Then later, I have explained clearly in the sermon that there are three conditions (*kayfiyyat*) of *mim* and *'ayn*. What do we call it? *Thalathah majari* (three paths). Three paths. In one, Janab Ali says, "*Ana 'abdun min 'abidi Muhammad.*" (I am a servant from the servants of Muhammad). In the veil. The lowest veil was sent to the world for Ali, the *'ayn-e-'azimah*, so that he may be in companionship with the Prophet, help you, and support you. And the prophets of old, the services they rendered, their reward should be given by the *mustaqarr* (the established one). He was sent for this purpose. And you accomplished that task. That is one, the lowest path. The *majra-e-adna* (lowest path). After that is the *majra-e-musawat* (path of equality), in which the Prophet says, "Ali and I are like this." He said this in many sermons. "O Ali, I am from you, and you are from me." Equal. Equal. Then the third one is what? "O Ali, you have been given five things that even I have not been given." You were given such a father-in-law... No, I was given such a father-in-law... What? Who is the father-in-law? The Noble Prophet. The Holy Prophet. "You were given such a father-in-law that I was not given." The Noble Prophet is saying this for himself. Then, "You were given such a wife that I was not given." Hazrat Fatimah. "You were given such sons that I was not given." These things are superior. You were given three things that I was not given.

The earlier phrase, "*matrahan li-shu'a'ihi*," does it allude to that? The *shu'a'* (ray) that was mentioned? Meaning... the complete *nur* (light) was connected with the Prophet. And its rays were received by Janab Ali. Meaning the entire *nur*... the complete *nur* is with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, because your *hijab* (veil)... this is the mention of the *hijab*. The *hijab* was very high. So the connection of the *nur* is from the Tenth for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. And from him, Ali received it. Due to the *hijab*.

"*Wa kana 'inda Muhammadin salawatullahi 'alayh 'ilmu ma kana... wa 'ilmu ma sayakun.*" (And with Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was the knowledge of what has been... and the knowledge of what will be). Is there a 'wa' (and) there? Yes. There is a 'wa'. So there isn't one here. Is there a 'wa'? Yes, there is. 'Wa' should be there. Yes. Let's assume it should be there. And with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was the knowledge... the knowledge of the thing that had been... that has been, and of what will be. "*Wa 'inda 'Aliyyin 'ilmu ma kana.*" (And with Ali was the knowledge of what has been). And with Ali was the knowledge of what has been... of what happened. This is the mention of the *hijab* of Ali. The *hijab* of Ali. With the Prophet was the knowledge of what has been and what will be. The Prophet made prophecies. And with Ali was the knowledge of what has been. Of what happened. Due to the *hijab* of Ali.

"*Wa lamma awfa Muhammadun salawatullahi 'alayh ma kana 'alayhi min al-khidmah...*" (And when Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, fulfilled the service that was upon him...). And when the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, completed the service that was upon you... that was upon you, in terms of service. "*...wa nassa 'ala 'Aliyyin Amir al-Mu'minin, salawatullahi 'alayh...*" (...and he appointed Ali, the Commander of the Faithful, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him...). And he appointed... he appointed Ali... upon Ali, who is Amir al-Mu'minin. "*...wa intaqala ila dar karamati Allahi Ta'ala...*" (...and he transferred to the abode of the generosity of Allah the Exalted...). And he transferred... he transferred towards the abode of the generosity of Allah Ta'ala. "*...sara Amir al-Mu'minin fi makanihi hijaban li-l-'aql al-'aashir.*" (...the Commander of the Faithful became in his place a veil for the Tenth Intellect). Amir al-Mu'minin became a veil... in your place, a veil for the *'aql-e-'aashir*. As long as the Prophet and Ali were there, only... the Prophet was the veil. When he passed away, Ali became the veil. Ali became the veil. "*Matrahan li-shu'a'ihi.*" (A place for his rays to fall). A place to fall... a place for your rays to fall. The rays of the *'aql-e-'aashir*. A place for them to fall. Janab Ali became. "*Kama kana Muhammadun...*" (Just as Muhammad was...). Just as the Prophet was. "*...wa al-'aashir mutajalliyan bihi.*" (...and the Tenth manifesting through him). And the Tenth is one who manifests through you, that is, through Ali. "*Naziran ilayhi mumiddan lahu.*" (Looking towards him, aiding him...). Looking towards you, helping you. "*...bi-wasatat al-jadd wa-l-fath wa-l-khayal...*" (...through the mediation of *jadd*, *fath*, and *khayal*...). Through the mediation of the *jadd*, the *fath*, and the *khayal*. "*...al-mutajarridin 'an al-ajsam.*" (...the ones divested of bodies). Such that they are divested of bodies. "*Alladhina hum 'Abd al-Muttalib wa Abu Talib wa 'Abdullah.*" (Those who are 'Abd al-Muttalib, Abu Talib, and 'Abdullah).

"*Alladhina hum 'Abd al-Muttalib wa Abu Talib wa Muhammad.*" (Those who are 'Abd al-Muttalib, Abu Talib, and Muhammad). So 'Abd al-Muttalib, meaning the veil of the *'ayn*, became the helper. Who? The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. Through whom? 'Abd al-Muttalib, Abu Talib, and the Prophet...

And *jadd* became Abu Talib, *fath* became, and... Muhammad became *khayal*.

So these are the... of Maula Ali? Yes, these are of Maula Ali. These three became... *jadd*, *fath*, and *khayal*. The helpers.

"*Wa 'Abd al-Muttalib huwa al-jadd...*" (And 'Abd al-Muttalib is the *jadd*...). 'Abd al-Muttalib is the *jadd*. "*...wa Abu Talib huwa al-fath...*" (...and Abu Talib is the *fath*...). Abu Talib is the *fath*. "*...wa Muhammad huwa al-khayal li-Amir al-Mu'minin.*" (...and Muhammad is the *khayal* for the Commander of the Faithful). Here, for Amir Muhammad *khayal*, just as it was above, shouldn't 'Abdullah also be *khayal*? Abu Talib is *al-khayal*. Is it written like that here? Yes. This... *sufara'* (emissaries) need to be *mutajarrid* (divested). "*'Abdullah huwa al-fath, wa Abu Talib huwa al-khayal.*" ('Abdullah is the *fath*, and Abu Talib is the *khayal*). Janab 'Abdullah passed away earlier, didn't he? From Janab Abu Talib. That's why this... according to that... perhaps he has said this. *Jadd*, *fath*, and *khayal*. Yes.

So, this سفیر (emissary), does he need to be *mutajarrid*? Yes. *Mutajarridin min al-ajsam*. (Divested of bodies). The three earlier ones also passed away before the Prophet's... After being divested of bodies, from the world of life, their emanation continues. It happens in life, and from there too...

"*Wa 'Abd al-Muttalib huwa al-jadd, wa Abu Talib huwa al-fath, wa Muhammadun huwa al-khayal li-Amir al-Mu'minin.*" (And 'Abd al-Muttalib is the *jadd*, and Abu Talib is the *fath*, and Muhammad is the *khayal* for the Commander of the Faithful). For Amir al-Mu'minin.

"*Wa li-hadha al-ma'na lam yazhar 'Abd al-Muttalib... wa 'Abdullah wa Abu Talib... fi haykal al-'Aliyyin salawatullahi 'alayh.*" (And for this meaning, 'Abd al-Muttalib... and 'Abdullah and Abu Talib... did not appear in the *haykal* of Ali, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him). Here, put Abu Talib in the middle. Put him above Abu Talib here. Because he passed away earlier. He was divested earlier. ...in the *haykal* of Ali, peace and blessings be upon him. In the *haykal* of Ali, peace and blessings be upon him.

"*Bal baqu fi ufq al-'aashir...*" (Rather, they remained on the horizon of the Tenth...). Rather, they remained on the horizon of the Tenth. On the horizon of the Tenth. "*...li-yakunu wasa'ita baynahu wa bayna Muhammadin wa 'Aliyyin 'alayhima al-salaam.*" (...so they could be intermediaries between it and between Muhammad and Ali, peace be upon them both). So that they may become intermediaries between you and between the Prophet and Ali, peace be upon them. Both of them... the three of them are for the Prophet as well, and for Janab Ali as well.

"*Baynahu*" means? Between him and... So that they may become intermediaries between you and between Muhammad and Ali, peace be upon them. *Baynahu* means between Ali. Here, it is only Ali. And between Muhammad and Ali. For him too, and for both of them too.

This aid that is being mentioned, *salawatullahi 'alayh*, what kind of thing is this? Is it manifest, or spiritual? The decrees (*ahkam*) of spirituality descend from there. What to do, what not to do. The decrees descend. It is the expression of the reality of a thing. I see, so it's acquiring knowledge, etc.? The expression of realities.

"*Wa 'ala hadha al-manha...*" (And according to this method...). "*Baynahu*" means? Janab Ali and... "*Li-yakunu wasa'ita baynahu...*" (so that they may be intermediaries between him...). *Baynahu* means Ali. Intermediaries for Ali. Then "*wa bayna Muhammadin wa 'Aliyyin*" (and between Muhammad and Ali). For him as well, and for both of them. At the time when both were there, at that time between them.

"*Wa 'ala hadha al-manha...*" (And according to this method...). And according to this method... "*...fa-inna kulla muqimin li-maqamin min al-maqamat ba'da nuqlatihi fa-huwa al-khayal lahu. Wa alladhi qablahu huwa al-fath. Wa al-sabiqu 'alayhima huwa al-jadd.*" (...every establisher of a station from the stations, after his transfer, is the *khayal* for it. And the one before him is the *fath*. And the one preceding them both is the *jadd*). So every establisher... for a station... So every establisher... who establishes, for a station from the stations... whichever Imam is established, his *muqim* (predecessor) is in which station? In the station of *khayal*. After his transfer, after his passing. "*Fa-huwa al-khayal lahu.*" (So he is the *khayal* for him). And the one before him is the *fath*. Before him, who is there? He is in the station of *fath*. And the one preceding them both... from those two, the preceding one is the *jadd*. He is in the station of *jadd*.

"*Wa kullu wahidin 'amilun fi mandudihi.*" (And each one is an agent within his extension/mandud). And every one is an agent in his *mandud*. In his *mandud*. First is *khayal*, after that is *fath*, after that is *jadd*. These three are... and who is *khayal*? The *muqim*. The *muqim*. He helps him in all his tasks. Then his *muqim*, then his *muqim*.

So Sir 'Abdullah is... and Abu Talib are... The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, passed away, didn't he? Before. That's why you are... established... This is why... Abdullah is *fath*. And *khayal* is Abu Talib, who is alive. So he is the *khayal*. He passed away later, according to that. But as it is said, "*'Abdullah 'ind Allah.*" (Abdullah is with Allah). When it was asked, what did he say? "*'Abdullah 'ind Allah.*" He didn't put a dot. Abdullah, 'Abdullah can be read. He didn't put dots. No dot here, no dot there.

"*Kama qala salawatullahi 'alayh: 'Takhaffafu talhaqu.'*" (As he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Lighten yourselves and you will catch up."). As he, peace be upon him, said, "O people... lighten yourselves, so that you may join." Meaning, reduce yourselves of sins so that you may go and join the angels. "*Fa-innama yantaziru bi-awwalikum quduma aakhirikum.*" (For the first of you only await the arrival of the last of you). For the first of you are waiting for the steps of your last ones. The departed are waiting for the ones who will come later to come and join them.

All... all the Imams... *natiq* and `wasi`... *ila Imam al-zaman...* and their *hudud*. *Fa ha'ula'i hum al-a'immah alladhina yakununa 'inda mufaraqatihim li kasa'ifihim al-a'za' al-ra'isah min dhalika al-haykal al-nurani alladhi huwa haykal al-Imam 'alayhi afdal al-salam.* (So these are the Imams who, upon their separation from their dense physical forms, become the chief members of that luminous temple, which is the temple of the Imam, upon him be the best of peace.) And these people are those who are... who are... near... when they leave their... *kasif*... their *kasa'if*, meaning their bodies... when they leave their bodies... those... which are the things... those believers... `mu'minin`... who are *walis*... their... Ahl al-Haqq (the people of truth) are also of two kinds. One are those who possess `ma'rifat` (gnosis) and the others are those who perform `ibadat` (worship). They are both the same, those who perform righteous deeds. All things... the first... the first thing is what is being explained. Okay, so they are those who leave behind their density. When they leave... their bodies... when they leave their bodies, then what happens at that time... those... the `hudud kiram` who perform good deeds, when they leave their bodies... then they become... `a'za' ra'isah` (chief members), from that luminous temple... the luminous temple of the Imam... its `a'za' ra'isah` (chief members) are formed. So this is also about the `mu'minin` (believers)... the `hudud kiram` will be mentioned later. Okay. *min dhalika al-haykal...* from that luminous temple... from that luminous temple which is the temple... of the Imam... Imam `alayhissalatu wassalam`... upon him and upon all of them be peace. These are the `suwarat` (spiritual forms) that are becoming part of the `haykal`. `Surat` and `nufus`. The `surat` (form) pulls the `nafs` (soul). `Nafs hissiyyah`. Both, becoming one, reach the `haykal` of the Imam. *Wa 'ala qadri mablaghi kulli wahidin minhum fil 'ilmi wal ma'rifati wal wilayati yakunu 'uluwwuhu fi dhalika al-haykal al-nurani wa yatluuhum ahl al-bayt...* No... *wa yatluuhum... wa 'ala qadri...* and according to the measure... and on the measure of the reach of each one of them... of each one of them in... in knowledge and gnosis and love, it is... of his... his... in that luminous temple. The level of luminosity in that luminous temple is based on the knowledge, gnosis, and devotion he has. `Ilm` is before `wilayat`. *fil 'ilmi wal ma'rifati wal wilayati...* (in knowledge, gnosis, and devotion)... all three are... it's not a matter of what comes before or after, it's about the thing itself. This... knowledge and gnosis and devotion... love. *yakunu 'uluwwuhu fi dhalika al-haykal al-nurani. wa yatluuhum ahl al-wilayat al-mahz wal a'mal al-saliha fi dhalika al-haykal.* (his loftiness is in that luminous temple. And following them are the people of pure devotion and righteous deeds in that temple.) And their followers are those... from them... those who have pure love... who perform love, and from righteous deeds... from that temple. Those people... the first thing is love. After that, what is there? Righteous deeds. The third thing is? True gnosis. All three things are there. Love, righteous action, and... knowledge. So those who possess knowledge, who perform actions, who have love, their rank is much higher. This is what is being said. Now, after this, what is there? Who are their followers? Those who have love, pure love, and righteous deeds, but they do not have true knowledge. *fa yakunu li kulli wahidin minhum...* so there is for each one of them... in their place... that which they deserve. They deserve... *lata'ifun duna kasa'ifi...* subtleties lesser than their densities. *duna kasa'ifi*. `Kasa'if`... these `lata'if` (subtleties) are... *yastahikquhu min lata'ifihi duna kasa'ifihi*. `Kasa'if` is not mentioned, `jism` (body) is not mentioned. `Lata'if` is... `surat` (form) and `nafs hissiyyah` (sensory soul) is mentioned. *wa amma kasa'ifuhum... wa amma kasa'ifuhum, fa takunu mahfuzatan fi a'azzi 'izzin wa ahrazi hirzin.* (And as for their dense physical forms, they are preserved in the mightiest might and the most protected protection.) *wa ahrazi hirzin... wa awzan dhalika annaha ta'udu ila al-sahih...* (and the most protected protection... and the measure of that is that it returns to the earth)... after separation... then to the mixture... then to the tempered mixture, then it returns to... the land of... then... to the rain, then... it becomes subtle to the point that it dissolves into vapor... or... it ascends to the sphere of the constellations... with its rays... and the simplicity of the seven planets... something after something... *wa amma kasa'ifuhum...* and as for their dense forms... their dense forms, so they are... they are preserved... when they are buried in the grave, after that... with the best honor... with the best honor, and with the best protection. With the best protection. And that is in this way, that... they return towards the `sahih` (earth), meaning to the soil. They return to the soil. `Sahih` means... just the body is being mentioned. The body. In this, the `nafs hissiyyah` and so on are not there. `Nafs hissiyyah` (sensory soul), `nafs natiqah` (rational soul) have already departed. So the entire `nafs hissiyyah` has departed? Sometimes the whole thing departs, sometimes it doesn't. Depending on their state... what their state is, according to that. How much he has... followed the `shari'ah` (religious law), according to that his... soul... is released. And that is... and this is the thing, that it returns towards the `sahih`... `sahih` meaning the soil... after the separation... of his `lata'if` (subtleties)... and then towards... the tempered mixture. To the tempered mixture. Meaning above, fire, air, water, soil... its effects, vapors rise... vapor of air, water, these things... mix. It is called `mizaj` and `muntazid`. Then it returns to the earth as rain. Rain. Then it returns... it returns to the land... towards... as rain... then it becomes subtle to the point that it dissolves into vapor. Then it... becomes subtle, to the point that it becomes vapor... and it ascends to the sphere of the constellations. And they ascend towards the sphere of the constellations. `Falak al-buruj` (sphere of constellations) is where? Below the `falak al-muhit`. First is what? `Falak al-muhit` (the encompassing sphere). After that, what is there? `Falak al-buruj`. After `falak al-muhit` is `falak al-buruj`. And below it are all the other spheres. The sphere of Saturn is there. After that, what is there? After Saturn, what is there? Then Mars... No. After Saturn? Jupiter... Jupiter. After Jupiter? Mars. After Mars, the sphere of the Sun. Then the sphere of Venus. Then the sphere of Mercury. Then the sphere of the Moon. Seven spheres are below it. *thumma... wa tas'adu ila...* and they ascend towards the sphere of the constellations. With its rays. With its rays. By means of... the seven planets. The seven planets are below it, right? From the sphere of the moon, above it are seven planets. Above the seven planets is the `falak al-buruj`. They reach the `falak al-buruj`. Little by little. A little after a little. *wa takhallafa shai'an min buruj fi amakiniha wa yanhadiru dhalika al-burdu ila al-ard...* (And it leaves behind something from the constellations in their places, and that garment descends to the earth.) And they become successors... they become... something... from the constellations... in their places... in their places. And that... garment... falls... towards the earth. Towards the earth. *wa yasiru turaban sahikan thumma...* (and it becomes a fine, pulverized dust, then...) and it becomes... dust... `sahiq`... pulverized, then... It is not being understood. The dust which is... what is it's place? They take a place in the `buruj` (constellations). And from the `buruj` some part of it falls from above, down. It... is only the `lata'if` (subtleties) form or... Its `kasa'if`... `jism` (body) is formed. Body is formed. *thumma yaltakhi ila... thumma yaltakhi ila...* (then he ascends until...) Then he is elevated... then he progresses, until he becomes... in the thousand-year realm (`alam al-alfiyyah`), a human. A human. *wa dhalika al-sa'id al-ka'in 'ala badali al-hafil huwa qismun min al-lahm wal jild wal mukhkh wal 'asab wal 'uruq wal ma...* (And that ascended one who is the replacement for the fallen one, he is a portion of flesh, skin, marrow, nerves, veins, and...) And that ascended one... the ascended one... who is... who is... the successor... for the one who falls. Who falls. It fell from above, so this went and became its successor from below. What is it? It is a portion... a portion of... flesh. Of flesh. Skin. Of skin. Marrow. Marrow and brain... so who... who fell, and whose `khalifa` (successor) did he become? Things ascend from here. Yes. The things are there, here... they ascend above, they go and take a place in the `buruj`. Yes. Seven of its... and from there, some things fall. So it is its own things, or from before? No, it's not its things. The one who has... he goes and... in the `dawlab-e-'alam` (wheel of the universe), he stays. In it... from above... things have ascended from here, so the things from before which were ready, they fell. Not its own things... its things. The things from before... the human from before... this goes and takes a place there as `khalifa`. There it takes a place. From there, the things that... whose appearance (`zuhur`) has to happen in the world... So its `hadd 'ali` (higher limit) will not be that... no, the ones from before that. As it used to be. The things from before were also there, right? Their things all fall. This goes and takes its place. The `buruj` do not remain empty, rather, a part of the `buruj` falls onto the earth. And this goes from here and takes its place. So that then in 720 years, their time to fall comes. This ascending, there's no text given for it, that... No, we will explain it. And a portion of flesh... it is a portion of... flesh. Of flesh. And skin... skin... and marrow... and marrow, and nerves... and nerves, and veins. And as for... the portion of bones... what do they say? In the `du'a`... *nur... nurun fi lahmi, nurun fi dami, nurun fi 'izami... nurun fi qalbi, nurun fi sam'i, nurun fi basari...* how many things are there? Twelve things. And seven are... seventeen. *Allahumma j'alli nuran fi qalbi* (O Allah, place light in my heart), one. *nuran fi sam'i* (light in my hearing).
