Of enmity, and of hatred, and of disliked matters. `wa ma iktasabahu min af'al al-khabiha` (and what he earned from wicked deeds). `wa'taqadahu...` The `alif` of the `if'al` form remains, all other `alifs` are dropped. `wa'taqadahu min al-i'tiqadat al-khabitha al-fasida` (and what he believed of the wicked, corrupt beliefs). And what he had earned from wicked deeds, and his belief, from wicked beliefs that are corrupting... which are going to be corrupted. `li-anna jami'a dhalika yabtani...` The letter `ya` has a `shadda`. `yabtani`. Yes, it's correct. `li-anna jami'a dhalika yabtani suratan latifan zulmaniyatan khabithatan mutashakkilatan 'ala shibh al-surat al-sharifa al-nayyira al-latifa` (because all of that builds a subtle, dark, wicked form, shaped in the likeness of the noble, luminous, subtle form). `'allati ibtanat min al-'ulum al-ta'wiliyya wal-hikam al-rabbaniyya wal-ma'arif al-ilahiyya` (which was built from the sciences of `ta'wil`, the lordly wisdoms, and the divine gnoses). Because all... all of that builds... it becomes a subtle form, a dark, wicked form, taking a shape... taking a shape in the likeness of the subtle form. Of the noble, luminous, subtle form. Just as a luminous form is created, so too is a dark form created. If a form is created, then it should also have a `haykal` (temple), and an `Imam al-azdad` (Imam of the opposites) should exist. It is not necessary. It is not necessary. Now, there... their gathering is in the `jawzahar-e-zulmani`, the gathering of their forms. There, a `haykal` is not mentioned. A `haykal` is only here that has been mentioned. Their gathering is there, of the forms. That which was built... yes. That which was built. `yusamma dhalik al-nafs al-zulmaniyya al-iblisiyya al-shaytaniyya` (and that soul is called the dark, Iblisi, satanic soul). And that soul is called... `nafs-e-zulmani`, `iblisiya`, `shaytaniyya`. `Fa-tasiru suratan nariyyatan muhriqah` (And it becomes a fiery, incinerating form). And it becomes a fiery form that is burning... incinerating. `kama qila fi al-surat al-nayyira: nafsun malakutiyyatun natiqa` (just as is said of the luminous form: an angelic, speaking soul). Just as it is said of the luminous form: `nafs-e-malakutiyya natiqa`. This one is called `nafs-e-malakutiyya natiqa`. This one... the luminous form. And this one is `nafs-e-zulmani`, `iblisiya`, `shaytaniyya`. `Wa rubbama sadafat tilka al-nafs al-shaytaniyya insanan` (And perhaps that satanic soul encounters a person). And sometimes... sometimes it comes to... or that satanic soul finds a person. `Fa-tamaththalat lahu naran hatta idha kharuba minha lam yajid shay'an` (So it appears to him as a fire, until when he gets close to it, he finds nothing). So it appears to him in the form of a fire. It appears as a fire at times, that dark, satanic soul-form. Until, when he gets close to that fire, he finds nothing. `wa rubbama harrakat ma yattasilu biha min shajarin aw thawbin aw baytin aw ghayri dhalik` (and perhaps it moves what is connected to it, like a tree or a cloth or a house or other than that). And sometimes it moves what is connected to it, from a tree or a cloth or a house or other than that. `wa rubbama baqiya shay'un min dhalik al-tasawwur al-khabith fi jismihi al-khabith` (and perhaps a thing from that wicked conception remains in his wicked body). And sometimes a thing from that wicked conception remains in his wicked body. The body... I mean if we take a Hindu's body, then the body will burn. It gets burned. The parts of the body remain. The parts of the body... however much is burned, even after burning, every part of his body remains. When God has created, a created thing cannot be annihilated (`fana`). What does `fana` mean? That a thing that has come into existence cannot become non-existent. Its form (`shakl`) can change, but it cannot become non-existent. The existence cannot be changed. The forms of existence can change, but existence cannot become non-existent. No one has the power. The Originator has created it. No one has the power to turn existence into non-existence. `fa-yuqbaru ma'ahu fa-tasiru naran` (so it is buried with him, and it becomes a fire). `fa-yuqbaru ma'ahu` (so it is buried with him). So it is buried with him. Who is buried? That conception. It is buried with him. The dark, wicked soul-form, the satanic soul. `fa-tasiru naran muhriqatan mu'adhdhibatan li-dhalik al-jism muddatan min al-ayyam` (and it becomes an incinerating fire, tormenting that body for a period of days). So it becomes a fire that burns... a torment is given to that body for a period of days. `fa-yura dhalik al-qabr yashta'ilu naran fi al-layl` (So that grave is seen to be aflame with fire at night). So that grave is seen... it is seen that that grave is aflame with fire at night. `wa yushahadu tahajjujuhu` (and its flaring is witnessed). And its flaring is witnessed. `fa-idha kharuba insanun min dhalik al-qabr lam yudrik tilka al-nar` (So when a person gets close to that grave, he does not perceive that fire). `li-kawnih la yudrikuha man kharuba minha` (because he who is close to it does not perceive it). Because he who is close to it does not perceive it. `Wa sahibu hadha al-qabr alladhi tasarrafa lahu tasawwuruhu huwa min akthar al-nas khubsan wa a'zamuhum jurman wa athaman wa ashaddahum 'adawatan wa nifaqan li-ahl al-haqq wa aktharuhum zulman lil-khalq` (And the owner of this grave, whose conception has acted upon him, is the most wicked of people, the greatest of them in crime and sin, the most severe of them in enmity and hypocrisy towards the people of truth, and the greatest of them in oppressing the creation). And the owner of this grave... upon whom such a fire... a burning one... the one who burns him is his own conception. He is the most wicked of people, and the greatest in crime, and in sin, and the most severe in enmity and hypocrisy towards the people of truth, and the greatest of them in oppressing the creation. These incidents were heard of very often. Yes. But now... Nowadays... these incidents of clothes burning or trees burning... `jawzahar`... such incidents are very rare now. Sayyidna Ikramali Saheb, in his travelogue, relates that we were... on the way from Bharuch, we were going to Baroda. Bharuch. In which year? 1255 Hijri is the incident. 1255 Hijri. From here, they went in bullock carts. Two bullock carts... they went where? Satara. They went to Satara. And from Panchvel, they reached Mumbai. From Mumbai, then... from there to Surat. From Surat, they went... from Surat to Baroda. This was in 1255 Hijri. In Bharuch, they had some relatives, so they went to them. And they stayed in a house. And he narrates the incident in detail. And you were teaching. With you were Sayyidna Sheikh Ibrahim Saheb and Sayyidna Fardali Saheb, both of them. They were studying with you. So in one room, inside the room, clothes were hung. Their clothes were hanging. Clothes were hung. And in another room, they were studying. Suddenly, a fire descended from the sky. Fire descended. And when the fire descended, all their clothes burned, the ones that were in the room. Lightning? Yes. Lightning struck. Lightning struck. There were heavy rains, lightning struck. And all the clothes burned. But you and your companions were all safe. And he took them all and then went to Baroda. When they reached Baroda, they received news that... people came out of the city to welcome them. At that time, it used to be like that. Outside the old bridge, people used to go for the reception. They expressed their joy there. And in Baroda, they performed a `ta'am-e-masarrat` (feast of joy). Yes. In one room, all... the other room was completely safe. And another incident of Sayyidna Sheikh Adam Saheb in Baroda... when he was renovating the house, the `jamatkhana`... he was renovating its house. While renovating, two people came to you. Two individuals came to you. From where? One's name was Nizamuddin. Nizamuddin. The other's name, he forgot. What can be said? So both of them came and related that they had gone to the cemetery, `Mumin-bagh`. They had gone to `Mumin-bagh`. And for `ziyarat` (visitation). They performed the `ziyarat`. After performing the `ziyarat`, there was a house there. Sayyidna Ikramali Saheb... not Munshi Sheikh Saheb... what's his name? Faiz Haider Saheb. Where Asadullah Saheb's Fateh Manzil is now. They stayed there. So at night, it rained. And after it rained, they stayed there. They saw from a distance that there is one grave upon which `nur` (light) is descending from the sky. There is a big difference between `nur` and `nar` (fire). `Nur` is a stream of light that was descending from the sky. And they came and informed me. So Sayyidna Sheikh Adam Saheb said, "Until now, many people used to say that such a `nur` descends on your grave, this happens, that happens. But I used to say, 'People say things.' But when these people came and told their firsthand account, then we went and... it was found to be true." It was confirmed that indeed, `nur` descends on that grave in this manner. And you wrote that you have investigated this matter with your own knowledge. That grave belongs to Muhammad Arif Saheb. Muhammad Arif is his name. And still, that grave has a `kendal` (niche) in it. For keeping a lamp. A hole has been made in it. For keeping a lamp, etc. Muhammad Arif Saheb. And when you moved from Ahmedabad, when the `du'at` moved to Baroda, when strife and corruption started to spread, they moved. At that time, there was no land there. Their brothers, people used to pray in their own homes. So you... Muhammad Arif Saheb, his own land, the land of Baroda, where the `jamatkhana` and `masjid` are now, that land he gave as a `waqf` (endowment) for the `jamat`. For the `masjid` and the `jamatkhana`. The reward for that, he received, was that `nur` descends on his grave. You have written this in full detail. And then a question was asked that we are building upstairs. Downstairs is a `sukna` (residence). Downstairs is a residence, a living house. We are building a `masjid` above it. And `da'wati` people are telling us that it cannot be built like that. So he sought permission from Syedna. He said, "I have my own... I have verified the matter through the `nass` (text)." That whichever portion you designate as a `masjid`, that is a `masjid`. Whether it is a portion, a flat, whatever it may be. The portion you designate as a `masjid` is a `masjid`. `tahiyyatul masjid` can be prayed in it. And the portion that is not, is not. That is how it was decreed. You then built the `masjid` and all. The grave is high. A high grave. Sayyidna Ikramali Saheb also has... Sayyidna... `Sayyid al-Rusul`... Besides him, there is another one, Yusuf bin Yusuf Khan. He was also a... he used to listen. `Zarfazlullah Saheb`... `Razi'an sakhiyyan` (content and generous). It is still written. Next to Sayyidna Ikramali Saheb. On the left. Yes, the grave is whitened. The `nur` on the grave... what is its significance? For the elevation of ranks, or for the body to progress quickly... what is this? The soul has already left the body. What... what is the point we can infer from this? When a person passes away, then his `tawajjuh` (attention) is first towards his body, the parts of his body. Then towards his `kafan` (shroud), the parts of his `kafan`. Then towards the soil of the grave. That is why the soil of his grave should be... Not from somewhere else... the soil of his grave should be used to fill it. That same soil should be put on him, not other soil. That soil, at least, should not be thrown here and there. It should be put on top of his soil. And after the soil of the grave, then his entire... his house, the sphere is very vast. The house he lived in, his attention is towards that. His... meaning his own... the soul's own attention. Yes, the soul's attention. The `surat`'s (form's) attention.

<!-- lecture 40 -->

...the body... that it takes whatever form it wants and does whatever it wants. That it takes form... that it takes whatever form it wants and does whatever it wants. And... and for this evil form/soul, after leaving it, what happens? For nafs... in Arabic, there are six particles. What do they do? They give a *zabar* [the vowel 'a'] to the *ism* [noun]. They give a *zabar* to the *ism*. `Inna`, `anna`, `ka-anna`, `lakinna`, `layta`, and `la'alla`. Six particles. `Inna` comes at the beginning of a sentence. Indeed. `Inna`. `Anna` comes in the middle of a sentence, in the meaning of "that". After that, `lakinna`... what is it? But. But... `lakinna`... `lakinna-Allaha 'alimun` (but Allah is all-knowing). It gives a *zabar*. It gives a *zabar* to the *ism*. `lakinna`. And, `inna`, `anna`, `ka-anna`. `ka-anna` means "as if". `lakinna`. `layta`—"if only". `la'alla`—"perhaps that...". "that" is an Urdu word which has been added. It gives a *zabar* to the *ism*. But if after `inna` the letter `mim`, `ma` comes, then its action is nullified. `innama-Allahu` (verily Allah is...). `inna-Allaha 'alimun` (verily Allah is all-knowing). Allah gets a *zabar*. But if `ma` comes after it... `ma` has three types. `ma` has three meanings. What are they? That which is not. What are the meanings of `ma`? One is negation. `ma` means "not". `ma` means "that which". And `ma za'idah` (an extra `ma`). Three. `ma` means "not". `ma` means "that which". `ma` can also be extra. Now here, there is `an`. It is Arabic. `inna`, `anna`. Then `an`. Now what will we read? Will we read `inna`, `anna`, or `an`? `an`. And `in`. `in` means "if". `an` means "that". `an tashakk...` and `in` and `an` come on what? They come on a *mudari'* [subjunctive verb]. They come on a *fi'l* [verb]. They do not come on an *ism* [noun]. `an tashakkala`. And there is one word, `anna`. What does that mean? Indeed. `anin`. `anna ya'innu aninun`. `anin` means crying, crying in sleep. `anin`. `anin` refers to crying. `ja'a aninuhu` (his cry came). That is also from `anna`. `anna aninan` (he cried a cry). So now `an` has come, so there is no *zer, zabar, pesh* [vowel markings] on it. What will we read? Will we read `inna`, `anna`, or `an`? Or will we read `anna`? It itself becomes a verb. That... Arabic has its own special characteristics, one must understand them. If it comes on... on a *mudari'*, then it should be read as `an`. If it... if it comes on an *ism*, if it has come on an *ism*, then it will be `inna`, meaning "indeed". `an tashakkala`. `an tashakkala`. `an tashakkala kayfa sha'at wa taf'ala ma sha'at` (that it takes whatever form it wants and does whatever it wants). `inna` gives a *zabar*, and this which is `an`... `an tashakkala kayfa sha'at`. "that it be formed", "that it be shaped". That it be shaped as it desires, and it does what it wants. And it does `wa taf'alu`. It should be `an yaf'ala`. He has put a *pesh* on the `lam`. The *pesh* is there. `an` gives `zabar`. `an yaf'ala`. `an yaf'ala`, `an yad...`. `an` means "that", it gives a *zabar*. It gives a *zabar* to the *mudari'*. Now he has put a *pesh* here. The *pesh* is not correct. `an tashakkala kayfa sha'at`. "that it be formed", a shape, as it desires. `wa taf'ala ma sha'at` (and does what it desires). It should do what it wants. Because... `Sha'at` - why did this come? What is the feminine thing? Shape. Form. No. Form is the `fa'il` [doer]. `taf'ala`. It is the form. `Surat al-khabitha`. Form is feminine, that is why `sha'at` was brought. `wa taf'ala ma sha'at` (and it does what it desires). What it desires, it should do. `li-annaha qad sarat nihayat al-sharr` (because it has become the extremity of evil). Because... `sha'at`, why did it come? What is the feminine thing? Shape. Form. No, the `fa'il` [doer] is what? `taf'ala`. It is the form. `Surat al-khabitha`. Form is feminine, that's why `sha'at` was brought. `wa taf'ala ma sha'at` (and does what it desires). It does what it wants. `li-annaha`... because that form becomes... has become... has become the end of... the extremity of evil. The extremity of evil. `kama anna tilka al-surata nihayat al-khayr` (just as that form is the extremity of good). Just as that luminous form is the extremity of good. The luminous form is the extremity of good, and the form of... evil... is the extremity of evil. `fa-hiya tashakkalu kama sha'at` (so it takes form as it wishes). So it takes the form as it wishes... `wa taf'alu ma sha'at` (and does as it wishes). And it does what it wants. `li-annaha qad faraqat dhalika al-kathif alladhi huwa al-jism` (because it has separated from that dense thing which is the body). Because it... leaves that dense thing... This is about the *surat al-khabitha* [evil form]. ...has left it... چھوڑ دیا ہے...has left that dense thing which is the body. Mawlana, for us, it doesn't have an existence, right? Evil in itself is not a thing. Distance from good is evil. It is your own creation. Now, what is the origin? It is the intellect. To move away from the intellect is to become the *nafs* [soul]. The *nafs* is also a thing, is it not? It is not something that will remain. It doesn't have permanence. That's the point. It is a thing made by your own hands, it has no permanence. `wa huwa al-mani'u laha min fi'li dhalika li-kathafatihi wa naqsihi` (and it is what prevents it from doing that, due to its density and its deficiency). And it is that which prevents it. And that body... prevents it. That is to say, as long as it was with the body, its powers were limited. When that evil form became separate from the body, its powers increased. Meaning, it no longer has the physical restraint. `wa idha faraqathu lam yabqi...` Is its body better than the *surat al-khabitha*? `Surat al-khabitha` is worse. `wa idha faraqathu lam yabqi laha lam yabqa laha`. `lam yabqa laha`. `mani'un`. When `lam` comes, what happens? When `lam` comes, it makes the verb jussive. It gives *jazm* to the *mudari'* verb. `lam`. Now how should we read the *zabar* here? `ya`... The `ya` has been dropped. Its final `ya`... the final part `ya`, has been dropped. `lam yabqa laha`. So when... it leaves it... it... that *surat al-khabitha* leaves the body... leaves the body, then there no longer remains for that form any preventing thing... any obstacle. `yamna'uha` (that which prevents it). That which was preventing it... that prevents it... from that thing which it intends. `li-annahu laha ka-al-sijn` (because it was like a prison for it). Because that body was like a prison. When they were in prison, their powers were limited. Now that they have come out of prison, they can do as they wish. `wa kana fi 'adl-illahi ta'ala an la tahjuz tilka al-nafs al-khabitha 'amma tastahiqquhu` (And it was in the justice of Allah the Exalted that that evil soul should not be prevented from what it deserves). And it was in the justice of Allah the Exalted that it should not... And it was... Allah the Exalted... in His justice... that there is no obstacle for that soul, the evil soul, for what it is deserving of. It should not be prevented. That it should not prevent. That it should not prevent. That evil soul. That evil soul from that thing... from that thing of which it is deserving. That is, Allah the Exalted also says this, that it should complete its give-and-take. That evil form. Because the scale of justice is established. `li-anna mizan al-'adl qa'imun` (because the scale of justice is established). Because the scale of justice is established. `fa-hiya tablughu ma tastahiqquhu min 'adhab` (So it reaches what it deserves of torment). So that evil soul reaches what it is deserving of, from torment. And other than torment. And from other than torment. `ma'a annaha min waqti mufaraqatiha li-jismiha` (along with the fact that from the time of its separation from its body...). Along with this, from the time of its separation from its body... `fa-hiya fi jami'i ma taf'alu bi-mashiyatiha wa ghayri mashiyatiha fi zarbin min al-'adhab` (it is, in all that it does, by its will and without its will, in a kind of torment). So... and other than torment... along with the fact that... along with this, this is also true... that from the time it leaves its body, that evil soul... at the time of leaving, from that moment... so it... all the things that it does... by its own will and without its will, it is in various kinds of torment. It is in a state of torment. The evil form is in a state of torment. But it has complete free will, too. It has free will in some things. It does not have free will in other things. It is acting by Allah's will. Its torments are complete. Both things: `mashiyatiha wa ghayri mashiyatiha` (by its will and without its will). `a'adhana-Allahu`... `bi-mashiyatiha`, meaning... by its will. By its... by its will, it acts. May He protect us. `a'adhana`. May He keep us in His protection. May Allah keep us in His protection, and His friends... in that matter. `fa-idha faraqat maskanaha alladhi huwa dhalika al-jism al-khabith, talabat al-su'ud, nafidhatan li-kharq...` `li-kharq al-hujub`. `talabat al-su'uda`. `talabat al-su'uda, nafidhatan li-kharq al-hujub`. `li-kharq al-hujub`. `fa-ta'kisuha ash'iat al-aflak raji'atan ila al-ard`. `ta'kisu`. `ya'kisu` or `ta'kisu`. `fa-ta'kisuha ash'iatu...` `raji'atan ila al-ard`. So it remains terrified, regretful. `hasira`. `hasira`. `tahumu hawla manzil dhalika al-jism alladhi kana fihi mahalluhu wa maskanuhu` (it roams around the place of that body, which was its location and dwelling). And the common people call it `mun'if`. They call it this. `wa tabqi... wa tabqi maghbunatan 'ala manzil al-jism wa qabrihi, tajulu muta'allimatan...` `tajulu muta'allimatan lima hiya fihi`. As Allah the Exalted has said... that the devils of humans and jinn... they inspire... some of them... to others... decorated words as a deception. `wa huwa fi athna'i dhalika` (and it is, in the midst of that)... `yajidu dhalika al-insanu al-jahilu bi-dhalika al-hal` (that ignorant human finds that state)... `aw imra'atan jahilatan, aw sabiyyan bi-hadha al-mathabah` (or an ignorant woman, or a boy of this disposition). Or a boy... who has this temperament. `wa tumazijuhu tilka al-surat al-khabithah`. So it mixes with him... it mixes with him, that evil soul... it descends into his house. `fa-yaqulu al-'ammatu: khalatuhu al-jinn, wa fa'alat bihi wa sana'at`. Chapter Six... the sixth section of the fourth chapter on the states of the soul... third section of the fourth chapter on... the third section. The third section of the fourth chapter of the third treatise. `thumma idha khalat tilka al-surah bi-dhalika al-insan wa al-insanah, yantiqu 'ala lisanihi`. Then that form... a form such as has mixed with that man or that woman... it speaks through his tongue. Through his tongue. `wa takadu ta'ti fi dhalika al-nutq bi-shay'in min al-ghaybiyyat wa al-hawadith al-ka'inah`. So why is this respite being given?
Yes?
So why is this respite being given?
So that the person from whom `qisās` (retribution) is to be taken can have `zuhūr` (manifestation). The one from whom `qisās` is to be taken, and the `qisās` is to be completed, when he has `zuhūr` (manifestation), then the full `qisās` can be taken. And after taking it, then everything is cleared.
The satanic act of tormenting and giving pain is also given as a respite. The `qisās` is there, after all. The time must come for it. `tanzilu ila-l-ardi` (it descends to the earth). They fall… they fall from the `mashi'at` (will) of the `Mudabbir` (Director)… from the `mashi'at` (will) of the `Mudabbir`, they fall. `man yastahiqqu`

So, `ghizā` (nourishment) is taken by those… uh… in those things, those foods and drinks. `ghizā` (nourishment) is taken by him. By him. `man` is its subject. `fa-yakūnu li-dhālika mā'baran`. So for them there is a passageway. A place to pass. Its passing place. For the `sūrat-i-khabīthah` (evil form). From that, `zuhūr` (manifestation) occurs. Meaning, eating that thing will have no effect on him?
It comes through him. Through him, in his children. In his children.
`thumma yazharu minhu 'inda-l-mulāmasati baynahu wa bayna zawjatihi` (then it appears from him at the time of intimacy between him and his wife). Then it appears from him at the time of intimacy between him and his wife.

`ilā an yazhara mawlūdan` (until he appears as a newborn). Until he appears as a `mawlūd` (newborn)… he is born as a `mawlūd` (newborn).
`wa yatarabbā fa-yablughu-l-huluma` (and he is raised and reaches maturity). And he is given `tarbiyah` (upbringing), so he reaches… `yatarabbā`, meaning he receives `tarbiyah` (upbringing). He receives `tarbiyah` and upbringing, so he reaches `bulūgh` (maturity). This is the `sīghah` of `tarabbā`, `tafa``ala`. This is… it is not `maf`ūl` (an object). It does not take a `maf`ūl`. `tarabbā`. Here, it means… there are two types of verbs, what are they? `lāzim` (intransitive) and `muta`addī` (transitive). `Lāzim` is that which has a `fā`il` (subject) but does not have a `maf`ūl` (object). And what is `muta`addī` called? It has a `fā`il`—a `fā`il` is necessary—and it… does not have a `maf`ūl`… it has a `maf`ūl`. `Tarabbā` is a verb for which… `tarbiyah pāta hai` (he receives upbringing). For "receives upbringing," there is no… there should only be a `fā`il`, not a `maf`ūl`. And `rabbā` means… `rabbā` means `tarbiyah deta hai` (he gives upbringing). `rabbā`. `rabbāhu` (he gave him upbringing). So here, a `maf`ūl` is needed. A `maf`ūl` is needed. In `tarabbā`, `tarbiyah pāta hai` (he receives upbringing). A `maf`ūl` is not needed. `rabbāhu`. A `fā`il` is needed, and a `maf`ūl` is needed. `Muta`addī`.
Hazrat, this… these idols that these people have, like Kali and so on… are they not these `majāmi'` (gatherings) or `haykal` (structures)? They are all `khabīth` (foul) things. They are all `khabīth` things.
But they don't go inside a `haykal`, as such. A `majma'` (gathering) just forms in the `'uqdatain`. No, in `'uqdatain` it is about the `suwarāt` (forms). Not the `māddah` (matter). The `māddah-i-khabīth` (foul matters) are what are having their `zuhūr` (manifestation) in this world. Their idols, these things, are `khabīth` matters. There is one `māddah` (matter) and one `sūrat` (form). They are material things, which are bad, which have not appeared in a good form.
`ilā an yazhara mawlūdan` (until he appears as a newborn).
`wa yatarabbā` (and he is raised). And he receives `tarbiyah`. `wa yablughu-l-huluma` (and he reaches maturity). He reaches the age of `bāligh` (maturity).
`fa-yakūnu ziddan li-dhālika-t-tawr wa wasiyyihi aw Imāmi-l-'Asr` (and he becomes the opposite of that cycle, and of its wasi or the Imam of the Age). And he becomes the `nātiq`'s `zidd` (opposite). `wa yajhadu maqāmahu` (and he denies his station). And he performs `jihād` against that `maqām`. No, `jihād`. `jihād` or `jahada` with a `hā`. `jahada` means to deny.
And he denies their `maqām` (station). `wa yajhadu maqāmahu` (and he denies his station). And… he performs `jihād`… no, he denies. And he denies that `maqām`.
`wa rubbamā yakūnu huwa-l-mutawālī`
`huwa-l-mutawallī` hai, `mutawālī` `likhe`
`huwa-l-mutawallī`
`huwa-l-mutawallī li-haqīqati-l-hadd alladhī huwa-l-maqāmu bi-nafsihi ka-l-Hārith ibn Murrah alladhī ghattā manzilata Ādam 'alayhi-s-salām` (and perhaps he is the one who takes charge of the reality of the hadd, which is the station itself, like al-Harith ibn Murrah who concealed the station of Adam, peace be upon him).
And sometimes it so happens that he is the `wālī` (ruler) of the killing of that `hadd` (rank). Of that `hadd`. Such that it is the `maqām` (station) itself. He intends to kill the Imam. `ka-l-Hārith ibn Murrah` (like al-Harith ibn Murrah). Like al-Harith ibn Murrah, who concealed the `manzilah` (station) of Ādam `alayhi-s-salām`.
So, concealing the `manzilah` is also a form of killing?
It is a `bātinī qatl` (spiritual killing). But he can also be a `qātil` (killer), that person.
`wa ka-Qābīl alladhī ghattā manzilata Hābīl wa-dda'ā maqāmahu wa qatalahu` (and like Qabil who concealed the station of Habil, and claimed his station, and killed him).
And like Qābīl, who concealed the `manzilah` of Hābīl, and claimed his `maqām` (station), and killed him. Hābīl and Qābīl. Janab Ādam and Hārith bin Murrah. The `qawl`… they are explaining where such `zuhūrāt` (manifestations) occur. From there, from the `'uqdatain`. They are mentioning that.
`wa ka-Rāsib alladhī kāna ziddan li-Nūh 'alayhi-s-salām` (and like Rasib who was the opposite of Noah, peace be upon him).
And like Rāsib, who was the `zidd` (opposite) of Nūh `alayhi-s-salām`.
`Rāsib`... was he a `farzand` (son)?
No, `Rāsib` was not a `farzand`. It is not necessary to be a `farzand`. It is said that he was not a `farzand`. It can be a `farzand`, it is said.
`wa ka-Hām alladhī kāna ziddan li-Sām wa qatalahu ba'da dhālik` (and like Ham who was the opposite of Shem and killed him after that).
And like Hām, who was the `zidd` (opposite) of Sām. They were brothers.
Then he killed him after that.
`wa ka-Nimrūd ibn Kan'ān alladhī kāna ziddan li-Ibrāhīm 'alayhi-s-salām` (and like Nimrod son of Canaan who was the opposite of Abraham, peace be upon him). And like Nimrūd bin Kan`ān, who was the `zidd` (opposite) of Ibrāhīm `alayhi-s-salām`. Such that he was the `zidd` for Ibrāhīm `alayhi-s-salām`. Nimrūd.
And he was from the family of Sām… from the family of Hām.
`wa ka-l-Walīd ibn Mus'ab alladhī kāna ziddan li-Mūsā 'alayhi-s-salām` (and like al-Walid ibn Mus'ab who was the opposite of Moses, peace be upon him).
And like Walīd bin Mus`ab, who was the `zidd` of Mūsā `alayhi-s-salām`.
`wa ka-Sahbūtā alladhī qatala 'Īsā 'alayhi-s-salām` (and like Sahbuta who killed Jesus, peace be upon him).
And like Sahbūtā, who killed… killed `Īsā `alayhi-s-salām`.
`wa ka-Abī Lahab wa Abī Jahl alladhayn kāna zidayn li-Muhammadin sallallāhu 'alayhi wa ālihi wa sallam` (and like Abu Lahab and Abu Jahl, who were two opposites of Muhammad, may God's blessings and peace be upon him and his family).
And like Abī Lahab and Abī Jahl, such that they were both opposites of the Prophet, `sallallāhu 'alayhi wa ālihi wa sallam`.
Here, the mention of Ibn Muljam… there is only mention of one `zidd`.
There is mention of two.
Whose?
In this book, Ibn Muljam is written.
There is a mistake here.
Before this, there is this… for Janab Ali.
Here it is. Perhaps there is a mistake in writing.
`Abū Bakr` is written. The writing has a mistake.
`wa ka-Abī Bakrin wa 'Umar`
And like Abī Bakr and `Umar. `la'natullāhi 'alayhimā alladhayn` (may God's curse be upon them both, who)… `kāna zidayn li-'Alī ibn Abī Tālib salawātullāhi 'alayhi` (were two opposites of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God's blessings be upon him).
Ah, `awwalan` (firstly)…
`wa ka-Ibn Muljam la'nahullāh alladhī qatalahu ākhiran` (and like Ibn Muljam, may God's curse be upon him, who killed him, lastly).
They were both `zidd`s (opposites) of Ali ibn Abi Talib. And… firstly. And… and like Ibn Muljam, who killed him lastly.
`wa ka-Mu'āwiyah la'natullāh alladhī kāna ziddan li-l-Hasan thumma sammahu` (and like Mu'awiyah, may God's curse be upon him, who was the opposite of al-Hasan, then he poisoned him).
And like Mu`āwiyah, may Allah's curse be upon him, who was the `zidd` of Hasan `alayhi-s-salām`. Then he gave him poison.
`wa ka-Yazīd la'nahullāh alladhī kāna ziddan li-l-Husayn` (and like Yazid, may God's curse be upon him, who was the opposite of al-Husayn).
`ziddan li-l-Husayn`
And Yazīd, `la'natullāh`… like Yazīd, may Allah's curse be upon him, who was the `zidd` of Husayn `salawātullāhi 'alayka`.
`wa ka-sh-Shimr alladhī qatalahu` (and like Shimr who killed him). Like Shimr, who killed you.
`wa ka-lladhī samma Mawlānā al-Mustansir Billah salawātullāhi 'alayhi` (and like the one who poisoned our master al-Mustansir Billah, may God's blessings be upon him).
And like that person who… like that person who poisoned Mawlānā Mustansir Billāh, `salawātullāhi 'alayhi`.
`wa ka-l-qātil li-Mawlānā al-Amir salawātullāhi 'alayhi` (and like the killer of our master al-Amir, may God's blessings be upon him). And like the one who killed Mawlānā al-Amir, `salawātullāhi 'alayhi`.
`wa ka-l-Imra'ati-l-Khaybariyya la'nahāllah allatī sammat an-nabī sallallāhu 'alayhi fi-t-ta'ām` (and like the woman of Khaybar, may God's curse be upon her, who poisoned the Prophet, may God's blessings be upon him, in the food).
And like Imra'at al-Khaybariyya, may Allah's curse be upon her, who poisoned the Prophet, `sallallāhu 'alayhi wa sallam`, in the food.
`wa ma'ahu rajulān` (and with him were two men). And with him were two men. With you.
`wa ma'ahu rajulān`. With the Prophet, there were two men. With the Prophet, there were two men. They were also partners in eating.
`fa-māta ahaduhumā` (so one of them died).
So one of them died… he passed away. One of them.
`wa da'ā rasūlullāh sallallāhu 'alayhi li-ahadihimā` (and the Messenger of God, may God's blessings be upon him, prayed for one of them). And the Prophet, `sallallāhu 'alayhi`, prayed for one of them.
`fa-salima` (so he was saved).
So he was safe. He was safe.
The word `salima` is used. With `salima`, you can also read `sallama`, you can read `salima`, you can read `saluma`. Each one has a different meaning. What does `sallama` mean? He handed it over. He said `salām`. `salima` means he was safe.
`fa-salima`.
`wa aqāma dhālika-s-summu ma'a-n-nabī sallallāhu 'alayhi ilā an kāna sababa rillatihi` (and that poison remained with the Prophet, may God's blessings be upon him, until it became the cause of his passing).
And that poison remained with the Prophet, `sallallāhu 'alayhi wa sallam`, until it became the cause of his passing. It came from `'uqdatain`.
From the time of the Battle of Khaybar until his passing, the poison remained in your body?
Yes. His passing was from that.
What did it say? The leg of the goat… the leg of the goat, after you had eaten, the leg of the goat testified, "O Prophet of God, stop! I am poisoned." It is poisoned. Your… the goat is not alive. The goat's… it has been cut. Its leg has been cut, and the leg, it has been roasted. It has been fried, all of that was done. It came before the Prophet and it gave testimony. This is a sign of the Prophet's greatness. When the Prophet… when Janab Ali `salawātullāhi 'alayhi` was asked that a certain prophet had this miracle, another prophet had that miracle, he said, "Our Prophet's miracle was that it was not just living animals that gave testimony, but the leg of a goat, which had been cut from the goat's body, its skin had been removed, it had been cooked, and it had been placed on the fire, and it was brought and placed, and it gave testimony to the Prophet of God, `alayhi-s-salātu wa-s-salām`, and informed you that 'I am `masmūm` (poisoned).'"
It said this after he had eaten?
After eating. So, that is, for previous `anbiyā'` (prophets), living animals gave testimony. And here for you, living animals gave testimony, and when the goat came cooked, it gave testimony.
Why did it testify after he ate? If it had testified before he ate, then some…
How would the `qisās` (retribution) be completed? That is why the greatness of the Prophet is being discussed, that see who the ones are. The enemy of Janab Ādam is who? Hārith bin Murrah. Hārith bin Murrah. And Janab… Qābīl. After that, then… Rāsib, the enemy of Nūh. Rāsib. And Janab Ibrāhīm's? Hām. Nimrūd. Nimrūd bin Kan`ān. The enemy of Sām was Hām. Janab Sām's enemy was Hām. And… The enemy of Janab Mūsā was Walīd bin Mus`ab. And for 'Īsā `alayhi-s-salām` it was Sahbūtā. And for the Prophet, Abū Lahab and Abū Jahl. Two enemies of the Prophet. `li-kulli nabiyyin shaytānun wa liya shaytānān` (for every prophet there is one devil, and for me there are two devils). For every prophet, there is one devil. And for me, there are two devils. So who are they? Abū Lahab and Abū Jahl. After that, what is there? For Janab Ali… they said, `kāna zidayn` (they were two opposites). So for Janab Ali, both of them, Abū Bakr and `Umar. And Ibn Muljam, who killed him in the end. And Mu`āwiyah, `la'natullāh`, was the `zidd` of Imam Hasan. And Yazīd and Shimr, the enemies of Imam Husayn, who killed you, who confronted you. For Mawlānā Mustansir also, and Mawlānā al-Amir.

<!-- lecture 42 -->

*...waqad yakoonu min haadhihil qabaa'is allatee hiya surun mujtami'ah fee 'uqdatayn alladhayni huma al-barzakh al-zulmaanee maa yujra 'alal nabaat fa-yakoonu summan qaatilan minhu talaaf al-maqaamaat al-shareefah kas-summi alladhee kaana sababan li-talaaf al-naatiq.* (And there may be from these vices—which are forms gathered in two knots, which are the dark isthmus—that which is made to flow upon the vegetation, so it becomes a deadly poison from which is the destruction of the noble stations, like the poison that was a cause for the destruction of the *Naatiq*). And it happens from these vices… This too can happen. *Waqad yakoonu*. Yes. This too is possible. And this too… From these vices, such forms exist which are gathered… which are forms that gather. They gather in two knots, such that they are both the *barzakh al-zulmani*. That which descends upon the vegetation (*nabat*), it becomes poison, a killer for the one who kills. From that, the noble stations are destroyed. Destruction… …is destroyed. Destruction… meaning, that is, it is destroyed, the noble stations are destroyed. Destruction means… To kill. It is killed. Death occurs. The death of the noble stations happens, like the poison such that it was the cause for the demise of the *Naatiq*, for the killing, for the death of the *Naatiq*. *Was-summu alladhee talafa minhu al-Hasan 'alayhis salaam.* (And the poison from which al-Hasan, peace be upon him, was destroyed). And from that poison, such that by it, al-Hasan 'alayhis salaam was destroyed. *Talaf* happened. In Urdu, we say *talaf hua* (he was destroyed). They were destroyed by it. *Mawlana Muslim bin Salwat, Mawlana al-Hasan bin Salwat…* and from this poison, such that by it, *Mawlana Muslim bin Salwat* and *Mawlana al-Shams bin Salwat* were destroyed. *Jamee'an*. *Jamee'an*. *Wa minhaa maa yaqa'u fil ma'aadin.* (And from it is that which falls into the minerals). *Wa yaqa'u fil ma'aadin.* And from these forms of vices, that which occurs in minerals… which occur in minerals, then they become… From them, swords, knives… and arrows. And from it are swords, and knives, and arrows. With which the noble stations are killed. Attack is carried out. Attack is carried out with it on the noble stations… whose mention has preceded. The swords with which the Imams were killed, the knife, the arrows, that is… The two knots whose forms they are, they descend. And in this… its parts take revenge. They are in the minerals. Yes, they can be in minerals or in vegetation. Who come to take revenge. *Yuftaku bihi fil maqaamaat al-shareefah al-saabiq zikruhaa.* (With which an assault is made on the noble stations whose mention has preceded). As has been mentioned before. *Li-anna haadhihil qabaa'is idhaa waqa'a minhaa 'alan nabaat kaana dhaalika al-nabaat sumoomman qaatilan li-man yaseeru ilayhi min al-maqaamaat al-shareefah al-masmoomah.* (Because these vices, when some of it falls upon vegetation, that vegetation becomes a deadly poison for those who go towards it from the poisoned noble stations). Because when those… vegetation… those vices… that which happens… when they happen, from them, on the stations, on the vegetation, then that is the vegetation… that vegetation is poisonous, deadly poison, killing, for those who reach… towards them, from the noble stations, who are poisoned. *Wa in waqa'a 'alaa ma'danin kaana minhu suyuufun wa sakaakeenu wa nisaalun lil-nabli yuqtalu bihaa man qutila min al-maqaamaat al-shareefah.* (And if it falls upon a mineral, from it come swords, knives, and arrowheads for the bow, with which are killed those who are killed from the noble stations). And if the occurrence… upon the mineral… and if it occurred on a mineral… those things come upon the mineral, then from it are swords, and knives, and arrows… arrowheads, for the bow… with which are killed… those who are killed from the noble stations. *Li-annahaa taqa'u 'alaa amthaalihaa min ma'aadin wal-nabaat al-madhmoomah al-mal'oonah.* (Because they fall upon their counterparts from the condemned and cursed minerals and vegetation). As it was said of Shimr, Shimr’s sword. The sword of Shimr, that was also described. *Li-annahaa taqa'u 'alaa amthaalihaa.* (Because they fall upon their counterparts). Because they occur… because they occur on their counterparts, from minerals and vegetation, which are condemned and cursed. *Fakullu shay'in minhaa mahfoozun li-saahibihi.* (So every thing from it is preserved for its owner). And every thing from it is preserved for its owner. It is preserved for its owner. *Wal-haafizu lahu huwa al-jaww al-zulmaanee.* (And the preserver for it is the dark atmosphere). And its preserver is the one who is in darkness. Its management continues. Its things are kept in preservation. Where to keep it, at what time to deliver it, its plans continue. So, *saahib*... protector (*muhaafiz*), what does that mean? For whom? For his… for its owner, it becomes a protector, meaning… A shield. A shield-like thing. Where is *muhaafiz*? *Mahfoozun li-saahibihi.* Meaning, it is kept safe. *Mahfooz* means it is kept. It is protected. Its protection is done so that when the one to be killed arrives, he can be killed with it. It is protected for its owner. The preserver is… The dark atmosphere. Such that they are two knots. *Bi-mashee'at al-mudabbir.* (By the will of the Planner). By will, of the Planner. *Wa moojib al-hikmah.* (And the requirement of wisdom). And by the requirement of wisdom. *Wa meezaan al-'adli lillahi ta'ala.* (And the scale of justice of Allah Ta'ala). And by Allah’s scale of justice. *Li-anna al-maqaama fee dhaalika al-'asri in kaana saahiba sayfin wa qatlin wa quwwatin wa ghalabatin kaanat suwar al-maqtooleen min al-azdaad al-saa'idat ilal 'uqdatayn al-muqtassah min dhaalika al-maqaam al-shareef.* (Because the station in that era, if he is the owner of the sword, killing, power, and dominance, then the forms of the slain from the opposites ascend to the two knots to take revenge from that noble station). Because the station… because the *maqaam*… the *Imam*… in that era… in that time, if he is the owner… if he is the owner of the sword, and killing, and power, and dominance… and killing, power, and dominance, then they are… then they are the forms of the slain, of the opposites, who are ascending towards the two knots… and they are the ones taking revenge… from that noble station. Because… *li-annahaa taseeru mu'ajjalatan.* (because it proceeds swiftly). Because it reaches… because it reaches with speed… with speed to the station of that cursed person, becoming a devil, they attack… they attack that station with killing, taking revenge… taking revenge from those… from those people… such that they had killed them. *Wa in kaana dawr al-maqaami fee dhaalika al-'asri dawra awaamirin wa nawaahin wa iqaamati hudoodin wa jaldin wa habsin wa nafyin wa maa yajree haadhal majraa kaanat suwar al-azdaad al-jaariyah 'alayhim dhaalika 'inda mawtihaa wa nazoolihaa min dhaalika al-barzakh sumoomman kamaa sabaqa fil qawl.* (And if the era of the station in that time is an era of commands and prohibitions, and establishing punishments, and flogging, and imprisonment, and exile, and what follows this course, then the forms of the opposites that are executed upon them near their death, and descend from that isthmus, are poisons, as has preceded in the discourse). And if the era of the station is in that time… an era of… of the *Imam*… *nurani*… in that era is an era… in that era, an era of commands and prohibitions. An era of commands and prohibitions, meaning, it is such a time when the Imam is manifest, giving commands, forbidding things. It is such a time. *Wa iqaamati hudoodin.* And establishing punishments. *Wa jaldin.* And *jald*, meaning… to whip them. *Jald* means to whip. Whipping, and imprisoning, and exiling, and that which… that which happens in this course, then are the forms of the opposites, which are جاری, flowing upon them… near their death, and their descent to that *barzakh*, from that *barzakh*, and their descent from it as poisons, as the discourse has preceded. And if the era of the station is in that time… that era’s… …*nurani*... In that era, an era… in that era, an era of commands and prohibitions. An era of commands and prohibitions, meaning it's a time when the Imam is manifest, giving commands, forbidding things, such a time it is. And establishing punishments, and *jald*, and *jald* means to whip them. *Jald* means whipping. Whipping, and imprisoning, and exiling, and that which is جاری happens in this course, then are the forms of the opposites, which are جاری, which are happening upon them near their death, and reaching their *barzakh*, and descending from it, and descending from it as poisons, as the discourse has preceded. Just as the Prophet and Sayyidna Ali, peace be upon him, faced opposition in various battles, those who took revenge… there was no one… In this, in that… Now, the promotions (*taraqqiyaat*) have to happen. Whose? The promotions of the gathering of Sayyidna Imam Husayn have to happen. Now, how will these promotions happen? If their wrongdoings (*ziyadati*) remain, their promotion is not possible. So, those wrongdoings which happened from the army, which was Ali's army, those who were against him… and the killing of women happened, and they were whipped, this happened, that happened, in that era. Now, its revenge has to be taken. If it's taken after that, then for that… the opposites (*azdaad*) which… they take on their own… their respective punishments (*jaza'*) which… the transgressions that happened, they should take revenge for them so that their retributions (*qisaasaat*) are complete and their further promotion can happen. It is a purification. So this planning (*tadbeer*), whose is it? That these things should come quickly? The planning is of the era, but the *jaww al-zulmaani* (dark atmosphere), the planning is through it. Its thing is protected. Through the two knots, its protection is carried out. So that too, just as… is subject to the planning. Yes. All these plans are of Allah Ta'ala, and of the Imam of the time, that the retributions should be completed. The retributions… he is the intermediary (*waasta*). That the giving and taking of retributions should be completed. This is the purpose. *Waqad yakoonu min suwari haa'ulaa'il mas'ooleen…* (And there may be from the forms of these accursed ones…). *wa minhaa shakhsun yusallimu dhaalika...* (And from it is a person who delivers that...). *wa minhaa shakhsun yusallimu dhaalika al-summa ilaa dhaalika al-maqaam al-shareef 'alayhi afdal al-salaam.* (And from them is a person who delivers that poison to that noble station, upon him be the best of peace). That… her grave was… *Yusallimu dhaalika…* And from them is that person… that person is who delivers… delivers that poison… to that noble station… upon him be the best of peace. The person who does such a thing, he too is a collection of curses. A collection of curses. He too is… from that… from that cursed form, which is gathering in the two knots. Just like the wife of Imam Hasan, 'alayhis salat was-salam, Ja'dah. She was from the same. *Wa qad yakoonu min suwari haa'ulaa'il mas'ooleen minhum la'anaatun min al-maqaamaati wal-hudood.* (And there may be from the forms of these accursed ones, curses from the stations and the punishments). And it happens… and it happens from the forms of these… from among them are curses from the stations and from the punishments… from the punishments. *Fa-yakoonu aktharuhum fee zulmihim wa 'akadu li-'adaawatihim wa shaytanatihim.* (So they are excessive in their oppression and most confirmed in their enmity and their devilry). Then they are excessive… they are excessive in their oppression… in their oppression and in confirming their enmity and their devilry. Sayyidna Amir al-Mu'minin, 'alayhis salat was-salam, had told the people of Iraq, the people of Kufa, who had committed transgressions against him and left him at the time, and gave him hardships, he cursed them, that such a person will be imposed upon you who will give you severe hardships, severe punishments. So he is saying that those curses that are… they all gathered, and it was said, where? In the two knots. And those curses, this Hajjaj… Hajjaj, who was the greatest tyrant, in him they gathered and came. Those forms came and gathered. And he committed all sorts of oppressions. *Kal-Hajjaj.* (Like al-Hajjaj). *Alladhee zahara li-ahl al-'iraaq.* (Who appeared to the people of Iraq). Who became manifest… who became manifest for the people of Iraq. *Wa awlaad al-a'immah al-mu'mineen allatee kaanat ta'lamuhu.* (And the children of the believing Imams, which she knew). *Fa-yajtami'u dhaalika...* (So that gathers...). So… having a judge… and their… like them… curses, conception, from the opposites… and from the opposites, they gathered… those things gathered… the curses and the opposites gathered… it became extremely severe… it became more severe… in harm, and in enmity for the people of Haqq. For the people of Haqq. *Wa li-jamee' al-khalq.* (And for all of creation). And for all creations. *Wa li-dhaalika...* (And for that...). And for that reason, that great calamity is a destroyer for the whole world. For the whole world. *Fa-jtama'at fee dhaalika al-barzakh al-muzlim ilaa an zaharat 'alaa ahl al-'iraaq.* (So it gathered in that dark isthmus until it manifested upon the people of Iraq). It gathered in that dark isthmus… which is the two knots… two knots… until it manifested upon the people of Iraq. So that whatever happened from his actions among them… whatever happened. *Wa ka-ibni Mahdi alladhee kaana min la'anaat al-hudood wa tasawwur al-azdaad.* (And like Ibn Mahdi, who was from the curses of the punishments and the conception of the opposites). And like… Ibn Mahdi… such that it was from the curses of the punishments, from the conception of the opposites. Such that the curses happened from the punishments. Yes? From the curses of the punishments. In the punishments, the curses that are there, on them, his conception… and the conception of the opposites, there too, such things are made. So curse is the opposite of prayer? Yes, curse. And in prayer, seeking mercy (*tarahhum*) is not permissible, but cursing is permissible. Cursing is that Allah Ta'ala may distance from His mercy. What does curse mean? Cursing means to distance. May he be distanced from the mercy of Allah Ta'ala. *Wa subbat 'alaa… Ibn Malaa'…* Ibn Mahdi… *Tasawwur al-azdaad li-ahl al-tihaamah.* (The conception of the opposites for the people of Tihamah). For the people of Tihamah. *Fa-jtama'at fee dhaalika al-barzakh.* (So it gathered in that isthmus). Then it gathered in that isthmus… In which isthmus? In the two knots. *Wa subbat 'alaa ulaa'ika al-mudillaat al-malaa'in.* (And it was poured upon those misguided, cursed ones). And they were poured upon… on the misguided ones… the cursed ones. *A'adhana Allahu min dhaalika bi-haqqi Muhammadin wa aalihit taahireen salawatullahi 'alayhim ajma'een.* (May Allah protect us from that, by the right of Muhammad and his pure progeny, may the blessings of Allah be upon them all). May Allah keep us in His protection from that… by the right of the Prophet and his pure progeny. *Al-Bab al-Khamis.* (The Fifth Chapter). This *darik* is a pair, this thing’s pair, of those who send curses. From the opposites of the two knots, that curse comes. Yes. From the conceptions of the opposites which gather in the two knots. Then, in addition to that, the curses that are done upon them, they all descend and create such people who are the worst in the world, like Hajjaj bin Yusuf al-Thaqafi. And Ibn Mahdi is mentioned. So their curses are also accepted? The curses that are there, the curses that happen, so on whom are the curses done? On those people who had given hardship to Ali. To Imam Husayn, they gave hardship. Those curses, when they take form, they descend upon the people of that era. Like Hajjaj, he didn't only torment the followers of Ali, but rather whoever came in his path, he gave them hardship, or killed them. Who accepts the curses? If we pray, then the Lord of the Time accepts. Here, who… The meaning of curse is this: *la'ana Allahu min rahmatihi* (may Allah curse him from His mercy). Before it, the forms of the opposites gather. To other forms, the forms of the opposites gather there. *La'ana Allahu min rahmatihi.* The promotion of the *awliya* also happens through this. That they have to take and give from them, that has to be completed. Just as you are the opposites, you have been commanded that the opposites are such that they do not only oppress the believers, but they let loose a flood of oppression on the entire nation. So what is it? Then Ali cursed them, saying, "Look, you are… such a person will be imposed upon you who will inflict great oppressions upon you." Not just on the believers, but… on those who had left him. *Al-Bab al-Khamis.* (The Fifth Chapter). *Al-Bab al-Khamis fee raaziq al-saadis.* (The Fifth Chapter in the Sixth Provider). A big chapter. Two, four, six, eight… Let's mention it. Three pages were read. Yes. Three pages have been read. Shall we read? *Al-Bab al-Khamis fee raaziq al-saadis wa huwa fee khamsati fusoolin. Al-fasl al-awwal minhaa.* (The Fifth Chapter in the Sixth Provider, and it is in five sections. The first section thereof). The fifth chapter in the sixth provider, which is in five sections. And the first section from it. *Wa amma ajsaamu haa'ulaa'il azdaad wa nufusuhum fa-innal nafsa al-waahid minhum 'inda mawtihi tashree'u fee jismihi wa yaseeraani shay'an waahidan.* (And as for the bodies of these opposites and their souls, indeed the single soul from among them at its death spreads throughout its body, and they both become one thing). *Wa yastaheelaan ilal turaab.* (And they both transform into dust). And the bodies of these opposites and their souls, so indeed the one soul from among them, any one of them, near its death, spreads into its body. In the believer, what happens? Their bodily parts become the soul. Here, what happens? Their soul becomes the body. The process is reversed. Sir, this… The soul spreads? Yes. Does it become smaller and then spread? The soul spreads out. So what happens? The soul spreads into the body. The soul spreads out, and it takes on a bodily form. The body doesn't grow. It spreads out. And it spreads out in such a way that the punishments of the grave are felt by him. Then in the future, the soul, no one can destroy it. It is a thing created by God. Whether the soul is bad or good, no one can bring its existence into non-existence. Now, its process has been explained, that the soul, wherever it is, will be a cause of torment for it. Until it completes its retributions, after which it will be given an invitation and it will accept the invitation. The nature of the soul will change. And they both become one thing. And they both become one thing. And they both transform into dust. *Thumma yas'adaani bukhaaran.* (Then they both ascend as vapor). They ascend as vapor. *Fa-yanzilaani mataran.* (Then they both descend as rain). And they descend as rain. *Wa yuhdithu min dhaalika al-matari al-buruqat al-muhliqat.* (And there are produced from that rain the destructive lightnings). And from that rain are produced lightnings that are destructive. *Wal-sawaa'iq al-mutlifaat.* (And the annihilating thunderbolts). And thunder that annihilates. *Wal-suyool al-mukhribat.* (And the ruinous floods). And floods that are ruinous. *Wal-barad al-mudirr.* (And the harmful hail). And hail that is harmful. *Wa dhaalika min fi'l al-muzaddaat fee jamee' al-awqaat.* (And that is from the action of the opposites in all times). And that is from the action of the opposites in all times. They continue their work. What? Their bodies and souls. The calamities that occur in the world, their effect is present in them. So the two knots also affect them, and these bodies and things also affect them. The two knots, a conception reaches them. What conception reaches the two knots? The body and soul. The body and soul, these things also… They happen. Meaning, severe cold, severe heat… *al-barad al-mudirr*, rain, floods, thunderbolts, thunder and lightning. *Wa yansabbaani ilal ardi fa-yaseeraani nabaatan wa hayawaanan.* (And they are poured upon the earth, and they become vegetation and animals). And they are poured… they descend on the earth. They descend on the whole earth. Vapors are formed, they rise, and descend upon the earth. *Wa yaseeraani nabaatan.* (And they become vegetation). And they both become… and they both become, those two… the soul and body… animal, and they take from it… who eat it, take sustenance from it… so that they get sustenance. So that he gets sustenance. *Wa yastaghriqu bihim al-'azaab al-adnaa.* (And the nearer torment is unleashed upon them). And the nearer torment is unleashed upon them. They are those two… dragons. And walking on the bridges of torment. And they are the seven dragons, from the torment of God. And Allah has kept us and His saints safe from that. So its first is the level of *rijs*. *rijs*. What did we say in *husayn*? *ra'u khunnar*. *ra', waw, 'ayn, khay, nun, nun, ra'*. *ra'u khunnar*. It is made gentle. *Wa awwaluhaa dark al-rijs.* (And its first is the level of *rijs*). So its first is the level of *rijs*. So this… this which… the vapors that form, from that, this vegetation is also formed and… it takes sustenance from that. And from that, the creatures of torment are born. The first torment that is, its description is being given. The first torment. *Wa awwaluhaa dark al-rijs.* So the first… its first level is *rijs*. *Wa huwa qamees al-bashar.* (And it is the human tunic). And it is the tunic of a human. Now our master used to say, don't say *qamees* (shirt), they would get angry. If you said *qamees*, he would say, "Don't say that, say *kurta* (tunic)." *Wa huwa qamees al-bashar.* And it is the tunic of a human. *Wa yaseeru dhaalika al-mughtadhee bihi nutfatan.* (And that consumer becomes a sperm-drop by it). Then that consumer becomes… that consumer of sustenance becomes a sperm-drop from it. The one who consumes sustenance from it becomes a *nutfah*. *Wa yartaqee ilaa rahimin fa-yakhruju min batni ummihi janeenan fee qameesin min qumus al-zanj wal-zabab wal-barbar wal-turk wa ghayrihim minal ladheena laa yasluhu mukhaatabat ahl al-haqq wa laa yanhaajoona minhaj al-rashaad.* (And it ascends to a womb and emerges from its mother's belly as a fetus in a tunic from the tunics of the Zanj, the Zabab, the Barbar, the Turk, and others like them, for whom addressing the people of truth is not suitable, nor do they follow the path of guidance). And he ascends to a womb, and emerges from his mother's belly as a fetus in a tunic from the tunics of the Zanj, and the Zabab, and the Barbar, and the Turk, and others besides them, from among those for whom it is not suitable to address the people of Haqq. It is not suitable to address the people of Haqq. And they do not walk on the path of guidance. *Wa laa yazaalu yantaqilu min qameesin ilaa qameesin ilaa an yastawfee fee kulli naw'in min haadhihi al-anwaa'i sab'eena qameesan.* (And he continues to transfer from one tunic to another until he completes seventy tunics in each type of these types). And he always remains… transferring from one tunic to another until he completes in every type from these types, seventy tunics. 490… 70,000 years. 70,000… No, it means 70 tunics in one level. Seven levels, so in this way… 490… 7 * 7 = 49. 490,000. He does not reach the whole tunic. Its method is that he reaches one tunic. It is possible that after that he may come back from the tunic. Not every person has to. A few… a very great… stubbornness, they complete all these tunics. Sir, apparently it doesn't seem like that many nations are in torment, it doesn't seem so. There are Turks, these days of course there is civilization and all. So Allah Ta'ala has concealed this in nations, that they are in torment? The ascending and descending are both gathered in one place, aren't they? Don't you think so? The ascending ones… have arrived at a single platform. Like, it has been explained before in an example that an animal… all are animals. There is a lawful animal and an unlawful animal. They are on one platform. The lawful animal is the one that is ascending. And the unlawful animal is the one that is descending. But they are on one platform. Similarly, among them too, there are Zanj, who are descending. There are… on that path, they have returned, that can also happen. Turning back. Turning back is… yes, that is, how do the manifestations happen? A thousand years were mentioned. They descend for a thousand years. Now for them, a thousand years have not been specified. But in one level, in seventy types, he wears one tunic. Like seventy levels were mentioned. 70 tunics. *Thumma kharaja min al-azdaad wal-mumtazid ilal khums al-'aks.* (Then he emerges from the opposites and the blended into the quintessence of the عكس 'reversal'). Then they emerge from the opposites… in the mixture… to *khums al-'aks*. *Wa huwa al-dark al-saanee.* (And it is the second level). And it is the second level. *ra'd*. *ray, waw, 'ayn*. *rijs*. What did we read before? What do we read in the du'a? *A'oodhu billahi min al-rijs al-najis.* *rijs*. So it is *wa huwa al-dark al-saanee al-mumaasil lil-tarkeeb al-bashariyyah wa hum al-qird wal-dubb wal-nasnaas wal-ghawl wal-'izaar wa amthaal dhaalika.* (And it is the second level, similar to the human composition, and they are the ape, the bear, the nasnas, the ghoul, the 'izaar, and the likes of that). And the second level is what is similar to the human form. And that is the monkey. So in the human form, the first tunic is human. The second is human-like, who are similar to the human form. And they are the monkey, and the bear, and the *nasnas*, and the *ghawl*, and the lizard, and various types. The *nasnas* is a creature in Arab lands, half a creature. This second one is also from *khums*. It is from *khums*. And its examples, its likes, that are human-like. *Wa yuslaku bihi fee kulli naw'in min haadhihi al-anwaa' sab'eena qameesan.* (And he is made to pass through seventy tunics in each type of these types). And they are made to pass through… they are made to pass through every type from these types, seventy tunics. *Ilaa an yastawfee jamee'ahaa.* (Until he completes all of them). Until he completes them all. *Wa huwa fee jamee'i haadhihi al-qumus al-waqtiyyah yatahaqqaqu lahu wujood al-'azaab.* (And he, in all these temporal tunics, the existence of torment is confirmed for him). And in all these temporal tunics, it is confirmed for him that he is in a state of torment. *Wa annahu waqa'a fee dhaalika mukhaalafat arbab al-haqq.* (And that he fell into that due to opposition to the lords of truth). And that he fell into that level due to opposition to the masters of truth. *Wa yaseeru 'aarifan bihim.* (And he becomes aware of them). And he becomes one who knows them. *Mutahaqqiqan lahum, 'aarifan li-ahl al-baatil alladheena wasala bihim wa waqa'a fee adraak al-'azaab.* (Confirmed for them, knowing the people of falsehood through whom he reached [this state] and fell into the levels of torment). And he becomes one who knows them, and is confirmed for them, knowing the people of falsehood through whom, due to them, he fell into the levels of torment. *Thumma yuslaku bihi fee khums…* It is pointed out to him that he sees. So it becomes known to him that this is the reason why he is in this state. He himself. Yes. Whoever is going into that level, he knows why he is going. Why he has gone. In this level of *khums*, it has been said. *Thumma yuslaku bihi fee khums al-'ars, wa huwa al-dark al-saalis wa huwa sibaa' al-barri wal-bahri.* (Then he is made to pass into the *khums al-'ars*, and it is the third level, and it is the predators of the land and the sea). And then he is made to pass into *khums al-'ars*. And that is the third level. And it is the predators of the land and sea. *Kal-usood.* (Like lions). Like lions. *Wal-numoor.* (And tigers). And tigers. *Wal-dhi'aab.* (And wolves). And wolves. *Wa amthaalu dhaalika minal sibaa' al-bahriyyah.* (And the likes of that from the predators of the sea). And its examples, like the predators of the sea. *Wa 'alal jumlah kullu dhee naabin wa mikhlabin barriyyin wa bahriyyin.* (And in sum, every creature with a canine tooth and a claw, of the land and the sea). And on the whole, every one with a canine, what do you call a canine? The one with canines. *Mikhlab*, the one with claws. Of the land or the sea. The unlawful animals, they don't have canines, they don't have claws. The unlawful animals, they have canines and claws. Canine means what? The teeth which tear and rip. And *mikhlab* is the claws like this. *Ilaa an yastawfee fee kulli naw'in min haadhihi al-anwaa' sab'eena qameesan.* (Until he completes seventy tunics in each type of these types). Until he completes in every type from these types, seventy tunics. *Wa huwa 'aalimun bimaa huwa feehi min al-'azaab, mutahaqqiqan lahu, 'aarifan li-ahl al-haqq wa ahl al-baatil.* (And he is aware of the torment he is in, confirmed for him, knowing the people of truth and the people of falsehood). And he is aware of what he is in. He is aware of what he is in, of torment, confirmed for him, knowing the people of truth and the people of falsehood. Confirmed for him, meaning he feels the torment. He feels that I am in this… Look, the bounty… he feels that this is the punishment of God. Because he sees humans, he is in the state of an animal. So Allah has given the mind that much power to him, that he understands that I am in this state for this reason. Why was this not given in the first tunic? In the human one? It has not been mentioned. *Thumma yuslaku bihi fee khums al-khars, wa huwa al-dark al-raabi', wa huwa hawaam al-barri wal-bahri kal-afaa'ee wal-hayyaat wal-'aqaarib wa ghayrihaa minal anwaa' al-laatee tushbihuhum fa-yatakhammasu fee kulli naw'in fee haadhihi al-anwaa' sab'eena qameesan.* (Then he is made to pass into *khums al-khars*, and it is the fourth level, and it is the crawling creatures of the land and the sea, like vipers, snakes, scorpions, and others from the types that resemble them, so he takes on a fifth form in every type in these types for seventy tunics). He is made to pass, you see, he is mute. He cannot speak. The animals which… in which he is mute, he cannot speak. He cannot make any sounds. In the tunic of *khums*, *wa huwa al-dark al-raabi'*. And it is the fourth level. And it is the crawling creatures of the land and sea. The whole class that crawls on the ground. Of the land and sea. Like vipers, and snakes, and scorpions, and other than them, from the types that resemble them. And they are clothed in a tunic in every type from these seventy types of tunics. *Ilaa an yastawfee jamee' dhaalika wa huwa mutahaqqiqan bimaa huwa feehi min al-'azaab, 'aarifan li-ahl al-haqq wa ahl al-baatil.* (Until he completes all of that, and he is confirmed in the torment he is in, knowing the people of truth and the people of falsehood). Until he completes them all, and he feels what he is in, of torment, knowing the people of truth and the people of falsehood. *'Aaliman annahu saara ilaa ma saara min al-'iqaab bi-mukhaalafati arbaab al-haqq wa ittibaa' ahl al-baatil.* (Knowing that he reached what he reached of punishment due to opposition to the lords of truth and following the people of falsehood). Knowing that he reached, that he reached the punishment which he reached, from the torment, by opposing the people of truth and by following the people of falsehood. *Thumma yuslaku bihi fee dark al-khums, al-musamma bil-najis wa hum tayr al-barri wal-bahri 'ala shaaqilat zawaat al-jawarih ilaa an yastawfee fee kulli naw'in minhaa sab'eena qameesan.* Then it is said that he is mute. Meaning in one tunic there is also dumbness. Yes. And then in the fifth tunic, sounds come out, like of vipers and such. No, there are sounds. But their specific speech, which is what is called human speech, is not there. There is screaming. The first is human, the second is human-like, the third is tearing and ripping, the fourth is crawling… Reptiles and amphibians. Crawling creatures. And the fifth is what is flying creatures. *Tayr al-barri wal-bahri.* (Birds of the land and the sea). Birds. Then he is made to pass through the fifth level, named *najis*. And they are the birds of the land and sea, in the form of predatory birds. Until he completes in every type from them, seventy tunics. *Wa huwa fee jamee' dhaalika mutahaqqiqan lil-'azaab alladhee laqiyahu, 'aarifan bihi, muta'alliman minhu, 'aarifan bi-ahl al-haqq wa ahl al-baatil, 'aaliman annahu saara ilaa maa saara ilayhi min al-'iqaab bi-mukhaalafati arbaab al-haqq wa ittibaa' ahl al-baatil.* (And he, in all of that, is confirmed in the torment which he has met, knowing it, learning from it, knowing the people of truth and the people of falsehood, knowing that he reached what he reached of punishment by opposing the lords of truth and following the people of falsehood). And he, in all that state, feels the punishment that has reached him, reaches him. He feels it, and he is pained by it, he knows the people of truth and the people of falsehood. He knows that he has reached where he has reached, of punishment, from the punishment, by opposing the masters of truth, and by following the people of falsehood. *Wa lawlaa ma'rifatuhu bi-dhaalika la-maa kaana lil-'azaab 'alamun wa laa lil-thawaab raahatun.* (And were it not for his knowledge of that, there would be no pain in punishment, nor any comfort in reward). And if he did not have knowledge of this matter, then for the punishment, there would be no pain, and for the reward, there would be no comfort. He feels that this punishment I have received is because of this sin I have committed. Because of these wrongdoings. All these are levels of sensation. This is... the animals that are lawful, they are separate from this whole situation? They are not in this level. Lawful animals... these levels have no connection to lawful animals. The level of lawful animals is for ascending. When they ascend, they don't come into one tunic after another. They go directly... Suppose a pigeon is slaughtered, so... it is not coming into these forms. Its part goes... its part becomes the human body. As much as of it became the human body, to that extent its salvation happened. The rest of the part... wherever it went, it has a share from that. Its part, the human body... It does not return in this same path. It returns by the lawful path. *Fa-idhaa stawfaa jamee' haadhihil khumus sulika bihi fil dark al-saadis al-musamma bil-naqs.* (So when he has completed all of these five quintessences, he is made to pass into the sixth level, named *naqs* 'deficiency'). When he completes all these quintessences, he is made to pass... he is made to pass into the sixth level, which is named *naqs*.

<!-- lecture 43 -->

wa dhahaba fi al-barri wal-bahri kal-afa'i wal-hayyat wal-'aqarib wa ghayrihim mimma yushakiluhum, fa yakhmasu fi kulli naw'in min hadhihil-anwa'i sab'ina qamisan ila an yastakmila jami'a dhalika wa huwa mutahaqqiqun lima huwa fihi minal-'azabi 'arifun bil-haqqi wal-batil, 'alimun annahu sara ila ma sara min al-'iqabi bi-mukhalafati arbaab al-haqqi wa ittiba'i al-batil.

And then he went... he will be made to go to the *qamis* of *khars* and he is among the *darik al-rabi'*. *thumma sulika* (then he was made to pass), he is made to go to the fifth *darak*, in the fifth *darak*, and that is the *qamis* of *khars*. *Nun nun* is there, no? Then there is *kha*, and then *nun nun*. From *ra*, what is meant? *Rajis*. From *ra*, *rajis*. From *waw*, *wakhs*. *Wakhs*. And from *'ayn*, *'aks*. And from *kha*, *khars*. *Khars*. And *nun*, two *nun*s have come. One *najis*, *is*, *naks*. When is the time of *najis*? *thumma sulika bihi* (then he was made to pass through it). Then they are made to go. It is necessary to read *sulika* continuously. See, he does not go, he is made to go. *Sulika*. It is in the passive voice (*majhul*). *thumma sulika bihi* (then he was made to pass through it). Then he is made to go, in the fifth *darak*, in the fifth *darak*. *thumma al-najis ma'al-najis* (then the impure with the impure). *wa hum tayrul-barri wal-bahri* (And they are the birds of the land and the sea). And they are the birds of the land and the sea. *yushakilu dhawatil-jawarihi ila an yastawfa...* The other is the human form. The human form. The other is human-like. Such animals that resemble humans.

What is the third level? Crawling creatures. Predatory animals. Predatory animals. Like lions, etc. *Usud*, lions, etc. *Usud*. And then, fourth... Snakes, scorpions, etc. Snakes, scorpions, etc., crawling creatures. And the fifth level? Flying creatures. Flying creatures. One is human-like, and four are animal levels. One human *darak*, and four are animal *darak*. It becomes five. *wa hum tayrul-barri wal-bahri mimma yushakilu...* who are similar... are similar to the *dhawat al-jawa...* yes, predatory animals. *Jarh*, to wound. They wound others, predatory animals. *ila an yastawfa...* Until he completes 70 shirts in every category. From these 70 shirts... *wa huwa fi jami'i dhalika mutahaqqiqun lil-'azab alladhi yanaluhu wa 'arifun bihi muta'allimun minhu 'arifun bi-ahl al-haqqi wa ahl al-batil, 'alimun annahu sara ila ma sara walihi min al-'iqabi bi-mukhalafati arbaab al-haqq*. *ila ma sara...* *ila ma sara ke baad kya hai?* (*What is after *ila ma sara*?*) *wali*. The meaning is... *ila ma sara walihi...* It must be *awwalihi*. Meaning the first ones... What is written in your book? In the printed book. *ila ma sara min al-'iqab...* *walihi...* It is not a word, nor a letter. *ila ma sara min al-'iqab* is written in it. *bi mukhalafati arbaab ahl al-haqqi wa ittiba'i ahl al-batil*.

And until he completes 70 shirts in every category. And he, in all of that, is aware. And he, in this state, in this state, is completely... is completely aware, is one who verifies the punishment that befalls him. They know, in it... is a knower of it, one who takes on the pain from it, one who gains pain from it. One who gains pain from it. *'arifun bi-ahl al-haqqi wa ahl al-batil* (a knower of the people of truth and the people of falsehood). One who knows the people of truth and the people of falsehood. *'alimun annahu* (knowing that he...). One who knows that he has reached the place where he has reached, he has reached from the punishment, from the punishment, from opposition, the people of truth... and from following the people of falsehood.

*wa law la ma'rifatuhu bi-dhalika kullihi, ma kana lil-'azabi 'alamun wa la lith-thawabi rahatun* (And were it not for his knowledge of all that, there would be no pain in the punishment, nor comfort in the reward). And if his knowledge of this matter were not there, all of it, then for the punishment... then there would not be for the punishment a pain, and not for the reward, a comfort.

*fa idhastawfa jami'a hadhihi sulika bihi fid-dark al-sadis wa huwa ath-thumma al-naks* (So when he has completed all of this, he is made to pass into the sixth *darak*, and it is then the relapse). And when he completes these... all the shirts, he is made to go to the sixth *darak*. And it was named *naks*. *wa lam yabqa ma'ahu 'ilmun bima huwa fihi* (And no knowledge of the state he is in remains with him). And no knowledge remains with him, of the state in which he is. Of the state in which he is. The *darak*, that is, the sense is gone. He is not in the first *darak*, and now, after this, the discussion of plants will begin. *li'annahu qad faraqa 'alamat al-hiss* (because he has departed from the world of sense). Because he has left the world of sense. *wa li-dhalika qala Allahu Ta'ala, wa minkum man yuraddu ila ardhalil-'umur likay la ya'lama min ba'di 'ilmin shay'an* (And for that reason, Allah Ta'ala said, "And among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit of age, so that he knows nothing after having known"). And for this reason, Allah Ta'ala says, "And among them are those who are turned back... Among you is he who is turned back, who is made to turn back to the state of *ardhal al-'umur*, so that... after having knowledge, he knows nothing."

And that is why the Almighty says, and among them are those who are turned back... among you is he who is turned back, who is made to turn back towards the most decrepit age, so that after having knowledge, he knows nothing. His mind becomes impaired, slowly, slowly. Allah Ta'ala also does this. *fa hadha misdaqu ta'miyatil-amri 'alayhi wa salbihi ma kana ya'lamu* (So this is the manifestation of the matter being obscured for him and the snatching away of what he used to know). So this is the manifestation... this is the manifestation of becoming ignorant of the matter, and of snatching away what he used to know. To forget, to forget the matter concerning him, and to have snatched away what he knew. *fa idha balagha hadhal-hadda, lam yabqa ma'ahu ghayru 'alatil-nama'* (So when he reaches this limit, nothing remains with him except the faculty of growth). And when he reaches this limit, nothing remains with him except the faculty of growth.

This remembering and not remembering, is this a state of the body or the soul? Now, after this, when he enters the state of plants, the quality of growth remains. Knowledge does not remain. Sense occurs. From sense, knowledge is born. An animal knows what to eat and what not to eat. An animal is in the state of knowing. In this state, his soul is stripped of all things except the faculty of growth. It is the state of plants. The growing soul remains. The sensing soul is taken away.

*alladhi huwan-nabatul-mahzuru al-qatilu al-muhliku lil-hayawan* (which is the forbidden plant, the killer, the destroyer of the animal). Such that he is a plant, that is forbidden and is a killer, one that destroys animals. Animal and man, it is destructive for both. *Al-muhliku lil-hayawan* (the destroyer of the animal). *Hayawan* here means a living being. The word here is also *hayawan*. Actually, the word is *hayawan*. In the dictionary, there is a *zabar* on *ha* and on *ya*. *Al-hayawan*. *alladhi huwan-nabatul-mahzuru* (which is the forbidden plant). Such that he is a plant. While descending, they descend from all the bad bodies. While ascending, they ascend from the good bodies. It is the same vegetative state they have, from which they ascend, but from good bodies. And while descending, from bad bodies.

*wa sulika bihi fid-dark al-sabi' alladhi yusamma al-daks wa huwal-ma'dinus-sanju wal-hajarul-wasikhul-khabithu ila an yastawfa fi kulli naw'in min anwa'ihi sab'ina qamisan* (And he is made to pass into the seventh *darak*, which is named *daks*, and it is the *sanj* mineral and the filthy, wicked stone, until he completes in every type of its types seventy shirts). He is made to go to the seventh *darak*, which is named *daks*. And it is the mineral... *sanj*, hard mineral, and a stone that is dirty, filthy, until he completes... in every type of its types, 70 shirts. And that is a mineral, it is *sanj*, a hard mineral. And it is a stone, a dirty, filthy stone, until he completes... in every one of its types, 70 shirts.
