Or making clear without it being clear. One should make it clear there, but there it is not made clear, without making it clear. Or in lengthening... what's an example of that? There are six such letters that come from the throat. So in that, it should come out properly from the throat. *Idhah*. What is it? *Idhah*. *Ha*. *Ha*, *kha*. *'ayn*, *ghayn*. There are six letters. They are... *'ayn* and *ghayn*... *fa* and *qaf*. These letters, with each other... the tongue should come out properly. If *ba* and *dal* come, then one should read it clearly. *Ba* and *dal*. *'aw raybin maddin*. There are letters for it... they are called *huruf halqi* (guttural letters). There are six *huruf halqi*. There used to be a book we would read... *Tajwid*. *'Ilm al-tajwid* (the science of recitation). In it, it is explained in detail that one should do it this way, do it that way. But the people who read... they read in such a way that what they are reading is not understood. They should read well.

Or *tashdidin*... Or *tashdid*. Or *hamza*, or *jazm*. How should one read *tashdidin*? *Tashdidin*. *Tashdid*. The *dal* at the end doesn't even come out. It shouldn't be like that. *'Aw tashdidin aw hamzatin aw jazmin* (Or *tashdid*, or *hamza*, or *jazm*). Or in pronouncing the *hamza*. Or in pronouncing the *hamza*, or *jazm*... or *jazm*. Usually, what happens is that the *tashdid* is not pronounced clearly. The *tashdid* should be pronounced clearly. What does *tashdid* mean? For the duration of two. Two durations. Two durations come. For two durations, that letter should be pronounced clearly. *Iyya*. The *ya* is for how long? Two durations. It should be pronounced clearly. Or from an *i'rab* that was not written. Other than what was written... other than what you wrote. Or from an *i'rab* that... you wrote. Allah did not write it... that *i'rab* in the Qur'an... we are giving that *i'rab*. Or... from us, upon completeness and perfection. And forgive us, O our Lord... O my Master... and do not take us to task, O our Master, when our hopes come to an end. *wa-rzuqna fadla man qara'ahu mu'addiyan haqqahu ma'a-l-i'rabi wa-l-qalbi wa-l-lisan* (And grant us the virtue of one who recites it, fulfilling its right, with proper vocalization, the heart, and the tongue). And grant us sustenance... from the virtue of his reading... who read it... who fulfilled his right with vocalization, with the heart, and with the tongue. *wa-h-balana fihi-l-khayra wa-s-sa'adata wa-sh-shahadata wa-l-bisharata wa-l-imana* (And grant us in it goodness, felicity, martyrdom, good tidings, and faith). And grant us in it... goodness, felicity, martyrdom, good tidings, and faith. What did he say here? *Mu'addiyan haqqahu* (fulfilling its right). One who fulfills its right. The right of reciting the Holy Qur'an should be fulfilled; make us like that. *Ma'a-l-i'rab* (with vocalization), with the heart, and with the tongue. Three things: *i'rab*, the heart, and the tongue. *Wa la takhtim lana...* *Wa la takhtim lana bi-sh-sharri wa-sh-shaqawati wa-d-dalalati wa-t-tughyan* (And do not seal our end with evil, wretchedness, misguidance, and transgression). *I'rab* means *zabar*, *zer*, *pesh*. *Zer*, *zabar*, *pesh*. And do not let our end be with evil and wretchedness and misguidance and transgression. *Nabbihna qabla...* Where did *i'rab* come from? Where do *i'rab* come from? Upon letters. Upon letters. How many letters are there? 28. There are 28 letters. The 28 letters are opposite what? The *Qisa-i Ibdaiyah*. The 28 of the *Qisa-i Ibdaiyah*. With the *Qisa-i Ibdaiyah*, there are 28. And the 28 letters... in the world, who were the ones who manifested them in a material form? It was the *Juz'-i Ibdai*. They were the ones who taught these letters, the letters of the alphabet, from *alif* to *ya*. And where did they come from? Where did the *Juz'-i Ibdai* get them from? From the *'Aql al-Awwal* (First Intellect). From the *kalimah la ilaha illa Allah* (the statement 'there is no god but Allah'). The *kalimah la ilaha illa Allah*. In the *kalimah la ilaha illa Allah*, there are 28. 28 letters came from there. Now, how were the *i'rab* (vowels) placed on them? In the *'alam al-niyyat* (World of Intentions). In the *'alam al-niyyat*, the *i'rab* were placed on these 28 letters. Because there too, who has them? The *Munba'ith al-Awwal* (the First Emanation) also has 28. And every circle that was formed, in it was a seating of 28 letters. In every circle. Whatever intellect it may be, in it, the circle that is formed has 28, to the extent that the circle of the Imam, peace be upon him, though it is said to be of a thousand, even a thousand, when it is added in different ways, it becomes 28. So this number 28 is a very special number. Now, the *i'rab* were placed on it. On what? On the 28 letters, the *i'rab* were placed. When were the *i'rab* placed? In the *'alam al-niyyat*. Otherwise, the letters were without *i'rab*. Why were the *i'rab* placed? Because in that realm, those who were foremost (*pesh-pesh*), who were foremost, who immediately, without delay, what did they do? They put their free will into action. What was given to them? Three things. What was the first thing? Life. Life. Existence. And after that, what was the second thing? Knowledge. Knowledge. What powers are in existence, the knowledge of that. The third is free will. Freedom. In that, he used his freedom to be foremost (*pesh-pesh*). He came to the forefront. On his *i'rab*, a *pesh* was placed. He came foremost. And the one who, from the circle, took a delay, he remained with a *zabar*. He remained with a *zabar*. Then he, that *zabar*... there were some people who did not remain in the state of *zabar*, but became *zer* (went under). What did they become? *Zer*. So they remained in the state of *zer*. So which is the highest movement? *Pesh*. The *pesh* movement. After that, the *zabar* movement. Then the *zer* movement. *Pesh*, *zabar*, and *zer*. Three. After that, what is there? *Madd*... no, after that is *jazm*. What is *jazm*? It got joined. One movement and... *Jazm* is what... it is *zabar*. *Jazm* is *zabar*. The *zabar* became a circle. It got bent. Its speed was not straight. It became crooked. What happened? It is actually *zabar*. What did it become? It got bent. [unclear]. Its state became like this. And after that, what is there? There is *madd*. What is *madd*? Two movements. First there is *jazm*, then after that there is *zabar*, *pesh*, *zabar*, *zer*. Three. *Maddo*. What is in *maddo*? On the *dal*, what is there first? There are two *dal*s, right? *Maddo*. Two *dal*s. In the *dal*, what is first? First there is *jazm*, then *pesh*. *Madda*. What is it? *Jazm* and *zabar*. *Maddi*? *Jazm* and *zer*. The *jazm* did not remain alone... its singular state did not remain, but what happened to it? It joined with something else. It got joined. One was crooked, one was straight. *Madda*, *maddi*. Now, after that, what comes? *Madd*. What is *madd* called? The one on top. There, what is the command? To stretch. Wherever a *madd* comes, it is the command to stretch. So why do we stretch? Wherever two such entities come together that a distinction has to be made between their ranks. It has to be clarified. It has to be explained with clarity. Because we have a method, that two... Allah the Almighty has created two ranks of the same nature. There will surely be some difference. There will surely be some difference. Two individuals of the same rank cannot be appointed to the same status. There will be some difference. So in it, now for instance, this has come... Where did *madd* come? And... *mawazi'iha aw taghyir*... Why did *madd* come? Two *alif*s came together. *Mawazi'iha aw taghyir*. If this did not come here, if the *alif* did not come, then there would be no *madd*. Or *taqdim*, or... *Shifa*. The *hamza* has come. The *hamza* is written like an *alif*. *Shifa'an*. It has to be stretched and read. Whenever you read the Holy Qur'an, pay attention to why the *madd* has come here. You will understand that the *madd* has come for this reason.

*Nabbihna qabl al-manaya min nawm al-ghaflati wa-l-kaslan* (Awaken us before death from the sleep of heedlessness and laziness). And awaken us before... before deaths, from the sleep of heedlessness and laziness. *Wa amminna min 'adhab al-qabri min su'al Munkar wa Nakir* (And grant us security from the punishment of the grave, from the questioning of Munkar and Nakir). And grant us security from the punishment of the grave, from the questioning of Munkar and Nakir. *Wa min akl al-didan* (And from being eaten by worms)... What is *didan* called? Worms. From the eating of worms. This is in the grave. Yes, in the grave. *Wa bayyid wujuhana yawm al-ba'th* (And make our faces white on the Day of Resurrection). People read it as *bayz*. They read it as *bayz wujuhana*. Its *tashdid* should be pronounced clearly. *Wa bayyid wujuhana* (And make our faces white). And make our faces bright on the Day of Resurrection. *Wa a'tiq riqabana min al-niran* (And free our necks from the Fires). And our... The *alif* has a *zabar*. *Wa a'tiq riqabana min al-niran* (And free our necks from the Fires). And free our necks... from the fire... free them. From the fire. From the fire. *Wa min sharri-l-hisabi wa-l-khusran* (And from the evil of the reckoning and the loss). And from the evil of our reckoning... and the loss... and the loss. *Bi-rahmatika ya Arham al-rahimin* (By Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful). Why did *ya Arham*... why did the *alif* come on *ya*... why did the *madd* come on *ya*? After it... two *alif*s came together in one place. *Bi-rahmatika ya Arham al-rahimin*. There is a command to stretch it.

*Tashdid* is... two... *jazm* and what is after it is *zabar*. Or *jazm* and *pesh*. *Sabbar*. In *sabbar*, what is there? There's a *tashdid*, right, on the *ba*? *Sabbar*. What is in *sabbar*? *Zabar* and *tashdid*. First, there's *jazm*. *Sab*. On the *ba*, there's a *jazm*. After that, on the *ba*, there's a *zabar*. Two things have been joined. The *ba* has come in two forms. The *ba* that... one *ba* with a *jazm* has come, and one *ba* with a *zabar* has come. So what happened? By joining the two, it became *sabbar*.

So these letters that came from the realm of the spirits and from the *kalimah la ilaha illa Allah*... So that is the original Arabic. Or the name of the language we have given is Arabic or... *Bi-lisanin 'arabiyyin mubin* (in a clear Arabic tongue). In the Holy Qur'an, has the word for the German language come? Germany, France... has Telugu come? Nice. The name of this has not come. *Bi-lisanin 'arabiyyin mubin* (in a clear Arabic tongue). In a clear Arabic tongue, it was revealed. Allah chose this language for His expression. *Bi-lisanin 'arabiyyin mubin* (in a clear Arabic tongue).

Now, how is the *pesh*? *Maddo*. In *maddo*, what is there? On the *dal*, there is a *jazm*, and then there is a *pesh*. First, on the *dal*, there is a *jazm*. On the second *dal*, there is a *pesh*. *Rabbun*. *Rabbun* means Lord. What is it? There is a *zwaad*, then on the *ba*, what is there? *Jazm*. And then... a double *pesh*... both can come. What is there? *Rabbi*. What will it be? There will be a *zer* at the end. *Rabbi*. *Jazm*... *Jazm* and *zer*. Two things have been joined. So one should especially... those who don't do it, or... they turn a *zabar* into a *zer*. They don't pronounce the letter clearly. While reading the Holy Qur'an, the entire letter must be pronounced completely. The entire letter. And the letter should be clear.

The meaning also changes completely. The meaning changes, but very few people understand the meaning. Now, for instance, if one writes `gadha` for a donkey... In Arabic poetry, there is a line: for a donkey, one writes `gadha`. How do we write `gadha`? With a *dal* and a *he*. The one with two eyes (`ھ`). One writes `gadha` for that. One reads `gadha` for `gadha`. Because in Arabic, what is there? This is not there, right? The `ھ` is not there. The one with two eyes, which is in Arabic... it's not in Arabic. In Arabic, there is `ha`. And in the Hindi language, it is there. So, when reading, one should keep in mind that one should read it this way.

So it is not necessary that everyone should be taught this. A few people can also read it, like this. It's better if they all read. Their... they open up, their qualities... Then there's also the possibility... The barrier of the gathering, the barrier of reading, is removed. It's good. How else will mistakes be known? If one reads, the mistake will be known, right? Or they can come privately and read, and the mistake can be pointed out.

<!-- lecture 52 -->

The second *fasl* from the third *bab*... from the sixth... from the second *bab*, from the sixth passage is: *fa da'al maqamat alaihimussalam* (so he called the *maqamat*, peace be upon them).
*fa du'a'ul maqamati alaihimussalam* (the call of the *maqamat*, peace be upon them).
*fa du'a'ul maqamati alaihimussalam* (the call of the *maqamat*, peace be upon them)...
*al-ins alladhina hum al-bashar wal-jinn alladhina hum hadhihil suwar* (the humans who are the mortals and the jinn who are these forms).
...and *tawfiq* (divine success)...
...*tawfiq*... *li yarji'u man yarji'* (so that he who returns may return). Not *tawfiq*. *tawqif*.
*tawqif*...
...and *tawqif* (to make aware). *li yarja'a man yarja'u* (so that he who returns may return), *wa yusirra man yusirru* (and he who insists may insist).
It's *yarja'a*, right? There's a 'li' here.
*wa yusirra man yusirru*.
*yusirra man yusirru*.
*li yarja'a man yarja'u*. Why does the *'ayn* have a *zabar* (vowel mark) here? Because of the `li`. It is `li an` (so that) hidden.
*li yarja'a*. *man yarja'u*, this one is as it is. A *pesh* (vowel mark) comes, just as a *pesh* comes on a *mudari'* (present/future tense verb), so it stays that way.
*yusirra man yusirru*.
*yusirra man yusirru*.
*bi du'ai hadhihil suwar al-khabisah* (with the call of these wretched forms/surahs).
So, they called. To call. So, the calling of the Imam. The calling of the Imams, peace be upon them.
...peace be upon them.
To the humans. Such that they are all mortals and jinn. No, they are mortals. The humans who are mortals, they call them too. And what do the Imams do? They also call the jinn. *wal-jinn* (and the jinn).
So, the calling of the *maqamat*, peace be upon them, to the humans. Such that they are mortals. And to the jinn. Such that they are *alladhina hum hadhihil suwar* (those who are these forms/surahs). Such that they are these forms. These forms which... what are they? They have reached the state of jinn, and they are being given the *da'wat* (call/invitation) there.
So, if these jinn even accepted the *da'wat*, they are not in the realm of life (*aalam-e-hayat*). Meaning that...
They establish faith through three things, right? That is, by word, by bringing truth to the heart, and by action. So how can the jinn do this?
They have been given services, haven't they? Within the *shams* (a spiritual rank), they are called *mustaqdimin*. Those jinn who accept the *du'a* (call), they are called *jinn-e-mahmud* (praised jinn).
And after accepting, services are entrusted to them. That "you have been given this service." In the *shams*, they have their services. How many people were mentioned?
How many were mentioned? One hundred and forty thousand. One hundred and forty thousand. There is a congregation of one hundred and forty thousand in the *shams*. When one moves from here, or falls, another becomes their successor (*khalifa*). They always remain.
So they are called *jinn-e-mahmud*. Services are performed concerning them. They perform those services. They are called *jinn-e-mahmud*, *mustaqdimin*.
So, these are the forms so that they become aware.
...and *tawqif* (to make aware).
They are to be made aware. So that whoever is to turn back, turns back. And whoever is to insist, insists. In that state, they are given the choice to either turn back or to remain firm in their insistence.
*wa fi du’ai hadhihil suwar*... *wa fi du’ai suwar al-khabisah... wa ijadatil mujibu minhum izharun lil-mu’jizati yuzhiruhul maqamu alaihis salam li man hawlahu min waliyyin wa ziddin wa munafiqin* (And in the calling of these wretched forms and the response of the one who answers from them is a manifestation of the miracle which the *Maqam*, peace be upon him, reveals to those around him from among the allies, opponents, and hypocrites), *li yakuna dhalika*...
*li yakuna dhalika akbara li iqamati hujjah wa asra’a li idhharil mahajjah* (so that this may be greater for establishing the proof and swifter for revealing the clear path), *li yastayqina alladhina utul kitab wa yazdad alladhina amanu imana* (so that those who were given the Book may be certain and those who have believed may increase in faith), *wa li yahlika man halaka ‘an bayyinatin wa yahya man hayya ‘an bayyinatin* (and so that he who was to perish might perish by a clear proof, and he who was to live might live by a clear proof).
And in the calling of these forms, those who are wretched, and in the acceptance of the one who accepts...
The call... *fi du'ai* and... The call... *fi du'ai hadhihil suwar al-khabisah*. Yes, in the calling of these wretched forms—inviting them to the right path—and their acceptance, those who accept from them, is a manifestation of the miracle. It is a manifestation of the miracle, which they reveal... which the Imam, peace be upon him, reveals... for those people who are around them... from the *wali* (friend/ally) and the *zidd* (opponent) and the *munafiq* (hypocrite). So that it may become... the greatest thing for the sake of establishing the proof (*iqamat-e-hujjat*). And a greater... faith.
And so that it may increase... so that it may increase for those who have believed, faith. That the faith of the believers may increase, and that certainty may be created in those who were given the Book. And so that they may perish... And so that those who perished may perish... who perished, perished with clear proof. And that he may live who lives with clear proof. With proof.
Now they narrate its incident.
*kama fa’ala Rasulullah sallallahu alaihi* (As the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's prayers be upon him, did). He sent the companions of Amir al-Mumineen, peace be upon him, to Yemen... with him... about the first and second...
It's not written in this one.
Yes.
No, it's not printed in this one.
It's not printed. About the first and second.
*ma'ahu Abu Bakr* (with him was Abu Bakr).
No, in the printed version it's just "with him were three companions." There are no names given.
*Abi Bakrin* (of Abu Bakr).
What... what's its... What is this? What is its explanation? What have they written? It's not clear.
*wa amarahum bi du’ai jinn alladhina hum bi wadi zahr wa musayyab* (and he commanded them to call the jinn who were in the valley of Zahr and Musayyab).
And... And as Rasulullah, Salawatullah Alayhi, did... in this capacity that he sent Amir al-Mumineen towards Yemen, and with him were three companions... *jaddadallahu azabahum* (may Allah renew their punishment). And he gave them the command. And he commanded them regarding the jinn.
*jaddadallahu azabahum* (may Allah renew their punishment). No, the three mentioned... the three people towards whom... or what is it? Who are the three? If it becomes known, then... The pronoun 'hum' (them), where does it refer? Allah the Exalted, may He renew their punishment, and he gave them the command. And he commanded those three to call the jinn. To call the jinn, such that they are all in the valley of Zahr and Musayyab.
*wa a’lamahum bi asmaihim* (and he informed them of their names). He made them aware of their names. "You are to call the jinn by saying these very names." In that desolate well, there are jinn. These are their names. You call them by their names.
The Noble Prophet said, "Whoever he answers..." This incident is written in great detail in Sayyidna Hatim's work. "Whoever receives an answer, he will be the *wasi* (successor) of the Prophet, of the Nabi."
*wa qala lahum yad’uhum awwalan Abu Bakrin* (And he said to them, "Let Abu Bakr call them first").
Abu Bakr.
And he said, "Let them be called... let Abu Bakr call them first."
*fa in istajabu lahu, wa illa da’ahum ‘Umar* (So if they respond to him, and if not, let 'Umar call them).
If they... give an answer for him, otherwise, let 'Umar call them.
*fa in istajabu lahu, wa illa da’ahum ‘Uthman* (So if they respond to him, and if not, let 'Uthman call them). And if... If they... give an answer to him, otherwise, let 'Uthman call them.
*fa in istajabu lahu wa illa da’ahum* (So if they respond to him, and if not, let them be called by) *‘Aliyyun ibn Abi Talib* ('Ali ibn Abi Talib). The full phrase is there. *Talib*, *Talib* is there.
Ali... No, the full correct... what is it? It's written with a pencil.
...and if not, let them be called by... Ali ibn Abi Talib.
Let them be called by Ali ibn Abi Talib.
*wa’lamu ann man ajabuhu minkum* (And know that whoever among you he answers).
*wa'lamu*... and know, you all. *wa'lamu an-na man ajabuhu minkum*...
What's written there?
*wasiyyi fikum* (my successor among you).
*wasiyyi*... *fa huwa wasiyyi fikum wa khalifati alaykum* (he is my successor among you and my caliph over you).
And know this, that the one whom they answered from among you, he is my *wasi* among you, and my *khalifa* over you.
*wa man ata’ahu fa qad ata’ani* (And whoever obeys him has obeyed me). And whoever has obeyed him, has obeyed me. *wa ‘asallaha* (and disobeyed Allah). And he has obeyed Allah. *wa man ‘asahu fa ‘asani wa ‘asallahu ta’ala* (and whoever disobeys him has disobeyed me and disobeyed Allah the Exalted). And whoever disobeys him, has disobeyed me, and disobeyed Allah the Exalted.
*wa dhalika azzalahum ‘ala ta’ati Amir al-Mumineen salawatullahi alayhi* (And that was to urge them towards obedience to Amir al-Mumineen, the blessings of Allah be upon him).
And that specific... and that thing is that you encouraged them to obedience. Obedience to Amir al-Mumineen, Salawatullah Alayhi.
*wa ‘ala ma’rifatihi fa madaw ‘ala halihim ila an balaghu San’a* (and upon his recognition. So they proceeded in their state until they reached San'a).
And so they passed in their states until they reached San'a.
Where in San'a is the Well of Alam, I don't know. We also went to San'a. By chance, we reached San'a. We had set out for Umrah. Who was it with us? You... who were you? You were there with us. We went for Umrah and reached San'a, reached Yemen. A strange incident occurred. We hadn't expected to go to Yemen. We were going for Umrah. The airplane he got was such that it went via San'a. And it reached San'a, and the airplane broke down there. The airplane broke down. So in San'a, we had to stay for one day. We got the opportunity to stay for one day. And one day in San'a... so, by chance, with Mulla Barakat Husain Sahab... he had the address of a Waqfi. You were there, right? Who else was with us? He had the address of a Waqfi. People who live there. He... we said, "Look for them." So they came and took us. And all the... San'a... especially, we had to do a *ziyarat* (visit to a holy site). On the mountain, there are graves. Whose... Sayyidna Muhammad ibn Zayd's grave is in front. What is it? Sa'dan. Husn Fasl Sa'dan, where Sayyidna Imam was born, Sayyidna Ja'far was born. Sayyidna Imam was not born in Tusi, Sayyidna Ja'far was born in Husn Fasl Sa'dan, in front. It's a high mountain. We went there. Sayyidna Muhammad ibn Zayd's grave. And Sayyidna Ja'far, and many other elders whose graves are there. We performed the *ziyarat*. Although there is a mosque in San'a, a special mosque, we didn't get time to go there. We had to return.
Now in San'a, they are saying... Bir Dhatil Alam is in San'a. *ila an balaghu San'a* (until they reached San'a). Until they reached San'a.
*wa kharaju ila haythu umiru* (and they went out to where they were commanded).
And they went out to the place where they were commanded.
The word `haythu`, `ila` gives a *zer* (vowel mark), right? How many letters give a *zer*?
Seventeen.
Seventeen letters. `Ila` is among them. *Ba, ta, kaf, lam, waw, mundhu, muz, khala, rubba, hasha, min, ‘ada, fi, ‘an, ‘ala, hatta, ila*. `Ila` is the last of the seventeen. So `ila` should give a *zer*. So it should be `ila haythi`. But `haythu`... the letters are of three types: *ism* (noun), *fi'l* (verb), and *harf* (particle). A *harf* is *mabni* (indeclinable), a *harf* does not change. It doesn't take *zabar*, *zer*, *pesh*. So, *ila haythu umiru*. `Haythu` will always be read as `haythu`. You won't read it as `haytha` or `haythi`. Even though `ila` comes before it. *ila haythu umiru*. Until they reached San'a. And they went out to the place where they were commanded.
*fa hatu fi ahadil mawazi’il wadi* (So they encamped in one of the places of the valley). So they encamped. They encamped in a place in the valley. One of the places in the valley.
*wa taqaddama Abu Bakrin* (And Abu Bakr went forward).
Three of them... it is written about the three of them like this. `aba`, `aba`. The three are written in this way.
First, Abu Bakr.
The `waw` and `be` are written in the same way.
*fa taqaddama Abu Bakr*.
First, Abu Bakr went forward towards... from a place. To a place from there. He was commanded to go forward towards it. And he was made aware of it, and his companions... *wa ‘urrifahu wa ashabuhu fi mahattihim* (and it was made known to him, and his companions were in their encampment).
And... first, Abu Bakr went forward towards a place from there, that he had been commanded to go forward towards it. And *wa ‘urrifahu*, of which he had been given the recognition (*ma’rifat*). *wa ashabuhu fi mahattihim*. And his companions are in their encampment. He went alone. The method that was shown. They were all present in the encampment. He was given the command to go and call the jinn. He went alone and called the jinn.
*wa hatafa bi a’la sawtihi ya fulan ya fulan ya fulan* (And he called out in his loudest voice, "O so-and-so, O so-and-so, O so-and-so").
And in a loud voice... he called. He called.
...he called in a loud voice... that "O so-and-so, O so-and-so, O so-and-so."
*fa lam yujibhu ahadun* (but no one answered him). So no one... no one came forward. No one. *yujibhu*. *ajaba, yujibu*. *ajaba* means to answer. *fa lam yujibhu ahadun*. So no one answered him.
*fa ‘ada ila ashabihi kha’iban* (so he returned to his companions, disappointed). So he returned to his companions, having lost hope.
*wa taqaddama ‘Umar ila dhalikal mawzi’i duna sahibihi* (And 'Umar went forward to that place without his companion). So 'Umar went forward to that place, leaving his companions behind.
*wa hatafa bi a’la sawtihi ya fulan ya fulan ya fulan* (And he called out in his loudest voice, "O so-and-so, O so-and-so, O so-and-so"). So in a loud voice, he said, "O so-and-so, O so-and-so, O so-and-so."
*fa lam yujibhu ahadun fa ‘ada ila ashabihi kha’iban* (But no one answered him, so he returned to his companions, disappointed). So no one came forward. So he returned to his companions, disappointed.
*wa taqaddama ‘Uthman fa fa’ala ka fi’li sahibayhi* (And 'Uthman went forward and did as his two companions had done). And 'Uthman went forward and did as his two companions had done before.
*wa lam yujibhu ahadun fa ‘ada ila ashabihi kha’iban* (and no one answered him, so he returned to his companions, disappointed). No one answered him. He returned to his companions, disappointed. He returned to his companions, having lost hope, unsuccessful.
*thumma taqaddama ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib ila dhalikal mawzi’i wa taba’ahu ashabuhu min haythu yazunnuna annahu la yarahum nazirin* (Then 'Ali ibn Abi Talib went forward to that place, and his companions followed him from where they thought he would not see them looking).
And... then Mawlana Ali ibn Abi Talib went forward to that place...
*salawatullahi alayhi*, or something is there.
To that place. And his companions followed him. And your companions followed you from where they thought that you would not see them. You went, you didn't see them, that the companions had followed behind them.
*li ma yakunu min amrihi wa amrihim ila an hatafa bi a’la sawtihi* (to see what would come of his affair and their affair, until he called out in his loudest voice).
What happens from your affair. What happens from your doing. And from their affair. Doing.
...until he called out in his loudest voice.
...until you called out in your loud voice, "O so-and-so."
*fa ajabuhu* (and he answered him). He gave you an answer.
*thumma da’a ya fulan* (then he called, "O so-and-so"). Then you called, "O so-and-so." Then he gave you an answer. So you kept calling, one after the other.
*wa hum yastajibuna lahu* (and they were responding to him). And they all kept accepting... answering you. They were answering you.
*thumma sallama alayhim* (Then he greeted them with peace). Then you said *salam* to them.
You should check it against Sayyidna Hatim's work to see what narration he has provided.
*thumma sallama alayhim*.
Then Mawlana Ali greeted them with *salam*. So those people said...
*fa qalu wa ‘alaykassalam* (so they said, "And upon you be peace"). Said, "Upon you too be peace."
*wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh* (and the mercy of Allah and His blessings).
*thumma da’ahum ila shahadatayn* (then he called them to the two testimonies).
What is it after that? *wa ‘alaykassalam*. Upon you be peace. After that, what is it? Did you write it? No. It should be written.
*wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh*.
*wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh*.
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib's...
From whom is it?
It's the same.
Mawlana Ali ibn Abi Talib.
Okay, good.
No, but the sentence has ended, right? *fa qalu wa ‘alaykassalam*. After that, what is it?
*Ya... ya Amir al-Mumineen, wa ‘alaykassalam* (O Commander of the Faithful, and upon you be peace). Peace be upon you, O Commander of the Faithful. *Ya Amir al-Muminina*. What's the word after that? They've cut it.
*wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh* (and the mercy of Allah and His blessings).
And may the mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you.
Then he called them to the two testimonies.
Then you called them. You called them to the two testimonies (*shahadatayn*). What are the two testimonies? *La ilaha illallah, Muhammadur rasulullah* (There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah).
*fa shahida man hum man shahida lillahi ta’ala bil wahdaniyyah wa li Muhammadin bir risalati wal ‘ubudiyyah* (So those among them who testified, testified to Allah the Exalted with Oneness, and to Muhammad with the Messengership and Servitude).
So, he who testified from among them, testified to Allah the Exalted with Oneness, and to the Prophet with Messengership and servanthood. What is servanthood? *Ashhadu anna Muhammadan ‘abduhu wa rasuluh* (I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger). *‘abduhu wa rasuluh*.
After that, what is it? *wa li ‘Aliyyin*.
It's above, right? *Amir al-Mumineen*.
*wa li ‘Aliyyin... Amir...*
It's not here.
It's above, *wa li ‘Aliyyin Amir al-Mumineen* (and to 'Ali, the Commander of the Faithful).
*bil wilayati* (with *wilayah* (authority)). And upon his *wilayah*.
*wa tashakhkhasa lahum minhum man tashakhkhasa* (And he who took bodily form from them took bodily form for them). And he took bodily form. He who took bodily form... And for you, from among them, he who took bodily form took bodily form.
*wa mada ma’ahum ithnan* (and two went with them). And two from among them went with you.
Two individuals, you took them with you. They came in a material form, that is what is being said.
*wa huma ‘Abdullah Mard-shah wa ‘Abdullah ‘Ard-shah* (And they were 'Abdullah Mard-shah and 'Abdullah 'Ard-shah).
What were their names? 'Abdullah Mard-shah and 'Abdullah 'Ard-shah.
*ila an wasalu ila Rasulillahi salawatullahi alayhi* (until they reached the Messenger of Allah, the blessings of Allah be upon him).
Until they all reached... Rasulullah, Salawatullah Alayhi. They reached the Prophet.
Sayyidna Hatim has narrated that there is a miracle of Mawlana Amir, Salawatullah Alayhi, about which a book has been published, a very thick book. What is its name? In it, this incident is detailed. It's also in this, *Saluni*. Do you have the second volume of *Saluni*? So tell me, we'll get it photocopied. I only have the first volume. You brought it from there. We'll get it copied.
*ila an wasalu ila Rasulillahi* (until they reached the Messenger of Allah). Until they reached Rasulullah, Salawatullah Alayhi.
*fa jaddadu islamahum bayna yadayhi* (so they renewed their Islam before him).
Where did you get it from?
From there.
*fa jaddadu islamahum bayna yadayhi*. So they renewed. They renewed their Islam before you.
*wa hasuna islamuhum* (and their Islam became excellent). And their Islam was very good.
*wa ‘adu ila ashabihim* (and they returned to their companions). And they returned. They returned towards their companions. Meaning they went back to that place, the Well of Alam. *‘adu ila ashabihim* would mean this, right?
*wa kana hadhal amru min akbaril mu’jizat lin natiqi wal wasiyyi salawatullahi alayhima* (And this affair was among the greatest of miracles for the Natiq and the Wasi, the blessings of Allah be upon them both). *fa ma zadahum ulakal munafiqin illa bu’dan wa kufran* (But it did not increase those hypocrites except in distance and disbelief).
And this affair was among the greatest of miracles for the Natiq and the Wasi. May the blessings of Allah be upon them both.
So, those... so it did not increase. So Allah the Exalted did not increase those hypocrites in anything except distance and disbelief. This incident did not increase those hypocrites in anything except distance and disbelief. The hypocrites meaning the first, second... those who went with them.
The second *fasl* from the second *bab* from *Suwar al-qabr*.
This *fasl* is the second, from the second *bab*, from the sixth passage.
*wa ka nuzuli Amir al-Mumineen alayhissalam ila bi’ri dhatil ‘alam marratayn li munajatihil jinn huna* (And like the descent of Amir al-Mumineen, peace be upon him, into the Well of Dhat al-'Alam twice for his communion with the jinn there).
This is not the incident of the Well of Alam, this is a different incident.
And the meaning of the descent of Amir al-Mumineen, peace be upon him, towards the Well of Dhat al-'Alam two times, and his calling the jinn there.
*wa qatlihi min qatala minhum bil islam man aslama* (and his killing of those whom he killed from them, and the Islam of those who accepted Islam).
And his killing... and his killing... of those whom you killed from among them, and the Islam of those who accepted Islam from among them.
The incident of San'a is not that of the Well of Alam. It's in Wadi Zahr wa Musayyab, and this is the Well of Alam.
*wa ka wusulil Ham bin al-Him ila hadrati Rasulillahi salawatullahi alayhi wa huwa qa’idun fi masjidihi* (And like the arrival of Ham bin al-Him to the presence of the Messenger of Allah, the blessings of Allah be upon him, while he was sitting in his mosque). And you are seated in your mosque.
*wal muslimuna hawlahu fa sallama alayhi bi sawtin yusma’u wa la yura lahu shakhsun* (and the Muslims were around him. So he greeted him with a voice that was heard but whose person was not seen). So he said *salam* to you. Ham bin Him. With such a voice that you could hear it, but his person could not be seen. He was not visible, but his voice was heard.
*fa qala lahu Rasulullah salawatullahi alayhi man anta* (So the Messenger of Allah, the blessings of Allah be upon him, said to him, "Who are you?"). The Messenger of Allah, Salawatullah Alayhi, said to him, "Who are you?"
*fa qala ana Ham ibn Him ibn Laqis ibn Iblis* (So he said, "I am Ham son of Him, son of Laqis, son of Iblis").
I am Ham son of Him, son of Laqis, son of Iblis.
*wa kuntu qad aslamtu lin nabiyyi Nuhin thumma li Ibrahim thumma li Musa thumma li ‘Isa alayhimussalam* (And I had accepted Islam for the Prophet Nuh, then for Ibrahim, then for Musa, then for 'Isa, peace be upon them).
And I had accepted Islam. I had accepted Islam for the Prophet Nuh, for Ibrahim, for Musa, for 'Isa. Peace be upon them.
*wa ana ashhadu an la ilaha illallah wa annaka Muhammadun ‘abduhu wa rasuluh* (And I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that you, Muhammad, are His servant and His Messenger). And I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that you are Muhammad, His servant and His Messenger.
*fa kana hadha min akbaril mu’jizat* (So this was among the greatest of miracles). So this was among the greatest of miracles.
*fa ma zadahum dhalika illa nufura* (But that did not increase them except in aversion). And it did not increase... that thing, except in aversion.
It did not increase them in anything except aversion.
*wa kan al-Ham ba’da islamuhu lin nabiyyi Nuhin sa’ada ila rutbatish shams bi wasatitil qamar kama sabaqa bihil qawl* (And Ham, after his Islam for the Prophet Nuh, ascended to the rank of Shams through the intermediary of the Qamar (moon), as the saying has preceded). And Ham, after his Islam for the Prophet Nuh, ascended towards the rank of Shams through the intermediary of the Qamar. As has been stated previously.
*ila an zahara Ibrahim alayhissalam* (until Ibrahim, peace be upon him, appeared).
Until Ibrahim, peace be upon him, appeared.
*ila an zahara Ibrahim alayhissalam*.
Until Ibrahim, peace be upon him, appeared.
*wanhadara al-Ham min haythu kana* (And Ham descended from where he was). He descended. Ham descended from where he was.
*fa aslama li Ibrahim alayhissalam* (So he accepted Islam for Ibrahim, peace be upon him). So... so he accepted Islam. He accepted Islam for Ibrahim, peace be upon him.
`Ibrahima` will be read. `Ibrahimu`? Why? It's a non-Arab name, `Ibrahimi`. It's a Hebrew name. Ibrahim, Ishaq, Yaqub, all are non-declinable. Even in the genitive case, they don't take a *zer*. Even in the genitive case, a *zabar* is read. *li Ibrahima alayhissalam*.
*wa ‘ada ila mawzi’ihi* (and he returned to his place). And he returned to his place.
*wa kadhalika li Musa wa ‘Isa alayhimussalam* (and likewise for Musa and 'Isa, peace be upon them). And similarly, it happened with Musa and 'Isa, peace be upon them. For them.
*ila an zahara Muhammadun salawatullahi alayhi* (until Muhammad, the blessings of Allah be upon him, appeared). Until Muhammad, Salawatullah Alayhi, appeared.
*wanhadara hatta aslama lahu* (And he descended until he accepted Islam for him). And he descended. He descended here until he accepted Islam for you.
*tuwuffiya* (he was made to die). And he was given death.
*wa ‘ada fi asra’i waqtin ila qamatis saniyah* (and he returned in the swiftest of time to the lofty stature). And he returned... with great speed. He was given death. And he returned in the swiftest time to the lofty stature. Towards the lofty stature. As the saying has preceded.
*li anna la budda li kulli man aslama minhum fil adwaril maziyah an yuslima li Muhammadin salawatullahi alayhi alladhi huwa natiqus sadis* (because it is necessary for everyone among them who accepted Islam in the past eras to accept Islam for Muhammad, the blessings of Allah be upon him, who is the sixth Natiq).
Because it is necessary. It is necessary for every person who accepted Islam from among them, from the jinn, in the past eras, that he must accept Islam for Muhammad, Salawatullah Alayhi, who is the sixth Natiq.
*alladhi tamma bi tamamihi khalqul jism ad-dini* (by whose completion the creation of the religious body was completed). Such that with his completion, the creation of the *jism dini* (religious body) is complete. With your completion, the creation of the *jism dini* is complete.
*wa yartaqi fil maratib ila an yablugha rutbatal bab* (and he ascends in the ranks until he reaches the rank of the Bab).
And he will progress. He will progress in the ranks until he reaches the rank of the *Bab* (Gate). To the Bab.
This is for the *mustaqdimin*.
Because they will have high ranks.
*allati hiya haddul ‘ismah* (which is the limit of infallibility). Such that it is the limit of *'ismah*.
So, this acceptance of Islam, after accepting Islam, the progression of ranks is rapid.
This is for the *mustaqdimin*. For the *mustaqdimin*, the ranks... that is, he was a believer... let's say he was a disbeliever. After that, he served, he performed services. He will get its reward, that he will reach the rank of the Bab, like Janab-e-Nabi, Salawatullah Alayhi.
*allati hiya haddul ‘ismah* (which is the limit of infallibility). The Bab, what is it? It is the limit of *'ismah*. The Imam has *'ismah* and the *Bab al-Abwab* (Gate of Gates) has *'ismah*.
So they became better than the believers?
Yes, because he served. For ages, he performed services.
*Ballaghanallahu wa iyyakum ila dhalikal majma’ish sharifi bi haqqi Muhammadin wa alihit tahirin salawatullahi alayhim ajma’in* (May Allah cause us and you to reach that noble assembly, by the right of Muhammad and his pure progeny, the blessings of Allah be upon them all).
May Allah the Exalted... may He cause us... May Allah the Exalted cause us and you to reach that noble assembly. Towards that noble assembly. By the right of the Prophet and the pure progeny, Salawatullah Alayhi.
When Janab-e-Amir al-Mumineen... an incident occurred, right? Who was he? What was his name? He came to you in Kufa, you were seated on the pulpit. And he came and... It's a very good... it's in this, in *Saluni*, this incident is there.
In their own... in *Tawil al-Da'a'im* it is. He said, "*Saluni qabla an tafqiduni*" (Ask me before you lose me). "Ask me before you lose me."
What was it? Ibn al-Kawwa? No, Ibn al-Kawwa was different, he was a hypocrite. So, a person came and said to you... So... he said, "O Amir al-Mumineen, I want to ask you a question." He said, "Ask." He said, "Where is Jibril right now?" "*Ayna Jibril?*" (Where is Jibril?). "At this moment, where is Janab-e-Jibril? Tell me." Janab-e-Amir al-Mumineen, peace be upon him, looked up, looked here, looked there, looked behind, turned and looked. Then he said, "I think you are Jibril."
I looked towards the sky, I looked towards the earth, I looked left, I looked right, but I could not find Jibril. So I know that you are Jibril. And you are so-and-so, son of so-and-so, son of so-and-so, son of so-and-so. This incident is narrated in great detail in *Saluni*. And... he... let out a cry and rose up high.
This incident is narrated in *Saluni*.
"*Ana azunnu anta Jibril*" (I think you are Jibril).
I think that you are Jibril.

The fourth chapter. *Dusre bab se chauthe suradiq se* (From the second gate, from the fourth pavilion). *Wa hadhihi surat al-khabith al-mufariqa lil-nufus min al-ajdad al-muttasila bi-kulli jism* (And this is the evil form, separated from the souls from the bodies, connected to every body). *Li-kulli jismin khabithin* (For every evil body). *Fa-sarat nihayatu khabithin lil-shar* (So it became the utmost evil for wickedness) *muqabalatan lil-nihayati-sharif allati hiya nihayatul-khayr* (in opposition to the noble end which is the end of goodness) *kama sabaqa fi hadha al-qawl* (as has preceded in this statement). And this evil form that has been released, the souls... from the bodies, that which became connected to that evil body, *har jism-e-khabith ke liye* (for every evil body), then its end became... *Toh ho gayi hai woh* (So it has become) the utmost evil... The utmost evil for wickedness. In opposition to the utmost noble... *Muqabil hone wali* (The one that becomes an opponent), the utmost... Like the end of goodness is the end of goodness. As preceded in this statement. The end of goodness is that which... Those who are good people, this *surat-e-khabitha* (evil form) works against them. *Kama* (as), just as it preceded in this statement. *Wa sidqu qawliha* (And the truth of its statement)... *Sidqu qawliha fi ma tukhbiru bihi min al-kainat* (The truth of its statement in what it informs of the beings) *wa al-hawadith al-jariya* (and the ongoing events) *li-ma kana min khidmatiha fi shari'at al-natiq* (due to what was from its service in the shari'a of the natiq) *wa khidmatiha li-ba'dh ahl al-haqq* (and its service to some people of truth) *bi-sidqin minha* (with truth from it) *wa nasihatuhu fa-kana... wa nasiha* (and his advice, so it was... and advice). And your statement became true... And at times, the very evil forms, they also narrate true things, he is saying. *Wa sidqu qawliha* (And the truth of its statement). And its statement becomes true in the thing about which it gives news... from the beings... from the beings and from the ongoing events... from the ongoing events, *li-ma kana* (because of what was), what happens from its service... what happens from the service of that *surat* (form), in the *shari'at-e-natiq* (shari'a of the natiq)... of the *natiq*... Like I have a screen, *nasb hai uske andar*. The thing which is that... What is he saying? Why did it happen like that? *Fi shari'at al-natiq* (in the shari'a of the natiq). Theirs which is... *li-ma kana min khidmatiha* (because of what was from its service). Because of its service in the *shari'at-e-natiq* (shari'a of the natiq). *Wa khidmatiha li-ba'dh ahl al-haqq* (And its service to some people of truth). And its service... the service of some people of truth... some people of truth... truth from it... *bi-sidqin minha* (with truth from it). With truth from it and from advice, it... in life... it had also said some true things, had done works of goodwill. Its compensation is given to it in life, that its word has a part of truth in it. *Wa kana sidquha...* The *natiq's shari'at*, meaning in the era of the *natiq*, it must have been... must have served. Must have advised. Its compensation is given to it in life. Then it became bad, evil... Yes, evil people also sometimes give true information, he is saying. Although they are evil in essence, they give true information. Why do they give true information? It is because at one time they used to speak the truth. Along with the truth, there was also wickedness in them. Both things were there. Because we have this, that *al-sharra la asla lahu fil-ibda'* (Evil has no root in creation). At one time, a person spoke the truth, served. Afterwards, he got corrupted. So what will happen? Will his truth go to waste? No. It will remain. Truth has no decline. For his truth, he will be given a reward. For his services, he will be given a reward. Whatever good deed he did, he will get its reward. *Wa kana...* This is for the *natiq*, not for the *masih* (messiah). *Fi shari'at al-natiq* (in the shari'a of the natiq). In the *shari'a* of the *natiq*. *Natiq ki shari'at* (the shari'a of the natiq). With anyone... *Natiq se to...* They can get corrupted even during the *natiq's* time, it can get corrupted anywhere. But if, along with getting corrupted, it has done some work of piety, it will be given its reward for it. It will not be punished for its statement. It is speaking the truth in its place, but it speaks the truth at times, and at times it does not. Now whatever... Here, it is said that its compensation will be given to it. For its truth that it has done, it will be given a reward. *Wa kana sidquha minha hadha al-sabab...* *Muttasila bi-kulli jismin khabith fa-sarat nihayatun khabithun lil-shar* (connected to every evil body, so it became an utmost evil end for wickedness). So it is evil for the bad, and for the good, they are good. No, no. This *surat-e-khabitha* (evil form), which is for every evil body, has become the utmost evil. In opposition to whom? Those who are extremely noble, who are the utmost good, in opposition to them, it is the utmost evil. Despite this, if it has done some work of piety, has been truthful, has done some service, has... taken care of the common people, of Allah's creation, its reward will surely be given to it. *Wa kana sidquha...* *Wa kana sidquha min hadha al-sabab adlan lillah li-kawnihi la yudhi'u saghiratan wa-la kabiratan min khayrin wa-la sharrin* (So its truth was for this reason, justice for Allah, because He does not let be wasted a small or large [deed] of good or evil). So, the truth of that *surat* (form) will be... from this reason, *'adl* (justice)... *'adl* (justice) from Allah the Exalted, because... because He does not let be wasted a small or a large... large... of good or of evil. Whatever good or evil a person does, whether small or big, he will be given its reward. *Fa-man ya'mal mithqala dharratin khayran yarah, wa-man ya'mal mithqala dharratin sharran yarah* (So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it). So he who does an act equal to a little, will see... the good, and he who does an act, a speck equal to evil, will see it. *Wa-humul-ghilan al-zahira allati dhakaraha rasulullah salawatullahi 'alayhi bi-qawlihi...* *Allati dhakaraha* (which he mentioned)... *allati dhakaraha rasulullah salawatullahi 'alayhi bi-qawlihi: la yaqulu al-ghilan* (which the Messenger of Allah, peace of Allah be upon him, mentioned in his saying: The ghouls do not say) *illa al-a'rab wa al-sibyan* (except to the bedouins and the children) *wa jami'u... awzhum wa azayim la ta'malu* (and all... their charms and incantations do not work) *illa min khawfi sharrihim* (except from fear of their evil). *Min khawfi sharrihim* (From fear of their evil). *Sharri min khawfi sharrihim* (Evil from fear of their evil). And they all... *Wa-humul-ghilan al-zahira* (And they are the apparent ghouls). They are desert ghouls, in appearance. They are desert ghouls in appearance, such that... The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, mentioned it... The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him... What is this? *Wa-humul-ghilan* (And they are the ghouls). Troops of jinn are *ghilan*. Whom the Messenger of Allah mentioned... He mentioned it in your statement that they do not... do not... affect... they affect... those ghouls... desert ghouls... desert ghouls... except the bedouins and children... children... they affect the children more, and those who are illiterate, they affect them more. *Wa jami'u...* And these who previously did, that their events are true... At times they speak the truth. So one should not even accept their word, meaning... meaning evil... It seems that their evil is only prediction, and that prediction turns out to be true. Why does the prediction turn out to be true? It is because they are being compensated for the fact that in the *shari'a* of the *natiq*, they have performed some services, and have also spoken some true things in that era. They supported the truth, that is why. But... their words... one should not verify... Sometimes their words are true, that is a different matter. Yes. Sometimes it turns out to be true. What can you do? If it turns out to be true, one should not understand that they are among the *awliya* (saints). It's not like that, he is saying. They... they are being given the reward for their truth. And all the amulets... All the amulets and incantations are not done... are not done except from fear of their evil. From fear of their evil. The amulets are given so that their evil... their evil... from fear of their evil, they are given. *Wa lam yu'mar bil-qira'ati...* The amulets that the *awliya Allah* (friends of God) give... It is because of this that they give. Because of their evil, they give. *Wa lam yu'mar bil-qira'ati...* *Wa lam yu'mar bil-qira'ati wa al-ta'awwudh 'inda al-nawm illa minhum* (And it was not commanded to recite and seek refuge at the time of sleep except from them). And it was not commanded... And a command was not given for recitation... for recitation and for *ta'awwudh* (seeking refuge)... *ta'awwudh* (seeking refuge) near... at the time of sleep... except from them. What does it mean? At the time of sleep, what *ta'awwudh* (seeking refuge) do they recite? *Qul a'udhu bi-rabbi al-nas, qul a'udhu bi-rabbi al-falaq*. *Allahumma la tu'minni makraka wa-la tunsini dhikraka wa-la taj'alni min al-ghafilin* (O Allah, do not make me feel secure from Your plan, and do not make me forget Your remembrance, and do not make me among the heedless). What does it mean? *Allahumma la tu'minni makraka* (O Allah, do not make me feel secure from Your plan). O Allah, do not keep me safe from Your plan. What does it mean? *La tu'minni makraka* (Do not make me feel secure from Your plan). What is meant by *makr*? Strategy. At night, their strategies are also ongoing, of the desert ghouls. O Allah, you, your plan... your plan, your strategies... should remain included in it. *La tu'minni* (Do not make me feel secure). From your strategy, do not keep me safe. *Wa-la tunsini dhikraka* (and do not make me forget Your remembrance). And do not let me forget your remembrance. May your remembrance always remain fresh. *Wa-la taj'alni min al-ghafilin* (and do not make me among the heedless). And do not keep me among the heedless. And it has been said that after this, a person should intend that I will wake up in the morning at such and such a time. Then... that... its... the cell for its thinking becomes fixed in the brain, and it wakes up at that time. And if it ever doesn't wake up, then Allah the Exalted has forgiven it, because it did intend, but drowsiness came over it. It has been explained. It has been explained by Sayyidna Ghulam Husain Sahab in *Sahifa-e-Chahalsawa*. *Wa-kadhalika al-ta'awwudh fi al-mawadhi' wa al-mawazi' al-muzlima* (And likewise seeking refuge in the places and the dark locations) *wa al-biqa' al-wasikha min khawfi sharrihim* (and the filthy spots from fear of their evil). *Biqa'*... *Buqatun, biqa'*. *Wa al-biqa' al-wasikha min khawfi sharrihim* (And the filthy spots from fear of their evil). And in the same way, seeking refuge is in urinals and... and... dark... dark... To read the *ta'awwudh* (seeking refuge). The *ta'awwudh* is in urinals. Urinals and dark places. They say "urinals" to... and dark places. And filthy places. From fear of their evil. If one reaches there, then what should one do? *A'udhu billahi min al-rijs al-najis* (I seek refuge in Allah from the impure filth). *Ta'awwudh* means to seek refuge. The meaning of *ta'awwudh* is to seek refuge. And with amulets, what do they do? They seek refuge. In writing. *Wa al-biqa' al-wasikha min khawfi sharrihim* (And the filthy spots from fear of their evil). In bad places, from fear of their evil. *'Aadhana Allahu min sharrihim wa min sharri aslafihim* (May Allah protect us from their evil and from the evil of their predecessors). May Allah keep us in His protection from their evil. *Wa sharri aslafihim* (And from the evil of their predecessors). And from the evil of their successors. And their followers. And their adherents. *Bi-haqqi Muhammadin wa alihi salawatullahi 'alayhim ajma'in* (by the right of Muhammad and his family, peace of Allah be upon them all). *Al-fasl al-khamis min al-bab al-thani min al-suradiq al-rabi'* (The fifth chapter from the second gate from the fourth pavilion). The fifth chapter, from the second gate, from the fourth pavilion. *Fa-lladhina yuslimuna min hadhihi al-suwar al-muqamat al-'aliya salamullahi 'alayhim hum al-jinn al-mahmudun.* *Aslama, yuslimu*. *Fa-lladhina yuslimuna* (So those who submit)... *yuslimuna min hadhihi al-suwar al-muqamat al-'aliya* (submit from these forms of the high stations) *salamullahi 'alayhim hum al-jinn al-mahmudun* (peace of Allah be upon them, they are the praiseworthy jinn). *Wa-lladhina baqu 'ala 'isyanihim hum al-jinn al-madhmumun* (And those who remain upon their disobedience, they are the blameworthy jinn). So those who bring Islam from these *suwarat* (forms)... from these *suwarat* (forms) for the Imam *'alayhis-salam*, peace and blessings of Allah be upon them... blessings of Allah be upon them, they are the *jinn-e-mahmud* (praiseworthy jinn). And those who remain... who remain upon their disobedience, they are the *jinn-e-madhmum* (blameworthy jinn). *Wa kathiran mimman yunsabu ilal-da'wat al-hadiya* (And many of those who are attributed to the Rightly-Guiding Mission) *salamullahi 'ala sahibiha* (peace of Allah be upon its master) *la yara* (does not see/believe)... *la yara bil-jinni bal yukadhdhibu bi-dhalika* (does not believe in the jinn but rather denies that). And many people... And many people who are attributed... who are attributed to the *Da'wat al-Hadiya* (Rightly-Guiding Mission), peace of Allah be upon its master... upon its master, do not... do not believe... do not believe in the jinn, but rather deny that matter. *Wa dhalika li-qillati...* *Wa dhalika li-qillati ma'rifatihim wa istighna'ihim bi-nufusihim wa tarkihim li-muwalat al-hudud al-mansubin min qibali awliya' Allah ta'ala* (And that is due to the scarcity of their knowledge and their being self-sufficient in their own souls and their abandoning of the allegiance to the Hudud who are appointed from the side of the Friends of Allah, the Exalted). And that... And many who... yes... and that is due to the scarcity of their *ma'rifat* (knowledge), the scarcity of their *ma'rifat* (knowledge). That the jinn exist, and the actions of these people that happen from behind the scenes, that also exists. But due to the scarcity of *ma'rifat* (knowledge), they do not have faith in it, he is saying. Why do they not have it? Generally, many people in the *Da'wat-e-Hadiya* (Rightly-Guiding Mission) think that this is just a saying, there is nothing like that. Hazrat, a question is arising that here, the evil spirits, the *arwah-e-khabitha* (evil spirits), are kept for this reason, that they should do their own, whatever *sawabikhat* (past deeds) there are, whatever... but these people, with their evil, are increasing their own evil. Meaning that by doing evil deeds, only in the world of bodies is any thing either increased... because it is a world of choice, either do evil or do good, and in the same way, increase your goodness or your evil. But here, the *sawabikhat* (past deeds) are not, but rather these people are moving further ahead from their evil deeds into their evil. Meaning that in a way, this entire thing is a world of choice. They have the right to take the *qisasat* (retributions), the *baqiyat* (dues) of their time. So that they may take the full *qisasat* (retributions), then... But besides that, they continue their evil. Their evil continues. The evil happens only with those for whom there are *baqiyat* (dues). They do it only with them for whom there are *baqiyat* (dues). They cannot do it with everyone. Then why do we say *a'udhu billah* (I seek refuge in Allah), this and that, why do we recite? We seek refuge. We ask Allah to keep them safe from evil. Meaning if some such mistakes happen from us, that in relations with them, something happened with us, then Allah the Exalted, with His grace and favor, should keep us safe from it. This is the world. In the world, there are various kinds of... someone says something harsh, something happens with someone, something happens with someone. How much will a person be careful? *Wa dhalika li-qillati ma'rifatihim* (And that is due to the scarcity of their knowledge). And that is because of the scarcity of their *ma'rifat* (knowledge). And that is because of the scarcity of their *ma'rifat* (knowledge). *Wa istighna'ihim bi-nufusihim* (And their being self-sufficient in their own souls). And their being self-sufficient. They think that whatever they have thought is correct. And their abandoning. Among the believers, there are many such in the *Da'wat-e-Hadiya* (Rightly-Guiding Mission) who have little *ma'rifat* (knowledge), and they think that what they have thought is the truth. And they have abandoned allegiance to the *hudud* (ranks). That is why their way of thinking is such that the jinn do not even exist. The *hudud* (ranks) who are appointed from the side of the *awliya' Allah* (friends of God)... *Wa yaquluna inna al-jinn hum ahl 'ilm al-batin wa al-ins hum ahl 'ilm al-zahir* (And they say that the jinn, they are the people of the knowledge of the inward, and the humans, they are the people of the knowledge of the outward). And they say... they say that the jinn, they are the people of the *'ilm-e-batin* (inward knowledge), and humans are the people of the *'ilm-e-zahir* (outward knowledge). Their meaning is only that this has been said in a *ta'wili* (interpretive) sense. It has not been said only in a *ta'wili* (interpretive) sense, but they also have a physical existence. It is *ta'wil* (interpretation) and it also has a physical existence. *Wa ma hunalika shay'un ghayra dhalik* (and there is nothing there other than that). And there is no thing there besides it. So both these things are correct. What has been stated, that who are the jinn? The people of *'ilm-e-batin* (inward knowledge). And who are humans? The people of *'ilm-e-zahir* (outward knowledge). And this is also correct that the *jinn-e-mahmud* (praiseworthy jinn) exist, just as humans exist. *Jinn-e-madhmum* (blameworthy jinn) also exist. *Jinn-e-madhmum* and *jinn-e-mahmud*, both exist. *Wa li-'amri...* *Wa li-'amri inna ahl al-batin hum al-jinn li-ijnanihim wa sitrihim 'an al-batin wa hum yanqasimuna 'ala qismayn: mahmud wa madhmum* (And by my life, indeed the people of the inward are the jinn because of their being hidden and their concealment from the inward, and they are divided into two types: praiseworthy and blameworthy). And I swear by my life... and I swear... and by my age... by my age. The people of the inward are the jinn, because of their being hidden... their being hidden and being concealed... and being concealed from the inward. This is also a correct thing, he is saying. And they are divided into two types, good and bad. *Wa al-mahmud* (And the praiseworthy)... *al-mahmud hum al-muntazimun fi silki al-haqq wa hududihi al-mustamsikuna bi-shara'i' al-tawhid wa awza'ihi al-'arifuna bi-ma'alim al-manazil wa hum falasifat al-ilahiyyun* (The praiseworthy are those who are organized in the thread of the truth and its ranks, who hold fast to the laws of tawhid and its statutes, who are knowledgeable of the signposts of the stations, and they are the divine philosophers). So, the good among them... So, the good among them are those who remain in the thread of truth and its ranks... and its ranks. And those who hold fast to the laws of *tawhid* (oneness of God) and its statutes, their statutes, their stations, those who know... the high stations. And they, and they are the divine philosophers. *Wa al-qism al-thani hum al-falasifat al-mu'attilun lil-wasa'it alladhina hum al-nuqaba' wa al-awsiyya' wa al-a'imma wa hududihim salawatullahi 'alayhim* (And the second type are the negating philosophers who deny the intermediaries, who are the nuqaba', the awsiyya', the a'imma, and their ranks, peace of Allah be upon them). And the second type are the philosophers who are *mu'attil* (negators)... *mu'attil* (negators)... those intermediaries, who are the *nuqaba'* (chiefs), and the *awsiyya'* (successors), and the *a'imma* (Imams), and their *hudud* (ranks). Blessings and peace of Allah be upon all of them. *Wa ha'ula'i adallu dalaalatan min al-firaq* (and these are more astray in error than the sects). And these people are more misguided than all the sects. The philosophers. The philosophers who are *mu'attil* (negators). Those people are the most... *Wa hum al-abalisa wa al-shayatin* (and they are the devils and the Satans). And they are the devils and the Satans. *'Aadhana Allahu minhum bi-haqqi Muhammadin wa alihi al-tahirin salawatullahi 'alayhim ajma'in* (May Allah protect us from them by the right of Muhammad and his pure family, peace of Allah be upon them all). In the apparent world, among humans also, there are two types. And in the inward, the jinn, they are also in their place. Both things are correct. *Wa amma al-ins fa-hum ahl al-zahir wa hum yanqasimuna qismayn: mahmud wa madhmum* (And as for the humans, they are the people of the outward, and they are divided into two types: praiseworthy and blameworthy). And as for humans, they are the people of the outward, and they are divided into two types, good and bad. *Wa al-mahmud hum al-qa'imuna bi-awza'i al-shari'a allati lam yubdilha al-mubtilun wa lam yughayyirha al-dallun wa hum biha qa'imuna ma'a 'iffat wa taharat wa salamat al-nafs min bughdh ahl al-haqq wa ittiba' al-nafs allati bil-su'i ammaratun wa hum qalilun* (The praiseworthy are those who uphold the statutes of the shari'a which the falsifiers have not altered and the misguided have not changed, and they are steadfast upon it with chastity, purity, and soundness of the soul from hatred of the people of truth and following the soul which commands evil, and they are few). So the good ones are those who establish... who establish the injunctions of the *shari'a* (law), which the falsifiers have not changed, and the misguided have not changed... the *shari'a*... the misguided. So they, with that *shari'a*, are those who establish it with chastity and with purity and with soundness of soul from hatred of the people of truth. And following the soul... the soul which... that evil-commanding soul. And they are few. *Wa al-madhmum hum al-qa'imuna bi-awza'i al-shari'a al-munasibuna li-ahl al-da'wat al-hadiya al-muzharuna lil-nusuk al-mubtinuna lil-ifk al-mubaddaluna lil-shar' al-muhibbuna li-akthar al-waza'* (The blameworthy are those who uphold the statutes of the shari'a, who associate with the people of the Rightly-Guiding Mission, who make a show of piety, who conceal falsehood, who alter the law, who love most of the burdens). And the blameworthy are those who establish the injunctions of the *shari'a*... Who are the blameworthy among them? Who are the blameworthy among them? Those who establish the injunctions of the *shari'a*, but they are antagonists... they are hostile to the people of the *Da'wat-e-Hadiya* (Rightly-Guiding Mission). They make an outward show of their worship. And they keep falsehood in their hearts. They establish... of the *shari'a*, meaning... meaning, they are hostile to the people of truth. Outwardly, they are attached to the *shari'a*, but in their hearts, there is hostility towards the people of the *Da'wat-e-Hadiya* (Rightly-Guiding Mission). Outwardly, they are ascetics, but inwardly, what are they? They are possessors of falsehood. I mean that they come into the *Da'wat-e-Hadiya* and do things like this. No, no, it's not like that. The common people. *Al-mubtinuna lil-ifk* (Those who conceal falsehood). Inwardly, they are... *Al-munasibuna li-ahl al-da'wat al-hadiya* (Those who associate with the people of the Rightly-Guiding Mission). In this manner. Those who are hostile to the people of the *Da'wat-e-Hadiya* (Rightly-Guiding Mission). It's a matter of the common people. *Al-muzharuna lil-nusuk* (Those who make a show of piety). They make a display of asceticism... of asceticism, but inwardly they... are against it. *Al-mubaddaluna lil-shar' al-muhibbuna li-akthar al-waza'* (Those who alter the law, who love most of the burdens). And they change... change the *shari'at* (law). What is *ma'na*? Allah has commanded, *famsahu bi-ru'usikum wa arjulikum* (wipe your heads and your feet). Wipe your heads, wipe your feet. Allah has commanded to wipe, what do they do? They wash their feet. If you go outside sometimes and perform ablution, they will see that he is washing his feet. He pours four to five mugs of water on his feet. Whereas Allah has... for us it has been said, if one washes their feet, one can wash them. But to say that Allah has only commanded me to wipe, and to wash them... a greater purity... a greater purity... If he does it with this understanding, his prayer will not be valid. If he does it with the understanding that washing the feet has been made obligatory, then his prayer... will not be valid. *'Aadhana Allahu wa jami'a ikhwanina minhum wa min muwalat al-awliya' 'anhum* (May Allah protect us and all our brothers from them and from allegiance to the friends of God away from them). May Allah keep us and all the brothers in His protection... He did not raise it... you did not raise your finger. I have an anecdote. We once... were in Masjid-e-Zubaydi. In Masjid-e-Zubaydi, we went with Hazrat Ishaq Sahab. We went there for prayer. A sermon was being given, and after that, it was time for prayer. It was time for the Maghrib prayer. And we prayed the Maghrib prayer with them. And after praying, Hazrat stood up and started praying his sunnah of Maghrib. After praying two rak'ahs of sunnah, a gentleman came and said, "Hazrat, please give me permission too, Maulana, give me permission too, that I may also pray. I also want to pray six rak'ahs. Give me permission." They only pray two rak'ahs, right? They pray two rak'ahs. "Give me permission too, that I may also pray." [unclear] In the presence of water, you performed tayammum with a stone? [unclear]

<!-- lecture 54 -->

`Al-Bab al-thalith min Sawabit al-'Adad fi Ithbat al-mabda' wal-ma'ad.` (The third chapter from *Sawabit al-'Adad* in proof of the origin and the return.) The third chapter, from *Sawabit al-'Adad*. This is the first discussion that comes. The first section. `Al-Fasl al-awwal minha fi-ma yash-hadu min siḥḥatihi ma awradnahu min al-qawl fi ma'ad al-nufus al-mutawaliyah wal-nufus al-khabithah al-'asiyah.` (The first section thereof concerning that which testifies to its soundness from what we have cited of the statement concerning the return of the loving souls and the evil, disobedient souls.) `Qawlu al-shakhṣ al-faḍil ṣaḥib al-rasa'il, salawat Allahi 'alayhi, fi risalatihi al-ma'rufah bil-jami'ah, ḥaythu qala: thumma inna al-insan al-faḍil al-'amil al-'alim la yazalu hatta yara a'malahu al-ḥasanat, wa-akhlaqahu al-jamilah, wa-ma yaẓharu minhu, wa-yasiru 'anhu, fi ḥusni al-siyasati allati yatahayya'u laha biha li-iqamat al-shari'ah, wa-talaqqi al-waḥy min al-mala'ikah, thumma idha faraqa al-'alama ṣara malakan bil-fi'l, wa-dakhala fi zumrat al-mala'ikah.` (The statement of the virtuous personage, the Author of the Epistles, blessings of Allah be upon him, in his epistle known as *al-Jami'ah*, where he said: Then indeed, the virtuous, active, and knowledgeable person persists until he sees his good deeds, his beautiful morals, what appears from him, and what proceeds from him in the excellence of conduct by which he is prepared for the establishment of the *shari'ah* and the reception of revelation from the angels. Then, when he departs from the world, he becomes an angel in actuality and enters into the company of the angels.) From the first section, whatever... `minha ma yash-hadu` (thereof, that which testifies), whatever has come, it is proven by that... that which testifies... that which testifies to the soundness of the statement that has come before from that statement... about the return of souls, the loving ones... which are loving, meaning those who love, and the souls that are evil and disobedient and sinful. It is the statement of the virtuous personage who is the Author of the Epistles. May the blessings of Allah be upon him. Blessings be upon him. `Fi risalatihi` (in his epistle). In your epistle, which is... `al-jami'ah`... yes, where you have stated... you have stated that the virtuous person, who is active and knowledgeable, continues... it always happens that he sees his good deeds and beautiful morals, and whatever is manifested from him, it takes him towards... good... good conduct... good... `bi... husn al-siyasati allati yatahayya'u lahu` (`husn`... of conduct, which is prepared for it...) He always remains until he sees his deeds, his good deeds, and his beautiful morals, and what is manifested from him. And he becomes, from it, with good conduct, for which he is prepared for the establishment of the *shari'ah*, and he receives revelation... he receives revelation from the angels. Then, when he departs from the world, he becomes `malakan bil-fi'l` (an angel in actuality) and enters into the company of the angels. Until now, he was not `malakan bil-fi'l`. He was `malakan bil-quwwah` (an angel in potentiality). Now he becomes `malakan bil-fi'l`. And `wa-dakhala fi zumrat al-mala'ikah` (and he enters into the company of the angels). He enters into the company of the angels. `Wa-qawluhu salawat Allahi 'alayhi isharatan ila ahl al-ḥaqq al-qa'imina bil-ḥaqq fi al-'ibadatayn al-zahirah wal-batinah, al-muttaṣilina bil-maqamat al-ilahiyyah, fa-inna mufaraqatahum li-hadha al-'alami yasiruna...` (And his statement, blessings of Allah be upon him, is an allusion to the People of Truth who uphold the truth in the two worships, the outward and the inward, who are connected to the divine stations. For indeed, upon their departure from this world, they proceed...) And his statement... your statement, salutations be upon you, is an allusion... it has been alluded to... those People of Truth... the Author of the Epistles has... the Author of the Epistles has. So, your statement, may the blessings of Allah be upon you, is an allusion to the People of Truth who are those who establish... who establish the truth in the two worships, the outward and the inward. And the outward worship is what? The inward worship is what? Action (`'amal`) is the outward worship. Knowledge (`'ilm`) is the inward worship. `Al-muttaṣilina` (those who are connected)... who are connected to the divine stations. They remain connected to the divine stations, meaning the `hudud kiram`. And then... so indeed, upon their leaving... their leaving this world... Whose leaving? The pronoun (`zamir`) is going where? `Hudud kiram`. `Hudud kiram`, towards the People of Truth, who have established with knowledge... outward knowledge and inward knowledge. So, upon their leaving this world, they reach... they reach the `hadrat al-'aliyyah al-sharifah` (the high, noble presence). `Wa-huwa qawluhu sara malakan bil-fi'l, wa-dakhala fi zumrat al-mala'ikah.` (And that is his statement: he became an angel in actuality and entered into the company of the angels.) And that is the statement... So, his statement... it is stated that `sara malakan bil-fi'l` (he became an angel in actuality). They become `malak bil-fi'l` (an angel in actuality)... `malak bil-fi'l`. This is a mention of the `nafs` (soul). `malak bil-fi'l`. The `nafs` and the `surah` (form). `Wa-dakhala fi zumrat al-mala'ikah.` (And he entered into the company of the angels.) And they enter the company of the angels... company of the angels. `Wa-zumrat al-mala'ikah ahlun li-dhalika al-majma' al-sabiq dhikruhu.` (And the company of the angels are worthy of that assembly whose mention has preceded.) And the assembly of angels... the assembly of angels is worthy of that assembly... is worthy of that assembly whose mention was made before. So, which is the assembly of angels? It is the `haykal al-sharif` (noble temple). `Thumma dhakara al-aḍdad hatta intaha ila qawlihi: fa-li-jahalatihi` (Then he mentioned the opposites until he reached his statement: So, because of his ignorance...) Then he mentioned the opposites. Then he mentioned the opposites... he mentioned the opposites, until he reached this statement of his... reached this statement of his. What? `Fa-li-jahalatihi bi-mubtadi'ihi wa-awliya'ihi sara 'aduwwan li-rabbihi, kharijan 'an ṭa'atihi, wa-idda'a li-nafsihi ma la yastaḥiqquhu wa-la yaliqu bihi, wa-huwa imam al-zalalati wa-ra'is al-jahalah.` (So, because of his ignorance of his Originator and His friends, he became an enemy to his Lord, departing from His obedience, and he claimed for himself what he does not deserve and what is not befitting him, and he is the Imam of error and the chief of ignorance.) What is your statement? So, because of his ignorance... because of his ignorance, with his `mubtada` (Originator)... Whose mention is this? Of the opposites. And of their `awliya` (friends)... he becomes an enemy of his Lord. He who departs from His obedience... from His obedience. And... `mudda'a li-nafsihi` (a claimant for himself). And he claims... he makes a claim for his `nafs`, for that which he is not worthy of. And... `Idda'a`, what is it from? `Du'a`? `Da'a` means he called. `Idda'a` means he called towards himself. `Idda'a`. `Infa'ala`. From `infa'ala`, it is `idda'a`. `Da'a` means he made a claim... he calls towards his `nafs` for that which he is not worthy of, nor is it befitting for him. Nor is he worthy of that which he is not worthy of. And he is the Imam of error (`zalalah`). He is the Imam of error and the chief of ignorance. Ignorance. `Fa-idha faraqa al-'alama bi-jismihi, sara shayṭana nafsihi, wa-nafsuhu la yufariqu jismihu, wa-habaṭa ila asfal al-safilin, yuwaswisu bil-ghawayah fi ṣudur al-nas, wa-yuhi ila amthalihi min al-mutaraddina al-ajsam, zukhrufa al-qawl ghurura, kama yuhi al-mala'ikah ila anbiya' al-ta'id, fa-yahbiṭu ilayhim bi-awamirihi wa-nawahihi, wa-yatanazzalu bi-amri rabbiha 'ala man yasha'u min 'ibadihi, kama akhbara subḥanahu: nazala bihi al-ruh al-amin.` (So, when he departs the world with his body, he becomes the shaitan of his own soul, and his soul does not leave his body, and he descends to the lowest of the low, whispering error into the breasts of men, and inspiring his likes from among the degraded bodies with specious words as a delusion, just as the angels inspire the prophets of support. So he descends upon them with his commands and his prohibitions, and he descends with the command of his Lord upon whomever He wills of His servants, as He, the Glorified, informed: The Trustworthy Spirit descended with it.) And when he leaves the world with his body... then he becomes the shaitan of his `nafs`... the `surah` (form) of his body. His `surah`. So from his `nafs` he becomes a shaitan... a shaitan of his own `nafs`. His `nafs` does not leave his body. And they fall... he falls to the lowest of the low. He falls to the lowest of the low, meaning... The `nafs` has become the body. The `nafs` should have acquired the `surah`, and gone with the `surah`. It is with the body, meaning materiality has increased even more in it. So `asfal al-safilin` means... `wa-habata`, and he falls to the `asfal al-safilin`, of error... That he whispers temptations of misguidance into the hearts of people. And he gives revelation... `wahy`... to his likes, who are among the bodies (`ajsam`)... who are among the bodies. So, it is deception... `zukhrufa al-qawli ghurura` (specious words as a delusion). With embellished speech... through deception... through deception. An embellishment of deceptive speech. Embellishment... `shingar` [Urdu for decoration]. `Kama yuhi al-mala'ikah ila anbiya' al-ta'id` (just as the angels inspire the prophets of support). Just as the angels give revelation to the prophets of support. `Fa-yahbitu ilayhim`. And he descends upon them... and he descends upon them... `bi-awamirihi wa-nawahihi` (with his commands and his prohibitions). From `amawir` and from `nawahi`. Meaning, just as `wahy` comes to the prophets from the angels, in the same way, this one gives `wahy` to people like himself, of evil things. `Wa-yatanazzalu bi-amri rabbiha 'ala man yasha'u min 'ibadihi.` (And he descends with the command of his Lord upon whomever He wills of His servants.) And they descend with the command of their Lord upon whomever He wills from among His servants. As Allah Ta'ala says that they descend... `al-ruh al-amin` (the Trustworthy Spirit).
