The fourth chapter (*bāb al-rābiʿ*) from the seventh *surād* (part). This section, the first of five, is a compilation from the seventh *surād*. And when our discourse reached its conclusion on the topic of *mabdāʾ wa-maʿād* (the beginning and the end) for the *walī* (friend of God), the *ẓāhirī* (the exoteric person), and the *ḍidd* (the opponent), and indeed the *mīzān al-ʿadl* (scale of justice) is established by Allah Ta'ala for His servants, `lā yughādiru ṣaghīratan wa-lā kabīratan illā aḥṣāhā` (it leaves behind neither a small nor a large [deed] but has enumerated it). And when our discourse concluded here, that is, it concluded with the discussion on *mabdāʾ wa-maʿād* for the *walī*, for the *ẓāhirī* individuals, and for the *ḍidd*. And that the *mīzān al-ʿadl* is established by Allah Ta'ala upon His servants. And it does not leave out, neither the small nor the big... It leaves out neither the small nor the big. `Yughādiru ṣaghīratan`. The object will be... It does not leave... It does not leave the small one... It does not leave the small one or the big one. Who does not leave it? The *mīzān al-ʿadl*. `lā yughādiru mīzān... mīzān al-ʿadl`. The *mīzān* is established. The *mīzān al-ʿadl* does not leave the small one or the big one, `illā aḥṣāhā` (but has enumerated it). ...except that it enumerates it. This... This *mīzān al-ʿadl* which... the *ʿāshiq*'s, that's what it is. The justice of Allah Ta'ala is what encompasses everyone, all of His creatures, whether he is a *walī*, a *ẓāhirī*, or a *ḍidd*. To each will be given as much as he thinks, as much as he acts. Sir, is the *wālī* (governor) of each era different for the *mīzān al-ʿadl* or is there one who is appointed? Whoever is appointed for it. Whoever is appointed. It is an appointed, established law of Allah. It is implemented. `Wa-jāzā ʿalayhā, in khayran fa-khayrun, in... in... in khayran fa-khayrun, wa-in sharran fa-sharrun`. `Wa-jāzā ʿalayhā`. And He gives recompense for it. He gives recompense for it. And He gives recompense for it. Whoever does anything small or big will receive its recompense. `In khayran`, this is `in`. If there is good, then it will be good. Then there will be good. `wa-in sharran fa-sharrun`. And if there is evil, then it will be evil. This is `in`. `Wa-dhakarnā...` Meaning, if he does good, he will get good in return. If he does evil, he will get evil in return. `Wa-dhakarnā...` `Wa-dhakarnā intiqāl al-nāṭiq dawr masmūman wa-naqlat waṣiyyihi bil-mawt... salawāt Allāh ʿalayhimā... maqtūlan`. `Maqtūlan`. `Wa-kadhalika mā wālānā al-Ḥasan wal-Ḥusayn wal-Mustanṣir wal-ʿĀmir, ṣalawāt Allāh ʿalayhim ajmaʿīn, alladhīna minhum man intaqala masmūman wa-minhum man intaqala maqtūlan`. And... and our... And in the same way... In the same way... `wa-dhakarnā`, we have already mentioned... We have already mentioned the passing of the *nāṭiq*... of the *nāṭiq*... the passing of... who were given poison... who were given poison. And of your *waṣī*, whose passing... who passed away... Both of them were blessed with martyrdom. `naqlat waṣiyyihi`. And the passing of your *waṣī*... The passing of your *waṣī*... *Amīr al-Muʾminīn*, *ṣalawāt Allāh ʿalayhi*. *Amīr al-Muʾminīn*, *ṣalawāt Allāh ʿalayka*. `Maqtūl`. Who were killed. And similarly our masters Hasan and Husayn and Mustansir and 'Amir, may the blessings of Allah be upon them all, among them were those who passed away by poison and those who passed away by being killed... those who passed away, that is, they passed away in a state of being poisoned. And among them were those who passed away in a state of being killed. `Wa-inna dhālika jarā ʿalayhim...` Don't read `wa-idh`. Read `wa-inna`. `Wa-inna dhālika...` `Wa-inna dhālika`. `Wa-inna dhālika jarā ʿalayhim bi-mūjib...` The meaning of `idhā` is 'if', the meaning of `inna` is 'indeed'. There is a difference. `Wa-inna dhālika jarā ʿalayhim bi-mūjib al-ḥikmah`. And indeed, that event befell them... That befell them due to the cause of... due to the cause of wisdom. `wa-qaḍiyyat al-ʿadl qiṣāṣan`. The case of justice as retribution... `ʿammā kāna min kulli wāḥidin min ahl dawrihi`. For what was from every single one of the people of their era. As retribution taken from each one, from the people of their era. `wa-dhāka anna al-qiṣāṣ wāqiʿun ʿalayhim, salām Allāh ʿalayhim, ṣafwat Allāh min khalqihi wa-umanāʾahu ʿalā waḥyihi wa-khulafāʾahu fī arḍihi wa-shuhadāʾahu ʿalā ʿibādihi, fa-lā suqūṭa lahu ʿan shayʾin min ʿālam al-ṭabīʿah jumlatun, wa-lā manāṣa li-ṣaghīrihi wa-lā kabīrihi wa-qalīlihi wa-kathīrihi`. And although there is no escape... it is a retribution... a retribution is due... a retribution is incumbent upon them, `salām Allāh ʿalayhim` (the peace of Allah be upon them). Allah's peace be upon all of them. And they are the chosen ones of Allah... They are the chosen ones of Allah... from His creation... from His creation. And they are His trustees... over His revelation... over His revelation. And His vicegerents are in His land. And His witnesses are... His witnesses are... over His servants. So there is no... It will not fall from them... escape for it... So not falling for it... from any thing... from any thing of the world of nature... from the world of nature in its entirety... all of it. And there is no escape for its small and for its big, for its few and for its many. `idh law kānat al-musāmaḥah jāʾizatan li-aḥadin min dhālika aw shayʾin minhu, la-kāna Awliyāʾ Allāh ʿalayhim al-salām aḥaqqu wa-awlā bil-musāmaḥah min jamīʿ al-khalqah`. And if there were... If there were *musāmaḥah*, meaning... Pardoning it, overlooking it. Overlooking it. Permissible... Permissible. For any one... For that matter... From that matter. Or for any thing... from it... Then indeed the *Awliyāʾ Allāh*, *ʿalayhim al-salām*, would have been more deserving and more worthy of pardon than all of creation. Do you understand? The way the law is for all of creation, it is the same for the *Awliyāʾ Allāh* as well. If forgiveness was permissible, then the *Awliyāʾ Allāh* would have had forgiveness first. They too were held accountable in matters of retribution. From them, or from the people of their era who were there at that time. Like with Imam Husayn, *ʿalayhi al-ṣalāt wal-salām*, what did they state? That Mawla Ali had fought battles. In those, how many... were killed, his... from their... from their side, who were... from their forefathers, they were killed. They took revenge for that... Its recompense was taken from Imam Husayn, *ʿalayhi al-ṣalāt wal-salām*. A person's actions are not limited to himself. It also affects the people of his era. The people of the era are held accountable. If they did it, then he will receive it. If they didn't, and the people of his era did, then the people of the era are held accountable. A matter happens with whom, a relationship is established with them, and their work is done. So for example... It is said that Imam Husayn... *ḥijāb* (concealment) appeared. Why did the *ḥijāb* appear? Because of the *ḥijāb*, some things had happened. So the same *ḥijāb* that was in the time of Mawla Ali. From any *ḥijāb*, it can appear. Retribution... good... Good deeds... for retribution... for good deeds... Good and evil, both. Good and evil, both. Good deeds come in handy. Your good deed came in handy. Allah's justice is operative over everything. ...`fa-lā suqūṭa lahu ʿan shayʾin min ʿālam al-ṭabīʿah` (so there is no exemption for it from anything in the world of nature). ...that is, it doesn't... So it is not exempt for it... For the *mīzān al-ʿadl*, from any thing from the world of nature. Meaning, no... thing from it... Nothing from the world of nature can escape from it. As you do, so shall you bear. `Wa-idh kāna al-qawl kadhālika, fa-lā manāṣa li-aḥadin min al-khalāʾiq ʿan dhālika, sharīfihim wa-mashrūfihim wa-ʿazīzihim wa-dhalīlihim wa-rafīʿihim wa-waḍīʿihim`. Since it is... there is no escape for anyone from creation. For any one from creation, from that matter, from their noble and... and other than the noble, their mighty and their humble, and their high-ranking and their lowly. `Idh mīzān al-ʿadl qāʾimun, wa-laysa lillāhi Taʿālā wa-lā li-aḥadin min ʿibādihi muḥābātun fī fiʿlin yafʿaluhu, khayran kāna aw sharran`. And... And it is not for Allah, nor for His... any one of His servants... favoritism... What does `muḥābāt` mean? Favoritism... `ḥayā`... What's written in yours? `Ḥaqq`. `Muḥābāt` is written. `Ḥayā` is written in yours. What's written in yours? Is it not `[unclear]`? `Muḥābāt`... It is not for Allah Ta'ala, nor between any servant... any servant... favoritism... in an act... in an act... that he does. From good... from evil... or... And there is no favoritism between Allah and any of His servants... any of His servants... in an act that he does, whether it is good or evil. `kamā qāla Taʿālā fī muḥkam kitābihi: fa-man yaʿmal mithqāla dharratin khayran yarah, wa-man yaʿmal mithqāla dharratin sharran yarah` (As God the Exalted said in His decisive Book: "So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it"). And as Allah Ta'ala has said in His Book... And whoever acts... an atom's weight of evil will also see that evil. Meaning, Allah Ta'ala will not show favoritism in this matter, of good and evil. Of good and evil. Automatically, if he does good, he will get its benefit. Automatically, if he does evil, he will suffer its loss. `Wa-hādhihi al-āyah wāqiʿatun ʿalā al-khalq ajmaʿīn, wa-kullu mā yafʿaluhu al-insān min khayrin aw sharrin ʿāʾidun ʿalayhi mukāfātan bihi illā mā aḥallathu al-sharīʿah wa-sallama mā ahlāluhā fī qiymatihi ʿan tarāḍin bihi wa-inqiyādin lahu, ka-mithl al-nikāḥ al-jārī ʿalā kitāb Allāh wa-sunnat rasūlihi, ṣalawāt Allāh ʿalayhi, fa-lā qiṣāṣa fīhi`. The second chapter (*al-faṣl al-thānī*) from the fourth chapter (*bāb al-rābiʿ*), from the fourth *surād*. The second chapter from the fourth chapter, from the fourth *surād*. `Wa-laʿalla qāʾilan yaqūlu: fa-inna qatl al-maqāmāt li-man qatalūhu, salām Allāh ʿalayhim, wa-jald man jaladūhu wa-ḥasb man ḥasabūhu, bi-mā amara Allāh Taʿālā bihi`. And... perhaps a speaker says... Perhaps a speaker says... Perhaps a speaker says... the killing of the Imams... the killing of the *maqāmāt*... among them, those whom... those whom they killed... whom they killed... Allah's... And... and whipping those whom they whipped... and... those whom the Imams whipped... And... stoning those whom they stoned... And... stoning whom they stoned... With the command of Allah... that which Allah commanded... that which Allah Ta'ala commanded. `man naṭaqa bihi kitābuhu al-karīm fī kathīrin min āyātihi, wa-ṣudūr anābiya min rasūlihi, wa-kāffat aʾimmat dīnihi, fa-lima wajaba fīhi al-qiṣāṣ, wa-usqiṭa ʿan al-nikāḥ maʿa kawnihī Taʿālā lā yughādiru ṣaghīratan wa-lā kabīratan illā aḥṣāhā`. And the pronouncement... of that matter... by the Prophet and... Then why was retribution obligatory in it? Then why was retribution obligatory in it? And it was dropped from marriage... it was dropped from marriage... despite His being such that He does not leave a small thing nor a big thing but enumerates it. Marriage means the one which... the marriage that is... the companionship which happens... in it... marriage which is... it happens with mutual consent... It is with consent. Sir, the punishment for *zinā* (adultery), which is that they stone them with rocks... So, now it's like, the evil that was done, it was between two people. But the ones who are stoning are from all sides. So this retribution, is it distributed among all of them? Or are all of them taking its recompense? How is it that the punishment is to be carried out on the person who committed the sin, but everyone is stoning him? By the command of Allah. By the command of Allah, because from it, collective harms are created. *Zinā* is such an act. From it, only shamelessness, collective harms are created. To remove those collective harms, this act is enforced. Although it is an act of two individuals. Yes. It's an act of two individuals. To remove the collective harms, so that such evils do not arise in the community, this command has been established by Allah Ta'ala. And it's not just in Islam, in every religion, this was the command. Among the Jews, among the Christians, among everyone. Then why was retribution obligatory in it? Meaning, it is a command of Allah, the battles that are fought, people are killed in them, on the command of someone... the incident of Mawla Ali, *ʿalayhi al-ṣalāt wal-salām*, has been narrated that in his battle... in the battle of Jamal, when he was going... the armies... جنابِ امو were moving forward, and a pregnant woman was there. She... at the door, she was sitting. As soon as the armies arrived there... they arrived. So from the stamping of the armies' hooves... the stamping of the hooves... she got worried and gave birth to a child. And the child died. Now, people came... her tribe came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn, and said that this woman died like this, and her blood money should be given. So, the blood money was taken. The case was presented. They said that it was a confrontation, so who will give the blood money for it? Amīr al-Muʾminīn said that it should be given from the public treasury. The blood money should be given from the public treasury. Then he asked, "First tell me this, did the mother die first or the child?" In the account of inheritance, to decide the matter of inheritance. What difference does it make? The ratio... then on the child... His heirs will get it. The mother's heirs will get it. And if the child died, then the child's heirs will be the heirs of his father. The mother is from another family, her... is different. The child is different, so his family, brothers, his mother, his father... the mother's father, brother... the mother gets it. And in the case of the child, then it will revert to the mother's side. So, there are ways to it, for its heirs. Then why was retribution obligatory in it, and it was dropped from marriage, with His being... `lā yughādiru ṣaghīratan wa-lā kabīratan illā aḥṣāhā` (He leaves behind neither a small nor a large thing but has enumerated it). Because Allah Ta'ala does not leave a small or a big thing, except that He enumerates it, He counts it. `Wa-qawl Rasūl Allāh... Wa-qawl Rasūl Allāh ṣalawāt Allāh ʿalayhi: mā yuṣību aḥadakum khadshat ʿūdin wa-lā ikhtilāj ʿirqin wa-lā nakbat qadamin illā bi-dhanbin, wa-mā yaʿfū Allāh ʿanhu akthar`. And the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him. It is stated that it does not afflict any one of you... a scratch... a scratch, meaning a prick... of a twig... a prick of a twig does not happen, and not the throbbing of a vein, and not the stumbling of a foot... and not the stumbling of a foot... except due to a sin. Except due to a sin. And what Allah forgives is much more. The sin has a connection with that twig, with that vein, or with the stumbling of the foot... the thing that comes in the foot, from that... `illā bi-dhanbin`. Meaning, these are previous retributions... retributions are being applied. And what Allah forgives is much more. Sins happen, which are forgiven. Sir, will the retribution of the era of concealment be received in the era of concealment, or can it be received in the era of manifestation? When the manifestations of both happen, from which it happened. The manifestations will happen, with that... But this is that... its... the supplications... in the narration of the supplication, what is narrated? In the virtues of supplication, it is narrated that... human beings... in the world, they make many supplications. And their supplications... are not accepted. So, on the Day of Judgment, when he is presented, and in his scale, some good deeds will be placed, so he will say that I did not do these good deeds, were they placed in my scale by mistake? Then he will be told that you made these supplications, and they were not accepted in the world, this is the reward for that. Then he will say, "I wish none of my supplications were accepted in the world." So that all this reward would be for me on the Day of Judgment. This is what Sayyidna Saheb Muqaddas liked this saying. And he said in the virtues of... Sayyidna Ghulam Husayn Saheb's book, there is a book. I saw it in Tayyib Musharraf. You see it. And... I left the book, I will see it. For three days, your mind was on it. Then he said, "The supplication... the virtues of supplication, you write it in a book... write it in a book." Then he asked, "Have you written it?" I said, "Yes." He said, "Tell me." Then I told him. He said, "Now print it." He said, "This is a special... virtue." Then he, with his own hand, in the book, he wrote it. Sayyidna Tayyib's name. When I was with Sayyidna Saheb Muqaddas, in his last days... and the pillow was also kept on the side... and the prayer rug was laid out... and the prayer call was given, you woke up. And... a pillow of cotton was kept... and... reading the book, "Read it to me." I read four or five lines. In it, there was a writing, it had to be changed. And he wrote it with a pen. He said, "It is good that you have come." That a person... makes a sacrifice. With the intention for a sick person. And the sacrifice... and still he passes away. So will he get the benefit of that sacrifice? So in it, it was answered that yes, indeed he will get the benefit. If it has not reached in this cycle, then in the next cycle, he will be given a multiplied reward. A multiplied reward will be given. What a good thing he said. What a good thing. `wa-mā yaʿfū Allāh ʿanhu akthar`. And that which is forgiven is much more. `fa-li-yaʿlam anna taslīm al-rajul mā yuslimu lil-marʾah min ḥāḍirin wa-mahrin wa-qabḍin wa-tarāḍin baynahumā maʿa iḥlāl al-sharīʿah lahu, law qad amāta ʿanhu ḥaqq al-qiṣāṣ fī dhālik`. So... so let him know... So let it be known that a man's delivering what he delivers to the woman of the present gift and dower, and taking possession, and mutual consent between them, along with the *sharīʿah* making it permissible, if he has died, the right of retribution in that matter has been nullified for him. Meaning, when it is done with consent, where is the question of retribution? When it is... done with consent. Like the things... from the goods, and the houses, and the lands, and the clothes, and other than that, when there is mutual consent in it, with buying and selling for a known price, retribution is not counted in it. With mutual consent... it happens in trade. But with it, the permissibility of the *sharīʿah* should also be there. *Zinā* can also be with mutual consent. Retribution is counted in that. It is made permissible by the *sharīʿah*, and it is with mutual consent. The other thing being said is about trade. `wa-law sallama alladhī sallama min ḥāḍirin wa-mahrin bi-ghayr iḥlāl al-sharīʿah lahu, la-lazima fīhi al-qiṣāṣ`. And if he were to deliver what he delivered of the present gift and dower without the *sharīʿah* making it permissible for him, retribution would be necessary in it. This `min ḥāḍirin`... `min ḥāḍirin wa-mahrin`. A present gift... A present gift, meaning some present things are given. The dower is... says that I will give it later. What do the common people do now? They get the dower forgiven before death. What do you do? She says, "I have forgiven the dower." `wa-law waṭiʾahā maʿa taḥrīm al-sharīʿah min ghayr dhālika bi-ghayr an yusallima lahā shayʾan min ḥāḍirin wa-mahrin, la-wajaba fīhi al-qiṣāṣ`. And if... if he had intercourse with her... despite the prohibition of the *sharīʿah* without that... without delivering to her any thing of present gift and dower, retribution would be obligatory in it. Meaning, the senior elders state this. A present dower. Meaning, there should be the permissibility of the *sharīʿah*, and if the dower is not given, then the retribution is on him. `kamā wajaba al-qiṣāṣ ʿalā al-maqāmāt fī afʿālihim hādhihi al-madhkūrah`. Just as retribution became obligatory upon the *Maqāmāt* in these aforementioned actions of theirs. Meaning, it is not necessary that the deeds done by the Imams were in this same cycle. It is possible that they were in a previous cycle, and along with that, retribution was taken in this cycle. As it is said in the narration of Mawla Ali that in his time, especially it is stated that Imam Husayn had to give its recompense. So in the same era it can happen, and in a previous era it can also happen. It can happen in a previous era. Here it is stated that in mutual dealings, the good deeds that are there, those are also settled. What example was given? That... it is stated that Mawla Ali... in it, it is stated that `khadam al-mawlā ʿabdahu` (the master served his slave). `khadam al-mawlā ʿabdahu`. The master served his slave. What did the master do? He served his slave. In the accounts of Sayyidna Badruddin Saheb Muqaddas, it is narrated that one time, he woke up for prayer, so... that gardener, what was his name, I forgot. So, he had served you at night. So in the morning when he woke up, he started pressing his feet. And he woke him up. He said, "Mawla, you are pressing, you are pressing." He said, "You served me at night, I served you during the day." Thus, `khadam al-mawlā ʿabdahu` has a special chapter in it. What is the chapter? The previous prophets, they served whom? The Imams were hidden, they were in concealment. And the prophets and the messengers served them. They faced hardships, were whipped, all these things, they bore hardships, were killed, were given poison. They remained hidden. So when the time came, the time of the Prophet, *ʿalayhi al-ṣalāt wal-salām*, all the prophets gathered there with you. So who served? Who was the representative of the hidden ones? It was Mawla Ali Murtada, *ʿalayhi al-ṣalāt wal-salām*. He served the Prophet. And all the retributions were settled. So these were the recompenses. Meaning, retributions don't just happen in evil things. The giving and taking is in both good and evil. He settled all those. When he called out in difficulty, the prophets called out to Ali. When he called out in difficulty, the prophets called out to Ali. `kamā wajaba al-qiṣāṣ ʿalā al-maqāmāt fī afʿālihim hādhihi al-madhkūrah`. Just as retribution became obligatory upon these Imams in their actions... despite the permissibility of the *sharīʿah* for them in that matter... in that matter. Although the *sharīʿah* has made it permissible. In a battle, you went. In a battle, what? Does the sword stop? Sometimes the horse runs, it runs over women. What to do? It's not possible to stop it. Then its recompense has to be given. `wa-amara Allāh Taʿālā bihi fī hādhihi al-ashyāʾ allatī dhakarnāhā min qatlin wa-jaldin wa-ḥasbin, lammā lam yaqaʿ bihā riḍan min al-maqtūl wa-lā sullima lahu qīmatuhu fī dhālik, maʿa iḥlāl al-sharīʿah lahā`. Your question's answer has come. And Allah's command in that matter is that these things, as we have mentioned, of killing and whipping and stoning, when it does not happen... with the consent of the one who is killed, and his value is not delivered to him in that matter, along with the *sharīʿah* making it permissible for it. Sir, are you raising all the questions or is Sayyidna Abdullah Hamid raising them? He is answering all the questions. Sayyidna Saheb said that all the questions you have asked are already present in the books. We don't know. All the questions that were asked are in the books. The answers have been given. We don't know, we haven't read them, so we... it doesn't encompass us. And Allah's command in that matter is that these things, as we have mentioned, which are from killing, and whipping, and stoning... when it does not happen with the consent of the one killed... the consent of the one on whom the action was done... The one on whom the action was done... He is a criminal... He has done a wrong act, people are stoning him. He is not consenting to being stoned. His... the retribution has to be given. And his value is not delivered... Meaning, the people who are stoning him, between them also some retribution will take place. Yes, that can also happen. Is that what you mean to say? Yes. That retribution can happen. And his value is not delivered in that matter... and his value is not delivered in that matter. Meaning, you... I will give the value, and you let me stone you. That doesn't happen. `maʿa iḥlāl al-sharīʿah lahā`. With the *sharīʿah* making it permissible for it... with the *sharīʿah* making the action permissible. The *sharīʿah* has made it permissible. But since there is no mutual consent, therefore, its retribution is obligatory. Or the one taking the retribution is taking it, or he is giving it. This is what is stated. Meaning, with the permissibility of the *sharīʿah*... The *sharīʿah* has made it permissible. The *sharīʿah* has gathered everyone and said, "The *sharīʿah* commands to stone." The one who has committed adultery, stone him. The *sharīʿah* has made it permissible. But is the person consenting? That is why in this case, whether it is from before, or it is for the future that he has to give. This is in the power of God. And for that reason, retribution was incumbent... So if it is not from before, and he is stoning him, then in the future, he will have to give... `wa-li-dhālika waqaʿa ʿalayhim al-qiṣāṣ bi-qiṣāṣ al-maqāmāt`. And for this reason, retribution was incumbent upon him for the retribution of the *maqāmāt*. The *maqāmāt* didn't escape either, so what can an ordinary person do? `ṣalawāt Allāh ʿalayhim ajmaʿīn`. May the peace and blessings of God be upon him. Now until we... when the eyelid blinks, then that also is retribution. Between it and that twig. It is retribution. And what was that twig? That was also a soul. A soul. It was a soul. It took the form of a twig. It had to give and take. That's what happened. `Bismillāh al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm`.

<!-- lecture 58 -->

`kalam al-la-ilaha` for the ignorant... negative and positive. What is negative and what is positive? In the sense of three, four, seven, twelve, what is it? A point (`nuqta`). With a dot and without a dot. Which are the letters with dots? One is `yā`. Both have them. And what is the other one called? `ʿAyn` and `ghayn`. A very fine `mawlā` has said in a `sharh`: `ʿayn`. He has composed a poem about it. `ʿAyn`.

“*Wajh-i is `ʿayn` ki munh khulne ki tujh se keh dun, kufr-i kafir ko yeh chahta hai ke ek dam niglun.*”
(Let me tell you the reason for this `ʿayn`'s open mouth, it wants to swallow the disbelief of the disbeliever in one gulp). Wow.

Meaning, the mouth of the `ʿayn` is open. What is it? Someone has said another verse that is also very good.
“*Wajh-i is `ʿayn` ki munh khulne ki tujh se keh dun, kufr-i kafir ko yeh chahta hai ke ek dam niglun.*”
(Let me tell you the reason for this `ʿayn`'s open mouth, it wants to swallow the disbelief of the disbeliever in one gulp).
And... there is more in this regard.

In this, that which is there, is concerning the `ʿayn`. Okay, two... this negative-positive. What are the three in this? There is `ʿayn`, `lām`, `yā`. `ʿAyn`, `lām`, `yā` are the three letters. And what are the four?

`Lām` and `yā` have forty. `Lām` has thirty and `yā` has ten. How many is that? Forty. And what are the seven? The seven are... seven are for `ʿayn`, seventy. Only `ʿayn` has seventy. And what are the twelve? The twelve are... `yā` and `nūn`. `ʿAyn`'s... the `yā` of `ʿayn`'s `nūn`, `lām`'s `alif` and `mīm`, and `yā`'s `alif` - five. Five and these seven, together make twelve. Twelve. That's how it is. It has been combined in several ways.

Now, here, that which is in this book... The video you saw, in the `majlis` of Sayyidna Hatim, there it was mentioned, what is the connection? The `maddat` of Sayyidna Hatim... the date of his birth, the date of his passing, Sayyidna Hatim. There, the `mawa'iz` of Mawla Ali, we have the 76th `majlis`. We have it from there. Before that, we don't have the `majalis`. From 77... there are one hundred `majalis`. From the 77th `majlis` onwards. The `majalis` before that, where are they? It was Mukhtar Muzni who came; we sent a message to him. They are available in Yemen, if you can send them... So that they can be published. The `majalis` before that... The seventy-seventh one becomes complete there.

In this... In this, it is mentioned that in Janab-i Ali, there were seventy such special characteristics (`khususiyat`) that could not be combined in any other person. Seventy special characteristics were such that they could not be combined in anyone. People... it was surveyed. A summary of it... this is this, a summary of it... this... in... so in any person, more than ten special characteristics could not be combined. Someone has two, someone has three, someone... more than ten special characteristics could not be combined in anyone. And a special characteristic is one to which Allah and His Rasul have given testimony. That is a special characteristic. In Ali, seventy special characteristics were combined. It has been enumerated in it. And its examples have also been given.

A `khutba` (sermon) was given by Janab-i Ali, `salam Allah 'alayh`. People came to you. And by chance, they were mutually discussing... Arab people, among themselves, which letter in the Arabic language comes the most? Everyone agreed that `alif` comes. `Alif` comes. The letter `alif` comes the most. So, they said that no speech is possible without `alif`. And Mawlay-i Ka'inat arrived there and gave a `khutba`, approximately a three-page `khutba`, in which `alif` is not present. Extempore. The `khutba`... it is mentioned in the first book. The first book... It is also in *Nahj al-Balagha*. And it is also in this book. A three-page `khutba` was given by you, in which `alif` is not present. And that too extempore. Extempore means what? `Fil-badīh`. It is called `murtajjal` in Arabic. `Murtajjal`. `Fil-badīh`. In Urdu, we say `fil-badīh`.

And in this, a `khutba` has been given by Janab-i Ali, `salam Allah 'alayh`. A `khutba` has been given. In it, there are no dots (`nuqta`). A thirteen-page... that is approximately a thirteen-page `khutba` which you have given, in which no dot is present.

And the seventy special characteristics, that is especially... He said that Umar sahib said, "`Lawla `Alī lahalaka `Umar`" (Were it not for Ali, Umar would have been destroyed). After compiling, it was found that he said this seventy times.

`al-Fasl al-thalith min bab al-rabi' min suradiq al-rabi'.`
(The third section from the fourth chapter of the fourth pavilion.)
The third section from the fourth chapter, from the fourth `suradiq`.
`Ma inna af'al al-maqamat wa awliya'ihim 'alayhim al-salam allati fa'aluha min mujahadat al-azdad wa qatli man qutila minhum wa haddi man haddawhu min al-umam wa hasbi man wajaba 'alayhim al-hasab.`
`Wa hasbi man wajaba 'alayhim al-hasab 'a'idun ajruhu 'ala hayakilhim al-nuraniyya wa 'ala nufusihim man qadamuhum li-dhalik min awliya'ihim, mujawhirin li-dhawatihim, mu'allin li-darajatihim wa maratibihim fi dar al-safa wa l-mahal al-mu'alla.`

And along with... he is connecting it with the previous statement. And along with it, this matter is also there, that the deeds of the Imams and their `awliya'`, peace be upon them, such as what they did, those actions, from engaging in `jihad` against their opposites (`azdad`) and killing those who were killed among them, and applying the `hadd` (prescribed punishment) on those upon whom they applied the `hadd` from the communities, and stoning (`kankariyan marna`) those upon whom stoning became obligatory... the reward of it returns to their luminous structures (`hayakil nuraniyya`) and upon the souls of those who they sent ahead for that from among their `awliya'`. This Arabic phraseology... its connections need to be understood. `Ala hayakil`, on their `hayakil nuraniyya`... In whose connection is this?

Meaning, this `qisas` remains in its place, but the reward will also be given. For acting upon the command of Allah, the command of the Rasul, the command of their `Uli l-Amr`, what they have killed, the `jihad` they have done, and applied the `hadd` - by their command they have applied the `hadd`, or stoned them, its reward also remains. The command is that when someone is being killed for fornication, then a group of Muslims should be present, to see everyone. Why was this commanded? So that in the future, no person would commit this. Its... he would not commit it. For this reason, this was established. The one who kills, he kills, but he does not kill out of personal enmity (`tarazi`). Both things are there. But he is killing by command. By Allah's command, he is killing. Allah, Who created him, Who is the Giver of life, by His command he is killing. So its reward remains with him. Both things are there, he is saying. How delicate a relationship this is, of `qisas`. By acting upon the `shari'at`, it is also `qisas`. `Qisas`. `A'idun ajruhu` (its reward returns). But with `qisas`, since the `qisas` is of the people of `ahl`, or in the future, a new `qisas` will happen, that is with the `mudabbir`. But along with it, its reward is very great. Because he is carrying out a command, and he is trying to eliminate impurity from the world. For this reason... `A'idun`, returning is its reward. Whose reward? What is the `pronominal suffix` returning to? To the implementation... the deed... the killing, the stoning... `A'idun ajruhu` (its reward returns)... The reward for the communities? `A'idun ajruhu`, its reward is returning. Whose reward? The reward of the one who did it. `A'idun ajruhu`. Upon... The `ummat` (community)? No... Towards the Imam. That which he has done... Who are the `maqamat` and `awliya'`? `Ma inna af'al al-maqamat`... `min mujahadat al-azdad wa qutila man qutila minhum wa haddi man haddawhu min al-umam...` This whole matter is being taken. The entire work is being taken. This `amr` (matter)... `amr` is its... `A'idun ajruhu`, the reward of that deed is returning to their luminous structures (`hayakil nuraniyya`). And upon the souls, and upon the souls of those who they sent ahead for that from among their `awliya'`. `Mujawhirin li-dhawatihim` (polishing their essences). Polishing is... their essences. `Mu'allin li-darajatihim` (elevating their ranks). Elevating their ranks and their stations (`maratib`) in the Abode of Purity (`dar al-safa`) and the elevated place (`mahal al-mu'alla`). So this is only about the Imam and Hudud.

`Li-anna tilka l-af'al allati fa'aluha tarhamu l-nafs...` To kill is not a good deed. To take someone's life is not a good deed. But, in one's own self-defense (`dafa'-i hifazat`), in one's protection. Someone came to kill you, what will you do? You will kill. The act of killing happened from you, but in defense of your own self, in the protection of your life. Or by the command of Allah Ta'ala and His Rasul or the `Uli l-Amr`. Its reward remains. But its `qisas` also remains.

`Li-anna tilka l-af'al allati fa'aluha talaban li-thawab Allah Ta'ala wa amrihi bi-dhalika tabaraka wa ta'ala wa ihlal al-shari'at lahu lam yakun ajruhu bi-dha'i'in bal 'alayhi al-qisas al-awfa.`
(Because those deeds that they did, seeking the reward of Allah Ta'ala and by His command for that, Blessed and Exalted is He, and to establish the shari'at for him, its reward was not lost, but upon him is the fullest requital.)
Because those deeds that they did, seeking the reward of Allah Ta'ala and along with being commanded by Him for that, Blessed and Exalted is He, and to establish the `shari'at` for him, its reward will not be lost. Rather, upon it is the fullest requital.

`Wa kana qisasuhum 'ala kathayifihim salam Allah 'alayhim bi-amr Allah Ta'ala bihi wa ihlal al-shari'at lahu li-karahiyat nufus al-azdad bima fu'ila biha wa qillat rada'ihim bihi...`
(And their qisas was upon their dense bodies, salam Allah 'alayhim, by the command of Allah Ta'ala for it and for the establishment of the shari'at for him, due to the aversion of the souls of the opposites to what was done to it and their lack of pleasure in it...)
It has been clarified. And their `qisas` will be upon their `katha'if` (dense bodies), upon their `katha'if` that have remained. Their `qisas`... In their forms, the progress that has been hindered, their `ajsam`... `qisas` remains. `Salam Allah 'alayhim`, by the command of Allah Ta'ala, along with the command of Allah, from Him, and to establish the `shari'at`, because of the aversion of the souls of the opposites (`nufus al-azdad`), because of the aversion of the souls of the opposites, and because of what was done to them, and the lack of their pleasure in it. They did not do it with their own pleasure. They were attacked (`hamla kiya gaya`), they were expelled (`nikal diya gaya`), an attack was made upon them, this was done. So, this which is done in defense (`mudafa'at`), then that is a different matter. Or if they themselves bring an army and cause bloodshed (`jang-o-jadal`), then that is a different matter.

`Li-anna mizan al-'adl qa'imun min Allah Ta'ala...` Up to here, Mawla Amir al-Mu'minin, what incident did he narrate? Meaning, you... a woman's death occurred. So what did you do? From where did you give the `diyat` (blood money)? From the `bayt al-mal` (public treasury), you gave her `diyat`. That the horses of the `bayt al-mal` galloped, the horses of the Muslims galloped, due to that, her death occurred. And she... was not guilty in that, there was nothing of hers to do with it. You gave `diyat` for it. But along with the `diyat`, what did you do? You gave blood money, but along with it, what did you do? What did you ask? "Whose death occurred first?" What difference does it make whose death occurred first? `Wirathat` (inheritance). What difference does it make to the inheritance? Either from the mother's side or the son's... Who are the heirs of the mother? Her children. Her... if she has only one child, if only one child is counted, is the child an heir or not? When does the child become an heir? If the child's death occurs before the mother's, then the child is not an heir. If the child remained alive afterwards, then the child becomes the mother's heir. And who are the mother's other heirs? If she has a husband. Who gets the inheritance first? Who are the rightful heirs of inheritance? First of all... when does the law of inheritance arise? What a person gives in their lifetime is a `hiba` (gift). When does the point of inheritance arise? At the time of death. At the time of death. And this is the command, that if a person gives a gift, if he does so in his terminal illness (`marad al-mawt`), then there is no consideration for it. Whatever gift you have to give, you must do it before the terminal illness. This has been especially commanded. So `hiba`, that which is there, is that he should give it to him. But even in that, what is the condition? Possession should be given to him. `Hiba` is, possession should be given to him. If possession is not given, it is in his own possession, he just wrote that it is a `hiba`, then that is not... it is not accepted. It is the law. So, now this... who are the first heirs in inheritance? The parents. First of all, a person's heirs are his parents, if they are alive. How much share do they get? One-sixth. 1/6th share. The mother, and the father gets 1/6th share. After that, who are the heirs? The husband and wife. The husband's... for the wife, the wife's for the husband. If there are children, then how much is it? And if there are no children, then... according to that. What is the wife's right? It has two aspects. An eighth part. And the husband's part is a fourth part. What did they say... Janab Abdullah ibn Abbas?

"`Laka l-thumunu min al-'ushri wa li-l-kulli tamallakti.`"
(For you is an eighth of a tenth, and of the whole you have taken possession.)
What does it mean? `Thumun` means an eighth part.
"`Laka l-thumunu min al-'ushri.`"
(For you is an eighth of a tenth.)
If you are claimants to the house of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in which you used to live, then at the time of the Prophet's passing, he had ten wives. And how much share was there? `Thumun`, an eighth part. It was the share of all ten wives. An eighth. "`Laka l-thumunu min al-'ushri`" (for you is an eighth of a tenth). The house that was there... and the rest was whose share? Janab-i Fatima's. It goes towards the children. "`Laka l-thumunu min al-'ushri, wa li-l-kulli tamallakti.`" (For you is an eighth of a tenth, and of the whole you have taken possession). You have seized it by force.

When did you say this? When... When did he say this? When Imam Hasan was... they were shooting arrows. He was not being allowed to be buried. Imam Hasan, `alayhi al-salat wa l-salam`, was not being allowed to be buried near the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. They instigated. The Banu Umayya. And the Banu Umayya... shot arrows, with the command of Hakam ibn al-As. And they said that I will not allow burial next to the Prophet, Imam Hasan, `alayhi al-salat wa l-salam`. At that time, Janab Abdullah ibn Abbas said this.

So this is the mention... The mention of inheritance was coming up. What happens in inheritance? A very wise point was said by Mawla during the `wa'z`. That if the wife... if the mother passed away first, then what will happen? The child will be the heir. And the child's heirs will... The child's heirs will be... who will be his heirs first? The child's parents. The mother has passed away. During the child's lifetime. How complicated a matter it has become. The mother will not get it. During the child's lifetime, the mother passed away, the mother will not get it. And the father will get it... the father is not present... we don't know if he is present or not. And after that, who will get it? The child's brothers and sisters will get it. If he doesn't have children. He is a child, he doesn't have a wife, nor... Now all of it will go to his brothers. To the brothers and sisters. To his paternal uncle, it will go. To the paternal uncle's children, brothers and sisters, to the paternal uncle...

And if the mother... if the mother is present and the child has passed away, then the child will get nothing. And the mother's relatives, all of them... The mother's father and mother are there, they will get it. What a difference it has made, with the sequence. The mother's father and mother will get it. If the mother has a husband, he will get it. If she has children, other children, they will get it. In this way.

`Li-anna mizan al-'adl qa'imun min Allah Ta'ala fi l-qitmiri wa l-naqir.`
(Because the scale of justice is established from Allah Ta'ala in the `qitmir` and the `naqir`.)
And because the scale of justice is established, from Allah Ta'ala, in the `qitmir` (membrane on a date-stone) and `naqir` (groove on a date-stone) also. This... in the date-palm... in the date, it is called... the `naqir`... The groove in the date-stone is called... `qitmir`... The membrane of the date-stone is what is written... `naqir` is what they call the... the hole in the date-stone... `qitmir`... `qitmir` is what is written... `naqir` is what they call the... the hole in the date-stone.

`Wa li-qa'ilin an yaqul, faqad 'alimna anna kathiran min al-maqamat wa l-hudud 'alayhim al-salam jahadu al-azdad wa qatalu minhum man qatalu wa haddu man haddu wa hasabu man hasabu thumma intaqalu ila dar karamat Allah Ta'ala min ghayri qatlin wa la sammin kama asaba dhalik...`
(And for a sayer to say, 'We have known that many of the Maqamat and Hudud, peace be upon them, fought against the opposites, and killed among them whom they killed, and applied the hadd on whom they applied the hadd, and stoned whom they stoned, then they passed away to the abode of Allah's generosity without being killed or poisoned, as befell that...')
And for a saying person, that he says... For a saying person to say this, that he says... "We have known that many of the `maqamat` and `hudud`, peace be upon them, engaged in `jihad` against the opposites (`azdad`), and killed among them whom they killed, and applied the `hadd` on whom they applied the `hadd`, and stoned whom they stoned. Then they passed away, to the abode of Allah Ta'ala's generosity, without being killed, and without poison, and not like that... so what is its reason? What is its reason?"

`Fa-l-ya'lam inna af'al tilka l-salawat Allah 'alayhim fi azdadihim wa 'ala adwarihim ikhtisasun minhum bi-hasbi ma taqaddama min af'alihim fihim fi adwar salafat wa 'asur taqaddamat.`
(So let him know that the actions of those, salutations of Allah be upon them, against their opposites and in their cycles, is a taking of qisas from them according to what preceded of their actions in them in past cycles and ages that have preceded.)
So he should know... So he should know that the deeds of them, `salawat Allah 'alayhim` (salutations of Allah be upon them), those... the `hudud`... those `awliya'` of Allah. Against their opposites (`azdad`), and in their cycles and their times, is taking `qisas` from them. They are taking `qisas`... `qisas` is being taken, `qisas` is being done... by virtue of what preceded of their deeds in them, in cycles that have passed and times that have passed. So he should know.

This `qisas` that is there... the original word for `qisas` is `qassa`. `Qaf`, `sad`, `sad`. `Qassa`. From it, `iqtisas`, to take `qisas`; `ikhtisas`, it has become a `lazim` verb (intransitive). And to take `qisas` is what they call `aqassa`. "He took `qisas`." `Aqassa`. And `ikhtisas` means... This is... There are seventeen forms of verbs (`abwab`). `abwab-i mazid`. With their coming, the meaning changes. To take, and to give. Mutual taking. What is mutual taking of `qisas` called? `Muqasasa`. It comes from `bab mufa'ala`. `Muqasasa`.

`Qisas` is to be taken from them, according to that which they had done in previous cycles, and in times that have passed.

`Fa-awjabat 'inayat al-ilahiyya ijtima'ahum fi zaman hadha l-maqamat wa l-hudud li-yakuna minhum lahum al-qisas 'amma salafa 'adlan min Allah Ta'ala wa iqamatan li-ma fa'aluhu min al-ma'asi.`
(So the divine providence necessitated their gathering in the time of these Maqamat and Hudud, so that there may be from them, for them, the qisas for what has passed, as justice from Allah Ta'ala and an establishment for what they did of sins.)
The meaning of `ijtima'` will be what? To gather. From `bab ifti'al`. Its meaning is 'to be'. To gather. And the meaning of 'to gather' is what? `Ajma'a`. From that comes `ijma'`. `Ajma'a`, he gathered. `Ijtima'`, he was gathered. `Ijtama'`, he was gathered. The difference in meaning is there.
Their gathering in the time of these `maqamat` and `hudud`, so that there may be from them, for them, `qisas`, for what they did previously, as justice from Allah Ta'ala, and to establish requital for the sins they committed.

`Wa subhana man la ya'zubu 'anhu mithqalu dharratin illa ahsaha, wa wajadu ma 'amilu hadiran, wa la yazlimu rabbuka ahada.`
(And glory be to Him from Whom not an atom's weight is hidden but that He has enumerated it. And they found what they did present, and your Lord does not wrong anyone.)
This is an verse from the Holy Quran. `Wa wajadu ma 'amilu hadiran wa la yazlimu rabbuka ahada`. It is `yazlimu`, is it `yazlimu`... `wa la yazlimu rabbuka ahada`.
So, glory be to God, from Whom not an atom's weight is hidden, except that He has enumerated it. And they found what they did present, and your Lord does not wrong anyone. `Ahadan`. Why did `ahada` come here? And why did `zabar` (accusative marker) come? Why did `pesh` (nominative marker) come? `Rabbuka`. `Ahada` is the... `maf'ul` (object). What did Mawla Amir al-Mu'minin compose? He composed that: "`Kullu fa'ilin marfu'un.`" (Every doer is in the nominative case). Remember this. "`Kullu fa'ilin marfu'un.`" Every `fa'il` (doer) has what? `Pesh` (nominative). It is raised. `Wa la yazlimu rabbuka`. What is `rabbuka`? It is the `fa'il`. Who does not do injustice? Your Lord. `Fa'il`. `Rabbuka`. `Ahadan`. What is this? It is the `maf'ul` (object). "`Kullu maf'ulin mansubun.`" (Every object is in the accusative case). Every `maf'ul` has what? It is given `nasb` (`zabar`). And "`wa kullu majrurin maksurun`" (and every object of a preposition is in the genitive case). And every... that which comes with a `harf-i jar` (preposition), that which has to be pulled, that which has to be pulled to move forward, what is that? It is `maksur` (broken). It has a `kasra`. What a strange state this is. What is it? Say it. Recite it. It is the speech of Amir al-Mu'minin. "`Kullu fa'ilin marfu'un.`" What does it mean? The person who moves forward, who acts, is the very first one to act, what is he? He is elevated. And after that? "`Kullu maf'ulin mansubun.`" `Maksur`. "`Kullu maf'ulin...`" The one who, upon seeing the doer, becomes like him, who tries to become like him after seeing someone who acts, he is the `maf'ul`, what is he? He is `mansub` (supported). He is given a `zabar` (support) on him. "`Wa kullu majrurin`" (and every object of a preposition)... what does it mean? The one who has to be pulled, for whom effort has to be made to bring him towards good, he is `maksur` (broken). He is given a `kasra` (break).
`Wa wajadu ma 'amilu hadiran`.
So, glory be to Him from Whom not an atom's weight is hidden, except that He has enumerated it. And they find what they did present, and your Lord does not wrong anyone.

Al-Fatiha.

<!-- lecture 59 -->

*Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*. *Fasl al-Rabi' min Bab al-Rabi'* (The Fourth Chapter of the Fourth Section), in *Sirat al-Rabi'* (The Fourth Path). The fourth chapter from the fourth section, from the fourth path. "Wa amma sa'ir al-ashya' allati taf'al..." (As for all other things that are done...). Why do we pass our hand over our face when reciting *Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*? Just as... from Allah... that... *ittisal* (connection). There is... but... five *a'la* (higher), five... Just as... that... in which way... that in the human body, there are five *a'la* (higher parts) and five *adna* (lower parts). Five... The lower ones are five. And in the lower ones, too, what is there? The ones that are lower, five and five, so there are four. In the hand... in this one too... and in the feet. From the feet, passing the hand over the face... In the *adna* (lower parts), the one that is the highest of all... The right hand is the highest of all. In the *adna*, the one that is the highest, with that, we create an *ittisal* (connection) with the highest part of the body, in the face. The one that is the highest in the body... the one that is the highest in the body... the one that is the highest in the body, near the face, we make a connection with it. From this, we take the meaning that... what meaning do we take? That similarly, the five *zawat* (essences) of the *'alam-e-nurani* (the Luminous Realm), their connection is established with the five *zawat* of the world. In the five *zawat*, whose was described in the Quran? *'Aql* (Intellect), *nafs* (soul), *jadd* (fortune), *fatah* (opening), and *khayal* (imagination). *'Alam-e-nurani*. And who is here? Imam, Bab, Hujjat... *Da'i* and *Ma'dhun*. *Da'i* and *Ma'dhun*. Imam, Bab, Hujjat... that their connection is always established with them.

So why only on *Bismillah*... why not on every *kalimah*? Yes, *Bismillah*... yes, that question was also stated along with this. The *kalimah* of *Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim* is the highest of all. It is the essence of all summaries. But higher than that, there is a *kalimah*. Which one is it? *La ilaha illallah* (There is no god but Allah). It is without dots. How many... are there? How many letters are there? 28. How many of them are dotted, and how many are without dots? Fifteen are dotted, and thirteen are without dots. Out of 15 and 28. Which are the dotted ones? Count them. Be, Te, The, Jim, Kha, Dhal, Ze, Shin, Dhad, Zhoe, after that Ghain, Fe, Qaf... Qaf is not there... Qaf. After Qaf? Nun. And then Ya. Fifteen have come. And thirteen are without dots. So, these letters that have come... in *Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*, there is... what is there? There is a repetition of five. *Khamsatun bi-iza'i khamsah* (Five in correspondence with five). Five in مقابل (comparison) to five. What is in it? Five repeated letters have come, and five non-repeated letters. The non-repeated ones are more excellent. In whose comparison are they non-repeated? The five individuals of the *'alam-e-nurani* (Luminous Realm): *'aql, nafs, jadd, fatah, khayal*. They are in comparison to it. Which ones? In *Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*, which are the non-repeated ones? Be. It has come one time. Sin. It has come one time. Mim... has come three times. Non-repeated... After that, Alif also is repeated, it has come many times. After that, Lam also has come many times. He... what is it? It is non-repeated. Nun... after that, Nun... *mukarar* (repeated) has come. What is the non-repeated one... Nun... then Ya. In *Rahim*, the Ya. How many? Five have become. Be... in each one, there is one non-repeated. A special quality. In *Bism*, Be and Sin, two are non-repeated. In Allah, He is non-repeated. In *al-Rahman*, Nun is non-repeated. Now what have they said here? The *'alam-e-jismani* (physical realm). That their connection is always established with them. Just as in *Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*, five repeated ones have come and five non-repeated ones have come, just as their connection with each other has become one single *kalimah*. In the same way, the five of the *'alam-e-nurani* (Luminous Realm) who are non-repeated, who do not have to make an appearance (*zuhur*) in the world. And the five repeated ones here, who have to make an appearance in the world again and again, their connection is always established with them. It is one single *kalimah*. Just as *Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim* is one *kalimah*, in the same way, the five from there and the five from here... their connection becomes one single *kalimah*. This is why the *ta'wil* (esoteric interpretation) we have begins with *La ilaha illallah* (There is no god but Allah). Its *ta'wil* has been stated. And after that, *Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*. *Ta'wil Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*. Sayyidna Mu'ayyad's treatise. And *La ilaha illallah* Sayyidna Mu'ayyad's... It begins with that, the *ta'wil*. Because everything is present within it.

The answer is, just as... why do we pass our hand? Just as in *Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim* there are five repeated and non-repeated, in the same way, in the human body there are five non-repeated and five repeated. And just as in *Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*, the repeated and non-repeated together became one single *kalimah*, in the same way, those of the *'alam-e-nurani* (Luminous Realm) and the physical realm, or the parts of the body, they come together to become one single body. In the same way, the map of the *'alam-e-nurani* too... the map of the *'alam-e-ruhani* (Spiritual Realm) is also like that; the *nurani* (luminous) and... in that realm, all the individuals become one. It is one *kalimah*. It is one *kalimah*. This is its answer. The *kalimah* of *Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*, the human body, and the *'alam-e-ruhani* (Spiritual Realm). All three... there is a correspondence in it.

Yes. This *kalimah*, *La ilaha illallah*, it is from God Almighty. *Nur-e-kalimah* (The light of the word). So, this *Bismillah*, whose is it from? Where did its creation... It came from the *Da'irah 'Aql-e-Awwal* (Circle of the First Intellect). From the *Da'irah 'Aql-e-Awwal*. It was revealed. All the verses of the noble Quran are from the *Da'irah Ibda'* (Circle of Origination) they have been revealed. But its entire source is *La ilaha illallah*.

*Wa amma sa'ir al-ashya' allati bihi taf'al min ghayri an tuhillaha al-shari'ah, aw ya'muru biha ahad al-maqamat aw bahdh hududihi, wa mithla qatli mayit al-insan min abna'i jinsihi, wa nahbi man yanhubuhu, wa ghadhbi man yaghdhibuhu, wa akhdhi man ya'khudhuhu zulman, wa yabtaghu ghashman. Fa-inna jawhara nafsihi yuzlimu mu'ajjalan*. And this is that all things... that they do with it... without it being made lawful by the Shari'ah, or being commanded by one of the Maqamat (stations) or any command... its author is... or it is commanded by any station or any limit, like the killing of a person from among his own kind... [unclear] to kill the person who kills the human from his own kind. What command does the Imam give? Meaning, the Imam should command the Imam... or something was done under command, or the Shari'ah made it lawful. Leaving that aside, whatever action a person does, bad deeds, like killing someone from his own kind. What is its... punishment? That is, he disobeys the *ahad al-maqamat*. And he doesn't follow the Shari'ah. No, no. The person who does some action which the Shari'ah does not make lawful, or whose command the Imam, *alayhi al-salatu wa al-salam*, does not give. Like, what? Killing. He kills one of his own kind. Or he loots whomever he loots. Or he usurps from whomever he usurps. Or takes from someone with oppression... and takes from whomever he takes, or he takes... he takes from someone with oppression. Or he seeks it through treachery. Then the essence of his soul becomes dark very quickly. *Wa yakunu tilka al-af'al hajizatan bayna nafsihi wa bayna sabil al-rushdi*. And those actions become a barrier between his soul and the path of guidance. He doesn't get the opportunity to come to the path of guidance. It becomes a barrier.

Hazrat, this... when the Imam issues a *hadd* (prescribed punishment), for instance, for killing someone, a *hadd* is issued, so after that is done, is his entire sin erased, or does some of it remain? That depends on the *qisas* (retribution) of the *Mudabbir* (the Governor), on the states of the *adwar* (cycles), on the states of the *karrat* (returns). In which *karrat* and in what way has he done it? Because in one *karrat*, the Imam has 360 *karrat*. In each *karrat*, what has he done, in what way is his... with the *Mudabbir*? It can be erased, it may not be erased. Prophet, *alayhi al-salam*. *Ma asarra man istaghfara, wa law kana sab'ina marrah*. (He has not persisted [in sin] who seeks forgiveness, even if it were seventy times a day). The person who has not persisted... is not included among those who persist. *Man istaghfara* (one who seeks forgiveness). The one who, after sinning, seeks forgiveness. *Man istaghfara*. *Wa law kana sab'ina marrah* (Even if it were seventy times). Even if it is seventy times. Why did they say seventy? Because after seventy, that's its limit. It gets included in the seventy names. *Wa law kana sab'ina marrah*. But these are not sins that are incurred with respect to other humans. A point has been stated here, that as many sins as a person commits in relation to Allah, He forgives them. But with His servants, which are alongside Him, Allah does not forgive those until that servant forgives him. Or such means are not created that its expiation comes to him, like the method of *Bitaq* was explained. *Bitaq*. Its... what is it called? Allah makes it reach him. Whomever it has to reach, He makes it reach. So that his sins are cleansed from it.

*Mukassifatun laha sa'iqatun laha ila turuq al-ghawaya, muritatun laha fi arbaq al-ma'asi, mubiqatun laha fi qaba'ih al-a'mal, da'iyatun laha ila manafi al-hudud, wa muqiyyatun laha 'an al-haqqi, muwaqqi'atun laha fi nari jahannama, allati la tarji'u laha rahmatun, mukhalladatun bi-'adhabi alim*. And the one that darkens it becomes one that drives the soul... and it drives it... that soul... towards the paths of error... driving it. It drives that soul... towards wrong paths... and it ensnares it... it ensnares that soul... in the snares of sins... it destroys it... it destroys that soul... in the evils of deeds... it invites it... it invites that soul... towards the hatred of the *hudud* (divine limits) and the enmity of the *ahl al-haqq* (people of truth), it makes it fall... it makes that soul fall into the fire of Jahannam, for which there is no hope of mercy. It remains forever in a painful torment.

What did they say... *lam yakunilladhina kafaru*. What did they say? *Lam yakunilladhina kafaru min ahl al-kitabi wal-mushrikina fi nari jahannama khalidina fiha*. (Those who disbelieved from the People of the Book and the polytheists will be in the Fire of Hell, abiding therein). *Abada* (forever) is not there. *Khalidina fiha*. *Ula'ika hum sharrul bariyyah*. (Those are the worst of creatures). *Wal-ladhina amanu wa 'amilus salihat*. (And those who believed and did righteous deeds). What did they say for them? *Ula'ika hum khayrul bariyyah*. (Those are the best of creatures). *Jaza'uhum 'inda rabbihim jannatu 'adnin tajri min tahtihal anharu khalidina fiha abada*. (Their reward with their Lord is gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever). The good people, for them is paradise, and in it, there is eternality. And here what is there? There is Jahannam, but *abada* is not there. This is a mercy from Allah.

*Wa la manasa laha ba'da dhalika min qisasin 'alayha wa la 'ala jismiha jami'a*. And there is no escape for that soul after that from the *qisas* (retribution) upon it and upon its body entirely. May Allah protect us and save us from the paths of destruction, by the right of Muhammad and his pure progeny, *salawatullah 'alayhim ajma'in*. May Allah protect us and save us from the paths of destruction. By the right of Sayyidna Muhammad and his pure progeny.

*Al-Fasl al-Khamis min Bab al-Rabi' min Sirat al-Rabi'*. The fifth chapter from the fourth section, from the fourth path. *Wa kadhalika af'aluha al-qabihah mithla al-zina, wa ma shakalahu. Fa-la budda min al-qisasi 'alayhi ma'a zulam jawhar al-nafs wa takassufiha wa-inhidariha 'ala ma sabaqa min al-qawl*. And similarly, vile and lewd acts, like *zina* (adultery/fornication) and what is similar to it, then *qisas* (retribution) is necessary upon it. What does *la budda* mean? *Budda* means a way out. *La budda* means there is no way out. There is no way out from *qisas*. It will surely happen. Its translation is usually done as "surely". Along with the darkening of the soul's essence, and its eclipse, and its descent, as was stated before.

*Hatta yakunu al-qisasu mu'ajjalan fi Qamis al-Riss alladhi huwa qamis al-bashar al-munhadira*. To the extent that the *qisas* happens quickly in the *Qamis al-Riss*, which is the *qamis* (form/garment) of the descending human. Which is the *Qamis al-Riss*? The first one? *Ra-'ufunnar*. *Riss*. After that, *waqas*. After that, *'aks*. *Ra-'uf*. After that, *khars*. After that, Nun? *Najis*. Then the second Nun? *Naks*. And the final Re? *Raks*. *Raks*. *Ra-'ufunnar*. *Raks*. So the first one that is, what is it? Human form. Its... human form. The first. After that, what is the second one? Animal-like... human-like? Monkey. Monkey. And then what is there? Tearing... After that, from the sea. Then, fourth, plant. After that, upon becoming soulless, what is it? Mineral. After the mineral, what? The seven stages have to be passed through. So, in this first stage itself, its *qisas* gets completed. *Kabair* (major sins)... human *kabair*.

*Wa rubbama baqiya minhu shay'un fi Qamis al-Waqs*. And sometimes a part of it remains for the *Qamis al-Waqs*. *Wa huwa al-tarkib al-mathil lil-bashar alladhi huwa al-qirdu wal-nasnasu wal-adaru wal-'adabu wa ashbahu dhalik, alladhina aktharu af'alihim...* And sometimes a thing remains from it in the *Qamis al-Waqs*, and it is the composition similar to a human, which is the monkey and the *nasnas* and the *adar* and the *'adab* and what is similar to that, whose actions are mostly... What have they written after that? *Nasnas*. What is *nasnas* called? *Rich* (bear)? Bear, no. The monkey, the gorilla. Gorilla. *Nasnas*. *Nasnas jinsun min al-khalq fi 'arabi al-shimal*. (Nasnas is a species of creation in the northwest). *'Arabi gharbi shimal... fi 'arabi shimal*. (In the northwest... in the north). *Lahum khalqun mughayyar*. (They have a changed form). *Yuqalu inna wujuhahum fi sudurihim*. (It is said that their faces are on their chests). It is said that their faces are on their chests, inside. *Wa yuqalu inna al-wahida minhum yuthbatu 'ala rijlin wahidah*. (And it is said that one of them stands on one leg). *'Ala rijlin wahidah*. What does it mean? He stands on one leg. *Wa hum fi ma hum fihi min al-nikah...* And they, in that state of copulation in which they are, its *qisasat* (retributions) are taken there.

*Thumma fi Qamis al-'Aks*. Then in the *Qamis al-'Aks*. *Wa 'ala qadri kasrati dhalika al-fi'l min qillatihi*. And according to the measure of the abundance of that act or its scarcity. Whatever he has done, by choice, he will get its recompense in that realm. Yes, in abundance. From abundance. No, from scarcity. Scarcity and abundance. *Min* is for comparison. Because... What's the scarcity? The scarcity of the act. The more *zina* he has done, the more retribution he will get. The less he has done, one time... *Li-annahu rubbama ya'bathu bil-mar'ati qawmun kasirun*. Because sometimes a large group of people has intercourse with a woman. *Fa-yakunu al-qisasu minhum mutafarriqan fi Qumus al-inhidar*. So the *qisas* from them is distributed in the *qumus* (forms) of descent. It's not in one stage, it happens in several stages. *Minha shay'un fi Qumus al-Riss*. Some of it is in the *qumus* of *riss*. *Wa shay'un fi Qumus al-Waqs*. And some of it is in the *qumus* of *waqs*. *Wa aktharu dhalika yakunu fi Qumus al-Waqs*. And most of that happens in the *qumus* of *waqs*. *Li-anna al-munakahah bil-qurudi wa sifatiha aktharu min al-munakahah bi-sa'ir al-hayawan*. Because copulation by monkeys... because copulation by monkeys, and its qualities, is more than copulation by all other animals. A lustful quality is greater in them. Regarding this, research has been done. About pigs, research has been done. This one... his own female, he incites her to be involved with another male. Its... research has been done on it.

*Wa kadhalika fa-inna munakahat ahl Qumis al-Riss aktharu min munakahat ahl al-Qumis al-Sawiyyah*. Let's leave it. *Allati hiya fi al-haqiqati qumus al-bashariyyah*. Which, in reality, are the *qumus* (forms) of humanity. The human dress, the copulation that happens in it, is less than what is in the *qumus riss*. They are more inclined to it. *La ma qad sara min al-hadaran wa mushakilun laha*. Not that which has become of the descended ones, and they are similar to them. *Thumma ma baqiya min al-qisasi fi dhalika kana fi Qumus al-'Aks*. And all the descended animals. When they had the choice in the human form, they performed such deeds, so now in all the *qumus* they go into, its effect will remain.

Meaning this, these other forms are temporary, just like that. Human beings go into forms, go into *qumus*, then come back. It is not permanent. Only *Qamat-e-Alfiyyah* is a permanency... *Qamat-e-Alfiyyah* is a *baraka* (blessing) for a limited time for every person. Yes. What is the real thing? *Qamat-e-Alfiyyah* is also a contingent thing. Why is it called *Qamat-e-Alfiyyah*? Because the *nurani* (luminous) forms that were created, what were they created as? On the form of *Qamat-e-Alfiyyah*. At that time, *Qamat-e-Alfiyyah* did not exist. So how were they created on *Qamat-e-Alfiyyah*? The answer to this was given that the thing that was, on that, *Qamat-e-Alfiyyah* was created. The *nurani zawat* (luminous essences) that were created there, how were they? They were on *Qamat-e-Alfiyyah*. And in accordance with that, when He wanted to create *Qamat-e-Alfiyyah* in the world, He created it in accordance with that, on that form. So it means that first there was *Qamat-e-Alfiyyah*. And... first, there was *Qamat-e-Alfiyyah* there. There. *Zawat-e-nuraniyyah*. In the world too, in the physical state also, first there was *Qamat-e-Alfiyyah*. Its degraded form... to make it... humanity came, animality came, minerality. So this is all a later matter. It's a later matter. This whole world that has been created, of density, of atoms, it is that world. One by one, things are taken away. In the animal realm, one thing is taken away from it. Then in the next one, a second thing, a third thing, a fourth thing. In the plant stage, only growth remains. Sensation is taken away. Sensation also remains a little. Sensation is taken away. After that, in the mineral, that is also all finished. In *khars*, sensation is taken away. Yes, one by one, things are being taken away.

*Wa innama waqa'a al-qisasu fi dhalika wal-'adhabu 'alayhi ma'a ma annahu min maradat wa taslim qimatihi*. And the *qisas* and punishment occurred for that, despite the fact that it was with consent and with the payment of its price. What are these? In these stages of descent. Animals, they have consent. Animals have consent because in their life, it had happened with consent. Adultery, etc., that was done. It was with consent. He paid and did adultery. It happened with consent. And paying its price. Just like prostitutes are there. They go, give money, and do it. *Li-kawnih waqa'a bi-ghayr tahlil-e-shari'ah lahu, fa-kana dhalika kadhalik*. Because of it occurring without the Shari'ah making it lawful for him, so that matter was thus. Just as in the realm of choice, it happened with mutual consent, so its punishment also has to be given. Because the Shari'ah has not made it lawful. But its punishment becomes a little different. In the animal realm, the punishment becomes different.

The acts that are vile acts... now these stages of descent that have been mentioned, they have been mentioned only about *zina*.
