Is it an *iḍāfī* construction or a descriptive one? It should be *bayt al-maqdis*... *bayt al-maqdis*. Or *al-bayt al-muqaddas*. If you say *al-bayt al-muqaddas*, then what? *al-bayt al-muqaddas*. What construction is this? It's adjective-noun. *al-bayt al-muqaddas*... the house which has been sanctified. It is adjective-noun. *Bayt al-maqdis*... what construction is this? The *iḍāfī* construction. *Bayt al-maqdis*... the house of sanctity. Just as in the glorious Quran, how is the construction? *Bismillāh al-raḥmān al-raḥīm*. What construction is *bismillāh*? It is an *iḍāfī* construction. The name of Allah. And what is *al-raḥmān al-raḥīm*? It is a descriptive construction. The attributes of Allah. *al-raḥmān al-raḥīm*, that's why the *kasra* comes. In the glorious Quran, from beginning to end, if one reads, then two things... two grammatical points should be kept in mind. Which is the noun, which is the verb, and which is the particle? If it is a nominal sentence, is it a nominal sentence or a verbal sentence? If it is a nominal sentence, where is the subject and where is the predicate? If it is a verbal sentence, then what should be in it? Verb, subject, object. Keep that in mind, and the mind's order will be set. Mawlānā 'Ali has stated it. What did he say? All words have three types: noun, verb, and particle. From these, sentences are formed. Sentences are of two types: one is a nominal sentence, the other is a verbal sentence. In a nominal sentence, what must there be? Subject and predicate. In a verbal sentence, what must there be? Verb, subject... first verb, subject, and object. The object is not necessary, it depends. Verb, subject. Whatever sentence you read, keep in mind whether this is a nominal sentence or a verbal sentence. And does it have all three things or not? The mind is trained on its own, and one can read Arabic in the correct way. And it has come in the report that He made him travel from Mecca to Bayt al-Muqaddas. What construction is *jā'a fi 'l-khabar*? Verbal. It's a verbal sentence. *jā'a fi 'l-khabar*. And thus it has come in the report that He caused you to be taken from Mecca to Bayt al-Muqaddas. *wa-maʿnāhu annahū arqāhu fi 'l-ʿilm ilā mā baynahū wa-bayna mutimm dawrihī wa-jumiʿa lahū min al-ʿilm wa 'l-ḥikmah mā yakūnu fīhim wa-mā yajrī ʿalayhi umūruhum wa-kayfa takūnu ḥudūduhum ʿalā mā urīda min al-ḥudūd al-ʿulwiyyah allatī ra'āhā bi-nafsihī al-ḥissiyyah*. And the meaning of that is that He elevated you in knowledge... He elevated you in knowledge towards what is between you and the *mutimm* of your era. And the *mutimm* is Janāb Abū Ṭālib. And he was gathered... knowledge and wisdom were gathered for him, which is in them. In *Laylat al-Isra'*, what happened? Where did you reach? *Qāba qawsayni aw adnā* (at a distance of two bow-lengths or nearer). You reached this station. What has been said about *qāba qawsayn*? *Qawsayn* means two bows. Who are they? Janāb 'Abd al-Muṭṭalib, Janāb Abū Ṭālib. And who is Allah? *'Ayn ḥazīrah*. *Subḥāna 'lladhī asrā*. Who is *subḥān*? *'Ayn ḥazīrah*. He elevated you so that you reached the final rank. What is your rank? The rank of *ḥijābiyyah*. You reached this rank. But you remained less than *qāba qawsayni aw adnā*. One bow is of 'Abd al-Muṭṭalib, one bow is of Abū Ṭālib. And whose is *adnā* (nearer)? It is of Janāb 'Abdullāh. *aw adnā*. And that which runs upon them from their affairs. And how their limits will be, upon that which was shown to you from the celestial limits, which he saw with his own sensory self. There, going there, the knowledge of the Kingdom was explained to you. That in the Kingdom, in the universe, how are plans executed? The inner knowledge of that was given to you. It is a great knowledge. What can I say? Where it has been stated that *wa-yuṭʿimūna al-ṭaʿāma ʿalā ḥubbihi miskīnan wa-yatīman wa-asīran* (And they feed, for the love of God, the indigent, the orphan, and the captive). That the three of them fasted. Who fasted? Janāb 'Ali, Janāb Fāṭimah, Janāb Imam Ḥasan, Imam Ḥusayn, and Janāb Fiḍḍah. Five individuals fasted. And after that, when it was time to eat, then at that time... first who came? The *miskīn* (indigent), the *yatīm* (orphan), and the *asīr* (captive). It has all been explained there. That the Imam's... the universe, the plans, they encompass the entire universe. We are frogs in a small well and we think this is the whole universe. The universe is very large. He has to carry out all the plans in it. So what is meant by *miskīn* there? *Miskīn* was fed. What is the meaning they took for *miskīn*? They took the meaning of *dā'ī* (missionary). The Imam, *'alayhi al-salātu wa-al-salām*'s, call... the call of the *khamsat al-aṣḥāb* (five companions)... in that call, there was a *dā'ī*. And he was called *miskīn*, from whom people used to find *sukūn* (peace). *Miskīn* has two meanings. One is a *miskīn* who is a pauper. And one *miskīn* is one from whom a person's heart finds peace. So, there was a *miskīn*. He came and... he was confined. Confined meaning... he did not have the right to give protection, and you gave him the right to give protection. You fed him, meaning you freed him from confinement. Who? The *panjatan pāk*. And who did it? What was the action? Janāb 'Ali got up and gave his piece of bread. Janāb Fāṭimah gave hers. After that, Imam Ḥasan gave, Imam Ḥusayn gave, and Janāb Fiḍḍah also gave. And both the children also gave. It was each one's call. Each one, from their own call, freed such people who were confined. He fed them. This is the meaning they took. Then *yatīm*. What does *yatīm* mean? Whose parents have died. And in the inner meaning, who is a *yatīm*? What is a *yatīm* called? *Durr-i yatīm* (a unique pearl). One who has no equal. *Durr-i yatīm*. He was such a person who was of a very high rank. And for some reason, he had been stopped. The command came for him, that he is a *durr-i yatīm*. His orphanage was ended by feeding him. So a *yatīm* is one who has been stopped. A *yatīm* existed. His parents were not there. Meaning, those who supported him were finished. His supporters... his mother and father who were there, they were finished. He was a *yatīm*. *Wa-asīran*. *Asīr*. *Asīr* means one who has been imprisoned. One who had been imprisoned. He was in such a place where the scholars of evil had control. He was in that place. He was in a state of captivity. A place where he could neither benefit nor be benefited. He was in such a place. He was given permission... and he was freed from that captivity. All these meanings have been taken. Now, from where in the universe did that person come? From which station did he come? Did he come from the sky, from the earth? Janāb Sayyidna has given the *ta'wīl*. *wa-min dhālika qawluhu ʿazza wa-jalla mā kadhaba al-fu'ādu mā ra'ā ilā qawlihī mā zāgha al-baṣaru wa-mā ṭaghā laqad ra'ā min āyāti rabbihi al-kubrā*. And from that is the saying of Allah, the Almighty and Glorious, *Mā kadhaba al-fu'ādu mā ra'ā* (The heart did not lie in what it saw)... up to His saying, *Mā zāgha al-baṣaru wa-mā ṭaghā* (The sight did not swerve, nor did it transgress). *Laqad ra'ā min āyāti rabbihi al-kubrā* (Indeed, he did see of the greatest signs of his Lord). Here too, what does Allah Ta'ālā say? He took him to see the great signs. And what did he see? He saw the great signs of his Lord. He saw God or not? The common people say, "I saw God." Here there is Masjid al-Haram and Masjid al-Aqsa, but there is no *ta'wīl* of *burāq* mentioned. The *ta'wīl* of *burāq* will be mentioned, in the *ta'wīl*. *yaʿnī bi-dhālika kulla 'l-ḥudūd al-ʿulwiyyah arāhā bi 'l-baṣar alladhī lam yazigh wa-huwa baṣar al-nafs al-ṣāfiyah min al-kadar*. He means by that every celestial limit... which He showed him with the sight that did not swerve, and it is the sight of the pure soul, free from turbidity. *wa-li-dhālika ruwiya ʿan baʿḍ azwājihī annahā qālat laylata usriya bihī wa 'llāhi mā bāta illā bayna saḥrī wa-naḥrī*. And for this reason, it is narrated from one of his wives—it is narrated from 'Ā'ishah—that she said, "On the night he was taken on the journey, by Allah, he did not spend the night anywhere but between my chest and my neck." Now what do *saḥrī* and *naḥrī* mean? We have to see that. *wa-fi 'l-khabar innahū lammā balagha ilā bayt al-maqdis atāhu jibrā'īl bi-markūb dūn al-baghl wa-fawqa 'l-dawābbah yusammā al-burāq fa-rakibahū*. And it is in the report that when he reached Bayt al-Maqdis, Jibrā'īl came to him with a mount smaller than a mule and larger than a beast of burden, named al-Burāq. So he rode it. Here, what is he saying? After reaching Bayt al-Maqdis, Jibrā'īl brought it for you. He didn't bring it to take him from Mecca to Bayt al-Maqdis. This meaning can be taken here. With a mount smaller than a mule... smaller than a camel, and larger than a beast of burden. A medium one. It was named al-Burāq. So he rode upon it. *wa-dhālika fi 'l-ta'wīl huwa 'l-ʿilm al-mubriq al-muḍī' alladhī huwa 'l-bayān fawqa ʿilm al-lāḥiq wa-dūnahī ʿilm al-imām wa-rukūbuhū iyyāhu istilā'uhū ʿalayhi*. And that, in *ta'wīl*, is the flashing, illuminating knowledge which is the clarification, above the knowledge of the *lāḥiq* (successor) and below it is the knowledge of the Imam (Abū Ṭālib). And his riding it is his mastery over it. *wa-suʿūduhū ilā 'l-samā' fi 'l-ta'wīl iṭṭilāʿuhū ʿalā malakūtihā wa-ʿilm mā fīhā*. And his ascension to the heaven, in *ta'wīl*, is his being informed of its kingdom and the knowledge of what is in it. The kingdom of the heavens was opened for you. *wa-min dhālika qawluhu ʿazza wa-jalla fī ibrāhīm ṣalawāt Allāh ʿalayh wa-kadhālika nurī ibrāhīm malakūt al-samāwāt wa 'l-arḍ wa-li-yakūna min al-mūqinīn*. And from that is the saying of Allah, the Almighty and Glorious, regarding Ibrāhīm, peace of Allah be upon him, *Wa-kadhālika nurī ibrāhīm malakūt al-samāwāt wa 'l-arḍ wa-li-yakūna min al-mūqinīn* (And thus did We show Ibrāhīm the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, and that he might be of those who are certain). The ranks of imamate, the ranks of messengership, he established them. And the true speech... the station of true speech is above all of them—above prophethood, messengership, imamate, and successorship. Who are the bearers of true speech? Three are the bearers. Who are the three? Hunayd, Ibrāhīm, and Hāshim. Hunayd, Ibrāhīm, and Hāshim. They are the bearers of true speech. Their rank was surpassed by the Prophet, *'alayhi al-salātu wa-al-salām*. How did his rank surpass theirs? Through *ḥijābiyyah* (the rank of the veil). The rank of *ḥijābiyyah* which you attained... in that... it is a strange domain... his rank became higher in that. *wa-jā'a fi 'l-khabar annahū ṣallā bi-jamīʿ al-anbiyā' wa-ṣalātuhū bihim fi 'l-bāṭin daʿwatuhū li-jamīʿ al-umam*. And it has come in the report that he led all the prophets in prayer. And his leading them in prayer, in the inner sense, is his call to all the nations. You gave the call to all the nations. And at that time, who was the *mu'adhdhin* (one who calls to prayer)? When the prayer was established, people said... the angels said, "So-and-so, so-and-so." They said, "The Master of Messengers has come." Janāb Prophet led the prayer. For all the prophets. And when it was time for the call to prayer, Janāb Ibrāhīm gave the call to prayer. Where did he give the call to prayer? On Safā and Marwah, it is said there. What? At the station of Safā and Marwah, standing, you gave the call to prayer. The explanation of Safā and Marwah that is given, it is the explanation of the Hajj. It is explained therein. The *mu'adhdhin* was Ibrāhīm, and the Imam was Janāb Prophet, *'alayhi al-salātu wa-al-salām*. For all the prophets. *wa-annahū buʿitha li-jamīʿihim kamā dhukira tamām al-kalām fīhi wa-ghayrihi*. And that he was sent for all of them, as has been mentioned in the completion of the discourse on this and other matters. *wa-ghayruhū min al-anbiyā' innamā buʿitha ilā qawmihī bi-aʿyānihim*. And others among the prophets were only sent to their specific peoples. *wa-qawluhu li-nuriyahū min āyātinā min āyātihī al-ẓāhirah allatī arāhu subḥānahū ḥudūdan allatī akhānahā baynahū wa-bayna anbiyā'ihī wa-malā'ikatihī fa-ra'ā āyatan kubratan minhum*. So, Allah's signs... such that He showed him... Allah, the Glorious, showed him... limits which He had appointed between Himself and His prophets and His angels. So he saw a great sign from among them. It is stated with regard to all the celestial limits... which he saw with his pure, insightful heart and heard with his hearing ear. And that is His saying: *innahū huwa al-samīʿ al-baṣīr* (Verily, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing). *wa-qawluhu ilā 'l-masjid al-aqṣā wa-qad dhakarnāhu mithāl al-mutimm al-maḥẓūr ʿalayhi 'l-mufātaḥah*. And His saying: *ilā 'l-masjid al-aqṣā* (to the Farthest Mosque), and we have already mentioned that it is an example of the *mutimm* (completer) upon whom initiation is forbidden. *wa-qawluhu alladhī bāraknā ḥawlahū fa 'l-barakah hiya 'l-ta'yīd wa 'l-mufātaḥah fa-kānat dhālika li-man qablahū wa-man baʿdahū*. And His saying: *alladhī bāraknā ḥawlahū* (whose precincts We did bless), so the blessing is the support and the initiation. And thus it was for those before him and those after him. *wa-qawluhu li-nuriyahū min āyātinā yaʿnī annahū idhā iṭṭalaʿa ʿalā dhālika min ḥudūd al-ʿulwiyyah naṣaba bi-idhā'ihā ḥudūdan sufliyyah*. And His saying: *li-nuriyahū min āyātinā* (that We might show him of Our signs), meaning that when he was informed of that from the celestial limits, he established in opposition to them the terrestrial limits. You saw the system of the celestial limits there, and that same system you established in your call. Jibrā'īl's station is with whom? It is varied. As the Prophet's rank elevated, Jibrā'īl's position also changed. So here he has not explained... it has not been explained here. At that time, when he progressed to that station, who he was has not been explained. And he has not explained the station where... beyond which even Jibrā'īl could not go. The station of *qāba qawsayni aw adnā* is that station. That is the station of *qāba qawsayni aw adnā*. When Jibrā'īl reached there, he said, "O Prophet of God, I cannot go beyond this." The verse of Janāb Sa'di is about this, is it not? "If I move a hair's breadth further, my wings will burn." My wings will burn. It's a beautiful verse. *fa-abda'a ṣalawāt Allāh ʿalayh min dhālika al-ʿilm alladhī ūtīyahū ilā asāsihī bi-mā yujīb an yaqbaḍahu minhu ilayhī fa-ʿallamahū iyyāhu wa-ahdā ilayhī an yu'addī min dhālika ilā man yūṣī ilayhi bi-sirrihī wa-yuqīmuhū min baʿdihī bi-mā yajib li-mithlihī wa-in yanqulahū kadhālika wāḥidan ilā wāḥid*. So he conveyed from that knowledge which he was given to his *asās* (foundation) that which was necessary for him to receive from him to him. So he taught it to him. One by one. He brought that knowledge of the *ta'wīl* of *Laylat al-Isra'* and conveyed it all to the Imams of his time. He established that this Imam will have this much, this Imam will have this much, this Imam will have this much. It's a whole universe. So he conveyed that knowledge which he was given to his *asās* what was required to be conveyed from him to him. And he instructed... that he convey from that, after him, to the person whom he appoints with his secret, and establish him after him with what is necessary for his like, and that he transmit it thus from one to one. *wa-kadhalika awdā'ahu wa-amarahu an yu'addī ʿanhu min amr ẓāhir al-sharīʿah*. And similarly, he entrusted it to him and commanded him to convey on his behalf from the matter of the exoteric Shari'ah. The explanation has not ended. There are more explanations. He has explained the meanings. Now the mention of the prayer of 27th is being explained. The one who performs a deed in it has the reward of twenty years. He was asked what should be done in it. He said... what should be done? He said, 22 *rak'āt* should be prayed. With 22 surahs. When he says the *salām* at the end of it... then what should be recited? Al-Hamd seven times, *Innā anzalnā* seven times, and Ayatul Kursi seven times. How many does that make? 21. And *Qul al-ḥamdu* is 22. In 22 *rak'āt*, 22 verses. Then he explained the supplication. And he said that on the morning of that day, he said, *Baʿatha Muḥammad ṣalawāt Allāh ʿalayh*. On the 27th of Rajab. The supplication is mentioned. Allah sent the Prophet on the 27th of Rajab. As a caller to the religion of Islam. The month of Rajab was an example for the rank of the Imam. The month of Rajab is for the rank of imamate. Isn't it? What did the Prophet say? 'Every Imam after me who rises... Rajab is his month.' 'O 'Ali, Rajab is the month of every Imam who rises after you.' It is the month of imamate. 'Sha'ban is my month, Ramadan is the month of Allah. Rajab is the month of the Imams from the Ahl al-Bayt.' After that, what did he say? 'And the Imams from the progeny of Ismā'īl ibn Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, were 30 Imams.' That is, Rajab has 30 days. It is based on 30 Imams from the progeny of Ismā'īl ibn Ibrāhīm, peace be upon them both. And the nights of Rajab are based on the progeny of Ismā'īl, and its days are based on the progeny of Isḥāq. Its nights are for the progeny of Ismā'īl. And the rising of the one who rises from the progeny of Isḥāq is based on the master of his era from the progeny of Ismā'īl, to whom the command is entrusted. It is all... The *mab'ath* of the Prophet took place in the 27th year of the creation. Because your birth, *ṣalawāt Allāh ʿalayh*... its meaning is that your birth... your *wilādat* is after 27 Imams from the progeny of Ismā'īl, who were in the veil. How many days remain of the month? After 27, three days remain. After the *mab'ath*, three days remain, which is an indication towards the three Imams who are remaining after your birth. Who are they? 'Abd al-Muṭṭalib, 'Abdullāh, and Abū Ṭālib. These three Imams. It is an indication towards them. And he who is chosen from among the Imams is 'Abd al-Muṭṭalib. During the time of these three Imams, you were born. 'Abd al-Muṭṭalib, Janāb Abū Ṭālib, Janāb 'Abdullāh. This is the indication. And in the 22 *rak'āt*, he is explaining that when the prayer is completed, they are examples of the limits, celestial and terrestrial, by which the call of imamate is established. He has given their names: Imam, *bāb*, *markaz*, *saff*, *bāb* of the circle, *ḥujjat*, *ḥujjat-i sayyārah*, *dā'ī-i balāgh*, *dā'ī-i aḥrām*, *ma'dhūn al-muṭlaq*. All the ranks. There are two or three more ranks. The *asās* is of 'Alī Nā. And the *nātiq* is of the Prophet... The birth of the *asās* was on the 27th of Rajab. But what is confirmed is the 27th of Rajab. This should be confirmed. 27th of Rajab. In this, he has explained this matter. It is a part of this. Muhammad al-Tayyib. The Seal of the Messengers. The light of God.

<!-- lecture 61 -->

Twelve were mentioned, to whom do they belong? Does someone have some, does someone else have some? Whose are they, the twelve? This is the original question. Are they of the twelve Imams? Or are twelve of this one, twelve of that one... whose are they? According to that, all the virtues are established. *Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*.

Yes. The thing about Hazrat Rajab, the 27th date, about the three Imams… after whom were these three Imams? What is their connection (*nisbah*) to Rasulullah (s), or is it to Mawla ‘Ali (s)?

It has a connection to both. The connection is to both. The birth of ‘Ali…

The question is, from Rasulullah, whose are you talking about? Are you talking about the *Hijab* or the *Muhtajib*?

They weren't there… three Imams... Mawlana Abu... Abdul Muttalib wasn't there either. Yes. What was stated in his book? *Abdullah ‘indallah* (The servant of God is with God). There, he removed two dots from both. He removed two dots. *Abdullah ‘indallah*. Below it, the dot was removed… the upper dot, the lower dot, both were removed. Now, the reader should understand what it is. Just as Hasan is Husayn. Everywhere it is like this: `ayatun wahidah` (a single verse/sign). `Kila-huma ayatun wahidah` (Both of them are a single verse/sign). Both of them are one verse. Mahdi and Qa'im. `Kila-huma ayatun wahidah`. According to that. Now, whenever the question about these three is asked, the question is that one must understand the three streams (*majari*). How are the streams? Are they in the highest stream (*majra-e a'la*), the middle stream (*majra-e awsat*), or the lowest stream (*majra-e adna*)? Where is this being discussed? It corresponds with that.

The `Ayn-e ‘Azimah` is the station of the *Muhtajib* in the realm of life (*'alam-e hayat*). And... that... the glory (*shan*) of `Ayn-e ‘Azimah` is different. `Ana al-awwal, ana al-akhir, ana al-zahir, wa al-batin` (I am the First, I am the Last, I am the Manifest, and the Hidden). Those who are in this world were made servants (*khadim*). Payghambar 'alayhis salat was-salam...

They were not alive...

Yes?

During the lifetime of the Prophet, the life of... Abdul Muttalib...

No, the Prophet had already been born. They were born into his lifetime.

...the time of *bi'thah* (the start of the prophetic mission), right? Of the three Imams...

No, not the time of *bi'thah*. The time of birth. They had already become a prophet, no? `Kun-tu nabiyyan` (I was a prophet). At that time, you had already become the bearer of prophethood. `Kun-tu nabiyyan wa adamu bayna al-ma'i wa al-tin` (I was a prophet while Adam was between water and clay).

When you were made a prophet, the three Imams were present, in this way... the connection.

And if Janab Abdul Muttalib and Janab 'Ali had passed away during his time, then the Prophet-Imam was present. The Prophet-Imam... that era was present. So in that way, three... with 'Ali, there were three, and there too, there were three.

The 124,000 *anbiya'* (prophets) that were mentioned... the *thalathah ha*... they are from among the *muta'akhkhirin* (the later ones), aren't they? Four, two, and one... the *thalathah ha*...

These *anbiya'* are from the lower ones. It's like... what was stated about the ranks (*maratib*)? *Mustajib* (the one who responds). After that? *Mu'min* (believer). Then? After *mu'min*, what is there? *Mukasir* (disputer). Then *ma'sum* (infallible). Then? *Da'i* (summoner)... *Da'i mahsur* (limited summoner)... *da'i*... *da'i balagh* (summoner of conveyance). Then, what is there? *Hujjah* (proof). *Hujjah*. Then *Bab* (gate). Then *Imam*. Ten ranks were stated. Now, after this, what begins? *Nubuwwah* (prophethood) and *Risalah* (messengership). *Imamah* (imamate) and *Wasiyyah* (executorship). *Nubuwwah* and *Risalah*, *Imamah* and *Wasiyyah*. Four ranks. Above this, the rank that exists is *nutq ilahi* (divine utterance). That is counted among the ranks of *Qa'imiyyah*. These four ranks are below. The level of *nutq ilahi*. Who are established at the level of *nutq ilahi*? These *anbiya'* are at the lower levels. The 124,000. In the ranks of *nutq ilahi*, it was said: `thalathah ha`. Janab Imam Hunayd 'alayhis salat was-salam. Then Janab Ibrahim 'alayhis salat was-salam, and Janab Hashim. Three *nutq ilahi*. And in the era of the Prophet, whoever is the seventh is the *sahib nutq ilahi* (possessor of the divine utterance). Now look, again the ten came. The principle came. How? Hunayd, Ibrahim, Hashim... then after that, seven Imams. Seven... with seven, there are seven Imams. Ten. Now the rest are *qurun* (eras).

Sir, they say that... during the lifetime of Mawlana Khadijah, Rasulullah did not take a second wife. So... the Hijrat... the Mi'raj... that event... that was an affair during the lifetime of Mawlana Khadijah. So then from where did 'A'ishah come in the middle, and from where...

Yes, they narrate it.

The narration was denied, right?

The narration was... a narration was created and then denied. If there was a little more, then there would be `hur` (celestial maidens) too.

*Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*.

`wa idha kan al-intaha bi al-qawli bina ila ma intaha, fa-nazidu fi iza... ma yajibu izahuhi, fa-naqulu` ... `ma yajibu izahu` ... `izahu, fa-naqulu an jami'` ... `fa` `ma yajibu izahu`. `‘ayn` has a `pesh`. `fa-naqulu an jami' hadha al-'alam al-bashari min natiqin aw wasiyyin wa imamin wa tabi'ihim wa ghayrihim min sa'ir al-nas, muftaqiruna fi bad'i wujudihim ila al-ta'lim.` And when our statement reached its end, then we add to its clarification what is necessary to clarify. Thus, we say that the entire human world, be it a *natiq* or a *wasi*, an Imam or their follower, and others from all people, are needy, in the beginning of their existence, of instruction.

`wa bi-dhalika nut... nadakh-khala al-kitab al-karim bi-qawlihi ta'ala: wallahu akhrajakum min butuni ummahatikum la ta'lamuna shay'an.` And for this reason, the Noble Book mentioned in His, the Exalted's, saying: "And God brought you out from the wombs of your mothers while you knew nothing." And Allah brought out... brought out you... and Allah brought out you from the wombs of your mothers while you knew nothing of any thing. `fa-ammat hadhihi al-ayah jami' al-khalq al-bashari, sharifihi wa mashrufihi.` And this verse became general for... thus this verse became general for all human creation, for its noble ones and its ignoble ones. ...that have been given nobility. Those who are lower than the low. `wa innama baynahum al-tafawut fi al-dhaka wa al-fitnah wa al-fikr wa al-qubul.` And indeed, the difference between them is in intelligence and sagacity, and thought and acceptance. `wa dhalika inna ashraf al-ashraf al-muntakha 'alayhim al-salam, natiqu dawrina wa abuhu ibrahim, wa ashraf al-awsiya' wa al-a'immah 'alayhim al-salam, amir al-mu'minin 'ali salamu-llahi 'alayhi wa 'alayhim, wa hum mimman ta'allama wa raqa fi al-ma'arif shay'an ba'da shay'in ila an balagha ghayat al-nutq, li-yakhudhu bi-dhalika`. And that is the fact that the most noble of the nobles, upon whom be peace, is the *natiq* of our era and his father Ibrahim, and the most noble of the *awsiya'* and *a'immah*, upon whom be peace, is Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali, peace of God be upon him and upon them, and they are among those who learned and progressed in the various branches of knowledge, thing after thing, until they reached the pinnacle of utterance, so they may take by that... And that is the fact... that the most noble of the nobles is the *natiq* of our era, on whom be peace, our Mawla, the Prophet 'alayhis salat was-salam, and his father Ibrahim. And they are from among those individuals who received instruction and progressed in knowledge, bit by bit, until they reached the final limit of utterance. They are born not knowing anything, but their speed is very fast. The speed of others cannot be like theirs. One person travels by walking, another travels by airplane. There is a huge difference between the two. Why does this happen? Their *'iddat* (preparedness)... the word *'iddat* has been used for it. Intelligence, sagacity, thought, and acceptance. Theirs is much greater. `wa yash-hadu bi-dhalika qawlu-llahi ta'ala fi ibrahim: wa kadhalika nuri ibrahima malakuta al-samawati wa al-ard wa li-yakuna min al-muqinin.` And the saying of Allah the Exalted concerning Ibrahim bears witness to this: "And thus did We show Ibrahim the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, that he might be of those who are certain." And the testimony for this fact is the saying of Allah the Exalted concerning Ibrahim, and in the same way, we showed Ibrahim the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. And perhaps... and so that they may become among those who are certain. And so that they may become among those who are certain. `wa isharatuhu ila malakut al-samawati wa al-ard, yuridu bi-dhalika al-'alam al-ruhani ba'da 'uluwwi rutbatihi wa kamali ma'rifatihi`. And his indication towards the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, he intends by that the spiritual world after the loftiness of his rank and the perfection of his knowledge. Thus his indication is towards the kingdom of the heavens and the earth; he intends by that the spiritual world. After your high rank... after they informed you of the ranks of the spiritual world. After the loftiness of your rank and the perfection of your knowledge. `wa bi-malakut al-ard al-hudud alladhina akhadha 'anhum fi bad'i amrihi`. And by the kingdom of the earth, [it means] the *hudud* (spiritual ranks) from whom he took in the beginning of his affair. And from the kingdom of the earth are those *hudud* from whom you, Janab Ibrahim, took in your initial affair. `wa 'ana hum bi-qawlihi ta'ala: falamma janna 'alayhi al-laylu ra'a kawkaban, qala hadha rabbi, falamma afala qala la uhibbu al-afilin.` And he meant them by His, the Exalted's, saying: "So when the night covered him, he saw a star. He said, 'This is my Lord.' But when it set, he said, 'I do not love those that set.'" And He alluded to all of them with the saying of Allah the Exalted, that when the night fell upon him, he saw a star. Janab Ibrahim said, "This is my Lord." But when it set, he said, "I do not love those that set." `falamma ra'a al-qamara bazighan qala hadha rabbi, falamma afala qala la-in lam yahdini rabbi la-akunanna min al-qawm al-dallin.` I do not... I do not love those that set. But when he saw the moon rising, he said, "This is my Lord." But when it set, he said, "If my Lord does not guide me, I will surely be among the misguided people." But when I saw the moon... shining brightly... when you saw the moon setting, you said, "This is my Lord." Shining brightly. He said, "This is my Lord." But when it set, you said that "If my Lord does not guide me, I will become among the misguided people." "If my Lord does not guide me, then I would become among the misguided people." `wa sa'ir al-ayah, wa ha'ula'i hum al-hudud al-jismaniyyun alladhina tawallaw tarbiyatahu wa ta'limahu fi bad'i amrihi, wa ta'allama minhum.` The rest of the verse. And these are the physical *hudud* who undertook his upbringing and his teaching in the beginning of his affair, and he learned from them. It is finished. Thus the entire verse became complete. And the rest of the verse. And these are the *hudud*... those are the *hudud* who are physical, such that they were in charge of your upbringing and your teaching in the beginning of your affair. Initially, the *hadd* (rank) of 'Ali was above your star. After that, what happened? He came to the moon. The one who was at the station of the moon was Bab Sharif. He came to him. Then after that... `wa ta'allama amir al-mu'minin fi bad'i amrihi min rasulillahi salawatullahi 'alayhima wa min khadijata bint khuwaylid wa ghayriha min al-hudud.` And Amir al-Mu'minin learned in the beginning of his affair from Rasulullah, peace of God be upon them both, and from Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, and from others besides her from among the *hudud*. And Amir al-Mu'minin received instruction in the beginning of his affair from Rasulullah, salutations of Allah be upon them both, and from Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, and from others besides her from among the *hudud*. You... Janab 'Ali's nurturer was... teacher was Janab Khadijah. And others besides her from among the *hudud*. `wa li-dhalika nasaba ilayha`. And for this reason, he attributed to her... and for this reason... it was attributed... you were attributed to Khadijah. How was it attributed? `wa muth-thila bi-'isa ibn maryam`. And he was likened to 'Isa ibn Maryam. And a parallel was drawn with 'Isa ibn Maryam. 'Isa refers to... Maryam is Janab Khadijah and Janab 'Ali is 'Isa, from a comparative perspective. A parallel was drawn with 'Isa ibn Maryam. `kama qala fihi al-kitab al-karim: wa lamma duriba ibnu maryama mathalan idha qawmuka minhu yasiddun.` As the Noble Book said concerning him: "And when the son of Mary was presented as an example, behold, your people turned away from it in laughter." And when the example of Ibn Maryam is given, your people turn away from it. You are likened to 'Isa ibn Maryam. The Prophet 'alayhis salat was-salam also said this, that "If, O 'Ali, I were to describe those things about you that I have not described until now, then people would revere your horse's... from the hoof... in the same way that they revere Janab 'Isa's donkey's hoof." This is what he said. It is a famous hadith. `thumma qawluhu 'alayhis salam: 'allamani rasulullah alfa babin min al-'ilm, infataha li min kulli babin alfa bab.` Then his, peace be upon him's, saying: "Rasulullah taught me a thousand chapters of knowledge, from each chapter a thousand chapters opened up for me." Then, your saying, Janab 'Ali's saying, that "Rasulullah gave me knowledge from a thousand chapters... from knowledge, a thousand chapters of knowledge... and He opened for me, from every chapter, a thousand chapters." It opened for me. It opened for me. It opened for me, from every chapter, a thousand chapters. Those that come from the grammatical form of *infi'al*, in them, what happens? There is no need for an object (*maf'ul*). The form of *infi'al*. What is it like? Verbs are of two types: an intransitive verb (*fi'l-e lazim*) and a transitive verb (*fi'l-e muta'addi*). In an intransitive verb, there is only a subject (*fa'il*); verb and subject. And in a transitive verb, there is a verb, a subject, and an object (*maf'ul*). All three are there. The form from which *infataha* comes, what is its meaning? It does not need an object. `infataha li`. "It opened for me." From every chapter... from every chapter, a thousand chapters. It's like this. `min kulli bab`. The `alfa bab`... its subject is what? Of what? `infataha li alfa babin`. That's why the `pesh` is there, it's specific to it. `infataha li alfa babin min kulli bab`. "It opened for me..." It has no object. Just like we read `inhazama`. `inhazama`. So it's not `inhazama`, it's `hazama`. If `inhazama`... then an object cannot come. You would say `inhazama al-ahzaba` (was defeated the parties). So what is the meaning of `inhazama`? "Was defeated." `Ahzab` means the parties. So what is the meaning of "was defeated the parties"? A mistake has remained in the scripture, a big one. What should it actually be? `hazama al-ahzaba` (He defeated the parties). `hazama al-ahzaba`. `hazama` means "He gave defeat." `inhazama` means "he was defeated." They say *munhazim*, right? *Munhazim*. One who is defeated. He was defeated. In the meaning of being defeated. So what would be the meaning? If you say `inhazama al-ahzaba`, what would be the meaning? "The parties were defeated." What does that mean? `wa-nhazama al-ahzab`. So what should it be? `wa hazama al-ahzaba` (and He defeated the parties). He gave defeat to the parties. `wa hazama al-ahzaba wahdahu` (and He alone defeated the parties). It's been coming down since then... from which scripture has it been coming?

`al-fasl al-thani min bab al-khamis min al-shawahid al-rabi'ah`. The second section, from the fifth chapter, from the fourth evidence. Look in the verses of the noble Qur'an. When you take out the entire noble Qur'an and look, it is `hazama` there. `inhazama` is nowhere to be found. In the noble Qur'an. The second section. The second section, from the fifth chapter, from the fourth evidence. `wa min al-dalili 'ala dhalika qawlu natiqi dawrina 'alayhis salam: akhadhtu min khamsatin wa sallamtu ila khamsatin wa bayni wa bayna rabbi khamsah.` And from the evidence for that is the saying of the *natiq* of our era, peace be upon him: "I took from five, and I entrusted to five, and between me and my Lord are five." And the evidence for this fact is from the saying of the *natiq*... our *natiq* of the era's saying that, peace be upon him, "I took from five and I entrusted to five, and between me and my Lord are five." `fa-al-khamsah alladhina akhadha 'anhum al-nutuqa' al-khamsah al-mutaqaddimuna 'alayhi, alladhina ta'allama kutubahum al-munazzalah 'alayhim, wa shara'i'ahum allati shara'uha, wa awda'ahum allati wada'uha, haqa'iqaha wa ta'wilatiha wa ma'aniha wa haqa'iqaha.` Thus the five from whom he took are the five *nutuqa'* (prophets) who preceded him, whose revealed books he learned, and their laws which they legislated, and their deposits which they deposited, their realities, their interpretations, their meanings, and their realities. Thus, five such that he took from them, those are the five *nutuqa'*. Before you... the five *nutuqa'* who were to come before you. Such that he learned from their books, which were revealed upon them, and their laws, such that they established them. And from the decrees... from the decrees and laws, such that they were established by them. And he verified... their interpretations and their meanings and their realities. `wa al-khamsah allati baynahu wa bayna rabbihi hum al-hudud al-diniyyah alladhina akhadha 'anhum wa ta'allama fi bad'i amrihi minhum.` And the five that are between him and his Lord are the religious *hudud* from whom he took and from whom he learned in the beginning of his affair. And five, such that between you and your Lord are the religious *hudud*, such that he took from them and received instruction in the beginning of his affair, from them. `wa raqquhu maratib al-din shay'an ba'da shay'in.` And they elevated him through the ranks of the religion, thing by thing. And they elevated you through the ranks of the religion, the *hudud*, bit by bit. `ila an balagha dhirwataha`. Until he reached its peak. Until they reached its peak. `wa hum ubayy wa zayd ibn 'amr wa 'amr ibn nufayl wa maysarah wa khadijah bint khuwaylid.` And they are Ubayy, and Zayd ibn 'Amr, and 'Amr ibn Nufayl, and Maysarah, and Khadijah bint Khuwaylid. Ubayy ibn Ka'b. Ubayy ibn Ka'b. And they are Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Zayd ibn 'Amr and 'Amr ibn Nufayl and Maysarah and Khadijah bint Khuwaylid. `wa hum hududu sahib al-waqt al-muqim lahu, al-mu'li rutbatahu, al-musallim ilayhi, wa huwa ibnu 'amm... abu talib.` And they are the *hudud* of the Master of the Time, who establishes for him, who elevates his rank, who entrusts to him, and he is the son of the uncle, Abu Talib. It is `ibnu 'amm`. `ammihi`. It is written `ammihi`, Abu Talib. `ammihi`. `ammihi`. `wa huwa 'ammuhu`. `wa huwa 'ammuhu, abu talib`. It is a subject and predicate. `wa huwa 'ammuhu`. `wa huwa 'ammuhu, abu talib.` And they elevated you in the ranks of the religion, bit by bit. Who are they? Ubayy... Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and... and who else? Zayd ibn 'Amr. I don't remember the name. Zayd ibn 'Amr. And then? 'Amr ibn Nufayl. Don't read it as 'Umar, 'Amr ibn Nufayl. And Maysarah. And then Janab Khadijah. Five. Janab Khadijah, yes. She gave you instruction and she is also the teacher of Janab 'Ali. And they are all the five *hudud*: Ubayy, Zayd ibn 'Amr, 'Amr ibn Nufayl, Maysarah, and Khadijah bint Khuwaylid. And they are the *hudud* of the Imam, the Master of the Imam, who is the one who establishes you and the one who elevates you to a high rank and the one who entrusts your affair to you. And he is your uncle, Abu Talib. Who is the Master of the Time? The Master of the Time is your uncle, Abu Talib. `wa amma al-khamsah alladhina sallama ilayhim fa-hum wasiyuhu amir al-mu'minin, wa abnahu al-hasan wa al-husayn, wa al-baqir wa huwa muhammad ibn 'ali, wa muhammad ibn isma'il salawatullahi 'alayhim ajma'in.` And as for the five to whom he entrusted, they are his successor, Amir al-Mu'minin, and his two sons, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and al-Baqir, who is Muhammad ibn 'Ali, and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, peace of God be upon them all. And five, such that he entrusted to them, they are your *wasi*, Amir al-Mu'minin, and your two sons, Hasan and Husayn, and Baqir, and he is Muhammad ibn 'Ali, and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, may the salutations of Allah be upon them all. `wa taslimuhu li-amir al-mu'minin 'alayhis salam`. This is a matter of *subur*. And this, yes. Mawlana Muhammad 'Ali, Mawlana 'Ali Zayn al-'Abidin. Muhammad ibn Zayn al-'Abidin. Mawlana Muhammad al-Baqir ibn Zayn al-'Abidin. Because the entrustment of the seven is especially for them. What was stated? The five from whom I took, who are they? The five *nutuqa'*. Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, and 'Isa. From them, he took. And the five between me... `wa sallamtu... akhadhtu`. What was stated? Between... `wa bayni wa bayna rabbi khamsah` (and between me and my Lord are five). Who are they? Between me and my Lord are five. Janab Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Janab Zayd ibn 'Amr, Janab 'Amr ibn Nufayl, Janab Maysarah, Janab Khadijah. These are the five. And to whom did he give? It is his *wasi*, Amir al-Mu'minin 'alayhis salat was-salam. When you... and his two sons, al-Hasan and al-Husayn. Because there is a famous hadith: `al-hasan wa al-husayn imaman qama aw qa'ada wa abuhuma khayrun minhuma` (al-Hasan and al-Husayn are two Imams, whether they rise up or sit down, and their father is better than them). That store of great glory which the Prophet 'alayhis salat was-salam possessed, from that, he bestowed the things of Imamate. Now, there are also things of the *Imamah al-mustawda`* (deposited Imamate) and things of the *Imamah al-mustaqarr* (permanent Imamate). The things that Janab Abdul Muttalib had gathered with Abu Talib, and having been gathered with Abu Talib, the *Imamah wa Wasiyyah* was combined, and the *Nubuwwah wa Risalah* was combined. Their things, you gave to Amir al-Mu'minin and Hasan and Husayn. Now after that, how did he give to Baqir? For Na'ib Baqir, you said, what did you say? "O Baqir, cleave the knowledge." His name is like my name. His name is like my name. And after that, how did he bestow upon Janab Muhammad ibn Isma'il? Through the *adhan* (call to prayer). In the words of the *adhan*, the first word is for the Prophet, and the second word is for Janab Muhammad ibn Isma'il. Here, Muhammad is because there is a connection to your name. They left out Ja'far al-Sadiq and Janab Zayn al-'Abidin. No, specifically, it has been explained that the name of the Imam... the Imams after him are especially given attention from him. All the Imams receive it. The Imam whose name resembles the Prophet's receives from the Prophet. The Imam whose name resembles 'Ali's receives from 'Ali. Especially. All the Imams have received it. Here, the five that are mentioned... they left out 'Ali Zayn al-'Abidin and Ja'far al-Sadiq. He did not state Imam Zayn al-'Abidin's name. But he stated specifically for the Prophet, for Janab Baqir... the era of Imam Zayn al-'Abidin was not one of dissemination; it was not an era of *nashr* (spreading knowledge). Who spread it? Janab Muhammad al-Baqir spread it. And why do they call him Sadiq? Ja'far al-Sadiq? Because he narrated the things of his father with truth (*sidq*). He is Sadiq for this reason. The one who actually narrated was Imam al-Baqir. He got such a time when the Banu Umayyah had been destroyed, they were fighting amongst themselves, he got the opportunity to narrate the Hadith of the Prophet. `wa taslimuhu li-amir al-mu'minin 'alayhis salam, wa al-hasan wa al-husayn 'alayhima al-salam, bi-qawlihim: al-hasan wa al-husayn imaman qaman aw qa'adan, wa abuhuma khayrun minhuma`. And your entrusting to Amir al-Mu'minin, peace be upon him, and to al-Hasan and al-Husayn, peace be upon them, by their saying: "al-Hasan and al-Husayn are two Imams, whether they rise up or sit down, and their father is better than them." He is saying... your name is... "two Imams, whether they rise up or sit down, and their father is better than them." And entrusting your affair to Amir al-Mu'minin, peace be upon him, and Hasan and Husayn, peace be upon them, from your saying that "Hasan and Husayn are two Imams, whether they rise up or sit down, and their father is better than them." It is not stated that after me... the Prophet is present, and it is being said that they are... that means they have become. They have become Imams. Both have become Imams. Whether they rise up or... and your father is better than them. And 'Ali has become better than Imamate. Both have become Imams. During the time of the Prophet himself. And 'Ali has become better than them, during the time of the Prophet himself. And their father is better than them. `wa taslimuhu li-al-baqir 'alayhim al-salam, bi-qawlihi li-jabir ibn 'abdillah: innaka sa-talhaqu waladan min waladi, hadha, fa-aqri'hu minni al-salam, wa qul lahu: qala laka jadduka ya baqir, ya baqir al-'ilm, abqirhu baqran.` And his entrusting to al-Baqir, peace be upon them, by his saying to Jabir ibn 'Abdillah: "Indeed, you will meet a child from my child, this one, so convey my peace to him, and say to him: Your grandfather said to you, O Baqir, O cleaver of knowledge, cleave it wide open." And your entrusting to Baqir, peace be upon them, by the saying... of Jabir ibn 'Abdillah, that "Indeed, you will soon meet my... a child of my child." You will meet. "You will meet my descendant, a child of my child, this one." Referring to Imam Husayn, he said, "My... this descendant of mine, Husayn, you will meet his descendant." "And convey my salam." "And say to them, from me... convey my salam to them from me." "And say to them that your grandfather said, 'O Baqir, O cleaver of knowledge, cleave it wide open.'" "Tear it open, that is, explain the knowledge thoroughly." `wa taslimuhu li-muhammad ibn isma'il, bi-shahadatihi lahu bi-al-risalah fi al-adhan, 'inda qawlihi: ash-hadu anna muhammadan rasulullah, li-anna shahadatahu salawatullahi 'alayhi li-nafsihi ghayru ja'izin, wa innama kanat al-shahadatu li-muhammad ibn isma'il 'alayhim al-salam.` And his entrusting to Muhammad ibn Isma'il, by his testimony for him of messengership in the *adhan*, at his saying: "I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God," because his own testimony, peace of God be upon him, for himself is not permissible, and indeed the testimony was for Muhammad ibn Isma'il, peace be upon them. And your entrusting to Muhammad ibn Isma'il, with a testimony... for messengership, in the *adhan*... from the saying of the one saying `ash-hadu anna muhammadan rasulullah`, salutations of Allah be upon him... because your testimony for yourself is not permissible. All other people may say it, the Prophet, how can he say `ash-hadu anna muhammadan rasulullah`? So he is saying that this is a testimony for him. And indeed, that testimony was... that testimony was for Muhammad ibn Isma'il, peace be upon them. `wa amma shahadat al-a'immati 'alayhim al-salam wa sa'ir al-muslimin, fa-hiya laka, li-annaka natiqun sadisun`. And as for the testimony of the Imams, peace be upon them, and the rest of the Muslims, it is for you, because you are the sixth *natiq*. What has been stated? The status of Janab Muhammad ibn Isma'il is very high. How many Imams will there be after the Prophet 'alayhis salat was-salam? How many Imams? Seven weeks. Forty-nine Imams. The forty-ninth Imam is the seventh *Hafti* (weekly). So who are the heads of the seven weeks? In the first week, Mawlana Muhammad ibn Isma'il. In the second week, Mawlana Ma'add al-Mu'izz. In the third week, Imam al-Tayyib 'alayhis salam. These seven... the remaining all 49 Imams... are superior to them. Imam al-Tayyib 'alayhis salam. The fourth, Mawlana Ma'add al-Thani. Mawlana Ma'add. Ma'add al-Thani is there. After that, who is there? Mawlana Ahmad. Mawlana Ahmad. Then after that, Mawlana 'Ali. Mawlana 'Ali is not there. In the sixth week, Bayazid. And in the seventh week, the son of Mawlana... the son of the present living Imam. These seven. These seven are... they are all superior to all... all the other forty-two Imams. But among them too, what is there? The rank of four is the most superior. Who are the four? Mawlana Muhammad ibn Isma'il. Then... Mawlana Ma'add al-Mu'izz. It connected with Imam al-Tayyib. So Mawlana Ma'add al-Mu'izz, according to that... now... Janab Hali, in his couplets, has said that... in the couplets, it is said that "I draw a line. You, without touching this line, make it bigger or smaller." The line should not be touched. That line... make it bigger or smaller. What can be done? You yourself stated in a couplet that below it, draw a big line. Then that line will become small. Below it, a small... above it, draw a small line, then this will become big. That line was not touched, but by drawing a small line and a big line... so it is like that. There are seven. Now remaining are Mawlana Muhammad ibn Isma'il. And then what is there? Mawlana... Imam al-Tayyib. And then there is... Ma'add al-Thani's connection is then with Mawlana Ahmad. Mawlana Ahmad. Mawlana... now after that, this... this Mawlana 'Ali, his connection is with the seventh. How many are left? Four are left remaining. The four words of `kalimah la ilaha`. Four are left. Now, among these as well, two are the most superior. Who are they? Mawlana Muhammad ibn Isma'il and the Sahib. Among them too, Muhammad ibn Isma'il's rank is `sahib kasbat al-ilahiyyah`. He is unique. One versus one. `Sahib kasbat al-ilahiyyah`. `wa shahadat al-a'immah wa sa'ir al-muslimin fa-hiya li-al-payghambar, wa qawnu shahadah musannatun fi al-adhan, li-ma kanat shahadah al-awwala 'alayhi`. And the testimony of all the Imams and all the Muslims, it is for the Prophet. And the testimony being twofold in the *adhan*, because the first testimony was upon him. And the testimony being twofold... and the testimony is made twice in the *adhan*, because the first testimony was to point towards him. `wa al-thani li-muhammad ibn isma'il`. And the second is for Muhammad ibn Isma'il. Because he is the one who completes the era, the master of the apostles, and to him... his rank is that in the *da'im*, the *mutimmin* of your era are... the *mutimmin* are... their rank is in comparison to the *sahib-e dawr*. Their rank is... all the seven *sahibs* are there. The six *mutimmin* are so high that in comparison to the *sahib*, they are... they are equals. Imam al-Hasan, Imam al-Husayn, Imam 'Ali Zayn al-'Abidin, Imam Muhammad al-Baqir, Muhammad Ja'far al-Sadiq, Imam Isma'il. Although they are Imams of one rank, in the seventh part of the week, but... the Imams of the second week, they do not compare to them, but rather they compare to the seventh one. `wa al-thani li-muhammad ibn isma'il, alladhi huwa mutimm al-dawr, wa sahib al-rusul, wa ilayhi ishara mawlana al-mu'izz salawatullahi 'alayhi 'alayhima fi du'a' yawm al-sabt, idh huwa al-natiq al-sabi', wa amma qa'im al-qiyamah 'alayhi dhikruhu al-salam, fa-amruhu a'la min dhalika, li-annahu ghayru muntazimin fi silk al-rusul.` And the second is for Muhammad ibn Isma'il, who is the completer of the era and the master of the apostles, and our master al-Mu'izz, peace of God be upon them both, indicated towards him in the prayer of Saturday, as he is the seventh *natiq*. And as for the *Qa'im al-Qiyamah*, upon him be the mention of peace, his affair is loftier than that, because he is not included in the chain of the apostles. And our master al-Mu'izz, peace be upon him, has indicated that in the prayer of Saturday. As he is the seventh *natiq*. Who? Imam Muhammad ibn Isma'il. The seventh *natiq*, who they say is the Qa'im 'alayhis salat was-salam, his rank is very high. You are the seventh *natiq*, he stated. And as for the *Qa'im al-Qiyamah*, upon his mention be peace, his affair is loftier than that, because he is not included in the chain of the apostles. `li-kawni kulli wahidin minhum 'udwan min a'da'ihi`. Because each one of them is a limb from his limbs. Because every one of the apostles is a limb from your limbs, O *Qa'im al-Qiyamah* 'alayhis salam. `idh al-qa'im al-kulli alladhi qad sara 'aqlan kulliyyan, ka-ahad al-'uqul al-ibda'iyyah al-mujarradah`. As the Universal *Qa'im*, who has become a Universal Intellect, like one of the primordial, abstract intellects. Because he is the Universal *Qa'im*, such that he has become the Universal Intellect, like one of the primordial, abstract intellects. `wa huwa al-qa'im bi-tadbir al-'alam`. And he is the one who maintains the administration of the world. And you are the one who maintains the administration of the world. `ka-ma sabaqa min amthalihi al-qa'imina bi-tadbir 'alam al-tabi'ah fi rutbat al-'ashir`. As has preceded from his likes, those who maintain the administration of the natural world in the rank of the Tenth. Just as it has preceded from you, from your likes, who are the administrators of the natural world, in the rank of the Tenth. In the rank of the Tenth. They are the representatives of the Tenth. The *Qa'im al-Qiyamah*, the administration of the entire era is yours. `wa muhammad ibn isma'il min sa'ir al-nutuqa' al-ilahiyyin, alladhina hum muhammad wa ibrahim salamu-llahi 'alayhim ajma'in, wa thalith lahuma, idh kullu wahidin minhum majmal al-maqamat taqaddamathu, wa sar al-nutuqa' du'at al-a'immah azmanihim, wa kullu wahidin minhum 'udwan min a'da' al-imam al-tali, li-imam 'asrihi ka-ma sabaqa bi-al-qawl`. And Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from all the divine *nutuqa'*, who are Muhammad and Ibrahim, peace of God be upon them all, and he is the third to them both. Since each one of them is a summary of the stations that preceded him, and the *nutuqa'* became the summoners of the Imams of their times. And each one of them is a limb from the limbs of the following Imam, for the Imam of his era, as has preceded in the saying. And Muhammad ibn Isma'il is from all the divine *nutuqa'*. Like the *natiq*... from the divine *nutuqa'*, whose rank of divine utterance was just mentioned. Such that they are the Prophet and Ibrahim, and peace be upon them all. And he is the third of those two. And he is the third of those two. Because every... every *natiq*... is a summary... a summary of the stations that preceded him. And all the *nutuqa'* are summoners for the Imams of their era. And every one of them is a limb from the limbs of the following Imam, for the Imam of his era, as has preceded in the saying. The *nutq* are also called *du'at*. So he is saying that these divine utterances have a different quality. The rank of the divine utterance is separate from that of the *natiq*. In the divine utterance, who is there? In this era, he has stated: Janab `thalathah ha`. Janab Imam Hunayd, and Janab Ibrahim, Janab... Prophet 'alayhis salat was-salam, Janab Muhammad ibn Isma'il. Four. And all the *sa'ib* (seventh) Imams who have come, the *sa'ib* Imams, they are all possessors of the divine utterance. The rank of divine utterance, they possess it. So... all these... but among them, the highest rank belongs to whom? It is stated that it belongs to Janab Prophet, Janab Ibrahim, and Janab... Muhammad... Janab Muhammad ibn Isma'il. These are... and the conflicts that are there, in them are strange points.

Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. *Al-faṣl al-rābiʿ. la-qāʾilin an yaqūla: fa-idhā kāna Mawlānā Aamir, radiyallahu 'anhu, qad intaqala ilā dāri raḥmatillāh, wa Mawlānā Imām al-Tayyib Abu 'l-Qāsim, salawatullah 'alayh, fī ḥālati ṭ-ṭufūliyyah, fa man al-muʿallim lahu?* So who is... *fa man al-muʿallim lahu?* So who is the teacher for him? *fa man al-muʿallim lahu fī awāni t-taʿlīm, wa man al-mufīd...* So who is the *mufid*... *wa man al-mufīd liman yu'allim 'alayhi fī ḥālati ṣigharihi min man yastafīdu 'l-qadūm 'alayhi wa 'l-muhājarata ilayhi. Fa l-yaʿlam annahu min waqti nassi abīhi 'alayhi wa satrihi lahu lā yufāriqu l-bāb ḥujjatan wa dāʿiyan wa nirās. Wa hum al-mufīdūna liman ittaṣala bihim wa quddira lahu 'l-muhājara...* *wa quddira lahu...* *wa quddira lahu 'l-muhājara ilā bayna yadayhi. Wa hum al-muʿallimūna lahu fī awāni t-taʿlīm mā yajib taʿlīmuhu, wa 'l-muraqqūna lahu fī rutbati d-dīn.* *Al-muraqqūna.* *Al-muraqqūna lahu fī rutbati d-dīn. Wa li-dhālika nītu bihi wa-stataru bi-stitārihi. Wa kullamā ʿānat nuqlatu wāḥidin minhum lam yantaqil ḥattā... ḥattā aqāma man yakhlufuhu fī maqāmihi wa yanūbu manābihi ilā an yablugha... yablugha salāmullah 'alayh... wa yaʿūdu mufīdan li-ḥudūdihi. Hādhihi...* *mufīdan.* *mufīdan.* *mufīdan 'alayhim barakātihi wa taʾyīdātihi wa mawāddihi kamā sabaqa min al-qawl fī jaddayhi Muḥammad wa Ibrāhīm, salawatullah 'alayhim.*

So, if for the one who says... some person asks this question... if... that Maulana Aamir, *radiyallahu 'anhu*, has passed away and gone to the abode of Allah's mercy, and Maulana Imam al-Tayyib Abu'l-Qasim, *salawatullah 'alayh*, is in a state of infancy... so who is his teacher? Who is the one who teaches him during the period of instruction? And who is their *mufid* (benefactor/teacher)? And who is the *mufid* for that person who migrates... who migrates towards him in the state of concealment, in his childhood? And that concealment, when he is in the period of concealment... from among those who desire to come to you and migrate to you. People who migrate and come, whether in a manifest (*zahir*) or hidden (*batin*) way. People who migrate physically are also there in concealment, and their supplications reach him. In both ways.

*Fa l-ya'lam...* (Let him know...). So he should know... they are giving the answer to the question now... that *annahu min waqti nassi abīhi 'alayhi* (that from the time of his father's designation upon him)... that when your... your father... from the time of your father's designation upon you... when your father designated you for this position... upon Imam al-Tayyib, *alayhissalam*. *Wa satrihi lahu* (and his concealment)... and your being concealed. He does not leave the *bāb* (gate), the *ḥujjah* (proof), and the *dā'ī al-balāgh* (summoner of the message). These three individuals are always with you. And they are the *mufid* for those... *li man ittaṣala bihim* (for whoever connects with them). For those people who are connected with you. *Wa quddira lahu 'l-muhājara ilā bayna yadayhi* (And for whom migration to his presence is destined). And for whom migration is destined... in your presence, before you. And those for whom migration has been granted, that they should migrate in your presence. *Wa hum al-muʿallimūna lahu fī awāni t-taʿlīm.* And they are the ones who teach you during the period of instruction. *Wa hum al-muʿallimūna lahu fī awāni t-taʿlīm mā yajib taʿlīmuhu* (And they are the ones who teach him during the period of instruction what must be taught). And they are the ones who teach you during the period of instruction. *Mā yajib taʿlīmuhu* (what is necessary to teach him). And *wa 'l-muraqqūna lahu* (and those who elevate him)... those who grant promotion (*taraqqi*) in the rank of religion. What is the word? *Muraqqūna*. How is it written? What is it from? *Raqa'*. *Raqa'*. From that... its meaning is promotion (*taraqqi*), to be elevated. No. What... what is the meaning of *raqa'*? To ascend. To ascend. *Taraqqi kiyā* (he made progress). What? The meaning of *raqa'* is *taraqqi kiyā* (he made progress). *Al-rāqī* (the one who ascends). The one who makes progress. From that, what is... *raqqā*... what would be its meaning? *Raqqā*. He gave promotion. The one who gives promotion. One who makes progress and one who gives progress. The one who makes progress is called *rāqī*. And the one who gives promotion is called *muraqqī*. *Raqqā, yuraqqī, muraqqī*. From that is *al-muraqqūna*. The *yā'* has been dropped. *Al-muraqqūna lahu* (those who elevate him). Those who give you promotion... in the rank of religion.

*Wa li-dhālika nītu bihi* (And for that reason, they were connected to him). And for this reason, they were joined with you. What is *nītu* from? What is your *nātā* (relationship) with them? What does it mean? In Urdu, we say it. What is your *nātā*? Meaning, what is your relationship? *Nūn, alif, ṭā'*. *Nātā*. Relationship. This is in the passive voice. *Nītu bihi* (they were connected to him). And for this reason, they were joined... they... with you. *Nītu bihi*. *Wa-stataru bi-stitārihi* (And they were concealed by his concealment). And they became hidden along with your being hidden. *Wa kullamā ʿānat nuqlatu wāḥidin minhum* (And whenever the passing of one of them draws near). And whenever the passing of any one of them is near... among them. The three... the *mufid* are... who are they? One is the *bāb*, the *ḥujjah*, and the *dā'ī al-balāgh*, who do not leave your presence. They are always there. And when the passing of any one of them occurs, *lam yantaqil ḥattā aqāma man yakhlufuhu fī maqāmihi* (he does not pass away until he has appointed one who will succeed him in his position). He does not pass away until he appoints those people to his position who are his successors. *Wa yanūbu manābihi* (And who deputizes in his place). And who are deputies in his place... in their place. *Ilā an yablugha...* (Until he reaches...). Until they reach... *salāmullah 'alayh* (peace of Allah be upon him)... his maturity. And they return... *wa yaʿūdu mufīdan li-ḥudūdihi* (and he returns as a benefactor for his ranks). And they become *mufid* for their ranks. As it happened in the case of Sayyidna Ja'far. Who were your... who was the *mufid*? Sayyidna Muhammad ibn al-Fayd, *'alayhissalam*. When he reached 20 years of age, he entrusted all his affairs and then after that, Sayyidna Ja'far became the *mufid*. It was mentioned that once, Sayyidna Ja'far and Imam... Sayyidna Muhammad ibn al-Fayd were teaching. Sayyidna Ja'far, you were either listening or studying, what was it... Something came up and Sayyidna Muhammad ibn al-Fayd said, "I don't understand this matter." At that time, Sayyidna Ja'far said that perhaps what is meant by this is this, and this... he gave some reference. So Sayyidna Muhammad ibn al-Fayd was very happy and what did he say? "*Al-ān ṣārat al-mawāddu Ja'fariyyah*" (Now the support/reinforcements have become Ja'fari). Now the support has become Ja'fari, he said. Your...
So the passing of all three is in their own power?
It is not in their power, it is when Allah decrees the time for that.
But they do not pass away until...
...they appoint a successor in their place. Some other person.
*Wa yaʿūdu mufīdan li-ḥudūdihi* (And he returns as a benefactor for his ranks). And they become *mufid*... the Imam himself becomes... the one who bestows upon them... upon his ranks... his blessings, support, and reinforcements. *Kamā sabaqa min al-qawl fī jaddayhi Muḥammad wa Ibrāhīm* (As was previously stated regarding his two grandfathers, Muhammad and Ibrahim). As it has been established from the statement regarding your two grandfathers, Muhammad and Ibrahim, *salawatullah 'alayhim*. Your grandfather the Prophet and your grandfather Ibrahim. The Prophet did what? He took from five, he gave to five. And my Lord... between me and my Lord are five. Tell me, who are they? Who are the five he took from? *Akhadhtu min khamsah* (I took from five). *Akhadhtu min khamsah*. Who are the five? Maulana... Ubayy... Ubayy ibn Ka'b. First Ubayy ibn Ka'b. After that... The Prophet. Who? What about Maysarah? Zayd ibn 'Amr. 'Amr. Zayd ibn 'Amr. First Ubayy ibn Ka'b, then Zayd ibn 'Amr, then 'Amr ibn Nufayl. To remember this, Zayd ibn 'Amr, 'Amr ibn Nufayl. After that, Maysarah. Then Khadijah. *Akhadhtu min khamsah* (I took from five). *Wa sallamtu ilā khamsah* (And I delivered to five). Who are the five he delivered to? He gave to five, who are they? Maulana... Maulana 'Ali... Maulana 'Ali ibn al-Abi Talib... Maulana al-Hasan, Maulana al-Husayn, and... who was he given to? Maulana... Maulana Muhammad ibn Isma'il. Maulana 'Ali... Maulana 'Ali. First is Maulana 'Ali. Imam al-Hasan, Imam al-Husayn, Maulana 'Ali ibn al-Abi Talib, Maulana Baqir, Maulana Ja'far al-Sadiq. That makes five. No, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib is not there. Maulana Muhammad ibn Isma'il is mentioned. In that, there was no mention of Maulana Isma'il. Let me see what's written... The five are... the five are the *ulu al-'azm*... *baynī wa bayna Rabbī khamsah* (between me and my Lord are five)... *silsilah sughrā* (the minor chain)... and... *Wa 'l-khamsatu 'lladhīna samawtu fī khāliqī fa-huma 't-tukhāhu 'l-khamsah* (And the five whom I named in my creation, they are the five brothers). The five I took from are the five *nutuqā'* (speaking prophets). After that, *sallamtu ilā khamsah* (I delivered to five)... and they are... Who are the five? Amir al-Mu'minin, 'Ali, Hasan and Husayn, al-Baqir, and Muhammad ibn 'Ali. Or Baqir, *ibtur al-'ilm* (cleave open knowledge). And Maulana Muhammad ibn Isma'il. These five were mentioned. 'Ali ibn al-Abi Talib is not in it. Maulana 'Ali, Hasan, Husayn, Maulana Muhammad al-Baqir, and Maulana Muhammad ibn Isma'il. And between me and my Lord are five. Who? The five *mu'allimin* (teachers) were mentioned. *Akhadhtu min khamsah* (I took from five). I took from five, I gave to five. The five he took from are the five *nutuqā'*... The five are... the *silsilah*... and *baynī wa bayna Rabbī khamsah* (between me and my Lord are five), those are the five *mu'allimin*. *Akhadhtu min khamsah*, who are they? The five *nutuqā'*. He took from the five *nutuqā'*. Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, 'Isa. I took from the five. *Wa sallamtu ilā khamsah* (And I delivered to five). Who are the five? That... my Lord, Imam... Imam Abu Talib... between them are five. Who are the five? The five *mu'allimin*. No... The five *mu'allimin*... *Wa 'l-khamsatu 'llatī baynī wa bayna Rabbī hum al-ḥudūd al-dīniyyah allatī akhadhtu 'anhum* (And the five who are between me and my Lord are the religious ranks from whom I took). The ones you have taken from. Who are they? Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Zayd ibn 'Amr, 'Amr ibn Nufayl, Maysarah and Khadijah. You were elevated above them. When you were elevated above them, then... It is said about you that you acquired Sayyidna Adam, who, in his form, the Prophet, *salatullah 'alayh*, acquired Sayyidna Nuh. And to whom? Sayyidna Ibrahim. He acquired the prophet. You acquired Sayyidna Musa and Sayyidna 'Isa. So, Sayyidna Adam, whose... the reality that was his... the spiritual form... Imam Husayn... Sayyidna Adam's was given to... Sayyidna Nuh's which was... the *surat* (form)... you gave to Sayyidna Fatimah. That of Sayyidna Adam was given... and that of Sayyidna Nuh... from that... the *surat* that was there, you gave to Sayyidna Fatimah. That is why you used to perform *nawḥā* (lamentation). And Sayyidna 'Ali, *salawatullah 'alayh*, you gave him that of Sayyidna Ibrahim. Imam al-Hasan was given that of Sayyidna Musa. And Imam al-Husayn, you gave him that of Sayyidna 'Isa. That is why Sayyidna Husayn and Sayyidna 'Isa are similar. What is the similarity? Six months... He also remained for six months in his mother's womb, and he also remained for six months. This is one similarity. Then what is it? A second similarity is what? That Sayyidna 'Isa was persecuted (*marqūb*). Sayyidna Husayn, *alayhissalatu wassalam*, was also persecuted. Two similarities. It is mentioned. *Ummuhumā batūlāt* (Their two mothers are *batūl*). This has also been said, that both their mothers were *batūl* (chaste/devoted). Your... Sayyidna Maryam, and your... Sayyidna Fatimah. Three similarities. And Sayyidna Musa, *alayhissalatu wassalam*, to whom was his *surat* given? You... to Imam Hasan... Imam al-Hasan, *alayhissalam*. Sayyidna Adam's... I don't recall. You had said in a *majlis* that I have kept... The Prophet's saying that the one of Sayyidna Adam, I have kept... [unclear] Sayyidna Adam... [unclear]. The one of Sayyidna Adam was given to... Sayyidna Ubayy... to Sayyidna Ubayy ibn Ka'b. Sayyidna Ubayy ibn Ka'b. These five were also given by you. From them, some things... the five prophets, their things you gave to these five. The ones you took from. In some book, this is also mentioned. It's in the book "Ibtida' al-Da'wah"... Three days after the martyrdom, his apparition appeared. That of Sayyidna 'Isa, his apparition appeared. That of Imam Husayn, his apparition also appeared. Sayyidna Ghulam Husayn mentions three. *Ummuhumā batūlāt* (Their two mothers are *batūl*)... he added this later.
*Wa qawluhu 'lladhī 'l-madhkūr tarbiyatan fī jaddayhi Muḥammad wa Ibrāhīm...* (And his statement which is mentioned regarding the upbringing in his two grandfathers, Muhammad and Ibrahim...). As it is with your grandfathers... Sayyidna दादा Muhammad and Ibrahim, *salawatullah 'alayh*. ...About Ibrahim, as you saw what? First, you saw the stars, then you saw... the moon, right? Then you saw the sun. When the sun set, you said, "*Lā uḥibbu 'l-āfilīn*" (I love not those that set). The same is with you, it was said that, well... three were mentioned... star, moon, and sun. Star, moon, and sun.
*Wa tawallā 'l-ḥudūd al-madhkūrah li-tarbiyatihi Mawlānā...* (And the aforementioned ranks took charge of his upbringing, our Master...). And he took charge of the aforementioned ranks. Who took charge? Imam al-Tayyib, *alayhissalatu wassalam*, when he reached maturity. *Wa hāʾulāʾi 'l-ḥudūd al-thalāthah hum al-mawsūlāt al-thalāthah min al-kawākib allatī takhtassu bi-sh-shams* (And these three ranks are the three connections from the planets which are particular to the sun). *Wa kawnuhā muddatan lahum wa liman dūnahā min al-kawākib* (And it being a provider for them and for those below them from the planets). *Idh al-Imām, 'alayhissalam, mawsūlun bi-sh-shams wa 'l-mumidd lahu wa li-l-ḥudūd al-thalāthah as-sābiqah 'alayhi fi 'l-wujūd alladhīna kānū mutawallīna li-tarbiyatihi fī ḥāli ṣigharihi wa taʿlīmihi, thumma ʿāda mufīdan lahum mufayyiḍan barakātihi wa taʾyīdātihi 'alayhim. Wa 's-salāmullāh 'alayhi mawsūlu 'l-qalb fi 'l-jism fa-l-mumidd limā fawqahu min al-ḥawāssi wa limā taḥtahu.*
And these three ranks... And these three ranks... they are connections. They are connected to the three... *ḥujjah*, and *dā'ī al-balāgh*. From the planets. They are connected to three planets. Which derive their light from the sun. Who are the three planets? Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars. *Wa kawnuhā* (And it being)... and being a provider for them... for the sun... and being a provider for them, *wa liman dūnahā min al-kawākib* (and for those below them from the planets)... for your *āftāb* (sun). And *kawnuhā*, right? *kawnuhā*... the sun is feminine. And its being a provider of support to them. And those who are below it from the planets. Because the Imam, *alayhissalam*, is connected to the sun. And he is the one who gives support to the full ranks... the three ranks that preceded him. And they are in existence. *Alladhīna kānū mutawallīna* (who were in charge). And who were... in charge of his upbringing for you, in your state of infancy and your instruction. Then he returned as a *mufid* for them. Then he turned back and became *mufid*. He bestowed blessings and support upon them. And *salāmullah 'alayh* is connected to the heart... connected to the heart in the body, in the form of the body. The sun is connected, and the heart is connected. The heart does what? And... in the body. So it is the one who provides support to its higher senses and to what is below them.
