...yantazir bi-awwalikum quduma akhirikum. Yantazir bi-awwalikum quduma akhirikum. The first ones are waiting, by means of your first ones, for the arrival of your last ones. First are waiting for those who are going to come after. Yantazir means they wait, your awwal... Your awwal, your first ones... the arrival of your akhir, your last ones. So this has been explained, that those who have reached first, they are waiting for all the people to come and join the gathering. The first ones are waiting for those who are to come. Yes, for those who are coming. For the akhir, those who will come later. Their taraqqi is connected to them. Yes. If they come, then this taraqqi... They will come, then... For the awwal, the awwal are waiting for the... So how can the awwal be... It's "bi-awwalikum," not for the awwal. The awwal are not... It's "yantazir awwalakum," not "bi-awwalikum." "yantazir bi-awwalikum." It is not "yantazir awwalakum," it is "bi-awwalikum." "yantazir bi-awwalikum." They wait, your... They wait... They wait for your awwal... They wait, by means of your awwal, for the arrival of your akhir. Those who have reached are waiting for the later ones to come. They will welcome them. That is... that is the meaning. That those who have reached first, they are waiting there for when the ones who are coming will arrive. The ones behind, when will they come and become qa'im... Like the awwal have a concept of being established towards the qa'im. That without a qa'im, he cannot make taraqqi until he establishes someone as a qa'im. Are they referring to that relationship? They do taraqqi... there... when they gather in the station of the 'Ashir, so the 'Ashir is waiting for when the akhir ones will come and it will become a great and glorious gathering. When all have completed their taraqqi. That is its meaning. Regarding hijabat, there was also a question. This hijabat that they do, so, as you say, the hijab that comes, is it bil-jism, inside the jism, belonging to the jism, like a covering over a nabi, a hijab comes in that form, or is it that... some ajza'... what is it? Hijab has been explained regarding... In other books, it has also been explained. That the nasut and sharif, which is... the nasut and sharif is... on the surat, there is no qisas. Yes. The surat is pure and clean. The nafs is pure and clean. Qisas is on what? On that which is of the earth. Yes. So at the time when... the time for giving qisas comes, and some person is present in the world, then a tahrik is given, as has been explained for all. They give tahrik to their hijab, and from it, that... where the nasut is, the nasut-e-sharif is, it comes and becomes muttasil with the one from whom qisas is taken. So that... what... in what shakl do they come? Any human who is in front of him. It appears to him that he is killing Imam Husayn. It is apparent that he is martyring Imam al-Husayn. Whereas he is not martyring Imam al-Husayn. It is that hijab with which his qisas are pending, that has come and become muttasil. The mudabbir is the Imam, 'alayhi al-salatu wa al-salam. The one whose qisas was pending, he comes at that time and becomes a participant in it. And he obtains his due from him. Who are the fida'i of Imam al-Husayn, 'alayhi al-salatu wa al-salam? Hazrat 'Abbas. Hazrat... Who are the fida'i of Hazrat 'Abbas? Janab Muslim bin 'Aqil. And with Janab Muslim bin 'Aqil, what happened is that the Imam, 'alayhi al-salatu wa al-salam... those with whom giving and taking was pending, he connected them. They came at that time. That nasut became a participant at that time. He is thinking that I am martyring Muslim bin 'Aqil. Whereas the one with whom his qisas was pending in the world, he was present at that time. This is what has been said in the books. So the hijab of Hazrat 'Abbas that came, so it took the shakl of Imam Husayn, salawatullahi 'alayh. The shakl of Imam Husayn. So the prominent shakl is... It is a shakl-e-misaal, any shakl. In any shakl, he can take form. As it has been said, regarding Mawlana Amin, salawatullahi 'alayh, an incident has been mentioned. They were gathered. They came and said that there is mention of food and also of prayer. They said that you are invited to our place today, and you had this conversation with us. Someone said, "What are you saying? Janab Aminuddin had food with us." Someone else said, "He had it with us." In this way, there were several individuals who said, "No, he had food with us." Then they asked him... So you have explained... you have given a very good explanation, that the kitab... He led the prayer for Salman al-Farsi in... In Mada'in. Mada'in is... He went to Mada'in and led the prayer. Whereas it was several miles away... a thousand miles away. So it is one thing and... So that... with... with 'Isa 'alayhi al-salam... Judas was changed. Yes. Judas was also changed... with 'Isa 'alayhi al-salam. *Shubbiha lahum* (it was made to appear so to them). A man, in Iraq, he was... doing... he was giving speeches. So a woman went. She said that... they had claimed... that *saluni qabla an tafqiduni* (ask me before you lose me). Ask me before you lose me. So they asked a question. That woman stood up. And she said that tell me... that Amir... Amir al-Mu'minin, 'alayhi al-salatu wa al-salam, left Madinah and went to Mada'in, and you led the prayer for Janab Salman al-Farsi. You led the namaz, the janazah prayer, and buried him. And 'Uthman's murder happened in Madinah, and Janab Amir al-Mu'minin was present in Madinah. Why did you not lead his prayer? So he said, "O woman, you are asking a question. Where have you come from?" She said, "I have come from Madinah." He said, "Did your husband give you permission to leave Madinah and come to Iraq? Did you come with your husband's permission?" So she said, "Tell me, how did 'A'ishah go from Madinah to Basra to fight? Did she go with the permission of the Prophet?" The question was very chakkardar. He was wearing a very large 'amama. He took off the 'amama and threw it. These are historical incidents. The Muslims did not allow him to be buried in Jannat al-Baqi'. That's why his... his... who had come? Muhammad bin Abi Bakr... they had come... your... those who had done the ghusl... The Muslims did not allow 'Uthman to be buried. So there was a graveyard next to it, the graveyard of the Jews, he was buried there. Now they have expanded that graveyard and included it in Baqi'. Previously, when we performed ziyarat, Janab Fatimah bint Asad and Janab 'Uthman ibn Maz'un... Mawlana 'Uthman ibn Maz'un... their two graves were in Jannat al-Baqi', outside the wall. Outside the fence. Janab 'Uthman... both graves were together. We went and performed ziyarat. Hazrat Mawlatuna Fatimah bint Asad and Hazrat 'Uthman ibn Maz'un... It was a graveyard, but the fence was... the fence was built to include it later. So the connection of nasl is that they were Jews... There were many reasons. He was buried in the Jewish graveyard... 'Uthman. And... and in those days, women were not allowed to visit graves. They were not allowed to enter Jannat al-Baqi'. It is still the case now. It is still the case now. So with me were Wazir behn and others, all were with me, women were there. We said we have to do ziyarat, how will we do it? There was a big building in front. So I took them to the top of the building. That was in front of the building. We climbed up, and from there we performed ziyarat of the graves. And 'Uthman ibn Maz'un was a very special companion of the Prophet, 'alayhi al-salatu wa al-salam. Very pious, very God-fearing. Janab 'Ali, salawatullahi 'alayh, when a son was born, Janab 'Abbas was born, Hazrat 'Abbas ibn 'Ali, and others... and the fourth son, your 'Uthman, your name... you named him 'Uthman. And after naming him 'Uthman, he said that I have named him after Hazrat 'Uthman ibn Maz'un, the companion. This... you have... He did not say this for any other name. For this name, he said. Hazrat 'Uthman ibn Maz'un, the companion. Names can be kept? Yes. From that tradition, can names be kept? Abu Bakr can also be kept. 'Abd al-Rahman... there are many names like that, 'Abd al-Rahman. We can keep them. That is, the mas'alah... The da'i... a da'i named Abu Sufyan passed away. Abu Sufyan. Abu Sufyan al-Hulwani and Abu Sufyan al-Khalafi. Abu Sufyan al-Hulwani, the two who... from Mahdiyya... 'Ubayd Allah al-Mahdi had sent them. Abu Sufyan's name.

<!-- lecture 64 -->

Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim (In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful). Wal-fajr (By the dawn). Wa layalin 'ashr (And [by] ten nights). Wash-shaf'i wal-watr (And [by] the even and the odd). Wal-layli idha yasr (And [by] the night when it passes). Hal fi dhalika qasamul li dhi hijr (Is there [not] in that an oath for one of understanding?). Alam tara kayfa fa'ala rabbuka bi 'aad (Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with 'Aad). Irama dhatil 'imaad (With Iram of the lofty pillars). Allati lam yukhlaq mithluha fil-bilad (The like of which were not created in the land). Wa thamoodalladhina jab-us-sakhra bil-wad (And [with] Thamud, who carved out the rocks in the valley). Wa fir'awna dhil-awtad (And [with] Pharaoh, owner of the stakes). Alladhina taghaw fil-bilad ([All of] whom transgressed within the lands). Fa aktharu fihal-fasad (And increased therein corruption). Fa sabba 'alayhim rabbuka sawta 'adhab (So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment). Inna rabbaka la bil-mirsad (Indeed, your Lord is in observation). Fa ammal-insanu idha mab-talahu rabbuhu fa akramahu wa na''amahu fa yaqoolu rabbi akraman (And as for man, when his Lord tries him and [is] generous to him and favors him, he says, "My Lord has honored me."). Wa amma idha mab-talahu fa qadara 'alayhi rizqahu fa yaqoolu rabbi ahanan (But when He tries him and restricts his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me."). Kalla bal la tukrimoonal-yateem (No! But you do not honor the orphan). Wa la tahaaddoona 'ala ta'amil-miskeen (And you do not encourage one another to feed the poor). Wa ta'kuloonat-turatha aklal-lamma (And you consume inheritance, devouring [it] altogether). Wa tuhibboonal-mala hubban jamma (And you love wealth with immense love). Kalla idha dukkatil-ardu dakkan dakka (No! When the earth has been leveled - pounded and crushed). Wa ja'a rabbuka wal-malaku saffan saffa (And your Lord has come and the angels, rank upon rank). Wa jee'a yawma'idhim bi jahannam (And brought [within view], that Day, is Hell). Yawma'idhiy-yatadhakkarul-insanu wa anna la hudh-dhikra (That Day, man will remember, but how will the remembrance avail him?). Yaqoolu ya laytani qaddamtu li hayati (He will say, "Oh, I wish I had sent forth [good] for my life."). Fa yawma'idhil-la yu'adhdhibu 'adhabahu ahad (So on that Day, none will punish [as severely] as His punishment). Wa la yoothiqu wathaqahu ahad (And none will bind [as severely] as His binding). Ya ayyatuhan-nafsul-mutma'innah (O reassured soul). Irji'i ila rabbiki radiyatam-mardiyyah (Return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]). Fadhkuli fi 'ibadi (And enter among My [righteous] servants). Wadhkuli jannati (And enter My Paradise).

<!-- lecture 65 -->

*Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim* (In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful). *Al-hamdu lillahi Rabb al-'alamin* (All praise is for Allah, the Lord of the worlds), *Al-Rahman al-Rahim* (The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful), *Maliki Yawm al-Din* (Master of the Day of Judgment). *Iyyaka na'budu wa iyyaka nasta'in* (It is You we worship and You we ask for help). *Ihdina al-sirat al-mustaqim* (Guide us to the straight path), *sirat alladhina an'amta 'alayhim* (The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor), *ghayr al-maghdubi 'alayhim wa la al-dallin* (not of those who have earned [Your] anger or of those who are astray).
